that Allah create a boy from the two of you «Allah does what He wills» (Q. 3:40) nothing defeats Him He speaks here of doing, and in the case of ʿĪsā of creating, because the case of ʿĪsā breaks the customary order more severely: this is doing, that is creating. «He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign» a mark of my wife’s pregnancy «He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people» you will be kept from speaking to them, [occupied] with the remembrance of Allah «for three days» this is the basis of the three-day retreat that the righteous undertake «except by sign» a gesture «and remember your Lord much, and glorify» pray «in the evening and the early morning» (Q. 3:41) [and] recall «when the angels said: Maryam, Allah has chosen you» selected you «and purified you» from men’s touch «and chosen you above the women of the worlds» (Q. 3:42) the people of your time meaning the world of her own time The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨There have attained perfection among men⟩

⟨many, and of women none has reached perfection except a few: Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, and Āsiya the daughter of Muzāḥim⟩ [32] ⟨, and Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid, and ʿĀʾisha the daughter of Abū Bakr, and Fāṭima the daughter of Muḥammad ﷺ.⟩ [33] Of them the poet says:
⟨Were women as we have mentioned, / women would be given precedence over men.⟩ [34]

The Prophet ﷺ said of ʿĀʾisha: ⟨You are the mistress of the women of the worlds.⟩ She said: ⟨How shall I be the mistress of women, when there are Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, and Āsiya the daughter of Muzāḥim, and Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid?⟩ The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Maryam is the mistress of the women of her world, and Āsiya is the mistress of the women of her world, and Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid is the mistress of the women of her world, and you are the mistress of women, just as I am the master of men.⟩ She is the most excellent of them. [35]
. «O Maryam»
«Be devout to your Lord» — obey Him — «and prostrate yourself and bow with those who bow» (Q. 3:43) — pray with those who pray — «That is of»

«the tidings of the unseen, which We reveal to you» — O Muḥammad — «and you were not with them when they cast their pens» — into the water, drawing lots — «which of them should take charge of Maryam; and you were not with them when they were disputing» (Q. 3:44) — over her guardianship. And recall «when the angels said»

Jibrīl «O Maryam, Allah gives you glad tidings of a word from Him» he is ʿĪsā «his name is the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, held in esteem» possessed of standing in this world, through prophethood «and the hereafter» through intercession and the high degrees «and of those brought near» (Q. 3:45) in the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The himma of a human being overpowers all created things. If you reflect on the case of Ḥanna bint Fāqūdā: she set her heart on a child who would be among the servants of the sanctuary, and so she asked for a child, and her child came as a girl — but a girl who jostled with the men in the stations until she became one of the men, until the Qurʾan described her: «And she was among the devoutly obedient men» (Q. 66:12) He did not say min al-qānitāt [with the feminine plural]. A girl as though she were a man — because her mother, when she asked for her, was attached to perfected men, and so Allah granted her a girl who attained the stations of the men. And Zakariyyāʾ, when he looked at the breaches of the customary order in Maryam’s case, he too set his heart on a child and asked for a child. Allah granted him a male child, Yaḥyā — but a male who did not marry and did not approach a woman. Through him appeared the state of Maryam, on which his father’s himma had been fixed, so that he became ḥaṣūr — not out of incapacity, but he abstained from women. And Maryam brought forth a child, ʿĪsā, through contact with Jibrīl, and so the child came to be characterised by the attributes of the angels, until he joined the highest assembly and dwelt in the heavens and came to fly with the angels. For this reason the child is affected by what his parents engage in at the time of his coming into being. «And he will speak to people in the cradle» as an infant, before the time of speech — when he was born he spoke, as will come in Sūrat Maryam «and in maturity» after forty years «and of the righteous. She said: My Lord, how shall I have a child when no man has touched me» in marriage «He said» the matter is «thus» — that a child be created from you without a father «Allah creates what He wills; when He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is» (Q. 3:46–47) so it comes to be. «And He will teach him the Book» writing «and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel» he memorised the Torah while he was in his mother’s womb «and a messenger to the Children of Isrāʾīl» (Q. 3:48–49) in childhood. Jibrīl breathed into the bosom of her shift and she conceived, and her affair was as has been mentioned

in Sūrat Maryam. When she conceived ʿĪsā, whenever she was alone, apart from people, ʿĪsā would speak with her while he was in her womb; and when people came, he occupied himself with the remembrance of Allah and left off speaking with his mother. «Then she brought him to her people, carrying him» (Q. 19:27) as will come. Yūsuf the carpenter was a relative of Maryam. He saw her pregnant and was astonished. Whenever he wanted to suspect her on account of the pregnancy, he looked at her righteousness and saw her far from suspicion; and whenever he wanted to clear her, he observed that she had conceived and had no husband. Until one day he addressed her: O Maryam, there is something in my heart that I keep pushing away from myself, and I have become unable to push it away. I must ask you a question: does a crop grow without a seed? She said: Yes. Does a tree grow without planting? She said: Yes. Is a child brought into being without a father? She said: Yes. Do you not see that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the crop grow before the seed? The seed came from the crop that Allah made grow without a seed, and the tree Allah made grow before any tree was planted, so the planting came from the tree that grew before the planting. And the child — do you not know that Allah created Ādam without a father and without a mother? The children are from Ādam, and Ādam has no father and no mother. So what was in his heart was healed completely; he became certain that Allah had granted her a child without a father. [36] «that I have come to you with a sign» a token of my truthfulness «from your Lord, that I create for you from»

«clay, in the form of a bird» like its shape «then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah’s permission, and I heal» I cure «the blind from birth and the leper, and I revive the dead by Allah’s permission» (Q. 3:49) He repeated this so that divinity would not be imagined of him. He used to revive the dead. One day they said: He revives the dead who have died recently, but as for one who died long ago, he is not able to revive him; we will not believe that you raise the dead unless you raise for us Sām son of Nūḥ, who died four thousand years ago. He said: Show me his grave. So they showed him his grave, and he called him: O Sām. He came out, and half his head had turned grey. They said to him: You have turned grey, yet you died in an age before greying? Greying appeared only in the time of Ibrāhīm, and Sām died a thousand years before Ibrāhīm. He said: When ʿĪsā called me, I was addressed from the side of al-Ḥaqq: Answer the Spirit of Allah. I thought the Resurrection had come, and so I was terrified, until I turned grey. ʿĪsā said to him:

Return to your place. He said: On condition that I do not taste the bitterness of death a second time. He said: How [is it with] the bitterness of death? He said: Since I died — you died four thousand years ago? He said: Yes. He said: To this moment I find the bitterness of death in my throat. [37] «and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up» you conceal «in your houses. Truly in that» the aforementioned «surely a sign» (Q. 3:49)

«for you, if you are believers» (Q. 3:49) «and confirming what was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you» in it so he made lawful for them, of fish and birds, whatever has no spur «and I have come to you with a sign from your Lord» (Q. 3:50)

He repeated it for emphasis and in order to build upon it. «So fear Allah and obey me» in what I command you. «Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This» is what I command you, «is a straight path» (Q. 3:51) «And when he sensed» [that is] knew «— ʿĪsā — disbelief from them», and they intended to kill him, «he said: Who are my helpers» my supporters, going «to Allah» so that I may help His religion? «And the disciples said: We are Allah’s helpers» the supporters of His religion — they are ʿĪsā’s adherents — «we believe in Allah, and bear witness» O ʿĪsā, «that we are Muslims» (Q. 3:52) «Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down» of the Gospel, «and we follow the Messenger» ʿĪsā, «so write us down with those who bear witness» (Q. 3:53) «And they plotted» the disbelievers of the Children of Isrāʾīl [plotted] against ʿĪsā, «and Allah plotted» against them, in that He cast ʿĪsā’s likeness upon the man who meant to kill him, «and Allah is the best of plotters» (Q. 3:54) And recall «when Allah said: O ʿĪsā, I am taking you» seizing you, «and raising you to Myself» from this world, without death, «and purifying you» setting you far away, «from those who disbelieve, and placing those who followed you» — they are the Muslims, because they agreed with him, not the Christians, who made him a god — «above those who disbelieved» in you, «until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return» that is, then your return is to Me, «and I shall judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ» (Q. 3:55) «As for those who disbelieved, I shall punish them with a severe punishment in this world» by killing and captivity, «and in the hereafter» by the Fire, «and they will have no helpers» (Q. 3:56). «But as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, We shall pay them their wages in full; and Allah does not love the wrongdoers» (Q. 3:57). «That» — what has been mentioned — «We recite to you, from the signs and the wise remembrance» (Q. 3:58) the firmly established; the Qurʾan. «The likeness of ʿĪsā» his case, «with Allah is as the likeness of Ādam»: Ādam’s case is the more extraordinary. «He created him from dust, then said to him: Be» a human being, «and he is» (Q. 3:59) and so he became a human being. «The truth from your Lord» concerning the matter of ʿĪsā, «so do not be of the doubters» (Q. 3:60) «And whoever disputes with you» argues with you — from among the Christians — «concerning him, after the knowledge that has come to you» concerning his case, «then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves» that we gather them, «then let us pray earnestly» let us implore in supplication, «and place Allah’s curse upon the liars» (Q. 3:61) by saying:

“O Allah, curse whoever lies concerning ʿĪsā.” They accepted that. The Messenger ﷺ called Fāṭima, took al-Ḥusayn in his arms and led al-Ḥasan by the hand, with ʿAlī walking behind them, and said: “Come out with your sons and your women.” Their priest said to them: “You know that he is truly the prophet who is mentioned in the Torah. If you engage him in mubāhala, no Christian will remain on the face of the earth without perishing.” So they went back and said: “We have left off the mubāhala.” The Prophet ﷺ said to them: “Accept Islam.” They said: “No.” He said: “Then I will fight you.” They said: “We will make terms with you for a payment.” So they made terms with him for two thousand robes each year and thirty coats of mail, giving him half in Ṣafar and half in Rajab. [38] «This is the true account, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:62) «And if they turn away» turn aside, «then Allah knows the corrupters well» (Q. 3:63) and He will requite them. «Say: O People of the Book» the Jews and the Christians, «come to a word that is even»

its import being even «between us and you» it is «that we worship none but Allah, and that we associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides Allah» «Then if they turn away» they turn aside from [Allah’s] oneness «say» you [say]: «Bear witness that we are Muslims» (Q. 3:64) affirmers of [Allah’s] oneness «People of the Book, why do you dispute about Ibrāhīm?» It was revealed when the Jews said that Ibrāhīm was a Jew and the Christians said that Ibrāhīm was a Christian. «People of the Book, why do you dispute» you contend about Ibrāhīm, claiming that he held your religion «when the Torah and the Gospel were not sent down until after him» by a long time. Judaism arose out of the Torah, and the Torah came down after Ibrāhīm; and the Gospel came down upon ʿĪsā after Ibrāhīm, and Christianity arose out of the Gospel. «Will you not then use reason?» [reason about] this. From here history came out of Allah’s Book: He argued against them by history. «Here you are — you have disputed about what you have knowledge of» concerning the matter of Mūsā and ʿĪsā «so why do you dispute about what you have no knowledge of? And Allah knows» his case «while you do not know» (Q. 3:66) He said, clearing Ibrāhīm: «Ibrāhīm was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was an upright Muslim, and he was not one of the idolaters» (Q. 3:67) «The closest of people» the most entitled of them «to Ibrāhīm are those who followed him» in his own time «and this prophet»

Muḥammad ﷺ. [39] «and those who believe» the Muslims, because they hold to his religion. «And Allah is the Protector of the believers. A party of the People of the Book wish that they might lead you astray; but they lead astray none but themselves» because the sin of their leading astray falls upon them. «and they do not perceive [it]. O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in Allah’s signs» [that is,] the Qurʾan. «while you bear witness? O People of the Book, why do you confound the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?» (Q. 3:68–71) This was treated earlier, in Sūrat al-Baqara.
«And a party of the People of the Book said» the Jews «Believe in what has been sent down upon those who believe» […]
«at the outset of the day» [that is,] its first part. «and disbelieve» in it «at its end, so that they may» [that is,] the believers, «turn back» (Q. 3:72) from their religion.

«And do not believe» [that is,] do not credit that anyone should be given the like of what you were given — these are their own words — «except in one who follows your religion. Say: Guidance is Allah’s guidance» and what lies outside it is error. «that anyone should be given the like of what you were given, or that they should dispute with you before» (Q. 3:73)

«your Lord» do not accept [it] until they argue against you before Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «Say: Bounty is in Allah’s hand; He gives it to whom He wills» So from where do you have it that no one is given the like of what you were given? «And Allah is Vast» abundant in bounty, «[Knowing]» (Q. 3:73)

of who deserves it. «He singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty. And among the People of the Book is one whom, [if] you entrust him with a qinṭār» a great sum of wealth, «he will render it back to you» because of his trustworthiness — like ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām, with whom a man deposited one thousand two hundred ounces of gold, and he rendered them back to him. «And among them is one whom, if you entrust him with a dīnār, he will not render it back to you» because of his treachery, «unless you keep standing over him» and that is Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf, with whom a man deposited a dīnār; he denied it and did not return it to him. [40] «That is because they said: There is upon us, concerning the unlettered ones» the Arabs, «no way» [that is,] no sin. «And they speak falsehood against Allah» (Q. 3:74–75)

by attributing that to Him «while they know» that they are lying (Q. 3:75) «Rather, whoever fulfils his covenant» the covenant he made with Allah «and is godfearing» fears Allah «then Allah loves the godfearing» (Q. 3:76) «Those who sell» who exchange «Allah’s covenant» His trust «and their oaths» their swearing falsely «for a small price» of the affairs of this world «those — there is no portion»

[that is,] no portion «for them in the hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them» out of anger at them, «nor will He look at them» that is, [nor will He] have mercy on them, «on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and theirs is a painful punishment. And among them» the People of the Book, «is a faction» a party, «who twist their tongues with the Book so that you may suppose it to be from the Book» which Allah sent down, «though it is not from the Book; and they say: It is from Allah, though it is not from Allah; and they speak falsehood against Allah while they know» (Q. 3:77–78) that they are lying. This was sent down when the Christians of Najrān said that ʿĪsā had commanded them to take him as a lord. «It is not» fitting «for a human being to whom Allah has given the Book, judgement» that is, understanding of the Law, «and prophethood, then to say to people: Be servants of mine rather than of Allah; but rather» he says: «Be rabbāniyyūn» scholars who act [on their knowledge], «by what you used to know» (Q. 3:79)

that is, you recognise «the Book, and by what you used to study» [that is,] you study it among yourselves. «Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords» (Q. 3:79–80) as the Ṣābiʾa took the angels, the Jews ʿUzayr, and the Christians ʿĪsā.

«Would he command you to disbelief after you have become Muslims?» (Q. 3:80) that is not fitting And recall «when Allah took the covenant of the prophets» their pledge «Whatever We have given you of a Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you» of the Book and wisdom — and he is Muḥammad ﷺ. «you shall certainly believe in him and shall certainly help him»
if you live to see him. «He said» [Allah] the Exalted, «Do you affirm?» that, «And have you taken» [that is,] accepted, «upon that My bond» (Q. 3:81)
[that is,] My covenant, «They said: We affirm. He said: Then bear witness» against yourselves and your followers, «and I am with you among the witnesses» (Q. 3:81)

and I am among the witnesses along with you «So whoever turns away after that» [after] the covenant «those are the transgressors» (Q. 3:82) «Do you seek other than Allah’s religion, when to Him has submitted» do you seek other than the religion of Allah? And there has submitted to Him «whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly» by the sword «and to Him you will be returned» (Q. 3:83) and you return to Him «Say» O Muḥammad «We believe in Allah and in what has been sent down»

«upon us, and what was sent down upon Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb and the tribes, and what was given to Mūsā and ʿĪsā and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them» in crediting and discrediting «and to Him we are submitters» (Q. 3:84) sincere «And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers» (Q. 3:85) «How shall Allah guide» Allah does not guide «a people who disbelieved after their belief and bore witness» and their bearing witness «that the Messenger is true, and clear proofs came to them» the manifest arguments «And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people» (Q. 3:86) «Those — their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of all people» (Q. 3:87) «abiding therein» that is, in the curse, or in the Fire, to which it points «the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be granted respite» (Q. 3:88) «except those who repent after that and make amends» [amend] their deeds «then indeed»
«Allah is Forgiving» to them, «Merciful» (Q. 3:89) toward them. This was sent down concerning the Jews. «Those who have disbelieved» in ʿĪsā «after» (Q. 3:90)

in Mūsā «then increased in disbelief» in Muḥammad «their repentance will not be accepted» when they gurgle in the death rattle and die as disbelievers «and those are the ones gone astray» (Q. 3:90) «Those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — there will not be accepted from any one of them the earth’s fill of gold» the measure of what would fill it «even if he were to ransom himself with it. Those — for them is a painful punishment» agonizing «and they have no helpers» (Q. 3:91) none to ward off [the punishment]
O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.

«You will not attain to piety» — its reward, which is the Garden — «until you spend» — give alms — «of what you love» (Q. 3:92). You will not find the Garden except by spending some of what you love of your property. It is not the spending alone, but the spending of what you love. Our Master addresses us with His words «You will not attain to piety until you spend of what you love» (Q. 3:92). On account of the revelation of this verse (āya), Abū Ṭalḥa gave his garden Bayraḥāʾ in alms — a plot of land with date palms in it and a well of the sweetest water among the waters of Medina. The Messenger ﷺ used to enter Bayraḥāʾ and find its water sweet. He said to the Messenger ﷺ:

Our Lord says «You will not attain to piety until you spend of what you love» (Q. 3:92). The dearest of my property to me is Bayraḥāʾ, and it is in the path of Allah; place it where Allah shows you. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Well done, well done! That is property that profits — māl rābiḥ — or property that departs — māl rāyiḥ. And I think that you should place it among the nearest of kin.⟩ So he divided it among his relatives.[1] Then Zayd b. Ḥāritha came and said

The dearest of my property to me is a steed I have, and here it is — I have given it in the path of Allah. So he handed it over to Usāma, his son.[2] When the verse came down, the Companions vied with one another and handed over vast wealth. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar loved almonds with sugar, and he used to buy them constantly and distribute them among the people, saying: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar loves almonds with sugar, and our Master says «You will not attain to piety until you spend of what you love» (Q. 3:92). ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was enamoured of a slave girl belonging to a wife [of his], and he asked her for the girl repeatedly, but she refused. When he assumed the caliphate the woman made the girl ready and decked her with every kind of ornament and robe, and brought her in to him and said: She is a gift from me to you, to serve you. He asked her: From where did you come to own her? She said that she had brought her from her father’s house. So he looked into how her father had come to own her, and he was told: An agent died owing debts, and property was taken, and she is from that property. He summoned the agent’s heirs and satisfied them, and he turned to her and said: You are free, in the path of Allah; you are free, for the countenance of Allah. It was said to him: After you have wearied yourself over her and cleared her of every doubt? He said: Our Master says «You will not attain to piety until you spend of what you love» (Q. 3:92).[3] Fuḍayl was ill, and he craved the flesh of chicken

and he struggled against his nafs (the soul) for forty nights, restraining it from the craving for the flesh of chicken. After forty nights the nafs overcame him in the craving for chicken, and he told the mistress of the house: I have been contending with my nafs and withholding it from the craving for the flesh of chicken, and it has overcome me, so today I must have the flesh of chicken. She said: Glory be to Allah! Why do you withhold it from a thing Allah has made lawful and which is within your reach? She went to the market and bought a chicken for a dirham and two dāniqs, and cooked the chicken in all manner of dishes, and brought it before him. A beggar then stopped and said: Give alms to the poor man. He said: Hand it to him. She said: This is something you love and I made it for you; I will do something for the poor man that is better for him, and you eat what you crave.

He said: What will you do for the poor man? She said: I will give him the price of the chicken; that is more useful to him, and you eat the chicken. He said: Excellent is what you have seen. Bring me the price. So she brought him the price, and he put the price and the chicken together and handed them both to the poor man, and said: Our Master says «You will not attain to piety until you spend of what you love» (Q. 3:92).[4] In truth, if Allah informs us that we do not attain piety except by spending some of what we love, then how shall we attain al-Barr? Only after spending all that we own.

Piety (al-birr) we attain by a part of what is ours, but al-Barr, who is Allah, we do not find except by spending all that we have. The servant must surrender his property, his children and his nafs to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and when he has done that he belongs to Allah, and whoever belongs to Allah, Allah belongs to him. He must follow the religion of Ibrāhīm. Ibrāhīm surrendered his property to his guests, his son to the sacrifice and his nafs to the flames[5], and so Allah took him as a khalīl (intimate friend of Allah), and said «and he was not one of the polytheists» (Q. 3:95). The servant must turn to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with the whole of himself, and so he attains the love of Allah and attains Allah’s walāya (sainthood). He must love Allah first, and he must love Allah’s awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah); for love of Allah’s awliyāʾ is not shirk (associating partners with Allah), as some of those of little understanding say — rather it is part of the love of Allah. The Messenger ﷺ told us that the servant is made to stand before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and He says to him

the Lord, Blessed and Exalted: ⟨What have you done for Me? As for your renunciation of this world, you chose ease for yourself; and as for your obedience to Me, you chose honour for yourself. Have you ever shown friendship for My sake to a friend of Mine, or enmity for My sake to an enemy of Mine?⟩[6] If he has shown friendship to a walī (friend) of Allah, or enmity to an enemy of Allah, that is the deed that endears him to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Whoever seeks to reach Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and lays claim to the stations without love for Allah’s awliyāʾ is a liar, even if he came with the worship of the two weighty ones [men and jinn]; he is only striking cold iron. One must take Allah’s awliyāʾ as friends and Allah’s enemies as enemies, and so travel thereby the path of Ibrāhīm, as will be mentioned in the verse «And whatever you spend of anything, Allah knows it» (Q. 3:92), and so He requites him for it. «All food was lawful to the Children of Isrāʾīl» (Q. 3:93) was revealed when the Jews came and said to the Messenger ﷺ: You claim to be upon the religion of Ibrāhīm, yet Ibrāhīm did not eat the flesh of camels or their milk, and you eat them. The Messenger ﷺ said to them: ⟨I adjure you by Allah: do you know that Yaʿqūb fell gravely ill and vowed that if Allah healed him of his illness he would give up the food dearest to him, which was the flesh of camels, and the drink dearest to him, which was the milk of camels?⟩ They said: Yes. He said: ⟨Then this prohibition of the flesh of camels and of milk came only from Yaʿqūb, and you say that it is from the religion of Ibrāhīm.⟩ The story in this is that Yaʿqūb, upon him be blessing and peace, vowed to Allah that if Allah granted him ten children and he entered Bayt al-Maqdis safely, he would sacrifice one of them in seeking nearness to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Allah granted him ten children, and when they had grown he went to Bayt al-Maqdis, until he came within a stone’s throw of Bayt al-Maqdis. An angel met him in the form of a man and said to him: O Yaʿqūb, you are strong, and I would like to wrestle you. So the two wrestled, and neither of them threw the other. The angel pressed him with his foot on his thigh, and the ailment of sciatica (ʿirq al-nasā) struck him. So he entered Bayt al-Maqdis while he was ill with the ailment of

sciatica. He suffered pain from this illness and took to crying out in the night, so he vowed that if he were cured of this illness he would give up the flesh of camels and their milk. This is the reason for the vow. The Children of Isrāʾīl then became followers of Yaʿqūb in this[7], and they wanted to make it out to be [part of] the religion of Ibrāhīm, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave them the lie with His words: «All food was lawful» — permitted — «to the Children of Isrāʾīl, save what Isrāʾīl forbade» — that is, Yaʿqūb — «to himself», and that was the camel.

«before the Torah was sent down» — and this was before the Torah came down — «Say: bring the Torah and recite it» — so that the truth of what you say may be made clear — «if you are truthful» (Q. 3:93). And they were dumbfounded. «So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that» — after the proof has appeared that the prohibition came only from Yaʿqūb’s side and not in the time of Ibrāhīm — «those are the wrongdoers» (Q. 3:94). «Say: Allah has spoken the truth» — in this, as in all of which He has informed — «follow the religion of Ibrāhīm» — which is the one I follow — «inclining to the truth» «Say: Allah has spoken the truth» — in this, as in all of which He has informed — «so follow the religion of Ibrāhīm» — which is the one I follow — «inclining to the truth» — turning away from every religion to Islam — «and he was not of the polytheists» (Q. 3:95). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, told us that this prohibition came from Yaʿqūb, upon him be blessing and peace. This is a person’s worship: he withholds himself from the desire for what is lawful, seeking nearness to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, as Isrāʾīl did. So likewise, all food is lawful for the servant of Allah when he travels the path to the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, save what the wayfarer has forbidden himself, in struggle against his nafs, «before the Torah was sent down» — before the greatest opening comes — «So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that» — by claiming to have arrived at Allah, Blessed and Exalted, without travelling the path — «those are the wrongdoers» — those who put things somewhere other than their place. «Say: Allah has spoken the truth; so follow the religion of Ibrāhīm, inclining to the truth» (Q. 3:95). Man is the greater world. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created things and made them into divisions. One division is luminous, and their living is the remembrance of Allah and the worship of Allah, which agrees with their kind: they are luminous, and their nourishment is of their own kind, luminous as well. Another division Allah created corporeal, like the animals: their living agrees with their kind, which is corporeal, and they have no worship. And man — Allah created him and joined in him both the corporeal and the luminous. His living is corporeal, agreeing with his body: food and drink. And the living of his spirit is the remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, because it is spiritual. So when a man struggles against his nafs until he has purified it of all the desires, he joins the spiritual ones and becomes of the kind of the angel, and he is better than the angel. So among human beings there is found one who is better than the angels. And when he busies himself with the desires of his nafs until he has killed his spirituality by following his animality, he becomes as though he were of the kind of the animals: «They are only like cattle; nay, they are further astray» (Q. 25:44), as He said in the verse: «Among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who keeps to a middle course, and among them is one who outstrips in good deeds» (Q. 35:32). So the one who wrongs himself is he who follows the desires until

he has killed the spirituality by the animality. That is the one of whom He said: «They are only like cattle; nay, they are further astray» (Q. 25:44), and of whom He said: «Those are the worst of creatures» (Q. 98:6). «And among them is one who keeps to a middle course» — in that he busies himself now with the animal desires and now with the worship of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: «they have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil; it may be that Allah will relent toward them» (Q. 9:102).

And a division that outstrips in good deeds: they purified the spirit of the desires of the nafs until they put the nafs to death altogether, and so they passed away in Allah and abided: «Those are the best of creatures» (Q. 98:7). And the wayfarer, by his struggle against the nafs and his withholding it from its desires, follows the religion of Ibrāhīm. Allah has spoken the truth in what He told: that whoever spends all that he has attains to union with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Whoever is Allah’s, Allah is his. So follow, then, the religion of Ibrāhīm, who surrendered his wealth to the guests, his son to the sacrifice, and himself to the flames: «inclining to the truth, and he was not of the polytheists» (Q. 3:95). Ibrāhīm set himself apart for Allah alone, and he made everything other than Allah an enemy to himself: «they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds» (Q. 26:77). By this road a person finds union with Allah, Blessed and Exalted

«And those who struggle for Our sake — We shall surely guide them to Our ways; and Allah is indeed with those who do good» (Q. 29:69). As for one who claims to have arrived at Allah, Blessed and Exalted, without this road, he is a liar, as this verse shows.
«And he was not of»
«the polytheists» (Q. 3:95). Whenever He mentions Ibrāhīm, He clears him of shirk.

And it was sent down when the Jews said: our qibla is prior to your qibla — meaning Bayt al-Maqdis. Allah said: «Indeed the first house set up» — as a place of worship — «for mankind» — on the earth — «is the one at Bakka» (Q. 3:96). It is the House that is at Bakka — Bakka being a dialectal variant of Mecca — or Bakka is specifically the spot upon which the Kaʿba stands[8]; or Mecca is the town, and Bakka is what lies beneath the House. And this
is preferable, because the House was before the town. So then, what the House stands upon is Bakka, and Mecca is the town and what lies around it

«He it is who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca» (Q. 48:24). It was named Bakka because it breaks the necks of tyrants[9]. It is the first house set up as a place of worship for mankind. The angels built it two thousand years before the creation of Ādam[10], and al-Aqṣā was set up [after it]. Al-Jalāl said[11]: ⟨and between the two was forty years⟩, and this is a slip of the pen on his part. Rather, the angels built the Kaʿba two thousand years before the creation of Ādam; and when Allah created Ādam, he took to performing the hajj to this House. After that Allah commanded him to build it a second time, and Ādam built it, and he continued for forty years performing the hajj to this House. After forty years Allah commanded him to build Bayt al-Maqdis, so between the two was forty years — that is, between Ādam’s building of the Kaʿba and his building of Bayt al-Maqdis[12]. As for what the commentator said, that the angels built it and that between the angels’ building and the building of Jerusalem was forty years, this is a slip of understanding on his part; rather, between the two was two thousand and forty years[13]. And in the hadith: ⟨The first thing that appeared upon the face of the water, at the creation of⟩

⟨the heavens and the earth, was a white foam; the earth was spread out from beneath it, and it is this Kaʿba⟩[14]. The House of Allah: facing it is al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, which is in heaven. «blessed» — a house possessed of blessing; its blessing is the safety of the wild beasts around it, and that whoever takes refuge in it is exposed to no harm: if a man meets his father’s killer there, he does not lay a hand on him — «and a guidance for the worlds» (Q. 3:96) — because it is their qibla. «In it are clear signs» — among them «the station of Ibrāhīm», the stone on which he stood when he built the House, so that his two feet left their mark in it, and it has remained until now, for all the length of time and the passing of hands over it; and among them is the multiplying of good deeds in it, and that the birds do not fly above it[15]. «And whoever enters it is secure» (Q. 3:97): whoever enters the station of Ibrāhīm is secure; he is not exposed to killing or wrong or anything else. This is from the blessing of this House. And among its blessings is the abundance of reward for whoever performs the hajj to it: ⟨Whoever performs the hajj and neither speaks obscenely nor commits transgression returns from his sins as on the day his mother bore him⟩[16]. ⟨Whoever performs the hajj once has discharged his obligation; whoever performs it a second time has lent to his Lord; and whoever performs it a third time has made his hair and his body forbidden to the Fire⟩[17]. And this House — all the prophets performed the hajj to it except four of them. From Ādam to Muḥammad ﷺ there is not one prophet among them but he performed the hajj, except four of them: Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ and Idrīs. All the rest of the prophets and the messengers performed the hajj to this House. Were it only an ordinary house, and the prophets and the righteous had come to it again and again from the beginning of time to this day of ours, that alone would be blessing enough for it — all the more so since it is the House

of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The angels built it, and they brought the Black Stone — whiter than milk, from the ruby of the Garden[18] — and set it in the Corner. And al-Ḥaqq, Majestic and Exalted, said: ⟨It is the right hand of Allah upon His earth; whoever touches it, it is as though he has clasped the hand of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted⟩[19]. And when Ādam had built it, and Shīth his son had built it, Ibrāhīm built it a fourth time. At Ibrāhīm’s building this Station was brought — it is a stone of about three cubits, upon which Ibrāhīm would stand to build the Kaʿba. The engineer was Jibrīl, upon him be blessing and peace; the builder was Ibrāhīm, khalīl Allāh; the apprentice who assisted him was Ismāʿīl; and Mīkāʾīl was the one who helped Ismāʿīl. Whenever Ibrāhīm was at work on the building, until the building rose higher than the stone upon which he stood, the stone — the Station — would stretch upward until Ibrāhīm reached the Kaʿba. He built it in this shape which you find: thirty cubits, while that upon which he stood is only three cubits. And the mark of Ibrāhīm’s feet is upon the Station to this day; the traces of Ibrāhīm’s foot are there, as though he had trodden upon it just now. People used to seek blessing from it, and the Saudis covered it for fear that people should see it — out of ignorance on their part. And this Station too is from the ruby of the Garden. You will not find a community in the world that has with it a thing verified to be from the Garden except the community of Muḥammad ﷺ: the Station of Ibrāhīm and the Black Stone

are from the ruby of the Garden[20]. There is nothing in this world from the Garden except these two. When Ibrāhīm had built it with this building and had completed its construction, Allah commanded him to call the people to the pilgrimage to this House. He said: How shall I call them, when they are non-existent, in the loins of their fathers? Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: Upon you is the calling, and the making heard is upon Me. So he stood upon the mountain of Abū Qubays and said: O people, your Lord has built a House and has called you to its pilgrimage, so make the pilgrimage. The pilgrims answered, every one of them, from all the regions of the world, while they were in non-existence. Whoever answered on that day must needs make the pilgrimage, and whoever did not answer does not make it, even if the means are abundantly at his disposal. Whoever answered once made the pilgrimage once, and whoever answered twice made it twice, and so for many times[21]. So you find the pilgrim, when he has made the pilgrimage, yearning to return to those places, by the call of Ibrāhīm:
«So make the hearts of some among the people incline toward them» (Q. 14:37). One of the righteous went repeatedly

to the pilgrimage until he had made the pilgrimage sixty times. Then one day he sat thinking about his pilgrimages, whether they had been accepted from him or not, and he heard a voice saying: So-and-so, do you invite to your house any but one whom you love? And his hope grew strong that Allah had answered him[22].

We, the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, do not do a thing that has no meaning and of which we understand nothing. The hajj is in the position of a king who has summoned a man to be his guest. It is the custom of great men, when they are invited to meet kings, that they cleanse themselves and put on new clothing, in honour of the king. So you find the one who enters ritual consecration (iḥrām) taking off the garments of his habit, his ordinary clothing

, stripping himself bare, washing, and putting on only an upper wrap, a waist-wrapper and a pair of sandals. When a king invites a guest and the guest comes to him, he comes to his private house and clasps his hand. So you come to the Sacred House of Allah, and the Black Stone is the right hand of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And the going out to Ṣafā and Marwa, and to Minā, and to Muzdalifa, and to ʿArafāt: it is the custom of kings, when they summon a great man and host him, that they go out with him for recreation to their quarters, and to their orchards, and to their domains. This is the going out to Minā, to ʿArafāt. And the return, at the completion of the hajj, is the day of the banquet; it is the Day of Sacrifice. Allah says «there is brought to it the fruits of all things» (Q. 28:57) — even human beings. For this reason He said «And to Allah is owed, from the people, the pilgrimage to the House» — Allah has made obligatory upon the people the pilgrimage to this House — «for whoever is able to find a way to it» (Q. 3:97) — a way — which the Messenger ﷺ explained as provisions and a mount[23].[24]

«And whoever disbelieves» — in Allah, or in what He has made obligatory, namely the hajj — «then Allah is without need of the worlds» (Q. 3:97) — mankind, the jinn and the angels — and without need of their acts of worship. This unbelief (kufr) came as a threat (tahdīd) to one who was able to perform the hajj and left it: ⟨Whoever is held back from this House neither by illness, nor by poverty, nor by an unjust ruler, and then dies without having made the pilgrimage — let him die a Jew or a Christian⟩

— a hadith[25]. «Say: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah» — the Qurʾan — «and Allah is witness over what you do» (Q. 3:98) — and so He will requite you for it. «Say: O People of the Book» — the Jews and the Christians — «why do you turn away» — you divert — «from the way of Allah» — His religion — «him who has believed» — by your giving the lie to the Prophet ﷺ and concealing his description — «you seek it» — you seek the way — «crooked» — bent, that is, inclining away from the truth — «while you are witnesses» — knowing that the religion that is approved is Islam — «and Allah is not heedless of what you do» (Q. 3:99) — of unbelief and of giving the lie; He only defers you to your appointed time so that He may requite you. «O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who have been given the Book, they will turn you back, after your faith, into unbelievers» (Q. 3:100). The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the Aws and the Khazraj were two tribes at enmity with one another for the span of a hundred and twenty years[26]; they were continually at war. When Islam came and they met the Messenger ﷺ, the first to meet him were six of them, and they gave him their pledge. In the following year they confirmed the pledge of the six by sending twelve of them, and they gave him their pledge. And in the third year they sent seventy-three men and ten women

and they confirmed the pledge at al-ʿAqaba[27]. After this the Messenger ﷺ emigrated to Medina, and they all entered Islam; there was no one in Medina, of the Aws and the Khazraj, who did not enter Islam, and so the Messenger ﷺ named them Anṣār. Every city was conquered by the sword except the city of the Messenger, which was conquered by the Qurʾan alone; its people came to be called al-Anṣār, and you would not know an Awsī from a Khazrajī. There was a Jew living near them who had known their Jāhiliyya, their enmity and their warfare, and he hated the Muslims and envied them and attacked them a great deal. When he passed by a company of the Anṣār sitting together, brothers who loved one another, that angered him. So he went to a youth of his and said to him: I passed by a company of the Khazraj and a company of the Aws who are brothers loving one another. I would have you stand before them and say: Remember the Day of Buʿāth — that is a day of war that took place between them — on that day so-and-so and so-and-so of the Aws were killed, and so-and-so and so-and-so of the Khazraj were killed. And he recited the poems they used to recite to one another when they fought, until two men of them quarrelled, an Awsī and a Khazrajī, and they said: If that day were to return, we would do to you as we did in the past. And they said: We return to it now. So they called one another to arms. The Khazraj cried: To the Khazraj! and the Aws cried: To the Aws! They took up arms and meant to fight one another. The Messenger ﷺ went out to them with the Muhājirūn and said to them: ⟨With the cry of the Jāhiliyya, and I am here among you? Allah! Allah!⟩ So they threw down their swords and every one of them embraced his brother — and this was from al-shayṭān (Satan) — and they returned better than they had been before. And this verse was sent down concerning them[28]; it takes in brothers in Allah until the end of time. «O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who have been given the Book» — the Jews — «they will turn you back, after your faith, into unbelievers. And how can you disbelieve» (Q. 3:100–101) — a rebuke
«while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds fast» — clings — «to Allah, he has been guided»

«to a straight path» (Q. 3:101). «O you who believe, fear Allah as He ought to be feared» — that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He be thanked and not denied, that He be remembered and not forgotten[29]. They said: O Messenger of Allah, who has the strength for this? So it was abrogated by His words, Exalted:

«So fear Allah as much as you are able» (Q. 64:16). It has been said that there is no abrogation here[30]; rather, whoever fears Allah as much as he is able has feared Allah as He ought to be feared. «And do not die except as Muslims» (Q. 3:102) — affirmers of the divine oneness. «And hold fast» — cling — «to the rope of Allah» — His religion —
«all together» — the rope of Allah is the community — «and do not become divided» — do not split apart after Islam — «and remember the favour of Allah»
His bestowal of favour — «upon you» — O company of the Aws and the Khazraj — «when you were» — before Islam — «enemies, and He brought together»
joined — «your hearts» — through Islam — «so that you became» — you came to be — «by His favour brothers» — in religion and in walāya

«And you were on the brink of a pit» — on the edge of a pit — «of the Fire» — nothing stood between you and falling into it but that you should die as unbelievers — «and He saved you from it» — by faith (īmān) — «thus» — as He makes clear to you what has been mentioned — «does Allah make His verses clear to you, that you may be guided» (Q. 3:103). al-Ḥaqq has directed us in this verse to this, that the way of our success is the godfearing (al-taqwā) of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Godfearing is of degrees. The godfearing of the generality is faith — the opposite of unbelief — faith in Allah

and compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition. The godfearing of the elect is that he remember Allah and not forget Him, that he thank Him and not deny Him, that he obey Him and not disobey Him. The godfearing of the elect of the elect is that nothing other than Allah ever cross the servant’s mind. To this the poet Ibn al-Fāriḍ points in his words:
⟨And were a desire for any other than You to pass over my mind, through inadvertence, I would judge myself to have apostatised.⟩[31]

That is the utmost of godfearing, that a man not turn his regard to anything other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and that cannot come about without the remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with the tongue. The remembrance of Allah with the tongue is the lowest remembrance, but remembrance with the tongue is indispensable, so that he may come to remember with the heart; and remembrance with the heart is reflection. When the servant reflects, either he reflects upon his nafs, and sees the baseness of his nafs and the ugliness of its work, and then he must flee from it to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; or he reflects upon Allah and upon what is with Him, and then he must desire Him, and so he flees from the nafs and goes to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. In either case the flight is to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And when he has fled to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and held fast to the religion of Muḥammad ﷺ, and taken on the ādāb (the proprieties) of the awliyāʾ of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and kept their company, he must arrive at what is sought. «And hold fast to the rope of Allah, all together» (Q. 3:103) — that is, the rope of Allah is the community. ⟨The hand of Allah is with the community⟩

So whoever parts from the community is quit of the religion.[32] ⟨The hand of Allah is with the community.⟩[33] The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Hold to the community, for al-shayṭān flees from the community; he is nearer to two than he is to three, and nearer to one than to two.⟩[34] This division is only division in doctrines, and enmity and hatred. As for division in the branches [of the law], without mutual hostility, it does not fall under this; and to it the hadith ⟨The disagreement of my community is a mercy⟩[35] points. The Companions disagreed among themselves most severely in the branches, yet there was no enmity between them, and this is praiseworthy. As for division in doctrines, that is what brings about enmity. The Messenger ﷺ drew a straight line and drew lines around it, and said: ⟨This is my path, straight, to which I call, and these are the ways that Allah has forbidden you.⟩ «And do not follow the ways, lest they part you from»

«His path» (Q. 6:153).[36] And he ﷺ said: ⟨The Jews split into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire; the Christians split into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire; and my community will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire save one. They said: And which is that one? He said: That which I am upon, and my Companions.⟩
That is, the sunna and the community.[37]

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reminded the believers; He reminded them — that is, He admonished them — of several things: «Hold fast to the rope of Allah» (Q. 3:103) — a command to hold fast to the Book, the sunna and the community, and not to divide; and that we should remember the favours of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, His bestowal of favour upon us. All these things require flight to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

«And let there be among you a community calling to the good» — and let there be among you a group calling people to the good — «and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And those» — the callers, the enjoiners, the forbidders — «they are the ones who prosper» (Q. 3:104) — they are the triumphant. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Allah has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and the martyrs envy for their nearness to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. They said: And who are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: They are those who make people beloved to Allah and who make Allah beloved to people. They said: That they make Allah beloved to people we have understood; but how do they make people beloved to Allah? He said: They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and when the people comply with the command of Allah and avoid His prohibitions, Allah loves them.⟩[38] This is a collective obligation. The Muslim community is obliged to have among it a party who call people to Allah, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He introduced min (from) to signify a part, because enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is not obligatory upon all people. Conditions are required for it. Knowledge is required first: one who does not know, when he enjoins or forbids, may well forbid what is right and enjoin what is wrong. This is the cause of innovation. And he must have standing, so that his word is accepted. But if, when he forbids a wrong, he commits something worse than it, then neither enjoining what is right nor forbidding what is wrong is obligatory upon him; and when the conditions are met in him, he is obliged to enjoin what is right and to forbid what is wrong. «And those, they are the ones who prosper» (Q. 3:104). The Companions of the Messenger ﷺ used to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and this is as it were the greater jihad. The Messenger said: ⟨A time will come when nothing of Islam remains but its name, and nothing of the Qurʾan but its written form. The worst of those whom the sky shades on that day will be their scholars and their reciters: their scholars through greed, and their reciters through ostentation in worship (riyāʾ).⟩ He said: ⟨You are in a time in which⟩

⟨the hearts are flourishing, and a time will come in which the hearts will be in ruins and the mosques flourishing with bodies.⟩[39] The kings grow arrogant, the rich grow miserly, the scholars grow greedy, the devotees make a show of their worship, and the merchants deal in usury. And the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨The first to be called to account on the Day of Resurrection are three; they are brought forward: one who bore the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, one who spent, and one who fought in the way of Allah and was martyred. He says to the reciter: You bore My Book — what did you do for Me? He says: I used to recite it in the watches of the night and at the ends of the day. He says: You did not intend Me by that; you intended that it be said, So-and-so is a reciter — only that; and it has been said. That is your recompense; you have nothing with Me. And He says to the rich man: What did you do for Me? I provided you with much wealth. He says: I used to give right and left, giving alms for Your sake. He said:⟩
⟨No, you did not intend Me by that; rather you wanted it to be said, ‘So-and-so is generous’ — and it has been said. Then the fighter in jihad is brought, and He says to him:⟩

⟨What did you do for Me? He says: I took up my sword and struck right and left until I was killed as a martyr. He says: You did not intend My face by that; you intended that it be said, ‘So-and-so is a hero, so-and-so is brave’ — and it has been said. These are the first for whom the Fire will be stoked.⟩[40] There must be sincerity (ikhlāṣ) of action for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and there must be the company of the righteous
«And do not be like those who became divided» — away from their religion — «and differed» — concerning it — «after the clear proofs had come to them»

and they are the Jews and the Christians. «And those — for them is a great punishment» (Q. 3:105). Recall «the day when faces will turn white and faces will turn black» — that is, the Day of Resurrection. As for the believers, the whiteness of their faith in their hearts passes over to their faces, so that they are all of them white of face; and as for the unbelievers, the blackness of their creed passes over to their faces, so that they are black. «As for those whose faces have turned black» — and they are the unbelievers, so they are cast into the Fire, and it is said to them in rebuke — «Did you disbelieve after your faith?» — on the day the covenant was taken, when every one of you said, ‘Yes indeed’ — «so taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. And as for those whose faces have turned white» — and they are the believers; may Allah make us and you among them — «they are in the mercy of Allah» — in His Garden — «they abide therein forever. These» — these verses — «are the verses of Allah, We recite them to you» — O Muḥammad — «in truth, and Allah does not want injustice for the worlds» — by seizing them for no crime — «and to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — in possession, in creation, and as servants — «and to Allah all matters are returned» (Q. 3:106–109). All matters come to pass to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «You were»

O community of Muḥammad ﷺ — in the knowledge of Allah, Exalted — «the best community brought forth» — made manifest — «for mankind» — the community of Muḥammad is the best community brought forth for mankind. For what reason? «you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah» (Q. 3:110). By these qualities they attained this excellence, and so they loved Allah, and they made the people beloved to Allah, and they made Allah beloved to the people. And the community of Muḥammad ﷺ is everyone who follows him, from whatever stock he has arisen — even the Jews: if they enter Islam they enter into this excellence. ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām was among the righteous of the Companions,

and he was originally of the Jews. So this excellence is not a matter of Arab descent alone, as the Arabs suppose, but rather it lies with the three qualities: «you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah». The proof is that Abū Ṭālib, the brother of ʿAbd Allāh the father of the Messenger ﷺ, is not of this community and did not enter into this excellence; and Salmān — we read this yesterday — ⟨Salmān is one of us, the Family of the House⟩[41]. So this excellence is attained only by following him. May Allah grant us and you to follow him ﷺ. «And if the People of the Book believed, it would be» — faith would be — «better for them» — even the People of the Book, the Jews, who are the worst of the creation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: if they believed in Allah it would be better for them, because they would enter into this excellence which belongs to the community of Muḥammad ﷺ — «Among them are the believers» — such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions — «but most of them are the transgressors» (Q. 3:110) — the unbelievers. «They will not harm you» — that is, the Jews, O company of Muslims, in anything — «except for some hurt» — with the tongue, by reviling and by threatening — «and if they fight you they will turn their backs to you» — routed — «then they will not be helped» (Q. 3:111) — against you; rather the victory is yours over them. «Abasement has been stamped upon them wherever they are found» — wherever they are come upon, so that they have no might and no refuge — «except» — being — «by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people» — you will not find a Jew but that he is seeking the protection of one state or another; as for independence, they will never find independence; and along with that, you see no rich man among them but you take him for a poor man, from the extremity of abasement and destitution — «and they have incurred» — they returned — «wrath from Allah, and destitution has been stamped upon them. That is because they» — by reason of their having — «used to disbelieve in the verses of Allah and to kill the prophets without right. That» — is for emphasis — «is for their having disobeyed» — the command of Allah — «and they used to transgress» (Q. 3:112) — passing beyond the lawful into the forbidden. «They are not all alike» — the People of the Book are not mustawin (level) — «among the People of the Book is an upright community» — an upright group, standing firm upon the truth, such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām — «who recite the verses of Allah in the watches of the night» — in its hours — «and they prostrate» (Q. 3:113) — they pray. «They believe»

«in Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and hasten to good works, and those are among the righteous» (Q. 3:114). They enjoin what is right and they forbid what is wrong, and they hasten — they press forward — in good works. Hastening to good works, and pressing forward, and vying with one another: to all of these the Qurʾan has called us. He said «Hasten» (Q. 3:133), and He said «Vie with one another» (Q. 57:21), and the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Press forward with righteous deeds before you are kept occupied⟩[42]. And He, Exalted, said «So vie with one another in good works» (Q. 2:148), which the Messenger ﷺ explained by his words: ⟨Seize five before five: your youth before your decrepitude, your health before your sickness, your leisure before your occupation, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death⟩[43]. A man asked one of the righteous, saying to him: What do you say about fasting on a journey? He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has commanded us to press forward and to hasten, and fasting on a journey is part of this pressing forward and hastening. He said: By Allah, he gave me an answer that is not among the answers of the jurists. «they hasten to good works» — the matter requires pressing forward and it requires hastening. Time passes without cease, and your breath is in portions. Man — numbered are his

breaths and his days, and when these are spent, death must come. Every breath that has gone out has gone out of the sum of your breaths, and every moment that passes is a portion of your life; and every day, and every week, and every month, and every year is something that is always being diminished and never increased. There must be, then, an end; there must be striving. The sea is deep — a ship is needed; the road is long — provision is needed; the Watcher is all-seeing — sincerity is needed. «And whatever good you do, you will not be denied it» — you will not lose its reward; rather you will be requited for it — «and Allah is knowing of the godfearing» (Q. 3:115), and so He requites them. «Indeed those who disbelieve, there will not avail» — ward off — «them their wealth nor their children against Allah» — against His punishment — «anything» — these two were singled out for mention here because a man sometimes wards [harm] off from himself with his wealth and sometimes seeks help from his children. «And those are the companions of the Fire; they abide therein forever. The likeness of what they spend» — the unbelievers — «in this present life» — in enmity to the Prophet ﷺ, or in voluntary alms (ṣadaqa) and the like — «is like the likeness of a wind in which there is a violent blast» — intense heat or cold — «that struck the tillage of a people» — the sown field of a people — «who had wronged themselves» — by unbelief — «and destroyed it» — so they got no benefit from it; and so too their expenditures are gone, and they get no benefit from them. «And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves» (Q. 3:116–117). The condition of an accepted deed is that the doer be a believer in Allah, intending the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for the unbelievers, when they perform some act of devotion, such as acts of voluntary alms or maintaining the ties of kinship, its likeness is as He said in the verse, «like the likeness of a wind» — only that, because the condition is missing, and one who lacks the condition does not produce what is conditioned upon it. And shirk is of two kinds: al-shirk al-jalī (manifest association of partners with Allah) and al-khafī (hidden association of partners with Allah). Just as the deeds of the unbelievers are not accepted, so too with those who make a show of their worship: Allah does not turn toward their hearts. Allah has no need of what is shared with Him; the deed in which another has a share He does not accept, and the heart in which another has a share He does not enter.[44] «O you who believe, do not take as intimates» — bosom friends; they are your friends whom you let in on your secrets — «from other than yourselves» — from those who are not of you, from among the Jews

and the Christians and the hypocrites. Do not befriend the Jews, nor the Christians, nor the hypocrites, and do not acquaint them with your secrets, for they are enemies to you.[45] «They will not spare you any ruin» — they do not fall short in working corruption against you — «They have wished» — they have longed for — «what distresses you» — they love nothing but your distress, your hardship, always, and the severity of harm upon you. «There has appeared» — there has become manifest — «the hatred» — enmity toward you — «from their mouths» — whenever they speak you understand from their speech their enmity toward you — «and what their breasts conceal» — of enmity — «is greater. We have made clear to you the signs» — of their enmity — «if you would reason» (Q. 3:118) — about that — so do not take them as allies. «Here you are, loving them» — you love them, the hypocrites and the Jews, for their kinship with you and for the friendship they stir up in falsehood — «while they do not love you» — and they do not love you, because they differ from you in religion. «And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able» (Q. 2:217). «The Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their creed» (Q. 2:120). This enmity has no cure, ever. «And you believe in the Book, all of it» — in all the Books — and they do not believe in your Book. «And when they meet you they say, ‘We believe,’ and when they are alone they bite their fingertips at you» — the tips of the fingers — «out of rage» — out of the intensity of their anger at what they see of your concord with one another; this is the utmost of anger — «Say: Die in your rage» — remain in it until death, for you will never see what gladdens you among the people of faith — «Indeed Allah is knowing of what is within the breasts» (Q. 3:119) — of what is in the hearts, and among it is what these men harbour. «If good touches you» — a blessing, such as a victory or spoils — «it grieves them» — that saddens them; they never wish good for you — «and if an evil befalls you» — such as a defeat or a drought — «they rejoice at it» — so do not take them as allies; this is the plainest proof of their hostility toward you — «And if you are patient» — but if you are patient — «and godfearing» — and you fear Allah — «and it will not harm you» — will not

harm you — «their scheming, in anything» — through godfearing toward Allah and through steadfast patience (ṣabr), their enmity will never harm you. «Indeed Allah encompasses what they do» (Q. 3:120). Indeed Allah is «encompassing» — knowing — «of what they do» — of all their deeds. «And» — recall — «when you went out early from your family, assigning the believers their positions for the battle» (Q. 3:121). This verse was revealed concerning the battle of Uḥud.[46] The Prophet ﷺ met the unbelievers on the day of Badr and fought them, and Allah routed them. Seventy of their chiefs were killed and seventy of their chiefs taken captive[47], and he returned to Medina. Abū Jahl, who was their leader, was killed, and ʿUtba was killed, and Shayba and al-Walīd — those who came out for single combat on the day of Badr, saying: “Single combat!” Young men of al-Anṣār came out to them, and they said: “Equals, equals — but we want our paternal cousins.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Where is ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Where is Ḥamza b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Where is ʿUbayda — or Abū ʿUbayda — b. al-Ḥārith[48] b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Go out to these men; it is only you they are calling.⟩ So they fought one another. As for ʿAlī, he killed his opponent — he was the first to kill in the path of Allah. Ḥamza killed his opponent. Abū ʿUbayda’s leg was broken, and ʿAlī and Ḥamza came and finished off his enemy and carried him to the Prophet ﷺ. «These two adversaries disputed concerning their Lord» (Q. 22:19), and for this reason

ʿAlī says: ⟨I am the first who will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection to the dispute.⟩[49] When they returned, Abū Sufyān swore that he would not wash himself of major ritual impurity, nor eat the flesh of camels, nor drink wine, nor oil his locks, until he had taken revenge for these men from the Prophet ﷺ. They set about gathering armies, until he came with three thousand, two thousand of whom he had hired with his own wealth.[50] The people of falsehood are able to spend upon falsehood more than the people of truth are able to, or more than most of them. They came to Mount Uḥud before the Prophet ﷺ knew of it, and when the Prophet ﷺ learned of that he gathered his Companions and consulted them. He said to them: ⟨These enemies have come out from Mecca, and here they are at Mount Uḥud. What do you advise me?⟩ ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy, who was a hypocrite, said: ⟨We shall not go out to them; we shall stay in our dwellings. If they remain there, they will remain in the worst of states; and if they storm in upon us in our houses, we shall fight them inside the town, with the women and the boys helping us. But it is not our custom to go out to battle.⟩ A young man of al-Anṣār came forward and said: “O Messenger of Allah, we are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood. They have come out from Mecca to Uḥud, and we are to stay in our houses waiting for them like women? This does not befit us. Rather, let us go out to them.” This was not the opinion held by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ went into

his house, put on his coat of mail, took up his weapon and came out. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy grew angry. He had three hundred of the hypocrites as his companions, who obeyed no command but his. So the Messenger ﷺ went out with a thousand less fifty[51], while the polytheists were three thousand. The Prophet ﷺ encamped in the ravine on the Saturday, the seventh of Shawwāl, in the third year of the Hijra, and he put his back and his camp toward Uḥud and drew up their ranks evenly. He stationed a force of archers and set ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr over them at the foot of the mountain, and said: ⟨Drive them off from us with arrows, so that they do not come upon us from behind. And do not stir, whether we are defeated or given victory.⟩ So the matter was set in order, and Allah sent down His sakīna (the indwelling peace from Allah) upon His Messenger. The east wind came and cast terror into the hearts of the unbelievers, and they set about killing them. On this occasion even the women came. Hind bt. ʿUtba, the wife of Abū Sufyān, came and said that if the men fled their women would divorce them, and that if the banner of Quraysh fell that day the women would have to carry it. A man of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār carried the banner and was killed; another took it and was killed, until fifteen had been killed over the banner of Quraysh. Then the banner fell and no one took it; a woman took it up. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Alas for Quraysh, when their banner is in the hands of women!⟩[52] So they were given victory, and the upper hand fell to the Muslims in less time than hours. When the archers who were with ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr saw that the fighting was finished and that victory had fallen to the Muslims, they hurried to the spoils. ʿAbd Allāh b. Jubayr said to them: ⟨Did you not hear what the Messenger ﷺ said: ‘We do not stir, whether they conquer or are conquered’?⟩ They said to him: “The matter is finished; nothing remains but the spoils alone.” They disobeyed the command of the Messenger, and Allah cast courage into the hearts of the unbelievers, so they returned and fought

the Muslims, and killed seventy-two of them[53] on the spot, and a great number of them were wounded. The Messenger ﷺ was wounded in his forehead, and they broke his front tooth ﷺ, and Ḥamza, the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger, was martyred[54]. And remember, O Muḥammad, «when you set out early from your household» — from Medina; or from your household, from the house of your family: he went out from the house of ʿĀʾisha on that day — «assigning» — settling — «the believers positions» — stations in which they were to stand — «for the battle. And Allah is hearing» — of your words — «knowing» (Q. 3:121) — of your states. And that was the day of Uḥud. «When two parties among you were minded» — and they are the Banū Salama and the Banū Ḥāritha, the two wings of the army — «to fail» — that the two of them should turn coward and withdraw from the fighting — when ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy the hypocrite went back, he and his companions, and said: For what are we to kill ourselves and our children? And he said to Abū Jābir al-Salamī — who had said to them, I adjure you by Allah, for your Prophet and for yourselves — If we knew there would be fighting we would follow you. But Allah made the two of them stand firm and they did not turn away. They came near to fleeing as the hypocrites fled, but Allah preserved them, so that there remained only seven hundred men with the Messenger ﷺ. «And Allah was the protector of them both» — their helper against failing — «and in Allah let the believers put their trust» (Q. 3:122) — let them rely on Him and on none besides Him. It was sent down when they had been routed, as a reminder to them of Allah’s favour, when

some of the Muslims said: How does this befall us, when we are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and upon his religion? «And Allah did indeed help you at Badr» — a place between Mecca and Medina — «while you were lowly» — through the fewness of your numbers and of your weapons — «so fear Allah, that you may be thankful» (Q. 3:123) — for His favours. «When» — an adverbial qualifier governed by ‘He helped you’ — «you said to the believers» — promising them, by way of reassurance — «Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you» — aid you — «with three thousand of the angels sent down» (Q. 3:124). «Yes indeed» — that will suffice you. And in al-Anfāl it is ‘with a thousand’, because He reinforced them with that first, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand, as He said, Exalted: «If you are steadfast» — in meeting the enemy — «and godfearing» — of Allah, in the matter of disobeying Him — «and they come upon you» — the polytheists — «in their onrush» — their moment — «this — your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels, marked out» (Q. 3:125) — marked with signs. And they were steadfast, and Allah fulfilled His promise to them, in that the angels fought alongside them on piebald horses, wearing yellow and white turbans which they had let hang down between their shoulders[55]. When they were steadfast on the day of Badr, five thousand of the angels came down: Jibrīl, with two thousand with him; Mīkāʾīl, with a thousand with him; Isrāfīl, with a thousand with him; the Angel of Death, with a thousand with him[56]. «And Allah made it not» — the reinforcement — «except as good tidings for you» (Q. 3:126) — and this is good tidings for the Muslims

when they know that the angels are fighting alongside them, this brings them good tidings. «and so that may be set at rest» — be still — «your hearts by it» — so do not be alarmed at the multitude of the enemy and at your own fewness — «and victory comes only from Allah» — and in reality victory does not come except from Allah, Blessed and Exalted — «the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:126) — not by the angels, but from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Victory does not come except from Allah. You will not find the word ‘victory’ in the Qurʾan but that the victory is from Allah, so that the servant may know that there is no helper but Allah: «If Allah helps you, there is none that can overcome you» (Q. 3:160), «help from Allah and a near victory» (Q. 61:13), «When the help of Allah comes» (Q. 110:1). You will not find true victory except that it is with Allah: «And Allah will surely help him who helps Him» (Q. 22:40), «If you help Allah, He will help you» (Q. 47:7). There is no helper but Allah. «And victory comes only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:126). He did that «so that He might cut off» — destroy — «a party of those who disbelieved» — by killing and by captivity — «or abase them» — humble them by defeat — «so that they turn back» — return — «disappointed» (Q. 3:127) — not having attained what they sought. And when the Messenger’s ﷺ front tooth was broken and his face was gashed on the day of Uḥud, he said: ⟨How shall a people prosper who have dyed the face of their Prophet with blood?⟩ There was sent down «You have no part in the matter»[57] — rather, the matter belongs to Allah, so be patient — «or He may relent towards them» — or Allah may relent towards them, by Islam — «or He may punish them» — and so He leaves them to die in unbelief and punishes them — «for they are wrongdoers» (Q. 3:128) — by unbelief. If Allah wills to guide them, He guides them to Islam; and if He wills to punish them, they die in unbelief, and they deserve that, because they are wrongdoers. As for the Messenger ﷺ, he has no part in the matter. And this is the utmost in

the greatness of the Messenger ﷺ: his affair is wholly the affair of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, so much so that he has no part in his own affair. «And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — in possession, in creation and in servanthood — «He forgives whom He will» — him for whom He wills forgiveness — «and He punishes whom He will». Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His forgiveness has no cause. There is no cause for the forgiveness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; He forgives whom He wills. He has forgiven unbelievers and He has forgiven the dissolute. However far the servant has gone in the evil of his condition, if Allah wills He guides him and forgives him. Forgiveness has no cause whatever, and it is withheld from none of Allah’s creation. May Allah forgive us and you, all of us. «And He punishes whom He will». «And Allah is forgiving» — to His awliyāʾ — «merciful» (Q. 3:129) — to the people of His obedience. «O you who believe, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied» — the usury they used to deal in during the Jāhiliyya: they would add to the sum when the term fell due and defer the demand, so that it became doubled and multiplied — «and fear Allah» — by leaving it off — «that you may prosper. And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the unbelievers» (Q. 3:130–131) — lest you be punished by it. «And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may be shown mercy. Hasten to a forgiveness from your Lord and to a garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth» (Q. 3:132–133). Hurry to righteous deeds, hastening to Allah’s forgiveness and hastening to Allah’s Garden, whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. The heavens are seven; the expanse of a heaven is a distance of five hundred years.
