To it points the saying of ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace: ⟨He who has not been born twice shall not enter the Presence.⟩ The sensory (ḥissī) birth and the spiritual birth. «And yours is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child; but if they have a child, then yours is a fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they may make, or any debt». In this, the child of the son is joined to the child by consensus. «And theirs» — that is, the wives, whether they be several or one — «is a fourth of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child» — by them or by others — «then theirs is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you may make, or any debt. And if a man is inherited from as kalāla» — he has no child and no parent; this is the explanation of kalāla — «or a woman» — inherited from as kalāla — «and he has» — that is, the one inherited from as kalāla — «a brother or a sister» — by the mother; and Ibn Masʿūd read it so — «then to each one of the two a sixth» — of what he left — «But if they are» — that is, the brothers and sisters by the mother — «more than that» — more than one — «then they are sharers in the third» — in which their male and their female are equal — «after any bequest made, or any debt, without causing harm» — without bringing harm upon the heirs — «as an injunction»

Allah enjoins upon you an injunction — «from Allah. And Allah is knowing» — of what He has ordained for His creation in the inheritance shares — «forbearing» (Q. 4:12) — in deferring the punishment of whoever opposes Him. The sunna has restricted the inheritance of those mentioned to such as have in them no impediment, of killing, or difference of religion, or slavery. «Those» — the rulings mentioned, from the matter of the orphans and what comes after it — «are the bounds set by Allah» — His ordinances, which He has set as bounds for His servants that they may act by them and not transgress them — «And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger» — in what He has ruled — «We shall admit him into gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein; and that is the great triumph. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His bounds, We shall admit him» — with both readings — «into a Fire, abiding therein; and he shall have» — therein — «a humiliating punishment» (Q. 4:13–14) — one that carries humiliation. «And those women who»

«commit the indecency» — fornication — «from among your women, call four of you to witness against them». When a man alleges fornication against his wife, he must produce four upright Muslim men who testify that they witnessed the man’s member enter the woman’s private part as the kohl-stick enters the kohl-jar. «If they testify» — against them — «then hold them» — confine them — «in the houses» — and keep them from mixing with people. This was the prescribed penalty for fornication at the beginning of Islam: they used to be confined and did not mix with people — «until death takes them» — the angels of death — «or» — until — «Allah appoints for them a way» (Q. 4:15) — a path to coming out of it. This was at the beginning of Islam. Then, when Allah prescribed flogging, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Allah has appointed a way for them: the unmarried with the unmarried, a hundred lashes and banishment for a year; and upon the married woman, stoning.⟩ And in the hadith, when he had made the penalty plain, he said: ⟨Take from me, take from me — Allah has appointed a way for them.⟩ «And the two who commit it» — that is, the indecency: fornication or sodomy — «from among you» — of the men — «then hurt them both» — with reviling and with beating with sandals — «But if they repent» — of it — «and make amends» — in deed — «then turn away from them both» — and do not hurt them — «Indeed Allah is ever relenting» — toward whoever repents — «merciful» (Q. 4:16) — to him. And this is abrogated by the prescribed penalty. «Repentance with Allah is only» — the repentance whose acceptance Allah has written upon Himself, by His bounty — «for those who do evil» — that is, disobedience — «in ignorance» — that is, being ignorant when they disobey their Lord — «then repent within» — a time — «that is near» — that is, before they come to the death-rattle — «those — Allah relents toward them» — He accepts their repentance — «and Allah is ever knowing» — of His creation — «wise» (Q. 4:17) — in His making. «And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds» — sins — «until, when death comes to one of them» — and he has entered upon the death-throes — «he says» — upon witnessing what he is in — «Indeed I repent now» — that does not profit him, and it is not accepted from him — «nor those who die while they are unbelievers» — likewise, whoever dies before repentance, his repentance is not accepted — «Those — We have made ready» — We have prepared — «for them a painful punishment» (Q. 4:18) — causing pain. «O you who believe, it is not lawful for you». The occasion of this verse’s revelation is what they used to do in the Jāhiliyya. When one of them died, his kinsman came and inherited his wives alone; if he wished, he married them without a bride-gift, and if he wished, he gave them in marriage and took the bride-gift. And when the father died, the son came into his father’s place and married his father’s wife; otherwise he gave her in marriage and took the dower. So the Exalted said: «O you who believe, it is not lawful for you» «to inherit women» — the persons of the women; they are not inherited — «by force» — being compelled to it — «nor» — that you — «hinder them» — prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping hold of them when you have no desire for them, so as to do them harm — «so that you may take away part of what you have given them» — of the dower — «unless they commit a manifest indecency» — fornication or recalcitrance — «and live with them in kindness» — with comeliness in speech, in maintenance and in sharing the night. Whoever marries a woman owes the conditions of marriage: maintenance, clothing, lodging, intercourse and good companionship. Whoever omits one of these five, the wife may divorce herself, and nothing is held against her. «And if you dislike them» — then be patient — «it may be that you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good» (Q. 4:19). When a man marries a woman and stays with her, and after that comes to dislike her, let him be patient in living with her, for in that steadfast patience (ṣabr) he finds much good, which is the reward of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; or Allah provides him a righteous child, and that is much good. There was one of the righteous men who married a bad woman, and she kept on injuring him as long as she lived, until she died. When she died he said, al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh Rabb al-ʿālamīn, and resolved that as long as he lived he would not marry women. When he had stayed some days, he saw in a dream that he was in his mosque and the angels were coming down and passing by him, and whenever an angel passed by him it said: ‘Is this the detested one?’ He said: ‘This is the detested one.’ ‘Is this the one who has lost?’ ‘This is the one who has lost.’ He was alarmed, but he was afraid to ask them, and they went on going back and forth like that. Then he could not restrain himself from asking, and said to them: ‘Who is the loser?’ They said to him:

You. The measure of the deeds of the people of the earth was being raised up for you every day and every night for the whole time of your marriage to the woman and her harming you; and when she died that was cut off, and you came to have no deed. So he awoke, and he married three in one day, and it came about that you would not see him

except that he had three or four with him. This is the meaning of «But if you dislike them, then perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good» (Q. 4:19). The harm a man finds from the mistress of the house — in that there is much reward for him with Allah; or the much good may be that Allah grants him a righteous child. «And if you wish to exchange one wife for another» — taking her in place of the other by divorcing her — «and you have given one of them» — the wives — «a great sum» — much wealth: if you have resolved to part from the woman and you have already given her much in the way of money and household goods — «then take nothing of it» — do not take anything from the woman after the divorce — «would you take it by calumny» — wrongfully — «and manifest sin» (Q. 4:20) — plain. Why do you take this money, when the money was given in exchange for something? «And how could you take it» — on what ground — «when you have gone in» — reached — «one of you to the other», for part of the man has reached part of the woman through the intercourse that makes the dower binding; since she has come to stand in this relation to him, and the cause of that was the money, how can you take this money afterwards? «and they have taken from you a covenant»

a pledge — «solemn» (Q. 4:21) — firm; and that is what the woman sees of the man’s love for her at that time. Or the solemn pledge is the stipulation that is stipulated at the contract. At the contracting of the marriage one says «then retention in kindness or release with good treatment» (Q. 2:229) — this is a stipulation, and the husband must observe this stipulation: he either retains in kindness or releases with good treatment. «And do not marry those women whom your fathers married». The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that a man died, and his son rose and came and sat beside his wife, wanting to take her as a wife after his father. The woman swore that this would never come about from her: after I have been with your father, it is not possible that I should ever be with you. The son said that he would certainly marry her by force, by inheritance. So the two of them brought their case to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed «And do not marry those women whom your fathers married» — a woman whom the father has married, it is not permitted for the son to marry her — «except» — that is, but — «what has already passed» — of your doing: what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, and after the revelation of the verse this marriage was forbidden — «indeed it»

marrying them — «was an indecency» — something vile — «and detestable» — a cause for the detestation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which is the most intense hatred — «and evil» — wretched — «as a way» (Q. 4:22) — a road. «Forbidden to you are your mothers» The verse named expressly the women

one of whom it is forbidden for a man to marry. It is forbidden for a man to marry his mothers: his mother, and his mother’s mother, and that one’s mother, and that one’s mother, on up. «And your daughters» — this takes in the daughters of one’s children, however far down: the man’s daughter, and the daughters of his children, and the daughters of those, and the daughters of those, to the end of time. «And your sisters» — from the side of the father or of the mother, likewise: every woman between you and whom there is a sibling bond from the side of the father or of the mother. «And your paternal aunts» — the sisters of your fathers and of your grandfathers. «And your maternal aunts» — the sisters of your mothers and of your grandmothers. «And the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister»

— and their offspring are included among them. «And your mothers who have suckled you» — and the mother who suckled the man before the completion of the two years — «and your sisters through suckling» — and joined to that, by the sunna, are their daughters. «And the mothers of your wives, and your stepdaughters» — and your rabāʾib (stepdaughters) is the plural of rabība, and she is the wife’s daughter by a man other than him — «who are in your care»

— whom you rear: a description that accords with what is usually the case, so it carries no counter-implication. What is usual is that the stepdaughter is in his care; but even if she is not in his care, the stepdaughter is forbidden. «of your wives to whom you have gone in» — the stepdaughter who is forbidden is the stepdaughter whose mother the man has gone in to — «but if you have not gone in to them» — if the man has contracted marriage with the woman’s mother and has not gone in to her — «then there is no blame upon you» — it is permitted for him to divorce the mother and marry the daughter, if she accepts — «and the wives of your sons who are of your loins» — when a son of one’s own loins has married a woman, she is forbidden to the father — «and that you should join together two sisters» — whether by lineage or by suckling, in marriage — «except» — that is, but — «what has already passed» — what came before, in the Jāhiliyya, of joining together two sisters: that is lawful — «indeed Allah is forgiving» — of what has passed from you before the prohibition — «merciful» (Q. 4:23). Allah has never forbidden anything in the Qurʾan and excepted what had already passed, save in two cases:

«And do not marry those women whom your fathers married» — He said: «except what has already passed» (Q. 4:22), «and that you should join together two sisters» — He said: «except what has already passed» (Q. 4:23). The reason for this is that these two cases occurred among certain of the forefathers of

the Prophet ﷺ. Kināna married his father’s wife, and among the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ there was one who joined together two sisters. Had it been forbidden and what had already passed not been excepted, this would have touched something of the honour of the Prophet ﷺ; but since the Prophet ﷺ is inviolate in his person, what came before the revelation of the verse is lawful, so that nothing should touch any part of the Prophet ﷺ. This is the wisdom (al-ḥikma) in this exception. These women — marrying them is forbidden. O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.

«And married women among women, except those whom your right hands possess» Allah has forbidden a man to marry the married women — that is, women who have husbands. A woman who is under a man: marrying her is forbidden. That is to guard the Muslim against sharing a woman with another, for this is not manly virtue (murūʾa); it is baseness. «except those whom your right hands possess» — except where it so happens that a man has taken captive a woman who has a husband: he has the strength to take possession of her without sharing her, and for this reason she has become lawful to him by ownership after the period of ascertainment (istibrāʾ). These are fourteen or fifteen among the women whom He has forbidden in marriage; and the sunna appended the sister through suckling, and affinity, and the joining of a woman together with her maternal aunt, and of a woman together with her paternal aunt. Those who did not accept this disallowed the abrogation of the Qurʾan by a report of single transmission (khabar al-āḥād):

«as men in wedlock» — married — «not as fornicators» — not committing fornication. When He had mentioned fourteen women, or fifteen, He made clear that He has made lawful what is other than that; and this making-lawful is perpetual in one class and not perpetual in another, just as the forbidden women are of classes. There is the woman whose prohibition is perpetual, and that is what has been mentioned of the women; and it is forbidden to marry the woman irrevocably divorced, and this prohibition is not perpetual — only until after [another] husband; and the woman who has a husband, only until after the divorce; and the woman in her waiting period, until her waiting period expires; and the second sister, until her sister is divorced; and the fifth, until the fourth is divorced. This prohibition is not perpetual. «So whatever you have enjoyed» — you have taken enjoyment — «of it from among them» — of those you have married, by intercourse — «then give them their bridal gifts»

their dowers which you have appointed for them — «as a prescribed obligation; and there is no blame upon you in what you have mutually agreed» — you and they — «upon, after the prescribed obligation» — by remitting it, or part of it, or adding to it. Additions [to the dower] in marriage: whenever the husband and the wife agree together, there is no harm in that. «Indeed Allah is knowing» — of His creation — «wise» (Q. 4:24) — in what He has ordained. «And whoever among you is not able [to afford] means» — wealth — «to marry the chaste women» — the free women — «the believing ones, then from those whom your right hands possess» — then let him marry the slave women — «from among your believing maidens» — among the believing slave women — «And Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another». Faith is a condition in marrying slave women, and faith is of the heart; for this reason He, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned «And Allah knows best your faith». So be content with its outward signs and commit the inward secrets to Him, for He is the one who knows them in detail. Many a slave woman surpasses the free woman. This is a reassurance concerning the marriage of slave women. Marrying the slave woman — the slave woman of another — is permitted if a person is unable to marry a free woman and fears hardship (al-ʿanat). And patience is better than marrying the slave woman, because you consign your child to slavery. This is the position of Mālik: that whoever is unable to marry a free woman and fears hardship may marry slave women. The position of al-Shāfiʿī is that nothing is stipulated in marrying slave women; he explained marriage as intercourse alone — if you are not able to have intercourse with free women at the time, and you have no free woman whom you may marry, then there is no harm in marrying the slave woman. «So marry them with the permission of their people» — their masters — «And give them» — hand over to them — «their bridal gifts»
their dowers — «with kindness» — without delay or diminution — «chaste women» — women of chastity — «not fornicating»

women who fornicate openly — «nor taking paramours» — intimates who fornicate with them in secret — «And when they are taken in wedlock» — they are given in marriage, that is, they marry — «and if they commit an indecency» — fornication — «then upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women» — the free women, the virgins, when

they fornicate — «of the punishment» — the prescribed penalty (ḥadd), so they are given fifty lashes and banished for half a year; and male slaves are reckoned by analogy with them. He did not make being in wedlock (iḥṣān) a condition for the penalty to be due, but in order to convey that there is no stoning upon them at all. «That» — the marriage of slave women when the means are lacking — «is for whoever fears hardship» — fornication — «among you» — unlike the one among the free men who does not fear it, for whom marrying her is not lawful; and likewise one who is able [to afford] the means for a free woman. Al-Shāfiʿī holds this. Excluded by His words «from among your believing maidens» are the unbelieving women: marrying them is not lawful for him even if he lacks [the means] and fears. «And that you be patient is better for you» — so that the child does not become a slave — «and Allah is forgiving, merciful» (Q. 4:25) — in granting latitude in that.

He, Blessed and Exalted, gave in this verse the ruling of marriage, what is lawful and what is forbidden. People differ over marriage according to the difference of their ranks: it is obligatory for one who is strong and of intense craving for desire — for such a one it is obligatory that he marry; and it is recommended (mandūb) in the case of the moderate man; and it is forbidden in the case of one unable to perform the act, or unable [to provide] maintenance and the dower. And when a person wishes to marry, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: ⟨Take for yourself the one who has religion.⟩ He is to choose, truly, the women of religion, the daughters of the righteous; and the virgin is to be chosen, because the virgin is more sincere in love. They said: as for the woman married before, if you marry her and she has no child by another, then half her heart is yours and the remaining half is the first husband's; and if she has a child from before you, then you have nothing of her — half her heart is for the first husband and the second half for the child; she consumes your provision and, more often than not, treats you as an enemy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned:

⟨Made beloved to me, of this world of yours, are women and perfume; and the delight of my eye is in the prayer.⟩ Women, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finds in his wives a help toward conveying the message; and every married man finds help from his wife in establishing the religion. Even if it were nothing but that she spares him the grinding and the kneading and the cooking and the washing and the sweeping of the house and the care of the child — all of this, had the man undertaken it himself, would have occupied him away from his religion. So the woman is not of this world; rather she is a help toward religion in the case of the Muslim. For this reason they said that the righteous woman is not of this world. And for this reason the Messenger said: ⟨Made beloved to me, of this world of yours, are women and perfume; and the delight of my eye is in the prayer.⟩ In the woman there is the beautiful face that reminds him of the beauty (al-jamāl) of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and in perfume there is the sweet scent, and its origin is from the Garden. So all of this was made beloved to him — but the delight of his eye is in the prayer. He did not say that the delight of his eye is by the prayer, but that the delight of his eye is in the prayer. The state (ḥāl) that he finds in the prayer is what his eye is delighted by ﷺ, not the prayer itself, the place of intimate converse: «And prostrate yourself and draw near» (Q. 96:19). «Allah wishes to make clear to you» — the laws of your religion and what is in the interest of your affair — «and to guide you to the ways of those before you» — the paths of the prophets in what is made lawful and what is made forbidden — «and to relent toward you» — He brings you back from His disobedience, in which you were, to His obedience — «and Allah is knowing» — of you — «wise» (Q. 4:26) — in what He has ordained for you. «And Allah wishes to relent toward you» — He repeated it in order to build upon it — «and those who follow the desires wish» — the Jews, the Christians, the Magians and the fornicators — «that you should deviate with a great deviation» (Q. 4:27). «Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you» — He makes the rulings of the shariʿa easy for you — «and man was created weak» (Q. 4:28) — he cannot be patient away from women and the desires. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, mentioned in this verse that He wishes four things for us, by His bounty, Blessed and Exalted:
He wishes to make clear to us the shariʿa; and He wishes to guide us to the straight path; and He wishes to relent toward us; and He wishes to

lighten [the burden] for us. «And those who follow the desires wish» — a faction of Quraysh who used to find fault with the ruling of the shariʿa. They would say: the Qurʾan has forbidden you your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts, yet you have married the daughters of the paternal aunts and the daughters of the maternal aunts; so on this reckoning marrying the daughters of the sister and the daughters of the brother is lawful — they are alike. The daughters of the sister are forbidden in the Qurʾan, and the paternal aunts are forbidden, yet you have married the daughter of the paternal aunt and you have married the daughter of the maternal aunt; so how have you forbidden the brother's daughter and the sister's daughter? «And those who follow the desires wish that you should deviate with a great deviation» (Q. 4:27). These are the ones who wished deviation for you, and Allah wished guidance for you. He wished four things for us: that He make clear to us the shariʿa — it is plain, its night like its day; and He wished to guide us to the straight path, which is the path to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and He wished to accept repentance from us, so that we return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and He wished to lighten [the burden] for us — and this is the greatest blessing upon us. He placed the lightening upon Muḥammad ﷺ and upon his community, so that their journeying came to be by assistance (maʿūna), as the journeying of those before us was by their own effort (muʾna). Ibrāhīm said: «I am going to my Lord; He will guide me» (Q. 37:99) — so the going, on Ibrāhīm's part, was

an effort of his own; and He said concerning Mūsā: «And when Mūsā came to Our appointed time» (Q. 7:143) — so the coming, on Mūsā's part, was an effort borne by Mūsā; and He said concerning Muḥammad: «Glory be to Him who carried His servant by night» (Q. 17:1) — so the night journey was an assistance, not an effort; and He said concerning us: «We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth» (Q. 41:53) — so the showing was from al-Ḥaqq, not from us: an assistance also. They were denied joining (al-waṣl) and unbroken union (al-wiṣāl), and Muḥammad ﷺ was given joining and unbroken union: «he drew near and hung suspended, so he was two bow-lengths away, or nearer» (Q. 53:8–9); and unbroken union: «the heart did not lie about what it saw» (Q. 53:11). And concerning us: ⟨Whoever draws near to Me by a span, I draw near to him by a cubit…⟩ — so all of this was by assistance

not by burden. «and man was created weak» (Q. 4:28), because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created things differing one from another. The angel is luminous: his life is in worship alone, and he continues in that and does not change. Beasts and animals — their life is in their appetites alone, and they do not change from that. And He created man weak, such that he cannot hold to one state; and so, through his weakness, he reached the highest station. Man, since he is weak, you find him at one time following appetite as though he were a beast; at one time he eats and at one time he marries and drinks; at one time he is angry and at one time he schemes; and at one time he prays and remembers Allah and devotes himself to worship as though he were an angel. This changing is in none but man. The angel cannot turn about into the state of the animals, and the animals cannot turn about into the state of the angel, while man is at one time an angel and at one time an animal. Because of man's weakness he cannot hold to one state, for the thing he loves most is eating: if the food is set before you and you begin to eat, half an hour does not pass before you are unable to eat. Drinking is likewise, and the appetite for women is likewise. If you stand, standing defeats you; and if you sit, you cannot keep on sitting; if you lie down on your side, you cannot keep on at that; if you sleep, you are unable to sleep on, and if you wake, you are unable to stay awake. Whatever man does, he does not continue in it but that he is unable to do it, because of his weakness. So, for this weakness, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, aided him, until he became the best of creation. Allah says: ⟨I am a king, living, who does not die. Son of Ādam, if you obey Me I will make you a king, living, who does not die⟩. By that he becomes the best of creation. And by this weakness too man is corrupted, until he becomes the worst of creation, because he cannot hold to one state: if he commits an indecency he passes from it to another indecency, and passes from that, and man never wearies; he does no evil but that he wishes to do an evil worse than that, until he becomes the worst of creation. So for this reason man is described as the best of creation and described as the worst of creation — this because of his weakness. This weakness is praise in the case of one whom Allah loves and blame in the case of one whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates. «O you who believe, do not consume your property among yourselves wrongfully» — by what is unlawful in the Law, such as usury and seizure by force. The inviolability (ḥurma) of a Muslim's property is like the inviolability of his blood. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made inviolable the property of the Muslim, and his honour, and his blood. «unless it be» — there come about —

«a trade» — a mutual sale between two persons — «by mutual consent among you» — and willingness of soul — so it is yours to consume. If you sell or buy, that is lawful for you. «and do not kill yourselves» — by committing what leads to their destruction, whatever it may be, in this world or the hereafter — «indeed Allah is merciful to you» (Q. 4:29) — in His forbidding you that. Man is not to fall ravening upon this world and so be avid for this world, such that, were he to lose his property, he would kill himself; for whoever kills himself, Allah has forbidden him the Garden. Or: «do not kill yourselves» — do not commit anything that leads to destruction. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ interpreted it when he rose at the hour before dawn (saḥar) and the cold was severe upon him, so he performed the dry ablution and prayed, and said: Allah says «and do not kill yourselves». And he said this interpretation in the presence of the Messenger ﷺ, and he did not reject it. It is said that killing the nafs (the soul) is its attachment to this world and its greed for it, because this world — her sons, who busy themselves with her, she must needs kill them to the last of them. ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace, was travelling, and with him was a Jew who claimed that he believed in him. ʿĪsā took three loaves and loaded them on the Jew. When the journey grew long the Jew stole one of them and ate it. When midday came ʿĪsā called him and said to him:

[Bring] the food. So he brought two loaves. ʿĪsā said to him: Where is the third? He said: I did not see it — he swore that he had not seen the third loaf. A gazelle passed by. ʿĪsā said to him: Tell this gazelle to come to me; say to it: Answer the Spirit of Allah. So he said: O gazelle, answer the Spirit of Allah. The gazelle came and lay down. He said to him: Slaughter it. So he slaughtered it. He said to him: Kindle a fire. So he kindled a fire and roasted, and the two of them ate. When they had eaten until they were full, ʿĪsā said to it: Rise, by the permission of Allah. So it rose and went away. The Jew said: This is a wonder. He said to him: By the right of the One who did this for us, where is the third loaf? He said: I did not see it. They went on and came to a sea. He said to him: This is a sea before us; what is to be done? He said: This we cannot cross except by ship. He said to him: Close your eyes. So he closed his eyes, and there the two of them were beyond the sea — they had crossed the sea. He said: Glory be to Allah, this is a wonder. He said: By the right of the One who did this for us, where is the loaf? He said: I did not see it. So they went on and found three heaps of gold, and the two of them sat down. ʿĪsā said to him: This is some gold for us; let us divide it between us — a part for me, and a part for you, and a part for whoever ate the bread. He said to him: I am the one who ate it. ʿĪsā said: Fie on you! All the signs you saw did not move you to tell the truth, and this world moves you to truthfulness. Take the heaps, all of them. And ʿĪsā went away from him. He remained sitting by the heaps of gold, unable to carry them and unable to go away from them; so he just sat by them. When night fell three men came and said: What are you doing here? He said: This gold is mine, and I am sitting here guarding it. So they killed him and took the gold — they were three, each of them took a heap. They sat until the morning, and hunger hurt them. They said: Let us send one of us to a village to buy us food for us to eat. So they sent one of them. When he had gone the two men took counsel together; they said: When so-and-so comes, let us kill him before we eat, and the gold will remain for us, the two of us. And when he went to the market he bought food and said: I shall put poison in it; when my two companions eat it they will die, and the gold will remain for me. So he put the poison in the food and returned to the two men; and when he set the food down they killed him there and then, and ate, and they died too. So ʿĪsā came back

and found all four dead beside the gold. He said: This is what this world does to its children. «And do not kill yourselves» — by following this world — «Indeed Allah is ever merciful to you» (Q. 4:29) — in forbidding you that. «And whoever does that» — what has been forbidden — «in transgression» — overstepping the lawful — «and wrongdoing» — an emphasis — «We shall make him enter» — We shall bring him into — «a Fire» — burning in it — «and that is easy for Allah» (Q. 4:30) — light. «If you avoid the grave sins of what you are forbidden» — they are those to which a threat attaches, such as killing, fornication and theft; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: they come nearer to seven hundred — «We shall expiate from you your evil deeds» — Allah forgives the small sins through the avoidance of the grave sins (kabāʾir) — «and admit you by a noble entrance» (Q. 4:31) — it is the Garden. The grave sins, they said, number up to seven hundred. The Messenger ﷺ was asked, and he said: ⟨Avoid the seven ruinous sins: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, killing a soul, consuming usury, consuming the property of the orphan, slandering a chaste free woman, and fleeing from the advance [of the enemy].⟩ [2] He ﷺ bounded the ruinous sins by these seven; they are what the verse mentions: «If you avoid the grave sins of what you are forbidden, We shall expiate

«from you your evil deeds». And it is said: [they are] everything for which a threat has come in the Qurʾan. «and We will admit you to a noble entrance» (Q. 4:31) — it is the Garden. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forgives sins and changes evil deeds into good deeds. «And do not covet what Allah has favoured some of you with over others» (Q. 4:32). It was sent down when Umm Salama said: Would that we were men, that we might fight in jihad and have the like of the reward of the men. So it was sent down. «And do not covet what Allah has favoured some of you with over others» — in respect of this world or of religion, lest it lead to mutual envy and mutual hatred — «for men there is a share» — a reward — «of what they have earned»

by reason of what they did of jihad and other things — «and for women there is a share of what they have earned» (Q. 4:32) — of obedience to their husbands and the guarding of their private parts. This verse (āya) forbids coveting what Allah has given to a person other than you; and that is because a man's felicity falls into three divisions: a felicity of the soul, such as intelligence and knowledge and the sciences, in quantity and in quality, and chastity and courage and generosity — all these are traits of character that attach to a man's soul; and a division of them is bodily, such as health and length of life, what attaches to a man's body; and [a division] external, such as many children and property and friends and brethren and good repute and people's love for the person, and other things besides. So when a man looks at a man with whom these things are abundant while he himself has nothing of them, either he wishes to obtain what the man has, or he wishes those blessings to pass away from the man. If he wishes them to pass away, that is envy; and if he wishes that there come to him the like of what has come to the man, that is emulation, and it is not an act of disobedience — except that the Qurʾan has forbidden us to covet what another man has in every case,

so then, let no one covet what another has. Do not say: O Allah, give me a house like so-and-so's house, and property like so-and-so's property, and a wife like his wife. It may be that a thing is good with one man and, when it is with another, is evil. There is many a one who had much property and his religion was sound, and if this property passed over to the one coveting it his religion would be corrupted. So then, let a man not covet what another has; rather let him ask Allah of His bounty. Let him ask Allah for that in which lies the soundness of his religion and of his world and of his hereafter.

And when you look into this you find that the supplication (duʿāʾ) which the Qurʾan taught us is the best of supplications absolutely: «Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and guard us from the punishment of the Fire» (Q. 2:201). And it is said: «and do not covet what Allah has favoured some of you with over others» (Q. 4:32) — in the good of this world; and to it points the hadith: ⟨Look to the one who is below you and do not look to the one who is above you⟩, because a man, whoever he may be, if he looks above himself sees one who has many times over what he himself has, and so he reckons what he has to be little, and his thanksgiving becomes little, and he may well envy him; and if he looks to the one below him, whoever he may be, he sees that he has surpassed many of the creatures in many things, and so he reckons what he has to be much and he praises Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So then, if you wish to look, look at the one beneath you — that is more conducive to thanksgiving — and do not look at the one above you — that is more conducive to envy and discontent. And this is in the matters of this world. But in religion there is no harm in your looking to the one who is above you, that you may take him as a model and struggle against your nafs until you are like him; and do not look to the one who is below you, lest you see yourself to be in a praiseworthy state. A man, however far he has gone in laziness and in paucity of works, if he looks to the one below him sees that his state is good. For this reason you are to look to the one who is above you and not look to the one who is below you. And when a man covets what another has and wishes its passing away, that is envy; and envy eats up the good deeds of the servant as [the fire] eats

ﷺ would keep good company with his wives, because they are deficient in intellect and religion. Whoever is patient with the harm they do finds with Allah a great reward. They said: Bearing with a woman in one thing is a bearing with twenty things. If a woman is angered and you bear with her anger, you have kept the child safe from the slap, and kept the calf safe from the blow, and kept the guest safe from being driven off, and kept the cooking pot safe from breaking, and kept the garment safe from tearing, and other things besides. If you anger her she harms all of these, and if you are patient you keep all of these safe. «And those whose rebelliousness you fear» — their disobedience to you, in that its sign has appeared — «admonish them» — so make them fear Allah — «and avoid them in the beds» — withdraw to another bed if they show rebelliousness — «and strike them» — a blow that is not severe, if they do not come back through the avoidance. When a woman shows rebelliousness (nushūz), the first way is that you admonish her. You say to her: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made obedience to me obligatory upon you — the carrying out of my command and the avoidance of what I forbid; and a woman, when her husband is pleased with her, enters the Garden. If she profits by this admonition, well and good; and if not, then avoid her in the beds. If she is deterred, that is that; and if not, then strike her a blow that is not severe, such that you do not break a limb. «And if they obey you» — in what is wanted of them — «then do not seek» — do not pursue — «against them any way» — when you have admonished her and she has accepted the admonition, do not say: I must needs strike her, wrongfully — «indeed Allah is High, Great» (Q. 4:34) — so beware of Him, lest He punish you if you wrong them. «And if you fear»
you know — «discord» — disagreement — «between the two» — between the two spouses; when discord has occurred between them — «then send» to the two of them

with the consent of them both «an arbiter» — an upright man — «from his people» — the husband's relatives — «and an arbiter from her people» (Q. 4:35) — from the woman's relatives. The husband appoints his arbiter to act for him in divorce and in accepting a compensation in return for it, and she appoints her arbiter to act for her in seeking divorce at her own instance (ikhtilāʿ). The two then exert their judgement and command the wrongdoer to return, or they part them if they see that. «If the two desire»

the two arbiters — «reconciliation, Allah will bring them to accord» — between the two spouses: He gives them power over what is obedience, whether reconciliation or parting (firāq) — «indeed Allah is Knowing» — of everything — «Aware» (Q. 4:35) — of inward things as of outward — «And worship Allah»

declare His oneness — «and associate nothing with Him, and» — do good — «to parents, kindness» — dutifulness and gentleness of demeanour — «and to kin» — relatives — «and orphans and the needy and the neighbour who is near» — the one near to you in neighbourhood or in kinship — «and the neighbour who is a stranger» — the one far from you in neighbourhood or in kinship — «and the companion at your side» — the companion on a journey, or in a craft; and it is said, the wife — «and the wayfarer» — the one cut off in the course of his journey — «and those whom your right hands possess» — among slaves — «Indeed Allah does not love one who is arrogant» — proud — «boastful» (Q. 4:36) — over people

with what he has been given. «Those who are miserly» — with what is obligatory upon them — «and enjoin miserliness upon the people» — with it — «and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty» — of knowledge and of wealth; and they are the Jews, for whom there is a severe threat; the predicate is elided — «And We have prepared for the disbelievers» — for that and for other than it — «a humiliating punishment» (Q. 4:37) — one that carries humiliation (ihāna) — «And those who spend their wealth to be seen of people» — making a show (murāʾūn) — «and do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day» — like the hypocrites and the people of Mecca — «And whoever has Satan for a companion» — a comrade who acts by his command, like these — «then evil» — wretched — «as a companion» (Q. 4:38) — is he. «And what would it cost them» — there is no harm upon them — «if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent of what Allah has provided them? And Allah is ever knowing of them» (Q. 4:39) — and so He will requite them. «Indeed Allah does not wrong» — anyone — «by the weight of a mote» — the weight of a mote, the smallest ant, by diminishing it from his good deeds or adding it to his evil deeds — «And if there be» — that is, the mote — «a good deed, He multiplies it» — from ten to more than seven hundred — «and gives from Himself» — from His own, together with the multiplication — «a great reward» (Q. 4:40). Allah may well give something from Himself in which the servant has no work, and that is as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨When the Day of⟩

⟨Resurrection comes, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stands and intercedes, and the prophets intercede, and the ulama intercede, and the martyrs intercede, and the believers, until none remains in the Fire but one who has no intercessor. Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: The prophets have interceded, and the martyrs, and the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah), and the ulama, and the believers; none remains but I, and I am the most merciful of those who show mercy. Look into the Fire: everyone in whose heart there is a dinar’s weight of faith — bring him out of the Fire. And they bring out a great many. Then He says: Look for whoever has half a dinar — bring him out. And they bring out a great many. Then He says: Look into the Fire for whoever has a mote’s weight of faith — bring him out. And they bring out a great many. And after that He takes a handful who never had any good to their credit at all, and He admits them to the Garden by His bounty and His generosity.⟩ This is the meaning of «And if there be a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward» (Q. 4:40): He gives something from Himself alone, in which the servant has no cause at all.

«So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness» — who testifies against it concerning its deeds, and he is its prophet — «and We bring you» — O Muḥammad ﷺ — «as a witness against these» (Q. 4:41) — a witness against these. When the Day of Resurrection comes, Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, is brought — and he is the first of the prophets — and it is said to him: ⟨Did Jibrīl convey to you that with which I sent to you?⟩ He says: ⟨Yes, Jibrīl conveyed it to me.⟩ ⟨And you — did you convey it to your people?⟩ He says: ⟨Yes, I conveyed it to my people.⟩

The nation of Nūḥ is called: ⟨Did Nūḥ convey to you?⟩ They say: ⟨No bearer of good tidings came to us, nor any warner.⟩ Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨Who will testify for you, O Nūḥ, that you conveyed?⟩ He says: ⟨The nation of Muḥammad ﷺ.⟩ And the nation of Muḥammad testifies that Allah sent down in the Qurʾan: «Indeed We sent Nūḥ to his people» (Q. 71:1) — to the end of the sura. So they testify that Nūḥ did convey and that they disbelieved; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ testifies that his nation is a middle nation, upright, the best, whose testimony is accepted. Then likewise on to the last of the nations; and Muḥammad ﷺ is brought as a witness against us ourselves. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting when Jibrīl came down upon him and said to him: ⟨Allah commands you to listen to the Qurʾan from Ubayy b. Kaʿb.⟩ So the Messenger sent for Ubayy and said to him: ⟨My Lord has commanded me to listen to the Qurʾan from you.⟩ He said to him: ⟨He named me by my name?⟩ And he wept for joy. And he began to recite from the beginning until he reached here:
«and We bring you as a witness against these» (Q. 4:41). Then the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ overflowed, and he said to him: ⟨Enough, enough!⟩

Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī was buried, and the two angels came to him and said to him: ⟨And who is your Lord?⟩ He said: ⟨Do not ask me — ask Him, Him. If I say that I am His servant and He does not accept it, there is no use in this. Ask Him: if He says that he is My servant, then that is that; and if not, there is no use⟩

⟨in my words.⟩ «On that Day» — the day of the bringing — «On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them» — they wish that they were dust, because of the enormity of the terror — as in another verse: «and the disbeliever will say: Would that I were dust» (Q. 78:40). The disbelievers wish that the earth should be levelled over them and that they should be dust. «And they will not conceal from Allah any speech» (Q. 4:42) — of what they did. At another time they do conceal it; they say: «By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists» (Q. 6:23). What lies between these two verses: «By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists» — this is concealment; and here He said «and they will not conceal from Allah any speech» — because they attempted the concealment: «By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists» — so Allah sealed their mouths, and the limbs spoke

No indeed: every limb spoke of what it had done, and so they concealed nothing. «O you who have believed, do not approach the prayer» (Q. 4:43) — the third of the verses on wine. When there came down «They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: in them is great sin, and benefit for people» (Q. 2:219), some drank and some left off. So ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf made a banquet and called in the chief men of the Companions, and they ate and drank wine, and they put our master ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib forward for the sunset prayer, and he recited Sūrat al-Kāfirūn with the omission of the lāʾāt (the instances of lā), all of them. So He said: «O you who have believed, do not approach the prayer» — do not pray — «while you are intoxicated» — from drink — «until you know what you are saying» — that is, until you are sober. Then the Messenger recited this verse, and ʿUmar said: ⟨O Allah, make clear to us concerning wine a clarification that suffices.⟩ Up to now the ruling had not been made clear. Some of them would drink when they wanted to sleep at night and be sober before the dawn prayer, so that they prayed without being intoxicated; and some left it off altogether, until the fourth verse came down, from Sūrat al-Māʾida, which forbade wine completely. «nor while in a state of major ritual impurity» — by penetration or by emission — «save as those passing through» — do not approach the prayer while you are in a state of major impurity, save as those crossing over, travellers — «until you have washed yourselves» — and so you may pray once you have washed. But before the washing, the prohibition is against approaching the places of prayer, that is, the mosques, except to pass through them without staying. If a person is in a state of major impurity he does not enter the mosque — not even the mosque of his house, his place of prayer; he does not stay in it, but only as one passing through. «And if you are ill» — with an illness such that water harms him — «or on a journey» — or you are travelling, and you are in a state of major impurity or of minor impurity — «or one of you has come from the privy»

it is the place appointed for relieving oneself, that is, he has incurred minor impurity — «or you have touched women» — you have had intercourse with them — «and you find no water» — with which to purify yourselves for the prayer, after seeking and searching; and this refers back to all but the sick — «then have recourse to»

aim at it, after the [prayer-]time has come in — «wholesome earth» — pure dust; and strike it two strokes — «and wipe your faces and your hands» — together with the elbows — «Indeed Allah is ever pardoning, forgiving» (Q. 4:43). This verse came down concerning the dry ablution (tayammum),

when a person has no water, or is ill with an illness through which he is unable to use water, or fears an increase in the illness, or its onset, or a delay in his recovery, as the jurists have said, then he may perform the dry ablution. It is that he aim at wholesome (ṭayyib) earth. Wholesome earth, for al-Shāfiʿī, is what brings forth vegetation; he took that from His saying «and the wholesome land brings forth its vegetation by the permission of its Lord» (Q. 7:58). And wholesome earth, for Mālik, is everything that appears upon the face of the earth from among the parts of the earth: dust, or salt-flat, or stone. «Have you not seen those who were given a portion» — a share — «of the Book» — and they are

the Jews «who purchase error at the price of guidance» «and they wish that you should stray from the way» (Q. 4:44) — that you should miss the road of truth, so that you may be like them. «And Allah knows best your enemies» (Q. 4:45) — better than you do. Allah knows the enemies better than we do, and so He informs you of them that you may avoid them

«And Allah suffices as a Protector» — as a guardian for you against them — «and Allah suffices as a Helper» (Q. 4:45) — as one who keeps their guile from you — «From among those who are Jews» — there are a people — «who distort» — who alter — «the words» — that which Allah sent down in the Torah of the description of Muḥammad ﷺ — «from their places» — the places in which they were set — «and they say» — to the Prophet ﷺ — «We hear» — your word — «and we disobey» — your command — «and hear, may you not be made to hear» — an imprecation, that is: may you not hear — «and»

they say «rāʿinā» — and it has been forbidden to address him with it, and it is a word of abuse in their tongue, from folly (al-ruʿūna), which is stupidity — «twisting» — distortion — «with their tongues, and reviling» — defaming — «in the religion» — reviling against Islam — «And had they said: We hear and we obey» — in place of «and we disobey» — «and hear» — only — «and look upon us» — look at us, in place of «rāʿinā» — «it would have been better for them» — than what they said — «and more upright» — more just — «but Allah has cursed them» — removed them far from His mercy

«for their unbelief, so they do not believe except a little» (Q. 4:46). «O you who have been given the Book, believe in what We have sent down» — of the Qurʾan — «confirming what is with you» — of the Torah — «before We obliterate faces» — effacing what is in them, of the eye and the nose and the eyebrows — «and turn them upon their backs» — making them like the backs of the necks, a single flat surface — «or We curse them»

transforming them into apes — «as We cursed» — as We transformed — «the people of the Sabbath» — the people of Dāwūd — «And the command of Allah is» — His decree — «accomplished» (Q. 4:47). He has mentioned in this verse that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, cursed the people of Dāwūd who transgressed on the Sabbath, as came earlier in Sūrat al-Baqara; in truth it was Dāwūd, upon him be blessings and peace, who cursed them: «Those who disbelieved among the Children of Isrāʾīl were cursed by the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā son of Maryam» (Q. 5:78). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made among His servants a people whose cursing is like His own cursing, Blessed and Exalted, and whose supplication (duʿāʾ) is like His own supplication, Blessed and Exalted; and they are His vicegerents (khulafāʾ). For Dāwūd and ʿĪsā both invoked Allah against a people and cursed them: «Those who disbelieved among the Children of Isrāʾīl were cursed by the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā son of Maryam» (Q. 5:78). Those who were cursed by the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā son of Maryam are the ones of whom al-Ḥaqq says here that He cursed them Himself. The cursing of Dāwūd is the cursing of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: «or We curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath, and the command of Allah is accomplished» (Q. 4:47). When it came down, ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām embraced Islam; and it was said that it was a threat with a condition, so when some of them embraced Islam it was lifted. And it is said that an obliteration and a transformation will take place before the rising of the Hour. «Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that» (Q. 4:48) — of sins. The occasion of this verse’s revelation is that Waḥshī, the slayer of Ḥamza, wrote to the Messenger ﷺ: I desire Islam, but a verse from the Book of Allah holds me back:

«And those who do not call upon another god alongside Allah» — and I have worshipped al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt; «and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden» — and I am the slayer of Ḥamza; «and do not commit fornication» (Q. 25:68) — and I have done this often. Then there came down: «Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work» (Q. 25:70). The Messenger ﷺ wrote this to him, and he said: I have resolved upon repentance, but I do not know whether, if I repent, I shall do righteous work or not. And he did not repent, so this verse came down: «Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that» — of sins — «for whomever He wills» (Q. 4:48) — forgiveness for him, by admitting him to the Garden

without punishment; and whomever He wills He punishes among the believers for his sins and then admits him to the Garden. This verse came down, and the Messenger ﷺ sent it to him, and he said: He has said «for whomever He wills», and I do not know whether I shall be among those He wills or not — until there came down: «Say: O My servants who have been prodigal against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins» (Q. 39:53). The Messenger ﷺ sent it to him, and after that he embraced Islam. People fall into classes. One class embraced Islam and did righteous work and died in that state; they are of the people of the Garden by consensus. And a class disobeyed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and repented and sought forgiveness for their sins; those are of the people of the Garden by consensus. And a class disobeyed and died before repenting; concerning those there is disagreement. The Murjiʾa say that acts of disobedience do a believer no harm — he simply enters the Garden — and that all the threatening in the Qurʾan is only in respect of the unbelievers, while as for whoever has merely believed, he is safe from all the threatening. And a party says that whoever has committed a grave sin has gone out of Islam; so whoever has committed

a grave sin is of the people of the Fire. The people of the sunna do not put a Muslim out of Islam on account of a grave sin; so if a Muslim commits a grave sin and dies before repenting, his affair rests with Allah. The truth in this is what the people of the sunna have said, on the evidence of this verse: «Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, and He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills» (Q. 4:48). That rests with the will: if He wills, He admits him to the Garden without punishment; and if He wills, He punishes him and then admits him to the Garden after a time. All of that rests with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The Muslims who have committed grave sins until they have merited entry into the Fire — when they enter the Fire they are not like the unbelievers in the Fire. The face that has prostrated itself to Allah never enters the Fire. Among them is one whose two feet are in the Fire while his person stands clear of the Fire, and among them one up to his knee, and among them one up to his backbone, and among them one up to his neck; but as for the face that has prostrated itself to Allah, the Fire does not touch it. These are the ones who, once they have been punished — after a day, or after days, or after a year, or after years — will come out of the Fire and enter the Garden. The last of the people of the Fire to come out of the Fire comes out and stands before Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and says: ⟨My Lord, take me to the gate of the Garden, and I shall ask nothing of You but this.⟩ So he makes a covenant with Allah that if he reaches the gate of the Garden that will suffice him, and he gives such covenants and compacts as he gives. Then the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨Bring him near to the Garden.⟩ And when he is at the gate of the Garden and looks upon what the Garden holds of bliss and of the wide-eyed maidens (ḥūr al-ʿīn), he waits a long while and says: ⟨My Lord, admit me to the Garden, though I have no share of it.⟩ So He admits him to the Garden. And he waits a time and says: ⟨My Lord, give me of the bliss of the Garden.⟩ It is said to him: ⟨Did you not give covenants and compacts that you would ask for nothing but what you were given?⟩ He says: ⟨My Lord, let me not be the least of Your servants in portion from You.⟩ Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨Make a wish. Would it content you if I gave you⟩

⟨ten times the measure of the world, in the Garden?⟩ He said: ⟨My Lord, are You mocking me?⟩ At that the Messenger ﷺ laughed. He said: ⟨No — I am able to do all things; I have given you ten times the measure of the world.⟩ This is the least of the people of the Garden in fortune. «And whoever associates partners with Allah has forged a sin» — a sin — «great» (Q. 4:48). «Have you not seen those who»

«hold themselves to be pure» — and they are the Jews. This verse came down concerning Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab and Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf, who praised themselves, saying: We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones. «Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills» — He purifies whom He wills, through faith (īmān) — «and they will not be wronged» — diminished of their deeds — «by so much as a thread» (Q. 4:49) — the measure of the thread of a date-stone. «Look» — marvelling
«how they forge lies against Allah» — by that — «and that suffices as a manifest sin» (Q. 4:50) — plain — «Have you not seen»

«those who were given a portion of the Book, believing in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt» (Q. 4:51). It was revealed concerning Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab; they were the chiefs of the Jews. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina the Illumined they made a covenant with the Messenger ﷺ that they would not make war on him and he would not make war on them, and that if they met with a case that needed help the Muslims would help them and they would help the Muslims, as with blood-money and the like. When the day of Badr came and the Muslims were victorious they said: This is the Prophet who is mentioned in the Torah; and they confirmed their covenant with the Messenger ﷺ. And when the day of Uḥud came in the following year they doubted, and said: After what has befallen the Muslims we do not know whether this is the Prophet who is to come at the end of time or not. So a company of them rode to Mecca and said to Abū Sufyān: Let us make a pact with you to fight Muḥammad ﷺ. He said to them: I do not trust you, because you are People of a Book and he is the possessor of a Book; he is nearer to you than we are. They said: No, he is the most hostile of our enemies, and we will fight him alongside you. Abū Sufyān said to them: I will accept nothing from you unless you prostrate to the idol: al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt.

So they prostrated to al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt, and they were learned men, out of envy of the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims. Abū Sufyān said to them: I set my religion before you and I set the religion of Muḥammad before you, and you are People of a Book, learned men; judge between us and Muḥammad: are we better than he in religion, or is he better than we in religion? We give the pilgrims drink, we feed the guest, we ransom the captive; and Muḥammad has severed kinship, parted from the Sanctuary, and brought a religion at variance with the religion of our fathers. They said: You are more rightly guided in the way than Muḥammad ﷺ; your religion is more rightly guided than the religion of Muḥammad. Allah Exalted said: «Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, believing in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt» (Q. 4:51)
two idols of Quraysh. Learned men who took to prostrating to the idol out of envy, and out of love of this world and nothing else. «and they say to those who»
«disbelieve» — to Abū Sufyān and his companions — «These» — you — «are more rightly guided in the way than those who believe» (Q. 4:51) — you, your religion

is more rightly guided than the religion of the Muslims. «Those are they whom Allah has cursed; and whoever Allah curses, you will never find for him any helper» (Q. 4:52) — any to ward off His punishment — «Or have they a share in the dominion?» — nay, they have nothing of the dominion; the Jews do not attain dominion, because of their envy — «for then they would not give the people a speck» (Q. 4:53) — some paltry thing, the measure of the notch on the back of a date-stone, so excessive is their miserliness. They combined envy and miserliness. «Or» — nay — «do they envy the people» — the Prophet ﷺ — «for what Allah has given them of His bounty» — they envied al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ and the Muslims for the bounty of Allah, which is prophethood and the multitude of wives; and they say: Had he been a prophet he would have been too occupied for women. «for We gave the family of Ibrāhīm» — [Ibrāhīm being] his forefather — such as Mūsā, Dāwūd and Sulaymān — «the Book and wisdom» — prophethood — «and We gave them a mighty dominion» (Q. 4:54). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, bestowed favour upon the family of Ibrāhīm, such as Mūsā, Dāwūd and Sulaymān. Mūsā was king of Egypt and Syria after the destruction of Firʿawn, and he was a prophet; and Dāwūd was a king and a prophet; and Sulaymān was a king who ruled the whole world, and a prophet. The One who gave this — was it not for Him to give Muḥammad ﷺ prophethood and the wives he had? «and We gave them a mighty dominion». Dāwūd had ninety-nine wives, and Sulaymān a thousand, between free women and concubines. In the shariʿa of Mūsā marriage was without limit of number, and for this reason Dāwūd married ninety-nine women, making them up to a hundred. And Sulaymān said: By Allah, I shall go in tonight to a hundred women, every one of them conceiving and bringing forth a horseman who will wage jihad in the way of Allah. And he forgot to say in shāʾa Allah. So he went in to them all, and none conceived but one, and she brought forth half a human being. And Sulaymān had a thousand women: three hundred

free women and seven hundred slave-girls; and the Messenger had only eleven. They envy him for this, while the prophets before him had this number and it did not debar them from their prophethood? This is the envy of the Jews. They combined miserliness and envy. Miserliness is that you withhold your property from another; envy is that you withhold from him the bounty of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The miser withholds his own bounty from another, while the envier, for his part, wants the bounty of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to be withheld from His servant. So Allah withheld dominion from them: they have no share in the dominion, because of their envy. This is why they say: the envious man will never rule. The envious man will never rule — why? Because man has been moulded to hate following another. A man obeys another man only for some cause that makes it preferable for him to be his follower, either provision that comes to him from him, or some bounty. So since Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who is the Fashioner of creation, has made His bounty run upon His creation and has thereby deserved worship from them, the envier who wants to cut off this bounty wants to depose Allah, Blessed and Exalted; because when human beings are certain that nothing comes to them from Allah, they see no reason to obey Him. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave an outward dominion to some people and an inward dominion to some people, and joined the two dominions in some people. The outward dominion is that of one who was a king over this world; and the inward dominion is the dominion of the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) and the ulama, which is inward. And whoever joined the two things, a king outwardly and a walī inwardly, or a prophet, has joined the two dominions. Among the prophets there is one who is a prophet and a king; and among the awliyāʾ there is one who is a walī and a king; and among them there is one who is only a walī

«That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He will, and Allah is the possessor of mighty bounty» (Q. 62:4). «So some of them believed in him» — in Muḥammad ﷺ — «and some of them turned away from him» — turned aside from him and did not believe — «and Hell suffices as a blaze» (Q. 4:55). «Indeed those who disbelieved in Our signs, We shall soon roast them» — We shall make them enter — «in a Fire» — they burn in it — «whenever are roasted»

are burnt — «their skins, We give them in exchange other skins» — by their being restored to their first state, unburnt — «that they may taste the punishment» — that they may suffer its severity — «Indeed Allah is Mighty» — nothing is beyond His power — «Wise» (Q. 4:56) — in His creation.
The unbeliever's frame is enlarged until the span between his shoulders is a distance of seventy years, and his molar is greater

than Mount Uḥud, so that the Fire may have full power to burn him. When they are burnt until they become charcoal, Allah restores them as they were. «other than them» is not [to be taken] in its own meaning; «other than them» means that they are restored to their [former] state, not that they are exchanged for skins other than them, because Allah does not punish a skin that has not disobeyed Him. «And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We shall admit them to gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein forever; they shall have therein purified spouses» — purified of menstruation and of every filth — «and We shall admit them into a deep shade» (Q. 4:57) — lasting; a shade that no sun effaces, which is the shade of the Garden. The Messenger ﷺ says:

⟨Indeed Allah has given His servant in the Garden what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has ever occurred to the heart of any human being. Recite, if you wish:⟩ «So no soul knows what has been hidden away for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward» (Q. 32:17). ⟨And the shade of a single tree — the rider travels in it more than a hundred years and does not reach its end. Recite, if you wish:⟩ «And extended shade, and water»

«poured forth» (Q. 56:30–31). «Indeed Allah commands you to render back the trusts to their owners» (Q. 4:58). This verse (āya) was revealed at the conquest of Mecca, when ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, took the key of the Kaʿba by force from ʿUthmān b. Ṭalḥa al-Ḥajabī, its custodian. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Mecca in the year of the conquest, he had refused him, and said: ⟨Had I known that he is the Messenger of Allah, I would not have refused him⟩, so the Messenger ﷺ ordered that it be given back to him, and said: ⟨Take it — everlasting and inherited⟩. He marvelled at that, and he [the Prophet ﷺ] recited the verse to him, and he accepted Islam. Then, at his death, he gave it to his brother Shayba, and it has remained among his descendants to this day. Although the verse came down on a particular occasion, its generality holds, by the indication of the plural. «Indeed Allah commands you to render back the trusts to their owners» — Allah commands His servants to render the trusts back to their owners — «and when you judge between people, that you judge with justice» — a command to justice — «Indeed Allah — how excellent is that with which He admonishes you» — rendering the trust and judging with justice — «Indeed Allah is Hearing» — of what is said — «Seeing» (Q. 4:58) — of what is done. The trust is of [several] kinds: a kind between the servant and his Lord, a kind between the servant and his nafs (the soul), and a kind between the servant and [other] creatures. The trust between you and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and that you comply with His command and avoid what He has forbidden. The trust between you and your nafs is that you not employ it in what harms it in your hereafter. When the nafs clings to something in which lies its harm, justice is that you employ it in that in which lies its safety in this world and the hereafter. And the trust between you and creatures: the nearest of creatures to you are wives and children, and you must discharge the trust concerning them. The child — you must give him a good name, and teach him the Book of Allah when he reaches the age of discernment, and teach him the religion, then command him to worship Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and when he comes of age, you marry him. And everyone who entrusts you with something — that you not betray him in his trust. «O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you» — the governors from among you; some say the commanders, and some say the ulama
«And if you dispute» — differ — «in anything, refer it to Allah» — to His Book — «and the Messenger» — during his lifetime, and after him

to his sunna — «if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. That» — the referring [of the matter] to them both — «is better» — for you than disputing and speaking by [mere] opinion — «and fairer in interpretation» (Q. 4:59) — in outcome. «Have you not seen those who claim» (Q. 4:60). The occasion of this verse's revelation: a Jew and a hypocrite fell into dispute. The hypocrite summoned [him] to Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf, that he might judge between them, and the Jew summoned [him] to the Prophet ﷺ. The two of them came to him, and he gave judgement for the Jew. The hypocrite was not satisfied, and the two of them went to ʿUmar. The Jew mentioned that to him, and he said to the hypocrite: ⟨Is it so?⟩ He said: Yes. So ʿUmar killed him. «Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you? They desire to seek judgement before the ṭāghūt»

the one of much insolence; he is Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf — «though they have been commanded to reject him» — and not to take him as an ally — «And Satan desires to lead them far astray» (Q. 4:60) — far from the truth — «And when it is said to them, Come to what Allah has sent down» — in the Qurʾan

of judgement — «and to the Messenger» — that he may judge between you — «you see the hypocrites turning aside» — turning away — «from you, utterly» (Q. 4:61). «So how, when an affliction befalls them» — a punishment — «for what their hands have sent ahead» — of unbelief and acts of disobedience. Are they able to turn away and flee from it? No. «then they come to you» — joined in construction to ‘they turn aside’ — «swearing by Allah, We intended nothing» — by their seeking judgement before someone other than you — «but kindness» — reconciliation — «and conciliation» (Q. 4:62) — a bringing together of the two adversaries by drawing them near in the judgement — «Those are they of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts» — of hypocrisy, and their lying in their excuse — «so turn away from them» — with forbearance — «and admonish them» — make them fear Allah — «and say to them, concerning themselves» — in the matter of their own selves
«a telling word» (Q. 4:63) — one that works upon them; that is, rebuke them that they may turn back from their unbelief. «And We sent no messenger but that he be obeyed»

— in what he commands and judges — «by Allah's permission» — by His command — «And if only they, when they wronged themselves» — by their seeking judgement before the ṭāghūt — «had come to you» — repentant — «and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them» — in it there is a shift of address (iltifāt) — «they would have found Allah ever relenting» — towards them — «Merciful» (Q. 4:64) — to them. «But no — by your Lord — they will not believe» — an oath — «until they make you judge in what has become tangled among them». The Muslim is not a Muslim unless he makes the shariʿa judge in what has passed between him and people. «then they find in themselves no constraint at what you have decided, and they submit in full submission» (Q. 4:65). This is the mark of Islam. ⟨None of you believes until his desire follows what I have brought⟩. A person complies with the commands of the Qurʾan, and complies with the sunna of the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨A time will come upon people when kingship is not set right save by killing and tyranny, and love is not to be found save by following people's desire, and wealth is not to be found with the rich save when the servant abases himself before them. The kings are arrogant, and the rich are miserly and tyrannical, and people love none but him who follows their desire. So whoever lives to see that time and is patient in poverty while he is able to have wealth, and is patient under abasement while he is able to have honour, and is patient under hatred while he is able to have love — for had he gone along with them in⟩

⟨their desire alone, they would have loved him — Allah will settle him in the enclosure of holiness on the Day of Resurrection⟩. ⟨Whoever revives my sunna shall have the reward of a hundred martyrs⟩. They said to the Messenger ﷺ: One who holds to the religion in that time — how

is his state? He said: ⟨His state is like one who grasps a live coal⟩. If he sets the coal down it goes out, and if he holds it, it burns him. And all this is the interpretation (taʾwīl) of this verse: «They will not believe until they make you judge in what has become tangled among them, then they find in themselves no constraint at what you have decided, and they submit in full submission» (Q. 4:65). The Book that Allah has sent down to us is this Qurʾan. He said: «Follow»

«what has been sent down to you» (Q. 7:3). Following it is nothing but complying with its command alone and avoiding what it forbids. And the Messenger ﷺ: «Follow him, that you may be guided» (Q. 7:158). The Messenger is the one who makes the Qurʾan plain, and this is his speech. Are we to leave this Qurʾan that was sent down upon him and take the doctrine of someone other than him? We have not understood following to mean this. «And had We prescribed for them, Kill yourselves, or go out from your dwellings» — as We prescribed for the Children of Isrāʾīl — «they would not have done it» — what was prescribed for them — «save a few». Had Allah made it obligatory upon this community that they kill themselves, they would have refused. ʿUmar said: ⟨Command me, O Messenger of Allah, and I will kill myself now⟩. Allah said: «save a few» — such as ʿUmar — «of them. And had they done what they are admonished to do» — of obedience to the Messenger — «it would have been better for them, and a firmer strengthening» (Q. 4:66) — a confirming of their faith — «And then»

— had they stood firm — «We would have given them from Us» — from Our presence — «a great reward, and We would have guided them to a straight path» (Q. 4:67–68). Some of the Companions said to the Prophet ﷺ: How shall we see you in the Garden, when you are in the highest degrees and we are

below you! So there came down: «And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger» — in what He has commanded — «those are with those whom Allah has favoured, of the prophets, the veracious, the martyrs and the righteous». And the Messenger ﷺ said:

⟨A man is with the one he loves⟩. Anas said: ⟨I have found no joy in Islam like my joy at the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:⟩ ⟨A man is with the one he loves⟩. «and how good are those as companions» (Q. 4:69) — companions in the Garden — «That»
«is the bounty from Allah, and Allah suffices as one who knows» (Q. 4:70). «O you who believe, take your precaution» — against your enemy — «and go forth»
go forth — «in companies» — in separate parties — «or march forth all together» (Q. 4:71) — gathered together — «And indeed among you there is he who tarries» — who would surely lag behind
from the fighting — «Then if a misfortune befalls you» — such as a killing or a defeat — «he says: Allah has favoured me, since I was not with them»
«a witness» (Q. 4:72) — present — «And if a bounty from Allah befalls you» — such as a conquest or spoils — «he will surely say» — in regret — «as though»
«there had been no affection between you and him» — acquaintance and friendship. He says: «Would that I had been with them, that I might attain a great attainment»

(Q. 4:73) — taking an abundant share of the spoils. Allah Exalted said: «So let those fight in the way of Allah» — to exalt His religion — «who sell the life of this world for the hereafter. And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed» — he attains martyrdom — «or conquers» — he prevails over his enemy — «then We shall give him a great reward» (Q. 4:74) — abundant — «And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight» — a rebuke — «in the way of Allah, and» — in the deliverance of — «the oppressed among the men and the women and the children» — those whom the unbelievers kept back from the emigration and harmed. Ibn ʿAbbās said: ⟨I and my mother were among them⟩. «who say» — supplicating — «Our Lord» — O our Lord —
«bring us out of this town» — Mecca — «whose people are wrongdoers» — through unbelief — «and appoint for us from Thee» — from
