Thy presence — «a protector» — who will take charge of our affairs — «and appoint for us from Thee a helper» (Q. 4:75) — who will defend us against them. And Allah answered their supplication, so He made the going out easy for some of them, and some of them remained until Mecca was conquered, and he ﷺ appointed ʿAttāb b. Asīd [over them], and he gave the wronged among them their due against the one who wronged them. «Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of the ṭāghūt» — Satan — «so fight the allies of Satan» — the helpers of his religion; you will overcome them, because your strength is through Allah — «Indeed the guile of Satan» — against the believers — «is ever weak» (Q. 4:76) — flimsy — «Have you not seen those to whom it was said: Restrain your hands» — from fighting the unbelievers, when they sought it at Mecca — «and establish the prayer and pay the zakat? Then when fighting was prescribed for them, lo, a party of them fear people» — the unbelievers — «as they fear Allah, or with a greater fear»

than their fear of Him. «And they said: Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had granted us respite» — why did You not grant us respite — «to a term close at hand. Say: the enjoyment of this world is little, and the hereafter is better for him who guards against» — the punishment of Allah — «and you shall not be wronged by so much as a thread» (Q. 4:77) — the measure of the husk of a date-stone — «Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even though you be in fortified towers» — raised high — «And if there befalls them» — the Jews — «a good thing» — fertility and plenty — «they say: this is from Allah; and if there befalls them an evil thing»

— drought and affliction — «they say: this is from you» — O Muḥammad, through your ill omen — «Say» — to them — «all» — of the good and the evil — «is from Allah. What ails these people that they scarcely comprehend» — they do not come near to understanding — «a word» (Q. 4:78). «Whatever befalls you» — O man — «of a good thing» — good — «is from Allah; and whatever befalls you of an evil thing» — an affliction — «is from yourself. And We have sent you» — O Muḥammad — «to mankind as a messenger, and Allah suffices as a witness» (Q. 4:79) — to your message — «Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you over them as a keeper» (Q. 4:80) — a keeper of their deeds; rather, a warner — «And they say» — the hypocrites, when they come to you: our affair is — «obedience» — to you — «but when they go forth» — go out — «from you, a party of them plots by night» — that is, harbours inwardly — «other than what you say» — to you in your presence, of professions of obedience, that is, disobedience to you — «and Allah writes down» — He commands the recording of — «what they plot by night» — in their scrolls, that they may be requited for it — «So turn away from them» — with forbearance — «and trust in Allah» — rely on Him, for He suffices you — «and Allah suffices as a guardian» (Q. 4:81) — one to whom affairs are committed — «Do they not then ponder» — reflect upon — «the Qurʾan» — and the meanings it contains — «Had it been from any other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy» (Q. 4:82) — contradiction in its meanings and disparity in its composition — «And when there comes to them a matter» — concerning the raiding parties — «of security» — by victory — «or of fear» — by defeat — «they spread it about» — they publish it abroad — «Had they referred it» — that is, the report — «to the Messenger and to those in authority among them» — the men of judgement, such as the chief Companions — «those who seek to elicit it would have known it» — who trace it out — «among them. And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you» — through Islam — «and His mercy» — to you, through the Qurʾan — «you would have followed Satan» — in what he commands you of indecencies — «save a few» (Q. 4:83). «So fight» — O Muḥammad — «in the way of Allah; you are not charged save with yourself» — so do not be troubled by their holding back — «and urge on the believers» — spur them on to fight

and rouse their desire for it — «It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve» — that is, the war of those who disbelieve — «and Allah is stronger in might» — than they — «and more severe in punishment» (Q. 4:84) — in chastisement than they — «Whoever intercedes with a good intercession» — one in accord with the shariʿa — «shall have a share» — of the reward — «of it» — by reason of it — «and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession» — one at variance with it — «shall have a portion» — a share of the burden of sin — «of it» — by reason of it — «and Allah is ever Keeper over all things» (Q. 4:85) —

all-powerful — «And when you are greeted with a greeting» — as when it is said to you: peace be upon you — «then greet» — the one who greeted — «with better than it» — that you say to him: upon you be peace, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings — «or return it» — that you say to him as he said: and upon you — «Indeed Allah is ever Reckoner over all things» (Q. 4:86) — one who takes account, and so He requites for it; and among these is the returning of the greeting of peace. The sunna has singled out the unbeliever, the innovator, the profligate, and one who gives the greeting to a man relieving himself or to one who is in the bath-house: it is not obligatory to return the greeting to them; rather it is disliked in cases other than the last, and to the unbeliever one says: and upon you. O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.

«Allah, there is no god but He. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection; there is no doubt of it». «Allah» — a proper name for the Divine Majesty — «there is no god but He» — and by Allah, He will surely gather you from your graves to the Day of Resurrection — «there is no doubt of it» (Q. 4:87) — there is no uncertainty in it. He, Blessed and Exalted, has sworn that He must gather us on the Day of Resurrection and then divide us: a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze. «And on the Day the Hour comes, on that Day they will be divided» (Q. 30:14), and a party in a seat of truth with an Omnipotent Sovereign. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has multiplied the mention of Himself in order to call the servant to abundant remembrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So there must be remembrance of Allah with the tongue first, then remembrance with the heart, then remembrance with the spirit; and at that point His being engulfs the being of all that is other than He, and the servant passes away and being passes away, and the true tawḥīd (the divine oneness) and the everlasting life are attained. «He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection» (Q. 4:87). The Resurrection is of three ranks: lesser, middle and greater. The lesser is the death of a man — whoever dies, his resurrection has come upon him. The middle is the death of all creatures at the first blast. The greater is the raising of the creatures and their gathering to the Day of Resurrection at the second blast. He has sworn that He must gather the creatures, and when He gathers them He must divide them: a party in the Garden, a party in the Blaze, and a party in a seat of truth with an Omnipotent Sovereign. «And who is more truthful than Allah in speech» (Q. 4:87) — in word. This is a report that has come to us from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and no one is more truthful than He

in speech. Every reporter — doubt finds its way into his report, whether it is true or a lie — except He, Blessed and Exalted: no doubt finds its way into His report; rather it is true. For that reason He mentioned that He is the most truthful of speakers. And so it has come in the hadith that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ⟨The son of Ādam has called Me a liar, and it is not for him to call Me a liar; and he has reviled Me, and it is not for him to revile Me. As for his calling Me a liar, it is his saying, 'He will not bring me back after death' — and I originated him, and the bringing back is easier than the originating. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has taken a son' — and I am the One, the Unique, the Eternally Self-Sufficient; I have not begotten, nor was I begotten, and there is none equal to Me.⟩. «What is the matter with you, that you are two parties concerning the hypocrites?» (Q. 4:88). When the people came back from Uḥud and purposed to join the unbelievers, the people differed about them: one party said, we shall kill them; and another party said, no. Some of them said, they are unbelievers; and some of them said, they are not unbelievers. «What is the matter with you» — what is your affair, that you have become — «concerning the hypocrites, two parties» — two factions — «while Allah has thrown them back» — He turned them back — «by what they earned» (Q. 4:88) — of unbelief (kufr) and acts of disobedience. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, decreed upon them that they should turn back from the jihad and join the unbelievers, because of their earning unbelief and disobedience. «Do you wish to guide him whom Allah has led astray?» — that is, to count them among the guided — «And whomever Allah leads astray, you will never find for him a way» (Q. 4:88) — a road to guidance. «They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved» — they disbelieved and wished for your unbelief — «so that you would be» — you and they — «alike» — in unbelief — «so do not take allies from among them» — whom you befriend — even if they make a show of faith — «until they emigrate in the way of Allah» (Q. 4:89) — a sound emigration that makes their faith real. Emigration was a condition of faith at the beginning of Islam, so whoever claimed faith and did not emigrate after the emigration of the Messenger ﷺ was a liar, until it was abrogated at the conquest of Mecca by his saying ﷺ: ⟨There is no emigration after⟩

⟨the conquest⟩. The hypocrites — the Muslims differed about them: some of them said that they are unbelievers, and some of them say that they are Muslims. «And Allah has thrown them back by what they earned» (Q. 4:88). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who turned them back to unbelief. So the deed was in reality from Allah, Blessed and Exalted — since He is the creator of the servant and of his acts — and figuratively from the servant. From here the two factions parted: the Jabriyya and the Qadariyya. The Jabriyya say: the servant has no act at all; all acts are the acts of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and so there is no sin upon the servant and nothing at all, because he has no deed. And they went astray because they did away with the obligations of the Law. The Qadariyya said: the servant is the creator of his own acts, the servant is able to create his acts, and so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has no entry into the acts of the servant. So they fell into unbelief by ascribing the act to other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The people of the Sunna took hold of a lesser compulsion: they say that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave us power over acquisition, so the acquisition is ours and Allah creates the deed at the moment of acquisition. And the recognizers joined together the two creeds of the two errant factions, and so were guided to the evenness of the path (ṣirāṭ). In reality they see the act as belonging to none but Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and this is not the doctrine of the Jabriyya in their view, but rather, by witnessing and plain sight, there is no agent in existence save Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And even so, outwardly they take upon themselves righteous deeds and avoid evil deeds as though they were the creators of their own deeds. So they brought out a result lying between the two traits: from between dung and blood they brought out pure milk, and that is the straight path. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has ascribed the act sometimes to Himself and sometimes to another. «Say: the angel of death, who has been charged with you, will take you» (Q. 32:11),

«Allah takes the souls at the time of their death» (Q. 39:42). The causing of death is in reality from Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and since He commanded the angel to carry out this command and the angel performed it, the angel was the one who took [the soul], while the one who takes it in reality is Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

And the servant too: when Allah created him and manifested Himself in him, He placed in him strength, intellect, knowledge and discernment, by which he is able to acquire a righteous deed and to avoid by it an evil deed; and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who carries out the creating [of the act]. This is the straight path. Whoever says that the act belongs to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has spoken truly; and whoever attributes the act to its doer figuratively — the Qurʾan has spoken with the like of this. «Do you wish to guide him whom Allah has led astray?» (Q. 4:88). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the One who led astray whoever went astray. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Allah sent Satan as one who makes [falsehood] alluring, and nothing of the leading astray is in his hands; and He sent me as a caller to guidance, and nothing of the guidance is in my hands.⟩ «They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved» (Q. 4:89). Whoever wishes that someone be an unbeliever is as though he were an unbeliever himself, because he has loved unbelief, even if for any person at all. «so that you would be alike. So do not take allies from among them» — befriending them — «until they emigrate in the way of Allah» (Q. 4:89). «But if they turn away» — and persist in what they are upon — «then seize them» — by capture — «and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them any ally» — whom you befriend — «nor any helper» (Q. 4:89) — by whom you gain victory over your enemy. «Except those who join themselves» — who take refuge — «to a people between whom and you there is a covenant» — a pact of security for them, as the Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with Hilāl b. ʿUwaymir al-Aslamī — «or those who come to you» — and — «have shrunk» — have become narrow — «their breasts» — from — «fighting you» — along with their people — «or fighting their own people» (Q. 4:90) — along with you — that is, holding back from fighting you and from fighting them. So do not approach them with capture or killing; and this and what comes after it is abrogated by the verse of the sword
«And if Allah had willed» — their being given power over you — «He would have given them power over you» — by strengthening their hearts — «and they would have fought you»

but He did not will it, and so He cast terror into their hearts. «So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace» — reconciliation; they have yielded — «then Allah has given you no way against them» (Q. 4:90) — a road, by capture and killing. «You will find others wishing to be secure from you» — by showing faith in your presence — «and to be secure from their own people» — by unbelief, when they return to them; and they are Asad and Ghaṭafān — «every time they are returned to temptation» — whenever they are called to shirk (associating partners with Allah) — «they fall back into it»

they fall in with the severest falling. «So if they do not withdraw from you» — by leaving off fighting you — «and offer you peace» — and do not offer you peace — «and restrain» — and do not restrain — «their hands» — from you — «then seize them» — by capture — «and kill them wherever you overtake them» — wherever you find them — «and those — We have given you against them a clear warrant» (Q. 4:91) — a clear and manifest proof for killing them and taking them captive, because of their treachery. «It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake» (Q. 4:92). The occasion of the revelation of this verse (āya) is that ʿAyyāsh b. Abī Rabīʿa, the brother of Abū Jahl by his mother, became a Muslim; and when he became a Muslim his mother said that she would not take shelter in any shade, nor eat, nor drink, until he turned back from Islam. So Abū Jahl travelled out with al-Ḥārith, a companion of his, and the two came to ʿAyyāsh and said to him: we have agreed with you about your Islam, but the Messenger ﷺ commands the keeping of the ties of kinship; so since the Messenger commands the keeping of the ties of kinship, come with us and keep the tie of kinship with your mother, and we will leave you upon your religion. And he accepted that. Then when they had taken him away, they seized him and bound his arms behind him, and Abū Jahl struck him a hundred lashes, and his companion struck him a hundred lashes likewise. So he said to al-Ḥārith: ⟨This one is my brother, my mother's son; he has struck me. But you — why do you strike me a hundred lashes? By Allah, I shall not meet you alone without killing you.⟩ After that al-Ḥārith went to Medina and entered Islam, and ʿAyyāsh returned and met him on the road alone and did not know of his becoming a Muslim, so he set upon him with the sword and killed him. Then he came to the Messenger ﷺ and said to him: ⟨I killed him before I knew of his becoming a Muslim, and after that it became clear to me⟩

⟨that he had become a Muslim⟩. He, Exalted, said: «It is not for a believer to kill a believer» — it is not fitting that a killing of him should issue from him — «except by mistake» — being mistaken in his killing of him. «And whoever kills a believer by mistake» — as happened with ʿAyyāsh — «then the freeing of a slave» — the manumission of a slave — «who is a believer, and a blood-money delivered» — paid over — «to his family» — and the blood-money (diya) is what is paid to the heirs of the slain — «unless they remit it as alms» (Q. 4:92)

unless they give it to him as a charitable gift, by pardoning it. And the sunna has made clear that the blood-money is a hundred camels: twenty she-camels in their second year (bint makhāḍ), twenty she-camels in their third year (bint labūn), twenty male camels in their third year (banū labūn), twenty she-camels in their fourth year (ḥiqqa) and twenty she-camels in their fifth year (jadhaʿa); and that it falls upon the killer's kin-group liable for blood-money (ʿāqila) over three years. «But if he be» — the slain one — «of a people at enmity with you, and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave» — upon his killer, as an expiation, and there is no blood-money. «And if he be» — the slain one — «of a people between whom and you there is a covenant» — a pact, like the protected peoples (ahl al-dhimma) — «then a blood-money delivered to his family» — and it is a third of the blood-money of a believer if he was a Jew or a Christian, and two-thirds of a tenth of it if he was a Magian — «and the freeing of a believing slave» — upon his killer. «And whoever does not find» — the slave, in that he lacks one and lacks what he might obtain one with — «then a fast of two consecutive months» — upon him, as an expiation. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not mention the move to feeding [the poor], as in the oath of repudiation (ẓihār); and al-Shāfiʿī held this in the sounder of his two positions. «as a relenting from Allah; and Allah is Knowing» — of His creation — «Wise» (Q. 4:92) — in what He has ordained. So whoever kills by mistake must free a slave, and if he does not find one, then a fast of two consecutive months. And likewise the real expiation, which is
that the servant set his own soul free from whatever

is other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and failing that, he keeps to abandoning food and drink and renounces this world and its desires, until he finds a purification from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his requital is Hell» (Q. 4:93). This verse was sent down concerning Miqyas b. Ṣubāba. Miqyas accepted Islam and was with the Prophet ﷺ, and his brother was with him, and he was killed

or something of that sort. This alerts you to the greatness of knowledge. Two words only, and Jibrīl travelled on their account a distance of two thousand years. Between us and the lowest heaven is a distance of five hundred years, and the heaven, its thickness is a distance of five hundred years, and the Qurʾan had been in the lowest heaven ever since it was sent down on the Night of Power. So he went a distance of a thousand and returned a distance of a thousand for two words only, which are «other than those possessed of injury». For this reason, when al-Rashīd asked Imam Mālik to teach him — to relate the hadith to him — while he was a king seated upon his couch, Mālik said to him: ⟨Knowledge is come to; it does not come. You must come yourself.⟩ Then when he came to him and the chair was set up for him, Mālik said to him: ⟨You must sit upon the ground in humility before I teach you.⟩ So he did, and he taught him. «Allah has given precedence to those who struggle with their wealth and their selves over those who sit at home» — on account of an injury — «by a degree» — an excellence, since the two are equal in intention and those who struggle have the increase of direct engagement — «and to each Allah has promised the best» (Q. 4:95) — the Garden. When He said «Those who sit at home among the believers, other than those possessed of injury, and those who struggle are not equal», those who sat at home supposed that they had no reward at all, and for this reason He said «and to each» — of the two groups,
those who sit at home
«Allah has promised the best» — the Garden — «and Allah has given precedence to those who struggle over those who sit at home» — [those sitting] for no injury — «by a reward»

«great» (Q. 4:95). «degrees from Him» — stations, some of them above others, of honour. The degrees of the one who struggles will be mentioned in Sūrat al-Tawba, in shāʾa Allah. «and forgiveness and mercy; and Allah is ever forgiving» — to His awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) — «merciful» (Q. 4:96) — to them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Yaḥyā said to his people: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded him to believe in Allah alone and that he associate nothing with Him, and commanded him to establish the prayer, and commanded him to fast, and commanded him to give alms, and commanded him to remember Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said to him: the likeness of one who associates partners with Allah is as a man who bought a slave and handed him money to trade with and to live from and to give the profit to his master; and the slave took to doing this work with the money and giving it to his master’s enemy and leaving his master. This is the likeness of associating partners with Allah. And when you are occupied with the prayer, do not turn aside to anything else. The likeness of one who turns aside in the prayer is as a man whom a mighty king has honoured and has brought before him to speak with him intimately, and he took to turning aside to another. And He commanded him to fast, and said to him: the likeness of fasting is a man who has an enemy, so he took a coat of mail and took a sword and weapons to fortify himself against his enemy — fasting is a shield. And the likeness of alms is as a man whose enemies took him captive and he bought himself from them with his wealth. And the likeness of one who remembers Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is as a man who fled from his enemies and entered an impregnable fortress, fortifying himself in it against his enemies. This is the likeness of one who remembers Allah, Blessed and Exalted.⟩ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨I command you with five: hold to hearing and obedience, and emigration, and jihad, and holding fast to the community.⟩ «Indeed those whom the angels take in death, wronging themselves» — by remaining with the unbelievers and abandoning emigration. Emigration was a condition in Islam at the beginning of Islam. «They say, ‘In what [state] were you?’ They say, ‘We were oppressed in the land.’ They say» — the angels, to them, in rebuke — «Was not Allah’s earth wide, so that you might emigrate in it?» — from the land of unbelief (kufr) to another country, as others besides you did. He, Exalted, said: «Those — their refuge is»

«Hell, and an evil destination it is» (Q. 4:97). Whoever abandoned emigration, He promised him Hell. «Except the oppressed among the men and the women and the children» — Ibn ʿAbbās said: ⟨I and my mother were among them.⟩ «who are unable to contrive a means» — they have no power for the emigration nor for the expense — «nor are they guided to a way» (Q. 4:98) — a road to the land of emigration — «Those — it may be that Allah will pardon them» — He gave them no definitive assurance of the pardon; rather ‘it may be’: they hope that Allah will pardon them — «and Allah is ever pardoning, forgiving» (Q. 4:99). «And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find a refuge» — a place of emigration — «abundant, and ampleness» (Q. 4:100) — in provision. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has promised everyone who emigrates that He will give him a spacious place and provide for him wherever he is. If we say that the emigration came to an end with the conquest of Mecca, that is because of its being a condition in the servant’s submission (islām) and his faith (īmān), and the emigration never comes to an end. There enters into the emigration from the place of unbelief to the abode of Islam: the emigration from innovation to the sunna, and the emigration from ignorance to knowledge, and the emigration from a place in which Islam is weak to a place in which Islam is strong,

everyone who moves from one land to another land for the good of his religion is an emigrant, until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: ⟨Emigrate, and you will bequeath to your sons glory.⟩
«And whoever goes out from his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger» (Q. 4:100). This verse was sent down concerning Jundub b. Ḍamra
al-Laythī

al-Laythī was a very old man, and he resolved upon the emigration, so he charged his slaves to carry him, and they carried him from Mecca to Medina, and he died on the road. The unbelievers used to gloat over him, saying: he fled from us and did not reach the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — he has lost twice over. And the Companions were saying: would that he had arrived, so that he might attain the reward of the emigration. So there was sent down: «And whoever goes out from his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him» — on the road — «it has indeed come to pass» — it is established — «that his reward is upon Allah; and Allah is ever forgiving, merciful» (Q. 4:100). The Muslims rejoiced at that, and so the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ⟨When the son of Ādam dies his work is cut off…⟩, is not to be taken absolutely. ⟨When a man dies his work is cut off except from three: an ongoing alms, and a righteous child who supplicates for him, and knowledge he has disseminated in the hearts of men.⟩ That is, whoever dies and leaves behind wealth: the wealth is the ongoing alms (ṣadaqa), and the child of the loins

is the righteous child who supplicates for his parents, and the child of the spirit is the knowledge he has disseminated in the hearts of men. And it is soundly established that whoever dies while he is reciting the Qurʾan and has not memorized it, Allah charges an angel to complete the memorization of the Qurʾan for him. So on this reckoning, the cutting off of the work at death is only for one who has no intention; as for one who was in a work in which he intended to continue, and death cut it off, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, completes it for him. The Qurʾan is an outward Qurʾan and an inward Qurʾan; the outward Qurʾan

is this one that we recite. If a man occupies himself with the recitation of the Qurʾan and dies before he has memorised the Qurʾan, our Master commands an angel to complete the memorisation of the Qurʾan for him, and so he is raised on the Day of Resurrection having memorised it, a bearer of the Book of Allah. So every righteous deed is included in the Qurʾan: whoever resolves upon jihad and dies without completing it, and whoever goes out for the hijra and does not arrive, and whoever goes out in search of knowledge — all of this Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will complete for him, and he is raised on the Day of Resurrection complete. His bounty is vast. «And when you strike out» — you travel — «in the land, there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer» — by bringing it back from four to two — «if you fear that they may harry you» — that they inflict something hateful upon you — «those who»

«have disbelieved» (Q. 4:101). [The condition] has no converse implication. The sunna has made clear that what is meant by the long journey is four burud (post-stages), which are two stages, even without fear. They shortened [the prayer] with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when they were as secure as they had ever been — that is, in great security. The verse came down only in a case of fear; the shortening was prescribed together with the fear at one and the same time, but when the fear is lifted it does not bar the shortening. «Indeed the unbelievers are to you a manifest enemy» (Q. 4:101) — plain in their enmity. «And when you are» — O Muḥammad, present — «among them» — and you are in fear — «and you lead them in the prayer, let a party of them stand with you» — and let another party hold back — «and let them take» — the party that stood with you — «their weapons» — with them — «then when they have prostrated» — prayed — «let them be» — the other party — «behind you» — standing guard until you have finished the prayer, and then this party goes and stands guard — «and let another party come that has not prayed, and let them pray with you, and let them take»

«their precaution and their weapons» (Q. 4:102) — with them, until you have finished the prayer. And he ﷺ did just that at Baṭn Nakhl; the two Shaykhs relate it. «Those who disbelieve wish that you would be heedless» — the cause of this is that the unbelievers wished, that is, longed, that you would be heedless when you stood for the prayer — «of your weapons and your baggage, so that they might fall upon you all at once» — by charging upon you and seizing you — «And there is no blame upon you, if there is harm upon you from rain or you are sick, that you lay down your weapons» — so do not carry them — «and take your precaution. Indeed Allah has prepared for the unbelievers a humiliating punishment» (Q. 4:102) — one carrying humiliation (ihāna). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on the raid of Banū Anmār. When Allah routed the enemies of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out alone and crossed the valley, and the sky was sprinkling a light rain, until he came to be far from his Companions. He sat down beneath a tree to relieve himself. Ghawrath, one of the unbelievers of Banū Anmār, looked at him and said: this is the Messenger, alone, withdrawn from his Companions; may Allah kill me if I do not kill him today. So he took his sword and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and drew his sword bare, and said: who will protect you from me, O Muḥammad? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Allah.⟩ He drew the sword, and fright and trembling seized him, and he fell, and his sword with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the sword and said to him:

⟨And you — who will protect you from me?⟩ He said: no one. He said: ⟨Say: lā ilāha illā Llāh, Muḥammad rasūl Allah.⟩ He said: I will not say it, but I will never make war on you, and I will not be with anyone who makes war on you. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the sword to the man and said to him: ⟨Go.⟩ He said: by Allah, you are better than I am. He said: ⟨I am more worthy of that.⟩ Then he went to

prayers in the day and night. He said: ⟨They are, O Muḥammad, five prayers in the day and night, and whoever brings a good deed shall have ten the like of it, so those are fifty prayers. The word is not changed with Me.⟩ Since the original obligation of the prayer was fifty prayers, and the unbelievers refused the prayer, He appointed for them on the Day of Resurrection fifty thousand years, each prayer a thousand years. For this the Resurrection is long upon them, and it became a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, because they left the prayer, fifty prayers every day, so each prayer a thousand years. He made them few, so they are five, and He set their times, because man is by nature given to putting things off. Had He not set the times of the prayers for us — pray the dawn prayer, the noon prayer, the afternoon prayer, the sunset prayer, the night prayer — those given to putting off would not have prayed the dawn prayer down to this time of ours; they would put it off. But He Himself set the time, so that you should not put it off, and He made the time wide as well, so that it should not be compulsion. You pray by your own choice; the time is wide. The one under obligation is able to perform the prayer by his own choice, and it is not by coercion. And He commanded a crier to call to the prayer; you hear the muezzin always, calling at every time to the prayer. He commanded the establishing of the prayer, «Establish the prayer» (Q. 2:43), and its performance in congregation, «and bow with those who bow» (Q. 2:43), and its performance in its time, «Indeed the prayer is for the believers a prescription at appointed times» (Q. 4:103), and He commanded humility in it, «those who are humble in their prayer» (Q. 23:2). Among them is he who has kept to this number, since Allah made fifty prayers obligatory: they impose upon themselves fifty cycles of the prayer (rakʿas) every day and night. The five prayers are seventeen cycles, and with the shafʿ (the even pair)

and the witr (the odd) — that is twenty. Whoever keeps to the two cycles of the dawn and the two cycles of the forenoon, and four before the noon prayer and four after the noon prayer and four before the afternoon prayer, and two after the sunset prayer and two before the night prayer, and ten cycles before the shafʿ and the witr — these are fifty prayers. Among the servants of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is he whom Allah has strengthened until he was in prayer continually. Among them is he who has found the perpetuity of the prayer; they are in prayer continually, «those who are constant in their prayer» (Q. 70:23), beyond «they guard their prayer» (Q. 70:34). Guarding these five is not perpetuity in the prayer. Among the servants of Allah there is he who has the perpetuity of the prayer, in prayer continually; and that is by the intention. A man intends that he is one who prays continually, and so he is one who prays continually. ⟨The intention of the believer is better than his deed, and the intention of the unbeliever is worse than his deed.⟩!
Those who have been granted the perpetuity of the prayer are those who performed this prayer until they reached the true nearness

«and prostrate yourself and draw near» (Q. 96:19), until they passed away from existence, and passed away from themselves, from existence and from the existence of existence, so that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, remains. They are there in prayer continually, in a single prostration; they do not raise their heads until the Hour comes. «Indeed the prayer is for the believers a prescription at appointed times» (Q. 4:103) — at the five times — or a prescription appointed over them: they are in the time of the prayer continually. «And do not flag in the pursuit of the people» (Q. 4:104). When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out a party in pursuit of Abū Sufyān and his companions when they had returned from Uḥud, they complained of their wounds — when Abū Sufyān said: our appointment is tomorrow at Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad, and he turned coward and said: next year, at Badr al-Ṣughrā. Some of the Companions pleaded excuses, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨By Allah, I shall go out to them even if I am alone, and none shall go out with me but one who was present at yesterday's battle.⟩ So they went out, complaining
of their wounds. And so there came down concerning them, «And do not flag» — do not grow weak — «in the pursuit of the people» (Q. 4:104) — in seeking out the people, the unbelievers
so that you may fight them. «If you are suffering pain» — you find the pain of the wounds — «then they too are suffering pain» — they find it — «just as you suffer pain»

like you, so do not be cowardly about fighting them. «And you hope» — you — «from Allah» — of victory and of the reward for it — «for what they do not hope» You exceed them in hope, and they have no hope at all; and they were patient, so you are the more entitled to steadfast patience (ṣabr). «And Allah is ever Knowing» — of everything — «Wise» (Q. 4:104) — in what He does. «Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth» (Q. 4:105). It came down concerning Ṭuʿma b. Ubayriq, a man of the Anṣār who used to display faith while in reality he was a hypocrite. He stole a coat of mail belonging to his neighbour and hid it with a Jew. The coat of mail had been stored in a place in which there was some wheat flour, and when he stole the coat of mail the wheat flour kept dropping along his path until he deposited it with a Jew. When the owner of the coat of mail demanded his coat, he saw the dropping of the flour until it reached the house of the Jew, so he asked him about the coat, and he said to him that Ṭuʿma b. Ubayriq had deposited it with him. And he summoned Ṭuʿma, and [Ṭuʿma] gathered a group of his own people, hypocrites like himself, and they swore by Allah that the Jew was the one who stole the coat of mail and that Ṭuʿma had not stolen it. So they came to the Messenger ﷺ, and he swore and his witnesses swore; and the Messenger ﷺ saw nothing but a Muslim claiming his own innocence, with Muslim witnesses swearing for him in whom he saw no suspicion at all, so his heart inclined to [the view] that the right was with him, and he wished to judge in his favour against the Jew. So there came down «Indeed We have sent down to you the Book» — the Qurʾan — «with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you» — by what He has taught you — «and do not be for the treacherous» — like Ṭuʿma — «a contender» (Q. 4:105) — contending on their behalf — «And ask forgiveness of Allah» — for what you had intended — «indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful» (Q. 4:106). The ulama differed over whether the Messenger ﷺ has independent legal reasoning (ijtihād) or whether it is not for him to reason independently, for he does not speak out of caprice: «It is nothing»

«but a revelation revealed» (Q. 53:4). Some of them said that he has no share in independent reasoning, and some of them affirmed that it is for him to reason independently ﷺ, but that when he reasons — after the verse — his reasoning is revelation. «that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you» Allah granted him that what Allah shows him is that which Allah has commanded. So his reasoning is revelation. «And do not be for the treacherous a contender» (Q. 4:105) — like Ṭuʿma — «And ask forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful» (Q. 4:106).

«And do not argue on behalf of those who act treacherously against themselves» — they betray them by acts of disobedience, because the evil consequence of their treachery is upon them — «Indeed Allah does not love one who is treacherous» — much given to treachery — «sinful» (Q. 4:107) — rather, He punishes him. «They hide themselves» — that is, Ṭuʿma and his people, out of shame — «from the people, but they do not hide themselves from Allah, and He is with them» — by His knowledge — «when they plot by night» — they harbour inwardly — «what He is not pleased with, of speech» — their resolve to swear denying the theft and to cast it upon the Jew
«And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do» (Q. 4:108). «Here you are» — O people of Ṭuʿma — «these who have argued» — you have disputed — «on their behalf»

about Ṭuʿma and his kin — «in the life of this world; then who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection» — when He punishes them — «or who will be a guardian over them» (Q. 4:109) — taking charge of their affair. No one will do that. When the verse came down, the Messenger ﷺ declared the Jew innocent and cut off Ṭuʿma's hand; and he fled to Mecca and apostatised and became a thief. One night he dug beneath someone's house until he found a hole by which to enter the house to steal, and the house collapsed upon him and he died. In the end it became clear that he was the thief. «And whoever does an evil» — an offence — «or wrongs himself» — by committing an offence confined to himself — «then asks forgiveness of Allah» — repents — «he will find Allah Forgiving» — towards him — «Merciful» (Q. 4:110). «And whoever earns a sin» — an offence — «then he earns it only against himself» — because its evil consequence is upon it, and he does not harm anyone else — «And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise» (Q. 4:111) — in what He does. «And whoever earns a misdeed» — a small offence — «or a sin» — a great offence — «then casts it upon an innocent man» — innocent of it — «he has borne»

he has taken upon himself «a slander» — by his casting it upon him — «and a manifest sin» (Q. 4:112). «And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you» — O Muḥammad — «and His mercy» — through [His] preserving you from error — «there would have purposed» — harboured the intent — «a party of them» — of Ṭuʿma's people — «to lead you astray» — from judging by the truth

by their deceiving you. «but they lead none astray but themselves, and they do not harm you in anything» — because the evil consequence of their leading astray is upon them — «and Allah has sent down upon you the Book» — the Qurʾan — «and wisdom» — the rulings it contains — «and He has taught you what you did not know» — of the rulings — «and the grace of Allah upon you is» — in that — «great» (Q. 4:113). This verse comprised several things: that nothing profits a person but his good deed and nothing harms him but his evil deed; that a person is obliged to repent and to strive at good works at every one of the times; and that the one who judges is obliged to deal justly between people. This one is a Jew, an unbeliever, and this one claims Islam and is an Arab; and when the right belonged to the Jew, the Messenger ﷺ judged in his favour by the command of the Qurʾan, and judged against the Muslim. For this reason they have said that a ruler who has no justice is like a river that has no water; a scholar who does not act by his knowledge and does not teach it is like wealth from which nothing is spent; a rich man who has no generosity is like a tree that has no fruit; a poor man who has no steadfast patience is like a lamp that has no light; and a woman who has no modesty is like food that has no salt. And they have said: the setting right of four lies in four — the boys, their setting right is in the schools; the elders, their setting right is in the mosques; the women, their setting right is in the houses; and the thieves, their setting right is in the prisons. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, bestowed knowledge upon His Messenger ﷺ, and He said that this is a great grace upon the Messenger ﷺ. Allah gave the Messenger ﷺ such greatness of rank as He has given to no servant other than him ﷺ. The rank of the Messenger ﷺ with Allah is of three degrees: he has a small rank, he has a middling rank, and he has a great rank. The small rank of the Messenger ﷺ is that everyone who teaches some good or teaches some knowledge, Allah apportions to him the reward of that, and He multiplies the reward of the teacher for his teacher, and multiplies that for the teacher of that one — the higher the chain, the greater the multiplication — until it ends at the Messenger ﷺ. So he has in every question the largest share of the reward and the merit, and everything of good that is taught issues from the Messenger ﷺ. This

is his small rank. His middling rank — none knows it in reality but the Messenger ﷺ; and his great rank — none knows it but Allah. Every day he ascends in the knowledge of himself and comes to know of himself what he did not know. And this is his asking forgiveness ﷺ: ⟨Indeed a clouding comes over me, so I ask forgiveness of Allah seventy times in the day⟩ — and in one narration, a hundred times. And he ﷺ is preserved from sin, incapable of committing any contravention with an incapacity belonging to his very essence, like a man's incapacity to fly in the air; and even so he was addressed with «Indeed We have granted you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what came after» (Q. 48:1–2). If we were to suppose that he had a sin, Allah has forgiven him what preceded and what came after. So then, his asking forgiveness — for what? And his clouding (ghayn) — of what? the recognizers see nothing other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and he is the imam of the recognizers; this clouding is not a clouding of things other than Allah (aghyār). A ʿārif asked him and he answered him: a clouding of lights, not a clouding of things other than Allah. That is, whenever he ascends in the Essence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there is renewed in him something of the recognitions (al-maʿārif), and he finds in himself of service and of al-ādāb (the proprieties) what that degree deserves in relation to this last self-disclosure (tajallī). So he comes to see that, whatever earnestness and exertion he was upon in the time past, it was deficient in relation to what he is upon now, and so he asks Allah's forgiveness for that. «There is no good in much of their secret counsel» — of what they confer secretly about

and talk about. The talk of people with one another is all of it idle chatter, with no good in it. «except» — the secret counsel of — «one who enjoins voluntary alms» — except one who commands people to pay out the voluntary alms (ṣadaqāt) — «or what is right» — or an act of piety, whatever act it be — «or setting things right between people» — or strives at the setting right of what is between people — «and whoever does that» — the aforementioned — «seeking the good pleasure of Allah» — and not anything else of the affairs of this world — «so We shall give him a great reward» (Q. 4:114). ⟨Every deed of the son of Ādam is against him⟩

⟨not for him — except one who enjoins voluntary alms or what is right, or strives at the setting right of what is between people⟩. Jibrīl said that he wished he were a human being so that he might be present in the gathering of a scholar; and he wished that he were a human being so that he might strive at the setting right of what is between people; and he wished that he were a human being so that he might dig a well and give drink from its water; and he wished that he were a human being so that he might attend the funeral of a Muslim or visit one who is sick. These — Jibrīl saw in them such merits as moved him to wish that he were a human being, for all the loftiness of his rank. «And whoever opposes the Messenger» — contravenes the Messenger in what he brought — «after the guidance has become clear to him» — the truth has become manifest to him by the miracles — «and follows a way other than that of the believers» — a path other than their path — «We shall turn him over to what he has turned to» — We shall make him a follower of the misguidance he has taken as his own; that is, We shall leave him alone with his misguidance in this world — «and We shall cast him» — We shall make him enter, in the hereafter — «into Hell» — so that he burns in it — «and evil is it as a destination» (Q. 4:115) — a place of return. Whoever contravenes the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is his requital with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and likewise whoever follows a way other than that of the believers.

For this reason the consensus of the community has come as a proof in the shariʿa and as a binding argument. «and follows a way other than that of the believers» (Q. 4:115). The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨My community does not come together upon a misguidance⟩ — the consensus of the community is preserved from error; the foundation of the shariʿa is

the Qurʾan, the hadith and the consensus of the community. The consensus of the community — its proof is «and follows a way other than that of the believers» (Q. 4:115). «Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him». The occasion of its revelation was given yesterday. «Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him» — He does not accept shirk (associating partners with Allah) — «and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills, and whoever associates partners with Allah has gone far astray» (Q. 4:116) — from the truth. «They call upon none besides Him» — besides Allah — «but females» — idols; He called them females because their names are all of them feminine, like al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt — «and they call upon none» — they worship, in worshipping them — «but a rebellious devil» (Q. 4:117) — one gone out from obedience. «Allah has cursed him» — removed him far from His mercy — «And he said» — Satan — «I shall certainly take from Your servants an appointed portion» (Q. 4:118) — cut off for me: I call them to obedience to me. Shirk is of three divisions: al-shirk al-jalī (manifest association of partners with Allah), al-shirk al-khafī (hidden association of partners with Allah) and al-shirk al-akhfā (the most hidden association of partners with Allah). Al-shirk al-jalī is the worship of idols; al-shirk al-khafī is the work of ostentation in worship (riyāʾ); and al-shirk al-akhfā is the seeing of what is other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him: whoever meets Allah with one of the divisions of shirk — then Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him. «And I shall certainly lead them astray» — by whispering; he leads the servants astray from the truth — «and I shall certainly fill them with vain desires» — I cast into their hearts the vain hope of length of life, and that there is no resurrection and no reckoning — «and I shall certainly command them, and they will surely slit» — they will cut — «the ears of the cattle» — and he has already done that with the camels with slit ears dedicated to idols (baḥāʾir); it will come in Sūrat al-Māʾida — «and I shall certainly command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah» — His religion, by unbelief (kufr) and by making lawful what He has forbidden and forbidding what He has made lawful — «and whoever takes Satan as a protector» — takes him as his patron and obeys him — «instead of Allah» — that is, other than Him — «has lost with a manifest loss» (Q. 4:119) — a plain loss, through his ending in the Fire made everlasting upon him. «He promises them» — length of life — «and fills them with vain desires» — the attainment of hopes in this world, and that there is no resurrection and no requital — «and Satan promises them nothing» — by that — «but delusion» (Q. 4:120) — falsehood. «Those — their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it» (Q. 4:121) — no turning aside. «And those who have believed and done righteous deeds» — the obligatory acts and the supererogatory — «We shall admit them into gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein forever — the promise of Allah in truth» — Allah promised them that and made it true in truth — «and who»
«is more truthful» — no one is more truthful — «than Allah in speech» (Q. 4:122) — in word. «It is not by your vain wishes» (Q. 4:123). This verse (āya) came down when

the Muslims and the People of the Book vied in boasting. The Muslims said: we are Muslims, and our religion is better than your religion, so we are better than you. And the Jews said: our religion is more excellent than your religion, and we are better than you. And He said: «It is not» — the matter is not contingent — «by your vain wishes nor the vain wishes of the People of the Book» — rather, by righteous work alone — «whoever does an evil shall be requited for it» — either in the hereafter or in this world, by affliction and trials, as has come in the hadith — «and he will not find for himself, besides Allah» — other than Him — «a protector» — to guard him — «nor a helper» (Q. 4:123) — to defend him from Him. Abū Bakr said: ⟨May my father be [your ransom], O Messenger of Allah! If everything of evil that we do we are to be requited for, then we are ruined.⟩ So the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Every affliction that comes down upon the believer — even a fever of a night, even the sickness of a child, the loss of property, even a thorn that strikes him — by it Allah takes away from the sins of the Muslim, until he meets Allah with neither a great sin nor a small one upon him.⟩ And this is the most fearsome verse for the ruler. While ʿUmar was walking in the districts of Medina with a company of the elders of the Companions, they looked at

a caravan. He said: ⟨Who are the caravan, and from where, and to where?⟩ They said: ⟨From a deep ravine to the Ancient House.⟩ He said: ⟨So they have gone in for this? They have come with the grand epithets. Say to them: let them tell me of the greatest verse in the Qurʾan, and the most fearsome verse in the Qurʾan, and the most equitable verse in the Qurʾan, and the most judicious verse in the Qurʾan, and the most hope-giving verse in the Qurʾan.⟩ So they answered: ⟨The greatest verse in the Qurʾan is Āyat al-Kursī, and the most equitable verse in the Qurʾan is⟩ «So whoever does an atom's weight of good shall see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it» (Q. 99:7–8), ⟨and the most judicious verse in the Qurʾan is⟩ «Indeed Allah commands justice and excellence and giving to kinsfolk, and forbids indecency and wrong and insolence» (Q. 16:90), ⟨and the most hope-giving verse in the Qurʾan is⟩ «Indeed Allah does not wrong by so much as an atom's weight; and if there be a good deed He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward» (Q. 4:40), ⟨and the most fearsome verse in the Qurʾan is⟩ «whoever does an evil shall be requited for it» (Q. 4:123). ʿUmar said: ⟨Is Ibn Umm ʿAbd among you? Is ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd among you?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ He said: ⟨A little vessel filled full of knowledge — we gave him up to the people of al-Qādisiyya in preference to ourselves.⟩ The answer came from ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd.

From Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn: ⟨You say, O people of Iraq, that the most hope-giving verse in the Qurʾan is⟩ «Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed Allah forgives sins»

«all of them» (Q. 39:53). ⟨But as for us, the Family of the House, we say that the most hope-giving verse (āya) in the Qurʾan is⟩ «And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well pleased» (Q. 93:5), ⟨because the Prophet will never be well pleased while one of his community enters the Fire.⟩ «Whoever does a wrong will be requited for it, and will not»
«find for himself, besides Allah» — other than Him — «any protector or helper» (Q. 4:123). «And whoever does of righteous deeds» — anything — «whether male»

«or female, and he is a believer, then those will enter the Garden, and they will not be wronged a whit» (Q. 4:124) — the measure of the notch in a date-stone. «And who is better in religion» — no one is better in religion — «than one who submits his face» — who yields and makes his deed sincere — «to Allah, while he is a doer of good»

— one who affirms the divine oneness — «and follows the creed of Ibrāhīm» — which agrees with the creed of Islam — «inclining to the truth» — inclining away from all the religions to the upright religion — «And Allah took Ibrāhīm as an intimate friend» (Q. 4:125) — a chosen one, pure in his love for Him. «And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — as possession, as creation and as servants — «and Allah encompasses all things» (Q. 4:126) — in knowledge and in power; He has never ceased to be so described. «And they ask you for a ruling» — they seek a fatwa from you — «concerning» — the affair of — «women» — their inheritance

«Say» — to them — «Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book» — the Qurʾan, of the verses of inheritance, and it too gives you a ruling — «concerning the orphan women whom you do not give what is prescribed» — made obligatory — «for them» — of the inheritance

«And you desire» — O you guardians — «to marry them» — you are averse to marrying them because they are ill-favoured, and you prevent them from marrying out of greed for their inheritance. raghiba: when it is made transitive with ʿan, it is aversion; and when it is made transitive with fī, it is desire. You are averse to marrying them because they are ill-favoured, yet you married them in order to take possession of their wealth; or «you desire» — you have a desire to marry them for the wealth they have, so that you may take possession of the wealth. «And» — concerning — «the oppressed among the children» — that you give them their rights — and He commands you «that you maintain justice for the orphans. And whatever good you do, Allah is ever Knowing of it» (Q. 4:127). Whatever good the servant does, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knows it and requites him for it. The children are the little ones. Allah mentioned them in the Book because there are in them beautiful traits: whoever is marked by them joins the righteous awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah). The child, when he grieves, weeps tears, and he does not pass the night harbouring rancour against anyone. If he quarrels with one like himself, he does not pass the night with enmity in his heart. And he speaks the truth in what he says. When boys quarrel and are questioned, they say nothing but the truth, and they pass the night upon the ground in humility. Everyone who takes on the character of boys becomes great. «And whatever good you do, Allah is ever Knowing of it» (Q. 4:127). So on this basis the servant strives always in righteous work, and Allah requites him for it. Abū al-Manṣūr was one of the great awliyāʾ. When his death drew near he began to weep, and he grieved a severe grief. He had a righteous son, and the son wondered at him and said: what is the matter with you, O my father? He said: ⟨I am travelling a road I have not known and have not been familiar with. The place I am coming to is not of what we know. This is what has made me afraid.⟩ When he died, the son set his heart on seeing him so that he might know how he fared; and he saw him four days after his death

So he asked him: O my father, what has Allah done with you? He said: The matter is graver than everything we used to suppose. I met adversaries pressing their claims, but I met a generous Lord, the most merciful of those who show mercy. I stood before Him, and He said to me: ⟨I kept you alive seventy years. What did you put forward in them?⟩ I said to Him: My Lord, here are sixty years, their fasting and their standing in prayer. He said: ⟨I accepted nothing of them.⟩ I said: Thirty pilgrimages. He said: ⟨I accepted nothing of them.⟩ I said: I went out forty times for jihad. He said: ⟨I have accepted nothing of them.⟩ I said: I gave in alms forty thousand dirhams from my own hand. He said: ⟨I have accepted nothing of that.⟩ I said: My Lord, then I am lost. He said: ⟨No. I do not destroy one like you, ever. You walked out on such and such a day and found a thorn on a road, and you turned it aside from the road for fear it should hurt a Muslim. For that I have forgiven you.⟩ «And whatever good you do, Allah is indeed knowing of it» (Q. 4:127).

«And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment» (Q. 4:128). This verse came down concerning the master of the worlds and his wife Sawda. When Sawda bt. Zamʿa grew old, the Prophet ﷺ was minded to divorce her — or rather, [by another account] he had already divorced her. So she sat down on the road to the mosque until the Prophet ﷺ passed by her. She said to him: ⟨I have no desire for marriage, but do not divorce me. Leave me among your wives, so that I may be one of your wives in the Garden; and my turn is a gift from me to ʿĀʾisha.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ accepted, and he used to apportion two nights to ʿĀʾisha and a single night to the remaining co-wives. Sawda remained with no night of her own, by a settlement with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept her so until he died, leaving her behind; she remained within his marriage bond until she became one of his wives in the Garden. So there came down «And if a woman fears» — anticipates — «from her husband» — her spouse — «ill-treatment» — his holding himself above her by abandoning

her bed and falling short in her maintenance, out of dislike for her and because his eye aspires to one more beautiful than she — «or turning away» — from her with his face — «then there is no blame upon the two of them that they should set things right between themselves» — there is no harm upon either of the two spouses in reaching a settlement on whatever they have agreed upon between them — «a settlement» — in the apportioning and the maintenance, by her giving up something to him, seeking the continuance of the companionship. The woman may waive her turn and may waive her maintenance and remain with her husband if she is content with that; and then it is for the husband either to accept that or to part from her — «and settlement is better» — if he does not accept all of this, he simply divorces her; and settlement is better than parting, than ill-treatment and than turning away — «and the souls have been made prone to niggardliness» — intense miserliness: they were created disposed to it, so that it is as though the souls were present to it, never absent from it. The woman can hardly be open-handed with her share of her husband, and the man can hardly hold his soul patient with her once he has come to love another — «and if you do well» — in consorting with women — «and guard yourselves» — against wronging them — «then Allah is indeed aware of what you do» (Q. 4:128) — and so He will requite you for it — «And you will never be able to deal equally between women» — to hold the women equal in love; this is not possible — «even if you are eager» — for that — «so do not incline with the whole of your inclining» — toward the one you love, in the apportioning and the maintenance — «so that you leave her» — that is, the one turned away from — «like one suspended» — who is neither husbandless nor possessed of a husband — «and if you set things right» — by justice in the apportioning — «and guard yourselves» — against wronging — «then Allah is indeed forgiving» — of what is in your hearts — «merciful» (Q. 4:129) — toward you in that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have eleven women together. The one he loved most among them was ʿĀʾisha, the daughter of al-Ṣiddīq; but he dealt equally in the apportioning, and when he apportioned anything among his wives he made the shares equal, and he would say: ⟨O Allah, this is my apportioning in what I have power over, so do not blame me for what You have power over and I do not.⟩ So he ﷺ did not act unjustly, and he dealt equally in the apportioning. The Prophet had no

house. Rather, when it was the turn of one of them he would come to her house only, and when her turn was over he moved on to another. He went round among his wives in this way, and he had no house — a Messenger only, and a Messenger does not build a house. The Companions understood that a gift which came to the Prophet ﷺ in ʿĀʾisha's house would make the Prophet gladder of it than any other gift, and al-Anṣār used to hold back their gifts, waiting for ʿĀʾisha's turn; so when ʿĀʾisha's turn came the gifts came in abundance, and when it was another's turn they lost that. Everything that came during the turn of one of them was hers. The wives of the Prophet ﷺ gathered and complained of that. They sent Fāṭima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ⟨Go to your father and tell him to deal justly among us in the matter of the daughter of Abū Bakr.⟩

So she came and said: ⟨The women have sent me to you; they ask you for justice in the matter of the daughter of Abū Bakr.⟩ He said to her: ⟨You are my daughter. It is not fitting for you to do anything but love what I love.⟩ She said: ⟨Yes⟩ — and she went. They asked her for the answer, and she returned them no answer. They sent Zaynab bt. Jaḥsh, and she spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he returned her no answer; she spoke much and he returned her no answer; then she spoke about ʿĀʾisha — she reviled her. ʿĀʾisha said: ⟨So I took to looking at the eye of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: would he consent to my answering her back or not? — until I answered her back with a word.⟩ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled and said: ⟨She is the daughter of al-Ṣiddīq.⟩ ʿĀʾisha said: ⟨So I knew⟩

⟨that it pleased the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that I should answer Zaynab back, and so I answered her until she fell silent.⟩ And this is his saying ﷺ: ⟨O Allah, this is my apportioning in what I have power over, so do not blame me for what You have power over and I do not.⟩ «And if the two separate» — if they let the divorce fall between them so that a parting takes place — «Allah will enrich each» — independently of the other — «out of His abundance» — out of the abundance of the bounty of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, by providing her with a husband other than him and providing him with a wife other than her — «and Allah is ever all-embracing» — embracing His creation in bounty — «wise» (Q. 4:130) — in what He has ordained for them — «And to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» — in possession, in creation and as bondsmen — «And We have enjoined upon those who were given the Book» — meaning the Books — «before you» — the Jews and the Christians — «and upon you» — O people of the Qurʾan — «that you should fear Allah» (Q. 4:131) — fear His punishment by obeying Him. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, enjoined the People of the Book and enjoined the people of the Qurʾan with godfearing (al-taqwā) of Allah, which is carrying out the command and avoiding the prohibition. When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Muljam — may Allah bridle him with a bridle of fire — struck ʿAlī b.

the last days, he gathered his sons and enjoined them: ⟨I enjoin upon you the godfearing of Allah in secret and in the open. I enjoin upon you the word of truth in contentment and in anger. I enjoin upon you justice toward the enemy and the friend. I enjoin upon you moderation in wealth and in poverty. I enjoin upon you work in vigour and in sloth. O my sons: there is no evil after which comes the Garden that is an evil, and no good after which comes the Fire that is a good. O my sons: whoever frequents the gatherings of the ulama is held in honour, and whoever comes to the gatherings of the base is held in contempt; and whoever digs a well for his brother falls into it.⟩ — until he said: ⟨So blessed is he who makes sincere his deed for Allah, and his knowledge for Allah, and his word, and his silence, and his speech, and his act, and his taking, and his leaving, and his love, and his hatred — for Allah, Blessed and Exalted.⟩ «And» — We said to them and to you — «if you disbelieve» — that is, in what you have been enjoined with — «then to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» — in creation, in possession and as bondsmen; and so their unbelief (kufr) does not harm Him — «and Allah is ever self-sufficient» — above His creation and their worship — «praiseworthy» (Q. 4:131) — praised in His dealing with them. «And to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» — He repeated it as emphasis, to establish what makes godfearing obligatory — «and Allah suffices as a guardian» (Q. 4:132). He repeated in the verse «To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» three times in three lines. It is not emphasis only; for each there is a sense. First: «To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» — in connection with what He commanded them of godfearing, that you should fear Allah: since what is in the heavens and what is in the earth belongs to Him, it is fitting that you should fear Him. And if you disbelieve, He is free of need of you and of your godfearing, because «To Allah belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth» — this is a teaching that He, Blessed and Exalted, has no need of the servants nor of their deeds. And He repeated it a third time so that you should trust in Him: He calls you to take Him as a guardian, and «Allah suffices as a guardian» — why should He not suffice as a guardian, when what is in the heavens and what is in the earth belongs to Him? «If He wills, He will take you away» — O people — «and bring others» — in your place — «and Allah is ever able to do that» (Q. 4:133). «Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and of the hereafter» — a man works his work for the hereafter and Allah gives him this world and the hereafter; and if he works for this world only and leaves the hereafter, he has nothing but what has been apportioned to him in this world, and he has lost the hereafter — «and Allah is ever hearing, seeing» (Q. 4:134). «O you who believe, be upholders» — standing firm — «in equity» — in justice — «witnesses» — to the truth

«for Allah» «and though» — the testimony be — «against yourselves» — then bear witness against them, by acknowledging the truth and not concealing it — «or» — against — «your parents and your nearest kin. If he be» — the one testified against — «rich or poor, Allah is nearer to them both» — than you are, and better knowing of what is of benefit to them — «so do not follow desire» — in your testimony — «that you may be just» — uprightness is indispensable — «and if you twist» — distort the testimony — «or turn away» — from giving it — «then Allah is indeed aware of what you do»

(Q. 4:135) — and so He will requite you for it. «O you who believe, believe» — persist in faith (īmān) — «in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger» — Muḥammad ﷺ, and it is the Qurʾan — «and the Book which He sent down before» — upon the messengers, meaning the Books — «And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His Books and His messengers and the Last Day has gone far astray» (Q. 4:136) — from the truth. «Those who believed» — in Mūsā, and they are the Jews — «then disbelieved» — by worshipping the calf — «then believed» — after that, by repenting — «then disbelieved» — in ʿĪsā — «then increased in unbelief» — in Muḥammad ﷺ — «Allah would not forgive them» — for what they persisted in — «nor guide them to a way» (Q. 4:137) — a road to the truth. «Give tidings» — inform, O Muḥammad — «to the hypocrites that theirs is a painful punishment» (Q. 4:138) — grievous; and it is the punishment of the Fire. «Those who take the unbelievers as friends rather than the believers» — because of the strength they imagine in them — «do they seek»

they seek «with them might» — they will not find it — «for might belongs to Allah altogether» (Q. 4:139) — in this world and in the hereafter, and none attains it but His awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah). «And it has already been sent down to you in the Book» — the Qurʾan — in Sūrat al-Anʿām. How can this be in Sūrat al-Anʿām, when that one came down in Mecca and this one came down in Medina? Because Allah's knowledge went before, that the ordering of the Qurʾan required that [this sūra] come before Sūrat al-Anʿām. Or: the presence of Allah has in it no future and no past. «that»

— that it is — «when you hear the verses of Allah» — the Qurʾan — «disbelieved in and mocked at, then do not sit with them» — the unbelievers and the mockers — «until they engage in some other talk. Indeed you would then be» — if you sit with them — «like them» — in

sin. «Indeed Allah will gather the hypocrites and the unbelievers in Hell all together» (Q. 4:140), as they gathered together in this world upon unbelief and mockery. «Those who lie in wait» — who await — «for you» — the turns of fortune; such is the hypocrites’ habit — «so if there be»
«for you a victory» — a triumph and spoils — «from Allah, they say» — to you — «Were we not with you?» — in religion and in jihad,

so give us a portion of the spoils. «And if the unbelievers have a share» — of victory over you — «they say» — to them — «Did we not gain mastery» — take control — «over you» — and give you power to seize them — «and keep you back» — we did not give them power to seize you and kill you, so we spared you — «from the believers» — that they should gain the victory over you, through our disheartening them and our sending you word of their news; so the favour over you is ours. He, Exalted, said: «So Allah will judge between you» — and between them — «on the Day of Resurrection» — by admitting you to the Garden

and admitting them to the Fire. «And Allah will never grant the unbelievers a way over the believers» (Q. 4:141) — a way to their extirpation. «Indeed the hypocrites would deceive Allah» — by their showing the contrary of the unbelief they conceal, so as to ward off from themselves His rulings in this world — «and He» — Exalted — «is deceiving them» — requiting them for their deception; so they are exposed in this world by Allah’s informing His Prophet of what they conceal, and they are punished in the hereafter — «And when they stand for the prayer» — with the believers — «they stand lazily» — heavily, with reluctance — «making a show to people» — with their prayer — «and they do not remember Allah» — they do not pray — «except a little» (Q. 4:142) — except out of ostentation in worship (riyāʾ). The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨That is the prayer of the hypocrite. A man holds back until the sun is on the point of setting, then rises and prays cycles of the prayer in which his heart is not present with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and he pecks at the prostrations as the cock pecks. That is the prayer of the hypocrite.⟩ «Wavering» — vacillating — «between that»
unbelief and faith. «not» — belonging — «to these» — the unbelievers — «nor» — belonging — «to these»

— the believers. «And whomever Allah leads astray, you will never find for him a way» (Q. 4:143) — a way to guidance. «O you who believe, do not take the unbelievers as allies rather than the believers. Do you wish to give Allah, against you,» — by your allying with them —
«a manifest warrant» (Q. 4:144) — a plain proof of your hypocrisy. «Indeed the hypocrites will be in the depth» — the place — «lowest of»
«the Fire» (Q. 4:145), and that is its bottom. «It has seven gates; to each gate a portion of them assigned» (Q. 15:44). The Fire is seven levels:

Jahannam, Laẓā, al-Saʿīr, Saqar, al-Jaḥīm, al-Ḥuṭama, al-Hāwiya. Jahannam is for the disobedient among the believers, Laẓā for the Jews and the Christians, Saqar for the polytheists, al-Jaḥīm for the Magians, al-Ḥuṭama for the worshippers of idols, and al-Hāwiya, which lies beneath all the levels, is for the hypocrites: «in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will never find for them a helper» (Q. 4:145) — any to ward off the punishment — «except those who repent» — of hypocrisy — «and set right» — their deeds — «and hold fast» — and put their trust — «to Allah and make their religion sincerely for Allah» — free of ostentation in worship — «those are with the believers» — in what is given them — «and Allah will give the believers a great reward» (Q. 4:146) — in the hereafter, and that is the Garden. «What would Allah do with punishing you» — Allah will not punish you — «if you are grateful» — for His blessings — «and believe» — in Him — «and Allah is ever grateful» — for the deeds of the believers, by rewarding them — «knowing» (Q. 4:147) — of His creation; nothing escapes Him. O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.

«Allah does not love the open utterance of evil speech, except for one who has been wronged». The occasion of its revelation: a man reviled Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not answer him; then he reviled him a second time and he did not answer him; then he reviled him a third time and he answered him. So Al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ rose and withdrew from the assembly, and Abū Bakr caught up with him and said to him: ⟨The man spoke against me several times and I did not speak; and when I spoke, you went away from us.⟩ He said: ⟨While you were silent, the angel was answering on your behalf; and when you spoke, the angel withdrew and the devil came — and I do not sit with him, so I withdrew.⟩ So this verse (āya) came down: «Allah does not love the open utterance of evil speech, except for one who has been wronged» (Q. 4:148) — like Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq,

may Allah be pleased with him. A man is barred from the open utterance of evil, in word and in deed, except with respect to the wrongdoer. If a man wrongs you, it is yours to speak of his wrongdoing, saying: so-and-so stole my property, so-and-so did such to me. There is no sin in this. Or if a man commits an innovation or a misguidance or open wickedness and casts off the cloak of shame — for whoever casts off the cloak of shame, there is no backbiting in his case, on the strength of the hadith: ⟨Mention the wicked man by what is in him, so that they may beware of him.⟩ And among the open utterances of evil speech that are permitted: the guest, if he is not honoured, may describe his host as one who does not honour a guest. «Allah does not love the open utterance» — He does not reward for the open utterance — «of evil» — rather He punishes for it — «of speech, except for one who has been wronged» — so He does not take him to task for uttering it openly — «and Allah is ever hearing» — of what is said — «knowing» — of what

is done. He does not love the open utterance of evil speech in the case of the common people; and He does not love the speaking of it within the nafs (the soul) in the case of the elect; and He does not love that it should pass through the mind in the case of the elect of the elect. «Allah does not love the open utterance of evil speech, except for one who has been wronged» (Q. 4:148). In it is the indication that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, does not love the open utterance of the secrets of Lordship before those who are veiled. The disclosure of the secrets of Lordship among the veiled is graver in Allah's sight than the forbidden. «except for one who has been wronged»
— except one whom the spiritual state (ḥāl) overcomes — «and Allah is ever hearing, knowing» (Q. 4:148) — of what is done — «If you disclose» — make manifest — «good» — of
the works of piety — «or conceal it» — do it in secret — «or pardon an evil» — a wrong — «then indeed Allah is ever pardoning, all-powerful» (Q. 4:149)

It is for the Muslim to utter evil openly concerning one who has wronged him; but if he pardons, then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, rewards him for that and is pleased with him. He confirmed it by [declaring] that He, Blessed and Exalted, is ever pardoning, all-powerful.
