For that reason it has come down that among the noble traits of character are that you pardon one who has wronged you, that you join with one who has cut you off, and that you give to one who has withheld from you. «Indeed those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and desire to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers» — by believing in Him but not in them — «and say, we believe in some» — of the messengers — «and disbelieve in some» — of them — as the Jews and the Christians did. «and desire to take between that» — unbelief and faith — «a way» — a road they go along — «those are the unbelievers in truth» — a verbal noun (maṣdar) confirming the content of the sentence — «and We have prepared for the unbelievers a humiliating punishment» (Q. 4:151) — one that carries humiliation (ihāna); it is the punishment of the Fire — «And those who believe in Allah and His messengers» — all of them — «and make no distinction between any of them; those — He will give them their rewards» — the recompense of their deeds — «and Allah is ever forgiving» — to His awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) — «merciful» (Q. 4:152) — to the people of His obedience — «They ask you»

— O Muḥammad — «the People of the Book» — the Jews — «to send down to them a Book from heaven». They said that they would not believe in the Qurʾan until it came all at once, as the Torah came all at once to Mūsā; and this they said out of obstinacy. If you reckon that outrageous, then «they have already asked» — their fathers — «Mūsā for greater than that» — the children, though they reach whatever they reach of obduracy and obstinacy, their fathers were harsher than they in obstinacy and obduracy; for they asked Mūsā this question — «so they said, show us Allah plainly» — with the eye — «so the thunderbolt took them» — death, as a punishment for them — «for their wrongdoing» (Q. 4:153), in that they were obstinate in the asking. They sought the sight of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with the eye out of obstinacy, not out of longing. Had it been love and longing they would not have perished; but it was out of haughtiness

and obstinacy and overbearing, and they took no warning from what had befallen their prophet: «Show me, that I may look upon You. He said: you shall not see Me» (Q. 7:143). If Mūsā was answered with this answer, for all the sublimity of his rank, then they the more so; and in spite of that they asked, out of obduracy: «Show us Allah plainly» (Q. 4:153)

They asked for something that was not theirs. They asked for the sight of Allah with the eye in this world, with their eyes, and this is barred for several reasons: that this world is the abode of His enemies, so it does not deserve to be the place of His manifestation to His beloved ones. Second, that in this world they attend to the secondary causes and live in it by attending to their livelihood; and were He to manifest Himself to them they would abandon this world altogether, and this would entail the cessation of works and the ending of the world. And also, it is the greatest honour (karāma), so it can only be in the greatest abode, which is the hereafter.

What is impossible is the sight of Allah today with the eye. As for the seeing that is the recognition (maʿrifa) of Allah — the recognition of Allah is first by faith (īmān), second by certitude, and third by direct vision after the person's death, as the Messenger says: ⟨Die before you die.⟩ And whoever wishes to look upon a dead man walking on the face of the earth, let him look upon al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. This requires being born twice and dying twice. And the sight of Allah after death is not barred to His beloved ones — may Allah make us and you among them. «so the thunderbolt took them» — death, as a punishment for them for their wrongdoing, in that they were obstinate in the asking — «then they took the calf» — as a god — «after the clear signs had come to them» — the miracles attesting the oneness of

Allah — «then We pardoned that» — and We did not extirpate them; We did not destroy them — «and We gave Mūsā a manifest authority» (Q. 4:153) — a plain, evident mastery over them, in that he commanded them to kill themselves in repentance and they obeyed him — «and We raised over them the Mount» — the mountain — «by their covenant» — when the Torah was sent down they refused to act by it, so Jibrīl tore up the mountain of Ṭūr, the measure of their camp, and called them to act by the Torah, failing which he would clap it down upon them — «and We said to them» — while it overshadowed them — «enter the gate» — that is, of the town — «prostrating» — a prostration of bowing — «and We said to them, do not transgress in the Sabbath» — do not transgress on the Sabbath by catching fish on it — «and We took from them a solemn covenant» (Q. 4:154) — upon that, and they broke it. These stories have all come before in Sūrat al-Baqara, and for that reason He abridges them: He takes a sentence and keeps it short, until He has enumerated all the kinds. «so for their breaking» — We cursed them because of their breaking — «their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right» — wrongfully — «and their saying» — to the Prophet ﷺ — «our hearts are wrapped» — they do not take in your speech — «rather Allah has set a seal» — Allah has sealed — «upon them for their unbelief» — so they take in no admonition — «so they do not believe except a few» (Q. 4:155) — of them, such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām and his companions — «and for their unbelief» — a second time, in ʿĪsā b. Maryam. The Jews did this in the time of Mūsā, and they increased in unbelief when they disbelieved in ʿĪsā, upon him be peace — «and their saying against Maryam a monstrous calumny» (Q. 4:156) — in that they accused her of fornication — «and their saying, indeed we killed the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah» (Q. 4:157) — in their claim. The Jews called ʿĪsā a liar and accused his mother of being a fornicatress, and [said] that ʿĪsā was a child of fornication and not one of the prophets. So ʿĪsā prayed against them. He said: ⟨O my Lord, if I am Your spirit and Your word, then destroy whoever has reviled me and reviled my mother, and transform them into apes and swine.⟩ So they were all transformed into apes and swine
When the Jews grew afraid of ʿĪsā's call against them, they plotted to kill him,

they purposed to kill him, and so they sent someone to kill him in his dwelling. When they purposed to kill him, Allah raised him — as will come — to heaven, and cast his likeness upon his enemy who had entered upon him, Ṭaṭyānūs. When they saw him they supposed that he was ʿĪsā, and they killed him, and they said: the face is the face of ʿĪsā and the body is the body of Ṭaṭyānūs. So they said: if this is ʿĪsā, then where is

Ṭaṭyānūs? And if this is Ṭaṭyānūs, then where is ʿĪsā? And even so they made bold to lie, and they said: we have killed the Messiah ʿĪsā son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah. For the whole of that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave them the lie, and said, giving them the lie: «And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them» — Allah cast his likeness upon his enemy, the one slain, and so he was killed and crucified — «And indeed those who differed concerning him» — concerning ʿĪsā — «are in doubt about it» — about his killing. When they saw the slain man — the face the face of ʿĪsā and the body not his body — a great doubt entered them — «They have, concerning it» — concerning his killing — «no knowledge, only the following of conjecture» — rather they followed only the conjecture they had imagined, that they had killed him — «And they did not kill him, for certain» — the truth is that they did not kill ʿĪsā — «Rather Allah raised him to Himself» — to the place of His good pleasure, or to His heaven — «And Allah is Mighty» — in His dominion — «Wise» — in His making (Q. 4:157–158). «And there is none of the People of the Book» — anyone — «but will surely believe in him» — in ʿĪsā — «before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be» — ʿĪsā — «a witness against them» — as to what they did (Q. 4:159). This is ʿĪsā, the Spirit of Allah. The two parties went astray concerning ʿĪsā, the Jews and the Christians. The Jews fell short concerning him, until they made him a child of fornication and his mother a fornicatress; and the Christians raised him above his measure, until they made him a son to Allah, or made him Allah Himself. And this is Allah's custom with every vicegerent (khalīfa): there must needs be excess and falling short. Whoever fell short concerning him was made wretched by him; and whoever went to excess, until he set him above servanthood and made him a god — he too was made wretched by him. ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace — Allah created him from His spirit, as He created Ādam: «Indeed the likeness of ʿĪsā with Allah is as the likeness of Ādam» (Q. 3:59). But every human being whom Allah created, He breathes into him a spirit from His spirit, and by this spirit he becomes a human being. Yet most of the children of man come to be in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers, and then this spirit descends; when this spirit descends, the human being is set apart from all created things by this spirit. And this spirit entered into Maryam without the mediation of men, and so she conceived ʿĪsā and bore him in

the Messenger ﷺ ⟨I am from Allah, and the believers are from me⟩, ⟨And were it not for you, I would not have created anything⟩, ⟨I am from the light of Allah, and the believers are from my light⟩, ⟨I am from Allah, and the believers are from my spirit⟩. This spirit is the Muḥammadan ḥaqīqa (inner reality). It is named in the hadith by names: among them the Light; among them the White Pearl; among them the Spirit; among them a spherical angel, an angel encompassing the angels, just as the angels encompass the children of man. And all this is an expression for Muḥammad ﷺ. And Allah mentioned that when He brought Ādam into being He breathed into him of His spirit; that spirit is the spirit of

Muḥammad ﷺ. And when He created the son of Ādam from an extraction of despised water, He breathed into him of His spirit; and ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace — He breathed into him of His spirit also. And since the spirits were in pre-eternity in ranks, the spirit of ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace, was the one that came directly next to the spirit of Muḥammad ﷺ. For this reason there was no prophet between him and him; and for this reason he did not come by the mediation of fathers — rather his father is Muḥammad ﷺ. So ʿĪsā was strong with this strength, more than the spirit of any other — granted that every spirit which has stripped itself of all that is other, and occupied itself with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and passed away from its own being, and been engulfed in the being of al-Ḥaqq, disposes over created things, be it little or much. And ʿĪsā, since he was the strongest of them, and the nearest of them to the spirit of Muḥammad, and the least of them in commerce with things, the effect of his spirit was greater than the effect of the spirit of any other; and it is nothing but a part of the spirit of Muḥammad only. Likewise Jibrīl was named a spirit, and he is from the spirit of Muḥammad ﷺ. «And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed those who differed concerning him are in doubt about it. They have, concerning it» — concerning his killing — «no knowledge, only the following of conjecture» — rather they follow the conjecture they have imagined — «And they did not kill him, for certain. Rather Allah raised him to Himself» — to the place of His good pleasure — «And Allah is Mighty, Wise» (Q. 4:157–158). And since the child is the secret of his father, it was ʿĪsā's due, upon him be blessing and peace, that he be spiritual, with no body appearing for him; but inasmuch as he breathed the spirit into Maryam, and Maryam took pleasure in that breathing, so that seed descended from her as from the rest of women, from Maryam's seed the body of ʿĪsā was built. Were it not for that, he would have been

spiritual, with no body! And since the child for the most part resembles what the woman beholds at the time of intercourse, ʿĪsā came to resemble Jibrīl. The woman at the time of intercourse — whatever she looks at, the child comes resembling that. This has happened among people many times. For this reason a child cannot be disowned from his father either by the absence of a resemblance or by a resemblance. A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: I am a white man and my wife is white, and a black child has come out for us; he is not mine. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Do you have camels?⟩ He said: yes. ⟨Are there any black among them?⟩ He said:

yes. He said: ⟨A strain drew it out from that black camel.⟩ On this basis the resemblance comes merely from the woman's seeing a thing. There was a woman whose husband was having intercourse with her while she was looking at two bears coupling before her, and the child came with four legs and four eyes, resembling what she had been looking at at the time of intercourse. For this reason ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace, came more like the spiritual beings than like the bodily ones. «And there is none of the People of the Book» — anyone — «but will surely believe in him» — in ʿĪsā — «before his death» (Q. 4:159) — the man of the Book does not die until he believes in ʿĪsā. And the delegation of Najrān was of two parts: among them were Jews and among them were Christians. The Messenger ﷺ said to them: ⟨Submit! Woe to you, submit! You know that I am the prophet who is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.⟩ The Jews said: Allah forbid that we should believe in you, when you count ʿĪsā

among the prophets, and he is nothing but a bastard child. And the party of the Christians said: Allah forbid that we should believe in you, when you revile ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨How do I revile him?⟩ They said:
you say: a servant to Allah. The Messenger ﷺ said to them: «The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant»

(Q. 4:172). They said: he is not a servant to Allah; rather he is a son to Him, or he is Allah, or the gods are three. Both parties disbelieved. For this reason, every one of them, when death comes to him and he sees the Angel of Death with his own eyes, the angel comes to him with ʿĪsā, saying to him: until you believe in ʿĪsā — and so he believes in him before his death. Or [the meaning is] that Allah will defer the descent of ʿĪsā. Allah, Blessed and Exalted — when He raised ʿĪsā to heaven, it was possible for Him to send him back for a while, so that they should know that he was not the one slain; but Allah deferred his descent to the end of time. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨The son of Maryam will descend among you as a just arbiter. He will kill the swine and break the cross and lift the jizya, and he will deal justly — he will establish justice in the earth, until wealth overflows, until no one will accept it.⟩ So then «before his death» — the pronoun refers back to ʿĪsā. There is none of the People of the Book but will believe in ʿĪsā before the death of ʿĪsā, when Allah brings him down at the end of time as the seal of the Muḥammadan walāya (sainthood), in honour of this community. So there is no walāya after the descent of ʿĪsā; he is the greatest seal. «And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them» — as to what they did (Q. 4:159). «So for a wrongdoing» — because of the wrongdoing — «of those who are Jews» — and they are the Jews

«We forbade them wholesome things that had been made lawful to them» (Q. 4:160) — these are the ones in His saying, «We forbade every animal with claws» (Q. 6:146), and the rest of the verse. The Jews committed the forbidden things, and so Allah forbade them wholesome things that had been made lawful to them. From this we know that committing what is prohibited brings about the denial of wholesome things, and that indulging in the wholesome things of the lawful prevents intimate converse with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So there must be renunciation of the unlawful, for fear that Allah bar you from the lawful and wholesome; and there must be renunciation of the lawful, lest you be denied intimate converse with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «And for their barring» — people — «from the way of Allah» — His religion — a barring — «much, and for their taking usury though they had been forbidden it» — in the Torah — «and for their devouring people's wealth wrongfully» — all of these they committed, and for this Allah forbade them the wholesome things of provision — «And We have prepared for the unbelievers among them a painful punishment»
— causing pain — it is the Fire (Q. 4:160–161).

The whole of the major sins arises from three things. The following of caprice: «And do not follow caprice, for it will lead you astray from the way of Allah» (Q. 38:26) — going astray, innovation, dissoluteness, arrogance: all these major sins arise from the following of caprice. So the following of caprice first, and love of this world second — ⟨Love of this world is the head of every sin⟩ — as the Messenger ﷺ said. By love of this world a man kills a soul and consumes usury; he devours people's wealth wrongfully and devours the wealth of orphans, and swears by Allah the perjurious oath, and shows enmity to the Muslims and hates them and envies them and is arrogant towards them and backbites them and goes about with talebearing among them. All of this — and there is no end to the major sins — has its origin in love of this world. And the third is the seeing of what is other than Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Seeing other than Allah carries a man to love of leadership, and love of leadership is the Kaʿba around which all evils circle. The following of caprice, love of this world, and seeing other than Allah: these three are the origin of the whole of the major sins.

rather he comes as a walī (a friend of Allah) who has no independent standing. The prophet is independent and the walī is a follower; and when he comes at the end of time he will be a following walī, not an independent prophet. So Abū Bakr and ʿUmar will be gathered between two prophets — this is among their distinctions. «So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews We forbade them wholesome things that had been made lawful to them, and for their barring many from the way of Allah, and for their taking usury, though they had»

«been forbidden it» — in the Torah — «and for their devouring people's wealth wrongfully» — by bribes in judgement — «And We have prepared for the unbelievers among them a painful punishment» (Q. 4:161) — causing pain. «But the firmly grounded» — the steadfast — «in knowledge among them» — such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām — «and the believers» — the Emigrants and al-Anṣār — «believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you» (Q. 4:162) — of the Books. Firm grounding in knowledge is what profits. Whoever reads knowledge and finds no understanding and no light to lead him to the truth is like a donkey carrying books. The ulama of the Torah all read the Torah and what is in it; and ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām read the Torah and understood, and knowledge took firm root in him. When he met the Prophet ﷺ he pronounced the two testimonies of faith (al-shahādatān): ⟨I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.⟩ He said: ⟨This is no face of a liar!⟩ And he said: ⟨When I saw him, by Allah, I found that I knew him better than I know my own son⟩ — as the Qurʾan said. This was because of the firm rooting of ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām's knowledge. And the Jews who read and did not understand and stood frozen with the texts were veiled from

«told you of» (Q. 4:164). In this verse he mentioned that Allah sent messengers whose accounts He narrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and sent messengers whose accounts He did not narrate to him. Al-Jalāl said: ⟨It is related that He, Exalted, sent eight thousand prophets, four thousand from the Children of Isrāʾīl and four thousand from the rest of mankind⟩ — he said this in Sūrat Ghāfir. Al-Suyūṭī disavowed this statement because of its weakness and its feebleness. This is a very weak report, and for that reason the commentator disavowed attributing it to himself and attributed it to the one who said it, who is Jalāl al-Maḥallī. What is well known is that Allah sent, of the prophets,

[…] one hundred and twenty-four thousand, half of them from the Children of Isrāʾīl and half of them from the rest of mankind. The messengers among them are three hundred and thirteen, or fourteen, or fifteen, according to the differing reports; and it is said two hundred and twenty-four thousand. All of this is the sayings of the ulama. And since Allah

in His saying «And messengers We have told you of before, and messengers We have not told you of» (Q. 4:164), we do not know how anyone could find his way to knowing their number. Among them is one of whom Allah told, and among them is one of whom He did not tell. The truth is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, manifested Himself by all His names upon the prophets: each name manifested itself in a prophet, just as each prophet is manifested in a walī. On this reckoning, the number of the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) and the number of the prophets — none knows them but Allah, because they are the number of the names. And the multiplicity of the names is His making Himself known, in that every atom in existence has a name manifested in it other than the one manifested in another. Just as the Presence of the Essence has no end and no one encompasses it, and the Presence of the Attributes likewise, so the Presence of the Names likewise. And when the names manifest themselves in the prophets, or the Presence of prophethood manifests itself in the awliyāʾ, the matter remains as it is. «And Allah spoke to Mūsā directly» (Q. 4:164) — without intermediary. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, spoke to Mūsā at Mount Ṭūr in intimate converse, after He had set up a veil of darkness beyond six hundred parasangs and manifested Himself by His light, so that the devils (shayāṭīn) and the jinn and the wild beasts and even the insects drew aside. So Mūsā heard the speech of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, without letter and without sound and without word. Of this speech Mūsā said that it was harder upon him than thunderclaps coming one after another upon him, and sweeter than the pleasure of sexual union ten thousand times over; and he hears with the whole of himself — his entire essence became hearing — and he hears the speech from every direction. It has no direction and no letter and no language and no sound. This is the speech of Allah. It was said to him: ⟨Where is Mūsā?⟩ He said:
⟨I am not Mūsā, nor do I know Mūsā.⟩ And this was at Ṭūr. If this intimate converse was an exalted station,

Man, in this form, had it as his due to recognize Allah, Blessed and Exalted, without the mediation of the messengers, because man knows by his intellect that every made thing must have a maker: the made thing does not stand except by a maker. If he sees a building, he knows that there is a builder. Even the donkey, which has no intellect — when a blow comes to it, it flees from the direction of the blow: it knows that there is one striking. When Allah made Himself known to us, the first thing He said — as in Sūrat al-Naḥl — was «He created the heavens and the earth» (Q. 16:3), «He created man from a drop of fluid» (Q. 16:4). Whoever looks into the heaven and the earth, and looks into man, knows that this made thing must have a maker. So our intellect brings us to the knowledge that there is an ilāh (deity); but the knowledge of that ilāh in His attributes, His names and His acts, and the knowledge of His command and His prohibition, His punishment and His bliss, His good pleasure as against His wrath — to this, had the prophets not come, no one would be guided. It is not possible for the intellect to apprehend a shariʿa without a prophet. So for this reason, had the prophets and the messengers not come, it would not be possible for us to worship Allah, Blessed and Exalted, even though it is possible for us to know the existence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So He sent the messengers to cut off the plea of anyone who would plead ignorance. Now, if a man falls into unbelief (kufr) or into error and stands before Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and pleads ignorance, Allah says: I sent the messengers; and after the messengers the ulama remained, and ⟨the ulama are the heirs of the prophets⟩, and by that He cut off their excuse.

«But Allah bears witness» — this came down when the Jews were asked about his prophethood ﷺ and they denied it. The unbelievers came to the Messenger ﷺ and said: Who bears witness for you to your prophethood, when the scholars of the two Books

have all denied your prophethood? Where is the witness? Allah said: «But Allah bears witness» — if they refuse to render the testimony, then Allah makes your prophethood plain — «by what He has sent down to you» — of the inimitable Qurʾan — «He sent it down with His knowledge» — knowing it. Allah, Blessed and Exalted: every prophet He sent, He joined his sending to the giving of a miracle; that miracle stands in the place of Allah's rising and bearing witness for this prophet that he is truthful. And Muḥammad ﷺ was given of the miracles what no prophet before him was given; those miracles are Allah's testimony for the Messenger ﷺ. So for this reason it does not come from a man of intellect that he should disbelieve in Muḥammad and believe in a prophet, because the proof of all the prophets is only the miracles, and he brought the miracles. How, then, should one who wishes to hold some prophet other than him to be truthful disbelieve in Muḥammad? And if a man holds that Muḥammad is not a prophet — everyone who saw the Messenger ﷺ and his effect upon the world knew that he is better than the prophets. «And the angels bear witness» — for you. All the angels bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. «And Allah suffices as a witness» (Q. 4:166) — you have no need of the angels' testimony, because Allah is enough for you and sufficient for you. «Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels, and those possessed of knowledge» (Q. 3:18), «The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers» (Q. 2:285). The first to bear witness to the oneness of Allah is Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and the first to believe in the Messenger is the Messenger ﷺ, and those possessed of knowledge after him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the best of deeds. He said: ⟨Knowledge.⟩ They said: We ask about deeds and you answer about knowledge? He said: ⟨With knowledge a little deed profits, and with ignorance much deed does not profit.⟩

«Indeed those who disbelieve» — in Allah — «and bar» — people — «from the way of Allah» — the religion of Islam, by their concealing the description of Muḥammad ﷺ; and they are the Jews — «have gone far astray» — from the truth (Q. 4:167). «Indeed those who disbelieve» — in Allah — «and have done wrong» — to His prophet, by concealing his description — «Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a way»

of the ways (Q. 4:168) — «except the way of Hell» — the way that leads to it — «abiding» — decreed to abide — «therein» — once they have entered it — «forever; and that is easy for Allah» — a light thing (Q. 4:169). «O people» — of Mecca — «the Messenger has come to you» — Muḥammad ﷺ — «with the truth from your Lord, so believe» — in him — and purpose — «good for you» — believe in the Messenger and purpose good; or: believe in the Messenger, [and] it will be better for you than what you are in — «and if you disbelieve» — in him — «then to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and the earth» — in possession, in creation and as servants (Q. 4:170) — so your unbelief does not harm Him
«And Allah is knowing» — of His creation — «wise» — in His making (Q. 4:170). «O People of the Book» — the people of the Gospel — «Do not»

«go to excess» — do not pass beyond the limit — «in your religion» — do not commit excess in your religion — «and say nothing of Allah but the truth» — nothing but the true word, declaring Him free of partner and of child — «Indeed the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, is the Messenger of Allah and His word, which He cast» — conveyed it — «to Maryam, and a spirit» — possessed of a spirit — «from Him» — from Allah, Blessed and Exalted (Q. 4:171).

ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace, is a son to Maryam: she carried him and bore him as the rest of women do, and she suckled him. He is the Messenger of Allah: Allah sent him as a messenger like the rest of the prophets and messengers. And he is the word of Allah, because he issued from a word alone, without a father. And a spirit, possessed of a spirit, from Him — this is an attribution of honour, not as they claimed, that since he was a spirit from Allah that entails that he is a part of Allah, and so he is His son. al-Rashīd had a Christian youth who was his physician and was accomplished in learning and in craft, and al-Rashīd loved him greatly and called him to Islam, and he refused; and every time he called him to Islam, he refused. One day al-Rashīd said to him: I do wish that you were a Muslim; were you a Muslim I would do such and such and such for you. He said to him: A verse (āya) in your Book keeps me from Islam, one that supports what I hold. al-Rashīd said to him: And what is it? He said: «Indeed the Messiah, ʿĪsā son of Maryam, is the Messenger of Allah and His word, which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him» (Q. 4:171). The Qurʾan says that ʿĪsā is a spirit from Allah, and this entails that he is a part of Allah; and that cannot be sound unless he is a son to Him. al-Rashīd was perplexed, and he gathered the ulama and asked them. They said to him: Pilgrims from Khurāsān have arrived here, and among them is a scholar learned in the tafsīr (Qurʾanic commentary) of the Qurʾan; he must surely have the answer to your question. So they sent to al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī al-Marwazī, and he came. He said to them: What is this specious objection that the enemy of Allah has cast at me? He reflected. He said: It was decreed in pre-eternity that this question should fall to me in your assembly, and I do not have its answer now; but it is upon me not to eat and not to drink until I render the due that is the answer to this objection. Open a room for me. So they opened a room for him, and he shut the room upon himself and read the Qurʾan from its beginning. He went on reciting the Qurʾan with reflection until he reached Sūrat al-Jāthiya: «And He has made subject to you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all of it, from Him» (Q. 45:13). Then he said: Open to me, open to me, for I have found an answer. So they opened, and he informed the youth and said to him: If «and a spirit from Him» entails that ʿĪsā is a part of Allah, then everything in the heavens and everything in the earth, all of it, is a part of Allah, because He said «and a spirit from Him» and He said «And He has made subject to you what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, all of it, from Him». So the Christian became a Muslim, and al-Rashīd rejoiced with a great rejoicing and rewarded him with much wealth. This spirit is the thing by which the Christians went astray, and so Allah named them those who go astray: they strayed from the knowledge of the truth. As for the Jews, they knew the truth and did not act by it, and so Allah was angry with them; and the Christians strayed from the straight path. The spirit of Allah in reality is Muḥammad ﷺ: from his spirit it was breathed into Ādam, and from his spirit it was breathed into ʿĪsā, and from his spirit it was breathed into a lowly fluid and it became a human being, and from his spirit it was breathed into Jibrīl, and from his spirit is this Qurʾan which we recite and which guides us to a straight path. «So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say» — the deities are — «Three»
Do not say that the deities are three. They went astray after ʿĪsā and split into four factions: a faction said that ʿĪsā

is the servant of Allah and His messenger — these are the ones who remained upon the religion of ʿĪsā; and a faction claimed that ʿĪsā is a son to Allah; and a faction claimed that ʿĪsā is Allah; and a faction claimed that the deities are three: ʿĪsā, his mother, and Allah. And 'the third of three' Allah has forbidden, as will come: «Those who say that Allah is the third of three have certainly disbelieved» (Q. 5:73) — and ⟨whoever imitates a people is one of them⟩, inasmuch as 'the third of three' is unbelief.

«that Allah is the third of three» — and ⟨whoever imitates a people is one of them⟩, inasmuch as 'the third of three' is unbelief. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, mentioned in the Qurʾan: «There is no secret counsel of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, nor fewer than that nor more but He is with them» (Q. 58:7) — yet He did not say 'He is their third'. He began the speech with «There is no secret counsel of three but He is their fourth» out of caution against saying 'He is their third'. And two — with every two Allah is their third; but since 'the third of three' is a creed of unbelief, the Qurʾan avoided this expression, and said: «There is no secret counsel of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, nor fewer than that nor more but He is with them». For this a man flees from resembling them: ⟨whoever imitates a people is one of them⟩!

«Desist» — from that, and bring — «what is better for you» — than it, which is al-tawḥīd (the divine oneness) (Q. 4:171). Abandon this creed and bring tawḥīd. In the Torah there are expressions which are what
led the Christians astray, and their intellects are deficient. The Qurʾan contains verses (āyāt)

muḥkamāt (unambiguous verses) and mutashābihāt (ambiguous verses). But this community — their intellects are ample, their comprehension complete. Allah ennobled Muḥammad with an ennobling greater than the ennobling of ʿĪsā. Each of them grew up weak; his people made him their enemy and made war on him. ʿĪsā remained weak until his enemies prevailed over him and claimed that they had killed him and crucified him. And Muḥammad grew up weak, and Allah gave him victory until he overcame the multitudes and triumphed over them, so that they all became his dependents. Had the intellects of this community been like the intellects of the Christians, we would have gone astray over Muḥammad and made him other than a servant — above the servants. But all of us know that, for all his honour and his nobility and the loftiness of his rank, he is a servant of Allah and nothing more. And these went astray and made their prophet a deity, or a son of Allah — and 'the Father' in the idiom of the Gospel is 'the Master'; whenever the word 'the Father' comes in the Gospel it means 'the Master'. They took it upon its outward sense only. And in

the Torah: Allah came to the olive, and went on to Mount Sinai, and dwelt in Fārān after that. The olive is the mountain upon which ʿĪsā lived in his time, and he is the vicegerent (khalīfa) of Allah. So he said that Allah came to the olive, and he means the vicegerent of Allah, who is ʿĪsā. Then He went on to the Mount — He came from Mount Sinai. Mount Sinai is where Mūsā was, a vicegerent for Allah; and so the vicegerency (khilāfa) passed to the olive, which is ʿĪsā; then it passed to Fārān and He dwelt there. Fārān is a name of Mecca. This points to three vicegerents on behalf of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: Mūsā and ʿĪsā and Muḥammad.

And to this points «and the olive, and Mount Sīnīn, and this town» (Q. 95:1–3) — each of them is the place of one of these vicegerents. «Allah is only one god, glory be to Him» — declaring Him free of that — «that He should have a son» — a son does not befit Him — «To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth» — by creation and by ownership, and ownership is incompatible with sonship — «and Allah suffices as a guardian» (Q. 4:171) — a witness to that. The lack of a son is a deficiency with respect to man, and a son is a deficiency with respect to al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted, because man desires to have a son who will be a help to him in the works he undertakes, and an heir to him after his death; and Allah is self-sufficient in His own essence, He desires no help, and He abides forever, He does not die and so be inherited from. What need has He of a son? So for this He argued against them with His saying «Glory be to Him; He is the Self-Sufficient» (Q. 10:68) — He is the Self-Sufficient; what has He to do with a son? We love children because of our poverty and our need, and He is self-sufficient: what has He to do with a son? So for this the lack of a son is a deficiency in our case, and a son is a deficiency in
His case, and a reviling. ⟨The son of Ādam has called Me a liar and reviled Me. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has taken a son'.⟩ «He will never disdain»

to be proud and to disdain — «the Messiah, to be a servant to Allah». When the Christians of Najrān said that the Prophet ﷺ had reviled ʿĪsā, because he said that he is only a servant while ʿĪsā is above that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: ⟨ʿĪsā will never disdain to be a servant to Him.⟩ «nor the angels brought near» — even the angels, who are with Allah, did not disdain to be servants to Allah. It is true that ʿĪsā is a spirit that was clothed with a body, and his spirituality prevailed over his corporeality; but since the angels, who are pure spirits and have not been clothed with a body, did not disdain to be servants, then all the more so ʿĪsā, who in any case has a body like the bodies of men. «And whoever disdains His worship and is proud — He will gather them all to Himself» (Q. 4:172). Whoever was too proud to be a servant of Allah will come on the Day of Resurrection a servant. «As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their wages in full» — the recompense of their deeds — «and He will increase them out of His bounty» (Q. 4:173) — what no eye has seen and no ear has heard and what has not occurred to the heart of a human being. Recite, if you will: «No soul knows what has been hidden for them of delight for the eyes, a recompense»

«And as for those who disdained and were proud» — of His worship — «He will punish them with a painful punishment» — an agonizing one; it is the punishment of the Fire — «and they will not find for themselves, apart from Allah» — other than Him — «any protector» — to ward it off from them — «nor any helper» (Q. 4:173) — to shield them from it. «O people» — the community of Muḥammad — «there has come to you a proof» — an argument — «from your Lord» (Q. 4:174) — against you; and it is Muḥammad ﷺ. Every messenger comes with a proof along with him, and to us there came a messenger who is himself a proof from our Lord, Blessed and Exalted — whereas Mūsā, his proof was in his staff: «So he cast his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent» (Q. 7:107)

And ʿĪsā — a table was sent down from heaven; and Ṣāliḥ — he brought forth a she-camel from the mountain. Each of them has his proof in something other than his own self; but the Messenger ﷺ is himself a proof from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and every part of his parts is a proof from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So the proof of his two eyes: he used to say, ⟨Straighten the ranks, for I see you from behind me as I see you in front of me.⟩ And the proof of his sight: «The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress» (Q. 53:17). And the proof of his nose: he said, ⟨I find the breath of al-Raḥmān from the direction of Yemen⟩ — that is, he smelled the fragrance of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, from the direction of Yemen. So after his death, in the caliphate of ʿUmar, Uways al-Qaranī came forth, the vicegerent of Allah in Yemen; he is the one whose fragrance the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

used to smell in his lifetime. This is the proof of his nose. And the proof of his two hands: «And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw» (Q. 8:17), «Those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to Allah; the hand of Allah is above their hands» (Q. 48:10). And the proof of his heart: «The heart did not lie about what it saw» (Q. 53:11). And the proof of his breast: ⟨he would pray and in his breast there was a bubbling like the bubbling of a cauldron, out of fear of Allah, Blessed and Exalted⟩. And the proof of his tongue: «Nor does he speak out of caprice; it is only a revelation revealed» (Q. 53:3–4). So when these limbs were all gathered together, his whole self became a proof. He went out from the earth and passed beyond the seven heavens and the Throne and the Footstool, until he reached the station of «he drew near and hung suspended» (Q. 53:8); and he passed beyond it to the station of «the measure of two bows»; and he passed beyond it to the station of «or nearer» (Q. 53:9). So for this Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said «There has come to you a proof from your Lord» (Q. 4:174). Muḥammad is himself a proof, and every part of his parts is a proof, whereas the prophets before him each had his proof in something other than himself. «We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and in themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth» (Q. 41:53). «And We have sent down to you a manifest light» (Q. 4:174) — it is Muḥammad ﷺ, He named him a light; or it is the Qurʾan, He named it a light, because it makes clear the truth from the false — «As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty, and He will guide them to Himself on a straight path» (Q. 4:175) — a road

straight — it is the religion of Islam. «They ask you for a ruling» — concerning the kalāla (one who dies leaving neither child nor parent) — «Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalāla» (Q. 4:176). They asked him
«If a man perishes» — he died — «having no child» — nor a parent; and that is the kalāla — «and he has»

«a sister» — from both his parents, or from the father — «then she has half of what he left» — she inherits from her brother the half — «and he» — the brother — «inherits from her if she has no child» — so if she has a male child, he has nothing; or a female, then he has what is left over from her share. And the sister or the brother may be from the mother, and his appointed portion is the sixth, as came earlier at the beginning of the sura — «then if they be» — the two sisters — «two» — or more, for it came down concerning Jābir, and he died leaving sisters — «then they have two thirds of what he left. And if they be» — the heirs — «brothers and sisters, men and women, then the male has the like of the portion of two females. Allah makes clear to you» — the laws of your religion — «lest you go astray» — that you not go astray — «and Allah is knowing of everything» (Q. 4:176) — and of that is the inheritance. It came down concerning Jābir, who died having neither child nor parent. Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ said: O Messenger of Allah, I am leaving behind

much wealth and I have no child; shall I give it in alms? He said: ⟨No.⟩ He said: shall I give the half in alms? He said: ⟨No, the half is much.⟩ He said: the third? He said: ⟨Yes, and the third is much. That you leave your heirs wealthy is better for you than that you leave them destitute, begging from people.⟩ So this verse came down concerning Jābir. Allah made clear the rulings of inheritance and Himself undertook the division of the estates, for Allah charged no messenger and no prophet brought near with the division of the estates. He has made obligatory

upon us the prayer, the fast, the zakat and the hajj, and He charged the Messenger ﷺ with making these things clear to us. It is he who made clear to us the manner of the prayer, that it is five prayers: this one is four cycles of the prayer (rakʿas), this one is three cycles, this one is two cycles; and he made clear to us the zakat, and he made clear to us the fast, and he made clear to us the hajj. Indeed He charged him ﷺ with making clear the whole Qurʾan: «that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them» (Q. 16:44) — it is he who expounded the whole Qurʾan to us.

As for the estates, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, undertook their division, because people are moulded upon the love of this world and eagerness for wealth; and the inheritance, since it gives to some people and deprives other people — had the Messenger himself undertaken this, there would have been in the hearts of some of them something against him ﷺ, and whoever hates him is wretched with a wretchedness after which there is no happiness ever. So Allah undertook the division of the estates and charged no one with it. The science of the appointed shares of inheritance (farāʾiḍ) has been described as half of knowledge, and it is a small compass, which a man completes in a short span. How is it half of knowledge, when knowledge multiplies without end? That is because man has only two states, life or death: so long as he is alive all the rulings run upon him, and when he dies there remains for him nothing but the appointed shares, nothing but the science of inheritance. For this it came to be half of knowledge.
Sūrat al-Māʾida
Medinan; one hundred and twenty-two verses; the last sura to be sent down.

«By Allah's Name: The Entirely Merciful, The Especially Merciful. O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts» — the ratified covenants that are between you and Allah, and those that are between you and the people — «There has been made lawful for you the beast of the cattle» — the beasts, all of them, are lawful: the camel and the ox

and the sheep, all of them, after the slaughtering. «except what is recited to you» — its prohibition, in «There have been forbidden to you the carrion» (Q. 5:3), to the end of the verse. So the exception is disjunctive, though it may also be conjunctive — «not holding lawful the game» — do not hold the game lawful — «while you are consecrated» — so long as you remain inviolate, consecrated in ritual consecration (iḥrām) for the hajj or the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumra) — «Indeed Allah decrees what He wills» (Q. 5:1) — of making lawful and the like; there is no objecting to Him. Al-Naqqāsh was an eloquent man, fluent in Arabic. One day he was called upon and it was said to him: can you make for us two lines only, like the Qurʾan? He said: two lines only — yes; for Allah issued His challenge with three verses, but as for two lines, I am able. So they shut a house upon him, and he remained three days and came out. He said: I am not able, and no one is able. I opened the written codex (muṣḥaf) when I entered the house, and there came out upon me the opening of «O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts. There has been made lawful for you the beast of the cattle, except what is recited to you, not holding lawful the game while you are consecrated. Indeed Allah decrees what He wills» (Q. 5:1) — two lines in which He made lawful all that He made lawful with an absolute making-lawful, and forbade all that He forbade with an absolute forbidding, and made exception twice, and commanded and forbade and praised Himself in a single line: «Indeed Allah decrees what He wills». «O you who have believed, do not profane the sacred rites of Allah» (Q. 5:2). A man came with sparks flying off him; he came to the Messenger ﷺ in Medina the Illumined, and when he was about to enter, the Messenger ﷺ said:

⟨There will enter upon you a man whose tongue is the tongue of a hypocrite and whose heart is the heart of a devil.⟩ Then he entered and claimed that he wanted Islam, so he instructed him in the two testimonies of faith (al-shahādatān), and he went out. He found the camels of the Companions outside Medina and stole them all and drove them off and fled to his people. They searched, and found no news of him. In the following year the Companions went out for the hajj, and when they entered the sanctuary they saw him driving the garlanded [camels]. They said: this is so-and-so, the driver of our camels; we must kill him — and they were in the sanctuary. So there came down: «O you who have believed, do not profane the sacred rites of Allah» — that is, the landmarks of His religion, by hunting, or by setting upon a wrongdoer in the sanctuary — «nor the sacred month» — by fighting in it — «nor the offering» — [the offering of] one who has driven his offering — «nor the garlanded» — and has garlanded them; so do not
you molest it. And do not make lawful «those repairing to the Sacred House» — those making for the Sacred House for the hajj; do not fight them
«seeking bounty» — provision — «from their Lord» — by trade — «and good pleasure» — from Him, by their making for it, in their corrupt supposition — «And when»
«you are released» — from ritual consecration for the pilgrimage (iḥrām) — «then hunt» — a command of permissibility (ibāḥa) — «and let it not drive you» — bring upon you — «the hatred of a people»

that is, the detestation of a people — «because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, that you transgress» — even the unbelievers of Quraysh who kept you from the Sacred House: do not transgress against them by killing in it, and still less against others than them — «And help one another to piety» — the doing of what you have been commanded — «and godfearing» — by leaving what you have been forbidden — «and do not help one another» — in it — «in sin» — acts of disobedience — «and transgression» — overstepping the bounds of Allah — «and fear Allah» — fear His punishment, by obeying Him — «indeed Allah is severe in punishment» (Q. 5:2) — for whoever opposes Him. «Forbidden to you is carrion» — the forbidden things among foods are these: eating carrion is forbidden, what has died of itself — «and blood» — that which is poured forth, the blood that comes out at the time of the slaughter — «and the flesh of swine» — forbidden, whether it was slaughtered or was not slaughtered — «and what has been consecrated to other than Allah» — in that it was slaughtered in the name of another than Him. The slaughter is in the name of Allah alone; it does not suffice in the name of any other than Allah — even the mention of the Messenger Muḥammad at the slaughter is forbidden — «and the strangled» — the one dead by strangling; so if a cow or a sheep is strangled and dies, it is carrion — «and the beaten to death» — the one killed by beating; if it is struck with a staff and falls dead, it is not to be eaten — «and the fallen» — the one that falls from a height to a low place and dies — «and the gored»

the one killed by another's goring of it — «and what the wild beast has eaten» — of it — «except what you have slaughtered» — you caught it with the spirit still in it, among these things, and slaughtered it. These things, if they have died, or have reached a state in which they must inevitably die, whether they are slaughtered or are not slaughtered, are carrion; and what you caught with the spirit still in it and slaughtered, and it moved after the slaughter and the blood flowed from it, is lawful — «and what has been slaughtered on the idol-stones» — in the name of the idol — «and that you seek division» — that you seek the apportionment and the ruling — «by the divining arrows» — the shafts from which the unbelievers used to take knowledge of the unseen. They had seven shafts with the keeper of the Kaʿba: one, 'my Lord has commanded me'; one, 'my Lord has forbidden me'; one, 'from you'; one, 'from other than you';

one, 'blood-money' or indemnity; one, left blank. If a man wanted to do any matter, he would come to the idol, and the keeper of the Kaʿba would bring something of water, and he would shake the shafts and set [them down]. If the shaft on which was written 'my Lord has commanded me' came out to him, he went out to what he wanted and said that the idol had commanded him to that, and that he had found the permission (idhn) from his lord. And if 'my Lord has forbidden me' came out, he desisted and said that his lord had forbidden him. And if they differed over the lineage of a child that was born, and disputed over its father, they came to the shaft: if 'from you' came out, they attached it to the lineage, and if 'from other than you' came out, they disowned it. And if a man was slain, if 'blood-money' came out they imposed the indemnity in his case, and if the blank came out they let it lie, that there was no indemnity in it. These are the divining arrows (azlām) by which they used to seek division before Islam. And there falls under it every prying into the unseen by a way not sanctioned by the Law; there falls under it whoever goes to the diviner and the soothsayers, and the seeking of guidance by dreams (istikhāra), and the tables — all this falls under this heading. As for the prophetic seeking of guidance, it is that you pray two cycles of the prayer (rakʿas) for Allah and supplicate that Allah choose for you what is better for you; whatever comes to pass after that is good. That is what agrees with the Law. As for prying into the unseen, that is contrary to the Law. «That is a transgression» (Q. 5:3) — a going out from obedience. And there came down at ʿArafa in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: «Today those who have disbelieved have despaired of your religion» — the Messenger ﷺ, when he emigrated to Medina and the ninth year came,

he set Abū Bakr over the pilgrims, and he ﷺ did not perform the hajj himself. When Abū Bakr had gone out, he sent ʿAlī after him, riding the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he came, Abū Bakr said to him: ⟨Am I the one sent and you the commander, or not?⟩ He said: ⟨No — you are the commander, and I am sent with you with the verses of Barāʾa, thirty verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Tawba.⟩ In them the Qurʾan annulled the covenants that were between the Muslims and the unbelievers at the beginning of Islam, and forbade that any polytheist should circumambulate the House after that year. They were barred from the hajj. The Arabs, for all their unbelief, used to perform the hajj every year, and in that year it was forbidden that any polytheist should make the pilgrimage to the House after that year. And in the tenth year he ﷺ went out himself and performed the Farewell Pilgrimage. When he entered consecration at Dhū al-Ḥulayfa, seventy thousand persons entered consecration with him. When he said Labbayka Llāhumma labbayka — here I am, O Allah, here I am — and the company said it, the voices of the pilgrims reached to the heaven. And when they entered Mecca and the Muslims saw the gathering of the pilgrims, this verse (āya) came down: «Today those who have disbelieved have despaired of your religion» — the unbelievers did not despair of the Muslims' apostatizing until the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage, when they saw his strength ﷺ — «do not fear them, but fear Me» — do not fear the unbelievers; fear none but Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And when he stood at ʿArafāt there came down: «Today I have perfected your religion for you» — its rulings and its obligatory duties. After this verse no obligation came down, neither lawful nor unlawful — «and I have completed My favour upon you» — by perfecting it; and it is said, by the entry into Mecca — «and I am well pleased» — I have chosen — «with Islam for you as religion» (Q. 5:3). A Jew said to ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him: ⟨A verse in your Book — had it come down upon us, the company of the Jews, we would have taken the day of its coming down as a feast.⟩ ʿUmar said: ⟨And which verse?⟩ He said: «Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favour upon you and am well pleased with Islam for you as religion» (Q. 5:3). ʿUmar said: ⟨We know the day of its coming down, and the Prophet ﷺ standing at ʿArafāt on the day of⟩

⟨Friday.⟩ ʿUmar answered him that the Muslims had taken the day of its coming down as two feasts: Friday is a feast day, and ʿArafa is a feast day. And on that day the feasts of all the communities came together — Friday, and the day of ʿArafa, and the feast day of the Christians, and the feast day of the Jews, and the feast day of the Magians: all of them fell on that day, and the feasts of the communities have not coincided on a single day before it or after it. When this verse came down, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, wept. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ⟨And why?⟩ He said: ⟨Because we were always in increase, and today, when He has perfected our religion for us, we know that the increase has come to an end; and a thing that does not increase must needs decrease.⟩ So ʿUmar was the most understanding of the Companions. This verse gave notice of the nearness of the death of the Messenger ﷺ: after eighty-two or eighty-three days he ﷺ died. «Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favour upon you and am well pleased with Islam for you as religion» (Q. 5:3). And the Prophet ﷺ said, while standing at ʿArafāt: ⟨A servant whom Allah gave the choice between what is with Him and remaining in this world for whatever span he wished, and he chose what is with Allah.⟩ So Abū Bakr wept, and said

the people: look at this old man! The Messenger ﷺ mentions a servant whom Allah gave a choice, and he chose a thing that is with Him — what has Abū Bakr to do with weeping at this? But Abū Bakr understood that the servant given the choice was the Messenger ﷺ, and he knew that if Allah gave him the choice between what is with Him and this world, he would never choose this world. So this was an announcement of the death of the Messenger ﷺ. In that standing of his ﷺ he said: ⟨Take from me your rites of pilgrimage, for perhaps I shall not perform the hajj after this year.⟩
And it was as he said ﷺ. And in that

standing he said: ⟨Lo, do not turn back after me as unbelievers, striking one another's necks. What day is this? What town is this? What month is this?⟩ He asked until we thought that he would change the name. He said: ⟨What town is this? What town is this?⟩ They said: ⟨Allah and His Messenger know best.⟩ He said: ⟨Is it not the Town?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ He said: ⟨What day is this? What day is this? What day is this? Is it not the day of the Feast?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes indeed.⟩ He said: ⟨What month is this? Is it not Dhū al-Ḥijja?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes indeed.⟩

He said: ⟨Indeed Allah has made inviolable to you the blood of the Muslims, and their honour, and their property, like the inviolability of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this town of yours. Lo, have I conveyed?⟩ They said: ⟨We bear witness that you have conveyed.⟩ He said: ⟨O Allah, bear witness. O Allah,⟩
⟨bear witness⟩, and he points with his index finger to the sky: ⟨Lo, have I conveyed?⟩ They say: you have conveyed the message and discharged the trust.
He says: ⟨O Allah, bear witness.⟩

At that standing the Messenger ﷺ gave word of everything that had been and everything that will be until the Day of Resurrection, down to the last child to be born, whereupon the Hour will rise — the Messenger ﷺ mentioned it. The Companions used to say: whenever something arose anew, we would recognise it from the saying of the Messenger ﷺ, as you forget a person who has been away from you and then, when he is present before you, you remember him. Whenever a thing came, we would simply remember it from what the Messenger ﷺ had told us of. «So whoever is compelled in a state of starvation» — famine — to eating something of what has been forbidden him, and he eats it — «not inclining» — leaning — «to sin» — to disobedience — «then indeed Allah is forgiving» — to him for what he ate — «merciful» (Q. 5:3) — to him in making it permissible to him. «They ask you what has been made lawful to them» — of food — «Say: lawful to you are the good things» — the delectable things, all of them lawful — «and what you have taught» — that is, the quarry of what you have taught — «of the hunting animals» — those that earn their prey, among dogs, beasts of prey and birds — «training them as hounds» — that is, setting them loose upon the game — «teaching them» — that is, you discipline them — «of what Allah has taught you» — of the ādāb (proprieties) of the hunt — «so eat of what they have caught for you» — even if they have killed it. It is lawful to eat the game if

the dog was trained and set loose with the name of Allah, and it killed and did not eat. «And mention the name of Allah over it» — when you set it loose — «and fear Allah; indeed Allah is swift in reckoning» (Q. 5:4). «Today the good things are made lawful to you» — the delectable among foods — «and the food of those who were given the Book» — that is, the slaughtered animals of the Jews and the Christians — «is lawful to you» — permitted. Food here — what is meant by it is the slaughtering only, because what is other than slaughtering among foods presents no difficulty in it. If a Jew or a Christian slaughters an animal, then eating its flesh is lawful for every Muslim. «and your food is lawful to them» — the food of the Muslims is likewise lawful to the People of the Book — «and the chaste women among the believing women» — the free women among the believing women; giving them in marriage is lawful — «and the chaste women» — the free women — «from among those who were given the Book before you» — the free women of the Jews and the free women of the Christians: giving them in marriage is permitted, it is lawful for you to marry them — «when you have given them their wages»

— their dowries — «chastely wedded, not as fornicators» — openly committing fornication with them. Fornication is named sifāḥ (pouring out). Sifāḥ is the pouring out, because the one who marries has a praiseworthy purpose, which is the seeking of a child and compliance with the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, while the fornicator has no purpose but the pouring out of the semen only; and for this it is named sifāḥ, and he musāfiḥ. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made lawful in this verse the giving of believing women in marriage to one another, because they are upon a sound religion, and the giving of Jewish and Christian women in marriage, because they are People of the Book — and though they have altered and substituted and swerved from the path, their religion is heaven-sent. As for the polytheist women who have professed no heaven-sent religion, they have no right to marriage with the Muslims. Giving polytheist women and the Magians in marriage is forbidden; and the difference between them and these others is that those [the People of the Book], though they are unbelievers, are upon a heaven-sent nurture, while these have had no prior heaven-sent nurture, and it is not fitting for a Muslim to marry from among them. «nor taking paramours» — from among them, with whom you commit fornication in secret. Marriage in the Jāhiliyya was of four kinds. The marriage known today: that the man comes to the woman's guardian and brings a dowry, and he contracts her to him. And a woman — a man would come to her and marry her, and another would come and marry her; and when she bore a child, they would gather the trackers (al-qāfa) to look, and when they said, ‘the child has in him the blood of so-and-so’, they attached him to so-and-so, and he would be the father. The Arabs used to love nobility of stock in children: if they saw a household whose traits of character were praiseworthy and who were

champions and possessed of noble traits of character, one of them would love to get a child like them. He says to his wife: when you have become pure, you will go to so-and-so and be with him as a wife to him until you conceive; when you have conceived, you will come back to me. So the wife comes to a man, consenting to remain with him as a wife to him, until, when she has conceived by him, she returns to her husband, so that the child may come out of noble stock; and they ascribe him to the father. And the women of the banners: the prostitutes who had banners, and they were just like shops, just like stalls — every man comes to them. The Muḥammadan shariʿa confirmed the first marriage, which is the contract by means of a guardian and a dowry and witnesses, and abolished all the other kinds of marriage; but if a man became Muslim, he was confirmed in his marriage, and the children who grew up out of unbelief are children who are attached [to their fathers] when they enter Islam. For this reason the shariʿa gave weight to their marriages after their entering Islam, as a comfort to them. Among the unbelievers there is no child of

fornication, because with them their contracts and other than them are alike; when they enter Islam, all of them — his lineage is sound. «And whoever disbelieves in the faith» — apostatises — «his deed has come to nothing» — his righteous deed before that, so it is not reckoned and he is not rewarded for it
«and in the hereafter he is among the losers» (Q. 5:5). «O you who believe, when you rise» — you intend to rise — «to the prayer» — and you being

in a state of minor ritual impurity — «then wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows» — this is the ablution — «and wipe your heads and your feet» — wash your feet — «up to the ankles. And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves» — then bathe — «And if you are ill» — with an illness that water would harm — «or on a journey» — travelling — «or one of you has come from the privy» — he has incurred ritual impurity — «or you have touched women» — the like of it has come before in the verse of al-Nisāʾ — «and you do not find water» — after seeking it — «then betake yourselves» — aim — «to good earth» — pure dust — «then wipe your faces and your hands» — together with the elbows — «with it» — with two strokes — «Allah does not wish to place upon you any hardship» — straitness. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, granted a dispensation in the ablution with earth (tayammum) when water is lacking or when one is unable to use it, because the religion of Allah is ease, in which there is no hardship. «but He wishes to purify you» — of ritual impurities and of sins — «and to complete His favour upon you» — through Islam, by the plain setting out of the ordinances of the religion — «that you may give thanks» (Q. 5:6) — for His favours. «And remember the favour of Allah upon you» — through Islam — «and His covenant by which He bound you» — He made a pact with you — «when you said: we have heard and we have obeyed. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is knowing of what lies within the breasts» (Q. 5:7) — of what is in the hearts; and of other than it, all the more so. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, imposed upon the one in a state of major impurity (junub) that he bathe — he washes the whole of his body — and upon the one in a state of minor impurity (muḥdith) that he perform the ablution; so the one in minor impurity, whether he has urinated or defecated, performs the ablution only. Why is the bath obligatory upon the emission of semen, while the bath is not obligatory upon the exit of excrement, which is by far more impure than semen and filthier? Because the appetite of intercourse engrosses the body of a person, so that he employs all the strength of his body, outwardly and inwardly, and for this reason the washing of the whole of his body is obligatory upon him — unlike food or drink, which you take in by a single extremity: eating is with the mouth, and drinking likewise, and for this reason nothing was made obligatory for them but the washing of the extremities. Or because intercourse is infrequent, so He made the bath obligatory in it, while urine and excrement recur often, so He was content with the washing of the extremities that are visible of people, such as the face

and the hands and the feet up to the ankles, as a lifting of hardship, because if a bath were obligatory in every [instance of] ritual impurity, it would be a hardship upon the Muslims. He said: «then betake yourselves to good earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it» — because He did not make clear the extent of the wiping. The sunna made plain the covering of the two limbs by the wiping, so al-Shāfiʿī was content with the wiping of the wrists, while Mālik said that it is to the elbows. As for the ablution, He stated the elbows expressly, and for this reason it is obligatory to
the elbows.
«O you who believe, be upholders» — ever standing — «for Allah» — in His rights — «witnesses in equity» — in justice — «and let not»

«let it drive you» — let it carry you — «the loathing of» — the hatred of — «a people, to your not dealing justly. Deal justly» — with the enemy and the friend — «it» — justice — «is nearer to godfearing» — there is no shariʿa that commands justice with the enemy save our shariʿa; our shariʿa has commanded us justice with the friend and justice with the enemy — «and fear Allah. Indeed Allah is aware of what you do» (Q. 5:8) — and so He requites you — «Allah has promised those who believe» — among you — «and do righteous deeds» — a goodly promise — «that they shall have forgiveness and a great reward» (Q. 5:9) — it is the Garden — «And those who have disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Blaze» (Q. 5:10). «O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you» (Q. 5:11). The occasion of this verse's revelation is that the Messenger ﷺ, when he came to al-Ḥudaybiya, a people of Quraysh purposed to stretch out their hands against them, to fall upon them treacherously, and Allah turned them back. Or when he came to Khaybar seeking that the Muslims assist him in the blood-money of a slain man, and they said to him: O Abū al-Qāsim, sit until we bring you food. So they went off, and a Jew climbed up and took an iron millstone they had and meant to drop it upon al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ so that he would die; and Jibrīl came to him and informed him, so he went out and returned to Medina. Or in the case we mentioned yesterday concerning Ghawrath, when he saw him far from his Companions and said: this is Muḥammad, far from his Companions; may Allah kill me if I do not kill him. So he came to him and meant to kill him with the sword, and Allah turned him back. Or Zaynab bt. al-Ḥārith
poisoned a sheep and fed it to him. «O you who believe, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when a people purposed to stretch out»
— in aggression — «to you their hands» — to fall upon you treacherously — «and He restrained their hands from you» — and preserved you from what they intended —

«And fear Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely» (Q. 5:11). «And Allah did take the covenant of the Children of Isrāʾīl» — by what will be mentioned hereafter — «and We raised up» — We appointed — «from among them twelve chiefs» — one from every tribe. The tribes (asbāṭ) of the Children of Isrāʾīl were twelve, and so Mūsā chose a chief from every tribe, and they were twelve: they are the chiefs of Mūsā — «and Allah said: Indeed I am with you» — with help and support — «If you establish the prayer and give the zakat and believe in My messengers and uphold them»

— you support them — «and you lend to Allah a goodly loan» — by spending — «I shall surely remit your evil deeds from you and shall surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers run. But whoever disbelieves after that from among you has indeed strayed from the level way» (Q. 5:12). So they broke the covenant. Allah Exalted said: «Then because of their breaking their covenant We cursed them» — We removed them far from Our mercy. «Then because of their breaking» — by their breaking their covenant — «and We made their hearts hard» — they do not soften to the acceptance of the truth — «they distort the words» — those that are in the Torah of the description of Muḥammad ﷺ — «from their places» — the places upon which Allah set them; that is, they alter them — «and they forgot» — they abandoned — «a portion» — a share — «of what they were reminded of» — commanded — «thereby» — in the Torah, of the following of
Muḥammad — «And you will not cease» — O Muḥammad — «to come upon» — to perceive — «a treachery» — an act of treachery — «from them» — and by the breaking of the covenant

«except a few of them» — those of them who submitted — «So pardon them and turn away. Indeed Allah loves those who do good» (Q. 5:13). This is abrogated by the verse of the sword. «And from those who said: we are Christians, We took their covenant» — likewise, as We took the covenant of the Children of Isrāʾīl — «and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of thereby» — in the Gospel — «so We stirred up» — We made it fall — «among them enmity and hatred until»

«the Day of Resurrection» — by their splitting apart and the divergence of their desires, so that every sect declares the other to be in unbelief — «And Allah will inform them» — in the hereafter — «of what they used to do» (Q. 5:14) — and so He requites them. «O People of the Book» — the Jews and the Christians — «Our Messenger has come to you» — Muḥammad — «making clear to you much of what you used to hide» — you conceal — «of the Book» — the Torah

and the Gospel — «and pardoning much» — of that — «There has come to you from Allah a light» — it is Muḥammad ﷺ — «and a Book» — a Qurʾan — «made clear, whereby He guides» — by the Book — «Allah, whoever follows His good pleasure» — in that he
believes — «to the ways of peace, and brings them out of the darknesses into the light» — faith — «by His permission» — by His will — «and He guides them»
«to a straight path» (Q. 5:16). «They have indeed disbelieved who said: Allah is the Messiah, son of Maryam» (Q. 5:17) — inasmuch as they made him an ilāh (a deity), and they are —
the Jacobites, a sect of the Christians. «Say: then who has power» — to ward off — «from» — the punishment of — «Allah anything, if»

«that He destroy the Messiah, son of Maryam, and his mother, and whoever is in the earth, all together» — no one has power over that, and had the Messiah been an ilāh (deity) he would have had power over it. «And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is powerful over everything» (Q. 5:17). «And the Jews and the Christians said: We are the sons of Allah» — each of the two groups said: we are the sons of Allah, that is, like His sons in nearness and in rank. Sons of Allah, because they said that they are the sons of ʿUzayr, and ʿUzayr is the son of Allah — «and His beloved ones»
They said that they are the beloved of Allah, relying on their being of the progeny of Ibrāhīm, and Ibrāhīm is khalīl Allāh (the intimate friend of Allah). They claimed this. «Say»

to them, O Muḥammad — «Then why does He punish you for your sins?» — if you are truthful in that? The father does not punish his son, and the ḥabīb (beloved) does not punish his ḥabīb, and Allah has punished you, so you are liars. «Rather, you are human beings from among those He created» — a kind of the children of
Ādam only; you have what they have and against you is what is against them. «He forgives whom He wills» — the forgiveness of him — «and He punishes whom He wills»

His punishing of him, with no objection against it. «And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the journey's end» (Q. 5:18). «O People of the Book»
«Our Messenger has come to you» — Muḥammad — «making clear to you» — the ordinances of the religion — «after an interval» — a cessation — «of the messengers»

since there was no messenger between him and ʿĪsā, and the span of that is five hundred and sixty-nine years. «Lest you say: No bearer of good tidings and no warner came to us» — had Muḥammad not come you would have said: no bearer of good tidings and no warner came to us — «Yet a bearer of good tidings and a warner has come to you, and Allah is powerful over everything» (Q. 5:19). Now Muḥammad has come, and he is a bearer of good tidings and a warner. Between Ādam and Nūḥ a thousand years, and between Nūḥ and Ibrāhīm a thousand years, and between Ibrāhīm and Mūsā two thousand years, and between Mūsā and ʿĪsā a thousand years, and between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad five hundred and sixty-nine years or six hundred years, and the Messenger ﷺ was sent. And now, after the Hijra of the Messenger ﷺ, one thousand three hundred and eighty-three years. And this world is seven days, and «indeed a day with your Lord is as a thousand years of what you count» (Q. 22:47). This world is seven days

seven thousand years. [Most of them] have passed; [what remains] will never reach a thousand, and there is no knowledge except with Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «And» — recall — «when Mūsā said to his people: O my people, remember the favour of Allah upon you, when He placed among you»

from among you — «prophets» — Allah made some of the prophets from the Children of Isrāʾīl — «and made you kings» — possessors of servants and retainers; the malik (king) is everyone who has a wife and a manservant and a maidservant: he is as though a malik. Or He made kings from among you.

«and gave you what He had not given to anyone of the worlds» (Q. 5:20) — of manna and quail and the parting of the sea and other than that. «O my people, enter the holy land» — the purified — «which Allah has written for you» — He commanded you to enter it, and it is Syria — «and do not turn back on your heels» — do not be routed in fear of the enemy — «for then you will turn back as losers» (Q. 5:21) — in your striving. «They said: O Mūsā, there is in it a people of great strength» — remnants of ʿĀd, tall, possessed of strength — «and we will never enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then we will enter» (Q. 5:22) — it. They turned coward and were afraid and refused the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and the command of the Messenger

«Two men said» — two men said to them — «of those who feared» — contravening the command of Allah — and the two of them were Yūshaʿ b. Nūn and Kālib b. Yūqannā, of the chiefs whom Mūsā had sent to uncover the condition of the giants. Mūsā appointed twelve chiefs, for every tribe a chief whom he would send to the tribe to which he belonged, and they would also bring word back to Mūsā from the tribe. So when Allah commanded the Children of Isrāʾīl to enter the holy land, and in it were giants, Mūsā sent twelve chiefs to find out the condition of the giants; and they saw, of the hugeness of their frames and the length of their statures, what bewildered them. When they returned, Yūshaʿ and Kālib said to them: ⟨Conceal what you have seen, except from Mūsā and Hārūn alone.⟩ But they did not conceal it.

They told the people the condition of the giants, and so they turned coward before them — except Kālib and Yūshaʿ alone.
