They were the two who feared Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and concealed the conditions of the giants except from Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace, and Hārūn. «Allah had bestowed favour upon them both» — with preservation from sin (ʿiṣma) — so the two of them concealed what they had learned of their condition except from Mūsā, unlike the rest of the chiefs, who divulged it and turned coward — «Enter upon them through the gate» — the gate of the town — and do not fear them, for they are bodies without hearts: the condition of the unbelievers — «and when you have entered it, you will be victorious» (Q. 5:23). They promised them that if they entered they would overcome the giants. And whence had they knowledge of that? By the promise of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: «Enter the holy land which Allah has written»

«for you» (Q. 5:21). Since Allah had promised them that the land was theirs, and they were confident in Allah's promise, they knew that they would be given victory over them; and for this reason they made the matter light for them: «Enter upon them through the gate» — the moment you reach the gate of the town you will overcome it — on the evidence of «And upon Allah rely, if you are believers» (Q. 5:23), for Allah has promised you the victory. The holy land is the land the prophets dwelt in, and the vessel is ennobled by the nobility of what it holds: it was made holy by reason of the dwelling there of the prophets and the messengers, for when what is held is good, the vessel is good. Yes, the giants dwelt in it too; but the good overcomes the evil, and for this reason the good prevailed over the evil, so much so that the dwelling of the giants did not keep the land from
being holy, since the prophets dwelt in it.
«They said: O Mūsā, we shall never enter it so long as they remain in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight» — them — «Indeed we»

«are seated» — indeed we are seated, holding back from the fighting (Q. 5:24). Here they refused the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger with the utmost refusal. «We shall never enter it». They were corporealists (mujassima), and for this reason they believed that Allah is a body that walks along with Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace.
«Go, you and your Lord» — or: and your Lord will aid you — «and fight. Indeed we are seated here» (Q. 5:24). «He said» — Mūsā, at that point —

«My Lord, I have power over none but myself and my brother» — and I have power over none but those two, that I might compel them to obedience — «so part» — separate — «between us and the wicked folk» (Q. 5:25). Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace, invoked against them, that Allah should part him from those who refused to carry out the command of Allah. Allah, Exalted, said to him: «Then indeed it»

— the holy land — «is forbidden to them» — that they should enter it — «for forty years» — it is in the accusative governed by «forbidden», or by «they shall wander» — forty years — «in the land» — and it is nine parasangs — «so grieve not» — do not sorrow — «over»

«the wicked folk» (Q. 5:26). Mūsā invoked against them, and they entered the wilderness of wandering (al-tīh) and were left bewildered for the space of forty years within nine parasangs. They would travel through the night in earnest, and when morning came, there they were in the place from which they had set out; and they would travel through the day

in the same way, until they had all died out except whoever had not reached twenty. It is said that they were six hundred thousand. Hārūn and Mūsā died in the wilderness, and it was a mercy for the two of them and a punishment for those others. At his death Mūsā asked his Lord to bring him within a stone's throw of the holy land, and He brought him near, as in the hadith. Yūshaʿ was made a prophet after the forty years and was commanded to fight the giants, and he set out with those who remained with him and fought them — and it was a Friday — and the sun stood still for him an hour until he had finished fighting them. Aḥmad related in his Musnad the hadith: ⟨The sun has not been held back for any human being save for Yūshaʿ, on the nights he marched to Bayt al-Maqdis.⟩ This is the story of Mūsā with the giants, together with the Children of Isrāʾīl: they refused the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and so Mūsā invoked against them with his words «So part between us and the wicked folk» (Q. 5:25), and Allah answered

his supplication, in that He informed him that they would wander in the land forty years. Mūsā grieved at this, and so it was said to him: «So grieve not over the wicked folk» (Q. 5:26) — do not sorrow over them; they only deserve the affliction that has befallen them. They wandered for the space of forty years within nine parasangs, by the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Had they reflected upon the sun or upon the stars, or looked to the sea, they would have found a way to get free of that patch of ground. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made them powerless, and so they remained for that span within a distance of nine parasangs — and it is said six parasangs — for forty years, as a punishment for them, because they went against the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for Mūsā and Hārūn, the two of them remained with them in the wilderness, and they had not gone against the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so how could the two of them be in the punishment when they were innocent? It is said that the two of them were not with them in the wilderness; and the sound view is that they were with them in the wilderness, but it did not harm them. It was for them coolness and peace, as the fire was for Ibrāhīm coolness and peace. This affair tells you the outcome of companionship: the Children of Isrāʾīl went against the command of Allah, and so they remained in the wilderness forty years; and Mūsā and Hārūn, who had not gone against the command of Allah — when they kept company with these wicked men, they remained in the wilderness with them forty years. And these wicked men, since Mūsā and Hārūn were among them, remained in the wilderness in the greatest favour: when they asked for food, Allah sent down upon them manna and quail, the most wholesome food found in this world; and when they asked for clothing, their clothing stayed neither soiling nor ever wearing out; and they asked for light in the darkness, and Allah sent columns of light; and they asked to be given water, and Mūsā struck his rock, and twelve springs gushed forth for them, «each people knowing its drinking place» (Q. 2:60). This was by the blessing of the companionship of Mūsā and Hārūn; and the remaining of Mūsā and Hārūn in the punishment along with them was by the ill fortune of the companionship of those who went against the command of Allah. So when they had remained in the wilderness forty years, Hārūn died — and he was more beloved among the Children of Isrāʾīl than Mūsā. When Mūsā told them that Hārūn had died, they accused him of having killed him, because he was more beloved to them than he was. So Mūsā called upon his Lord, and Allah sent down the angel, and he brought Hārūn

So he uncovered to them his state, and they knew that he had died unslain. When the death of Mūsā drew near, Mūsā asked that Allah should not take him except in the Holy Land; so He brought him near to Jerusalem by a stone's throw, and he died there. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Had I been there, I would have shown you his grave, by the red sand-hill.⟩ A matter of prophethood. «And recite» — O Muḥammad — «to them the news of the two sons of Ādam» — recount to them the story of the two sons of Ādam, Hābīl and Qābīl — «in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice» — to Allah; and it was a ram for Hābīl and a crop for Qābīl — «and it was accepted from one of them» — and he is Hābīl, in that a fire came down from heaven and consumed his offering — «and it was not accepted from the other» — and he is Qābīl; so he grew angry and harboured envy in himself, until Ādam went on the hajj. «He said» — to him — «I will surely kill you». He said: why? He said: because your offering was accepted and mine was not. «He said: Allah accepts only from the godfearing» (Q. 5:27). Ādam, upon him be blessing and peace, had married Ḥawwāʾ, and she conceived by him twenty pregnancies, in each pregnancy a boy and a girl. Ādam would take the girl from this pregnancy and marry her to the boy from that pregnancy; so the difference of the pregnancies stood in place of the difference of lineages in the shariʿa of Ādam. When the time came for the marrying of Hābīl and Qābīl, Ādam wanted to marry Qābīl's sister to Hābīl and Hābīl's sister to Qābīl. Qābīl refused, and said that his own twin was more beautiful than Hābīl's twin and that he was not content with this: he must marry his own sister. Ādam spoke with him, and he said to him: you have only wronged us (jurta ʿalaynā); this is no ruling of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. So Jibrīl came down and said: Allah commands you to offer a sacrifice. If Allah accepts Hābīl's offering, then he has the better right to the girl who is disputed over; and if He accepts Qābīl's offering, then likewise. As for Hābīl, he used to raise livestock, so he chose a handsome ram and implored Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to accept it from him, and he set it down. Qābīl was a ploughman, so he went to his crop and took an ear of grain,

took the grains that were in it and cast them around the ram, and said: if Allah wills, He accepts from me; or He does not accept from me — as for me, I must have what I want. So Allah did not accept from him, because, as He said: «Allah accepts only from the godfearing» (Q. 5:27). And a white fire came down from heaven and carried Hābīl's ram up to heaven, and Qābīl's ear of grain remained. So he envied him, and said to him: Allah has accepted from you and has not accepted from me. He said to him: «Allah accepts only from the godfearing». He wanted to kill him, but he feared Ādam. Ādam used to go to the hajj every year; so when Ādam had gone to the hajj, he threatened him that he would kill him. Hābīl said: «If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds» (Q. 5:28) — in killing you. «Indeed I want you to return» — to go back — «with my sin» — with the sin of killing me — «and your sin» — which you committed before — «so that you become one of the companions of the Fire» — and I do not want to return with your sin if I kill you, and so be one of them. This is Hābīl, one of the godfearing, and Qābīl was the opposite of that. When he threatened him with killing, he said that he would not kill him, because he himself fears Allah; and whoever kills his believing brother bears his own sin and the sin of his slain brother — and he wants that for him and does not want it for himself. How is this, when the Muslim loves for the believer what he loves for himself? He said this only as an admonition from him: he admonished him that whoever kills his brother returns with his own sin and the sin of the slain, so that he might be held back from killing him — not that he wished for him to fall into that. «And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers» (Q. 5:29). This is an admonition. «So it prompted him» — made it alluring — «— his soul — to the killing of his brother, and he killed him, and he became» — he came to be — «one of the losers» (Q. 5:30) — by killing him. And he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead man upon the face of the earth from the children of Ādam; so he carried him upon his back after his death for a time. «So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth» — digging up the dust with its beak and with its feet and heaping it over a dead crow that was with it, until it had covered it — «to show him how to conceal» — to cover — «the corpse of his brother» — the carcass of his brother — «He said: woe to me! was I unable» — [incapable] of — «to be like this crow, and so conceal the corpse of my brother? And he became one of the regretful» (Q. 5:31) — over having carried him. And he dug for him and covered him. This is the story of Qābīl and Hābīl. It was the first act of disobedience that fell upon the face of the earth: Qābīl envied his brother Hābīl and killed him. Ādam was absent — he was at the hajj — and he saw that the earth had changed and had grown dusty, and the waters had all been

sweet, and the waters of the seas all turned salt; and all the trees — their fruits had been good — so the earth and the fruits and the waters changed. Ādam knew that something had happened upon the earth. When he returned he looked and did not see Hābīl, and he said to Qābīl:

where is Hābīl? He said: I am not his keeper. He said to him: you have killed him. And he denied that he had killed him. So they went to the place where he had slaughtered him, and behold, the earth had drunk Hābīl's blood and no trace of him remained. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, threatened the earth for swallowing the blood of the slain, and after that the blood came out of the earth; and when the reproach had fallen upon the earth for that, the earth remained such that it does not drink the blood of anything slaughtered — even a chicken: it stays upon the face of the earth. When that happened, Ādam knew that Qābīl had killed Hābīl, so he drove him out; and he settled in Yemen and took to trading and to play, and he fathered children of the reprobates, with no good in them. That story Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to recount to the Children of Isrāʾīl, because they had opposed the command of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and had refused to enter the Holy Land; and he recounted to them the story of the two sons of Ādam. It was among the secrets of their books, and the Prophet ﷺ was unlettered, born in the land of the Ḥijāz; he had not read, nor had he kept company with anyone who had read anything. So he brought them what was hidden of their own sciences. This is the most telling proof of his messengership ﷺ. Many of the Jews accepted Islam because of these two stories. «Because of that» — which Qābīl did — «We decreed for the Children of Isrāʾīl that» — the matter is — «whoever kills a soul not for a soul» — that it killed — «or» — for other than — «corruption in the earth» — which it committed in the earth, of unbelief or fornication or highway robbery or the like — «it is as though he had killed all mankind; and whoever gives it life» — in that he refrains from killing it — «it is as though he had given life to all mankind» (Q. 5:32). Ibn ʿAbbās said: ⟨in respect of the violation of its inviolability and the safeguarding of it⟩. The killing of a single soul is not equal in crime to the killing of all mankind; but He alerts us that the killing of one of us is like the killing of all — just as, if we knew that so-and-so wanted to kill us all, we would all stand to repel him. If we know that he wants to kill

«And there had come to them» — the Children of Isrāʾīl — «Our messengers with the clear proofs» — the miracles — «yet indeed many of them, after that, in the earth are transgressors» (Q. 5:32) — exceeding the bound, by unbelief and killing and other than that. And [what follows] was sent down concerning the ʿUranīs, when they came to Medina sick, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted them to go out to the camels — the camels of the zakat — and to drink of their urine and their milk. When they recovered they killed the herdsman of the Prophet ﷺ and drove off the camels. They were sick and professed Islam, so the Prophet sent them to the camels of the zakat and said that they should drink their urine — this is a medicine for them — and their milk — this is sustenance for them. So they recovered; and when they had recovered and grown strong they killed the herdsman of the Prophet ﷺ and drove off the camels of the zakat and went back to their unbelief. So this was sent down concerning them: «The recompense of those who make war on Allah and His Messenger» — by making war on the Muslims — «and strive in the earth for corruption» — by highway robbery — «is only that they be killed, or crucified, or that their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides, or that they be banished from the earth» (Q. 5:33). Allah sent this down concerning the highway robbers. The commentators have spoken on this verse (āya): «that they be killed, or crucified, or that their hands»

«from the earth» (Q. 5:33) — the earth of Allah is wide; and it is not permissible that we should mean by it that he is banished from one town to another, because that is a harm to everyone: if he is banished from one town and left in another town, that would be a harm to the people of that town. What is the meaning of «or that they be banished from the earth»? That he be confined in prison — that is the banishment from the earth. They are four: whoever takes property and kills a soul is crucified and killed; whoever kills and does not take property is killed; whoever takes property and does not kill has his foot and his hand cut off; and whoever has committed none of these, but has entered among the number of those who make war, is put in prison.

This is the meaning of «that they be killed» — they are killed if they have killed; «or crucified» — if they took property and killed; «or that their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides» — if they took property and did not kill; «or that they be banished from the earth» — they are put in prison if nothing is established against them. «That» — the aforementioned recompense — «is for them a disgrace» — abasement — «in this world; and for them in the hereafter is a great punishment» (Q. 5:33) — it is the punishment of the Fire. «Except those who repent» — of those who make war and the highway robbers — «before you have power over them: then know that Allah is forgiving» — to them for what they committed — «merciful» (Q. 5:34) — to them. If one of those who make war turns back and repents before he is seized, his repentance is accepted. «O you who believe, fear Allah» — fear His punishment, by obeying Him — «and seek» — ask — «the means of approach to Him» (wasīla) — what brings you near to Him of obedience to Him. He made the commentary on the two phrases one single thing: «Fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him»: fear Allah by leaving off what He has forbidden, and seek the means of approach to Him by doing what brings you near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He began with godfearing (al-taqwā), and what is meant by it here is the leaving of what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has forbidden. The averting of harms takes precedence over the securing of benefits. «And seek the means of approach to Him»: perform acts of obedience that bring you near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in closeness. The means of approach to Allah, Blessed and Exalted — they have differed over them. They said: every deed a man performs of

the supererogatory works of good is a means of approach between him and Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And we have read in the Qurʾan three verses, each verse of which comprises a means of approach to Allah, Blessed and Exalted: «Say: if you love Allah, then follow me, and Allah will love you» (Q. 3:31) — know that following the Prophet ﷺ in all sayings and deeds is a means of approach by which a man draws near to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And He said: «And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face» (Q. 18:28) — keeping company with the righteous. «And follow the way of him who turns to Me» (Q. 31:15) — keeping company with the people of dhikr and the recognizers (al-ʿārifūn) of Allah. One of the righteous said at his death: ⟨I counsel you to fear Allah in secret and in the open; and to eat little, to sleep little, to speak little; to forsake acts of disobedience and sins; to leave the desires for the length of your days; to shun the company of the foolish among mankind; and to keep the company of the noble righteous. The best of people is he who benefits people, and the best of speech is what is little and tells much. And know that what profits is godfearing, and what saves is righteous deeds and sound faith — not high birth and not lineage. And let not Satan delude you with the many boasts of your fathers and your forefathers: urine — its origin is good, clear water; and Allah brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living.⟩ «And strive in His way» — to raise His religion high — «that you may prosper» (Q. 5:35) — that you may win. «Indeed those who disbelieve — if» — it were established — «that they had all that is in the earth, and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them; and for them is a painful punishment» (Q. 5:36). «They wish» — they long — «to come out of the Fire, but they are not to come out of it; and for them is a lasting punishment» (Q. 5:37). When the people of the Fire enter the Fire — may Allah shield us from that — they regret with a regret like which there is no regret, and they wish to ransom themselves from the punishment of Allah with everything they possess, and they wish to come out of the Fire, but they are not to come out

of it. «And the thief, male and female: cut off their hands» (Q. 5:38) — the right hand of each of them, from the wrist. And the sunna has made clear that the amount for which it is cut off is a quarter dīnār and upward, and that if he repeats, his left foot is cut off at the joint of the foot, then the left hand, then the right foot, and after that he is disciplined with beating. He mentioned that the thief, male and female — their ruling is that their hands be cut off; and the sunna has made clear that the amount for which the hand is cut off is a quarter dīnār. A Jew raised an objection against Islam. He said: this Islam is inconsistent, in that it has made five hundred dīnārs obligatory as the blood-money for a hand — whoever cuts off a man's hand gives him five hundred dīnārs — while a man who has stolen only a quarter dīnār has his hand cut off. What is the matter with it? Ibn Ḥajar answered him that it is trustworthiness that made the hand dear, until it came to be five hundred dīnārs, and treachery that made it cheap, until it came to be only a quarter dīnār. This is the wisdom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And He began with the man in the mention of theft, because the man is stronger at theft than the woman, just as He began with the woman in fornication, in His words, Blessed and Exalted: «The fornicatress and the fornicator» (Q. 24:2) — because the woman is stronger at fornication than the man: if the woman does not consent, the indecency never occurs. «as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment» — a penalty for the two of them — «from Allah» — Blessed and Exalted — «and Allah is»

«Mighty» — prevailing over His affair — «Wise» (Q. 5:38) — in His creation. «But whoever repents after his wrongdoing» — turns back from the theft — «and makes amends» — his deed — «then Allah will relent toward him; indeed Allah is forgiving, merciful» (Q. 5:39). In expressing it in this way there is what has gone before. So his repentance does not remove from him the claim of the human being, the amputation and the returning of the property. Yes: the sunna has made clear that if he is pardoned before the matter is brought up to the imam, it lapses; and al-Shāfiʿī holds this. «Do you not know» — the interrogative is for affirmation — «that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He will» — punishing him — «and He forgives whom He will» — forgiveness for him — «and Allah is powerful over everything» (Q. 5:40) — and of that is the punishing and the forgiving. «O Messenger, let not grieve you» — the doing of — «those who race into unbelief» — they fall into it swiftly, that is, they display it whenever they find an opportunity — «and from among those who say» — min (from) is for explication — they said — «We believe, with their mouths» — with their tongues — «and their hearts have not believed» — and they are the hypocrites — «and from among those who are Jews»

a people, «listeners to falsehood» — which their rabbis have fabricated, a listening of acceptance — «listeners» — from you — «for a people» — for the sake of a people — «others» — among the Jews — «who have not come to you» — among them is one who comes to the Prophet ﷺ, takes the report, and goes off with it to the Jews. «Who have not come to you» — and they are the people of Khaybar. Two married persons among them committed adultery, and they were loath to stone them, so they sent Qurayẓa to ask the Prophet ﷺ about the ruling. «They distort the word» — which is in the Torah, such as the verse of stoning — «after its places» — upon which Allah had set it — «they say» — to those whom they had sent — «if you are given this» — the distorted ruling, that is, the flogging, Muḥammad having given it to you as his ruling — «then take it» — then accept it — «and if you are not given it»
in that he gives you a ruling contrary to it, «then beware» — of accepting it — «and whomever Allah wills to try» — to lead astray — «then you will never possess for him»
«anything against Allah» — by way of repelling it — «those are they whose hearts Allah does not will to purify» — of unbelief (kufr) — «theirs in this world is»
«disgrace» — humiliation, through public exposure and the jizya — «and theirs in the hereafter is a great punishment» (Q. 5:41). «Listeners to falsehood»
«devourers of unlawful gain» — the unlawful, such as bribes — «so if they come to you» — that you may judge between them — «then judge between them, or»
«turn away from them» (Q. 5:42). This option is abrogated by His saying, «and that you judge between them» (Q. 5:49), and the rest of the verse. So judgement between them is obligatory

when they bring their case to us, and that is the sounder of al-Shāfiʿī's two views. And were they to bring their case to us together with a Muslim, it would be obligatory by consensus. «And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you in anything. And if you judge» — between them — «then judge between them with justice; indeed Allah loves the just» (Q. 5:42) — those who are equitable in judging, that is, He rewards them. «And how is it that they make you their judge, when they have the Torah with them, in which is the judgement of Allah» — by stoning. They did not intend by that the knowing of the truth, but rather what was easier for them. «Then they turn away» — they turn aside from your judgement of stoning, which agrees with their own Book — «after that? And those are not the believers» (Q. 5:43). The Jews of Khaybar, when a nobleman among them committed adultery, would lighten the ruling of Allah for him: they flogged him and took property from him; and when one who was not a nobleman committed adultery, they stoned him. Two noblemen of their eminent men committed adultery, so they sent to the Prophet ﷺ, hoping they might find some dispensation with him. He said to them: ⟨The ruling of Allah is stoning.⟩ They said: you have dealt harshly with us, O Abū al-Qāsim; this is not the ruling of Allah. He said to them: ⟨This is the ruling of Allah, and it is in the Torah.⟩ They said to him: how do you know that it is in the Torah? He said: ⟨Bring the Torah.⟩ So they went and brought the Torah. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣūriyā was reading it, and when he reached the verse of stoning he placed his finger upon the word of stoning and read what came after it. ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām was present, and he had the Torah by heart, so he moved his hand aside and read the verse of stoning to the Prophet ﷺ — the Prophet neither reads nor knows writing. When it became clear that this was the ruling of Allah, the Prophet ﷺ took the two of them and stoned them, and they were angered. They are the ones whom this verse reproaches. They did not come to the Prophet ﷺ seeking the ruling, because they knew the ruling; they only wanted something easy for them. Had they wanted the ruling, the Torah would have sufficed them. This is the ruling of Allah in the Torah. «Indeed We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance» — from error — «and light» — a plain exposition of the rulings — «by which the prophets judged» — of the Children of Isrāʾīl — «who submitted» — they yielded themselves to Allah, Blessed and Exalted

The prophets after Mūsā, of the Children of Isrāʾīl, had no books and no law. Rather every prophet of the prophets of the Children of Isrāʾīl held fast to the Torah alone. Every prophet in his generation guided the people by the Torah, just as the ulama guide the people now by the shariʿa of Muḥammad ﷺ. For this reason he ﷺ said: ⟨The ulama of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Isrāʾīl.⟩ The prophets after Mūsā judged by the Torah: «Indeed We sent down»
they yielded themselves to Allah, «for those who are Jews, and the rabbis» — the learned among them — «and the scholars» — the jurists — «with what they were entrusted to keep»
— they were given it in trust; Allah made them its keepers — «of the Book of Allah» — so Allah made the Torah a deposit held with the Children of Isrāʾīl.

For this reason they were able to distort and to alter, and so they changed and altered — unlike the Qurʾan. He said: «Indeed We, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its keepers» (Q. 15:9). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has taken upon Himself the keeping of the Qurʾan from distortion and alteration, so it will not be altered until the Day of Resurrection — so much so that a boy, if he hears a distortion of the Qurʾan from an eminent reciter, corrects it for him. This is by the keeping of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «and they were witnesses to it» — that it is true — «so do not fear the people» — O Jews — «and fear Me»

in concealing it — «and do not sell» — do not exchange — «My signs for a small price» — of this world, which you take in return for concealing them — «and whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the unbelievers» (Q. 5:44) — whoever abandons the ruling of Allah and judges by other than the ruling of Allah, those are the unbelievers. And the Prophet ﷺ mentioned: ⟨Five for five: no people broke a covenant but that their enemy was given mastery over them; nor did they judge by other than what Allah has sent down but that poverty spread among them; nor did indecency appear among them but that death spread among them; nor did they skimp the measure but that they were denied the produce of the earth and were seized by years of dearth; nor did they withhold the zakat but that the rain was held back from them⟩ «And We prescribed» — We made obligatory — «for them therein» — in the Torah — «that»

«the soul for the soul» — the soul is slain for the soul, when it has slain it — «and the eye» — is put out — «for the eye, and the nose» — is cut off — «for the nose, and the ear» — is severed — «for the ear, and the tooth» — is pulled out — «for the tooth, and for wounds, retaliation» — retaliation (qiṣāṣ) is exacted in them where it is possible, as with the hand, the foot, the male member and the like; and that in which retaliation is not possible — in it there is the arbitrated indemnity (ḥukūma), at the discretion of the imam. And this ruling, though it was prescribed upon them, is established in our own shariʿa. Everything the Qurʾan mentions of the ruling of the Torah and the Gospel whose abrogation has not been made plain to us is a ruling for us; this is a ruling for us. «So whoever gives it as alms» — by way of retaliation, in that he gave himself up to it — «it is an expiation for him» (Q. 5:45) — for what he has committed. Whoever gives retaliation as alms — that is, the killer gives himself up to be killed — it is an expiation for him. Or whoever gives it as alms by way of retaliation: one to whom it fell due to kill a man and who then pardoned him, seeking nearness to Allah — it is an expiation for him. From this verse (āya) Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī differed over the prescribed penalties (ḥudūd): al-Shāfiʿī said that the prescribed penalties are deterrents (zawājir), and Mālik said that the prescribed penalties are restoratives (jawābir). So whoever has a prescribed penalty fallen due upon him and gives himself up, and the penalty is carried out upon him — it is an expiation for him, and the verse indicates that. And the hadith of al-Ghāmidiyya:

a woman who committed fornication after marriage (iḥṣān). She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: I have committed fornication; carry out upon me the prescribed penalty that Allah has made due upon me, and I am pregnant from the fornication. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: ⟨Go, until you deliver your child.⟩ So she went and delivered, and she came with the child, suckling him. She said: carry out upon me the prescribed penalty that Allah has made due upon me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: ⟨Go, until you wean him.⟩ He is a prophet of mercy. So she went, until she had weaned the child; then she came again, and he was carrying bread and eating it. She said to him: the boy is weaned, and here he is eating; carry out upon me what Allah has made due upon me. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that they take her out to al-Baqīʿ and stone her until she died. They pelted her with the stones, and when the stones bore hard upon her she fled; so they overtook her and stoned her

until she died. They mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and one of them said: we have stoned the wicked woman. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Do not say 'the wicked woman'. She is wholesome. By Allah, had the people of Medina shared in her repentance, it would have purified them all!⟩ This showed us that the prescribed penalties are restoratives. And al-Shāfiʿī says: the prescribed penalties are deterrents, set up to deter others only, and the sin remains. Al-Shāfiʿī was severe on this.

«So whoever gives it as alms, it is an expiation for him» — whoever gives himself up for the prescribed penalty to be carried out upon him, that is an expiation for him; and this indicates that the prescribed penalties are restoratives. «And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down» — in retaliation and in other matters — «those are the wrongdoers» (Q. 5:45) «And We sent following» — We made to follow
«in their footsteps» — the prophets' — «with ʿĪsā son of Maryam, confirming what was before him» — what preceded him — «of the Torah, and We gave him»

«the Gospel, in which is guidance» — from error — «and light» — an exposition of the rulings — «and confirming what was before it of the Torah» — in the rulings it contains — «and a guidance and an admonition for the godfearing» (Q. 5:46). And We said: «And let the people of the Gospel judge»
«by what Allah has sent down therein» — of the rulings — «And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the transgressors» (Q. 5:47)
«to you» — O Muḥammad — «the Book» — the Qurʾan — «with the truth, confirming what was before it» — what preceded it — «of the Book»
«and as a guardian» — a witness — «over it, so judge between them» — between the People of the Book, if they bring their case to you — «by what has been sent down by»
«Allah» — to you — «and do not follow their desires» — turning aside — «from what has come to you of the truth. For each one of you We have appointed» — O you

communities — «a law» — a shariʿa — «and a way» — a clear road in religion upon which they walk — «and had Allah willed He would have made you one community» — upon a single shariʿa — «but» — He divided you into parties — «that He might test you» — that He might try you —
«in what He has given you» — of the differing revealed laws, that He might see which of you is obedient and which disobedient — «so vie with one another in good works»

hasten to them. «To Allah is your return, all together» — your return is to Allah, all of you, by the resurrection — «and He will inform you of that wherein you used to differ» (Q. 5:48) — of the matter of religion — and He will requite each of you according to his deed. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the True Sovereign, and He is the one who disposes of His creation however He wills. It is His to set a ruling in force for a span of time, then to bring that ruling to an end and bring another ruling; there is in this no objection against Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He sent the prophets, and all of them agreed upon the creed, which is the oneness of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, the magnifying of the Creator, and compassion for creation. All of them agreed upon this, because Allah charged the prophets: uphold the religion and do not become divided in it. And the division there is division in the creeds. ⟨The Jews divided into seventy-one sects, all of them in the Fire; and the Christians divided into seventy-two sects, all of them in the Fire; and my community will divide into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire save one — what I and my Companions are upon.⟩ that is, those who are upon the sunna and the community

⟨The hand of Allah is with the community.⟩, and the division intended there is division in the creeds. As for disagreement in the branches, there has come concerning it: ⟨The disagreement of my community is a mercy.⟩ — because whoever follows a scholar meets Allah safe. Allah completed the revealed laws with the shariʿa of Muḥammad ﷺ, and He sealed the books with His Mighty Book, which He named a guardian over all the books, after the books of Ādam had been words only: «Then Ādam received words from his Lord»
(Q. 2:37). And the books of Ibrāhīm were words: «And when his Lord tried Ibrāhīm with words» (Q. 2:124) — and the books of Mūsā were scrolls only

«the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā» (Q. 87:19). This is a Book that is a guardian over all the books. And just as his Book is the most excellent of the heavenly books, and his religion the most excellent of religions, and his community the best community, so he is the most excellent of all the prophets, by consensus.

And every one of them gave his community good tidings of Muḥammad ﷺ, the last of them being ʿĪsā: «and bringing good tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad» (Q. 61:6). He did not name him Aḥmad, because their language is not Arabic; but he said: ⟨It is better for you that I go. I go to my Father⟩ — in the language of the Gospel 'the Father' means 'the master' — ⟨my returning to my Father is better for you, and the Paraclete will come to you: the Spirit of truth.⟩ The Paraclete (al-Bāraqlīṭ) in their language means Muḥammad, or Aḥmad. And he said: ⟨When he comes he will confirm me, as I confirm him.⟩ And it is mentioned in a verse: ⟨He, when he comes, says nothing but what Allah has said to him, and does nothing but what⟩

⟨Allah has said to him! And were I to live to see him, he would deserve that I tie his sandal for him and wipe his foot for him.⟩ No creature has come after ʿĪsā more exalted in worth than ʿĪsā in this rank, except Muḥammad ﷺ.
«And judge between them by what Allah has sent down, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they seduce you» — that they not seduce you, that is,

lead you astray — «away from some of what Allah has sent down to you. But if they turn away» — from the judgement sent down, and they desire something other than it — «then know that Allah only wishes to afflict them» — with the punishment in this world — «for some of their sins» — which they have committed, among them the turning away; and He will requite them for all of them in the hereafter — «And indeed many of the people are deviators» — gone out of the religion (Q. 5:49). «Is it the judgement of the Jāhiliyya that they seek?» — do they seek, do they demand, the judgement of the Jāhiliyya, of flattery and partiality — «And who is better than Allah in judgement» — none is better in judgement than Allah, Blessed and Exalted — «for a people» — that is, in the sight of a people — «who are certain» — of Him. They were singled out for mention because they are the ones who ponder it (Q. 5:50). «O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians» — the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy b. Salūl used to go and befriend the Jews and the Christians, and when he was forbidden that he would say:

⟨Reversals come about, and we shall have need of them one day.⟩ «O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies» — making allies of them and showing affection to them — «Some of them are allies of others» — the unbelievers are united in unbelief (kufr); unbelief is all one creed; all the unbelievers are agreed upon unbelief and all of them are against the Muslims — «some of them are allies of others». «And whoever of you allies with them, he is of them» — one of their number. Whoever befriends the unbelievers has gone out of the religion — «And indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people» — by their allying with the unbelievers (Q. 5:51). «So you see those in whose hearts is sickness» — weakness of belief, like ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy the hypocrite — «hastening to them» — in allying with them — «saying» — by way of excuse — «We fear that a reversal may befall us» — that time may turn with it against us, whether drought or defeat, and Muḥammad's affair will never be brought to completion, and then they will not provision us. He, Exalted, said: «Perhaps Allah will bring the victory» — the help for His prophet, by making His religion manifest — «or a command from Him»

by the rending of the hypocrites' covering and their exposure — «so that they become, over what they concealed within themselves» — of doubt and of allying with the unbelievers — «regretful» (Q. 5:52). «And those who believe say» — to one another, when their covering is rent, in astonishment — «Are these the ones who swore by Allah their most binding oaths» — the utmost of their effort in them — «that they were indeed with you» — they used to say that they were with the Muslims. He, Exalted, said: «Their deeds have come to nothing» — their righteous deeds were made void — «so they have become» — they have come to be — «losers» — in this world by the disgrace and in the hereafter by the punishment (Q. 5:53). «O you who believe, whoever turns back» — goes back — «of you from his religion» — to unbelief. A telling of what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knew would come to pass. This verse came down before this matter occurred, and a group did apostatise — Jalāl said — after the death of the Prophet ﷺ. «then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him» (Q. 5:54). He ﷺ said: ⟨They are the people of this man⟩, and he pointed to Abū
Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.

«humble toward the believers, mighty» — severe — «toward the unbelievers» (Q. 5:54). In the first age eleven sects apostatised. Three sects apostatised in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. Among them was al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī; he apostatised in Yemen and gained mastery over Yemen, until he drove out Muʿādh b. Jabal, the governor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger ﷺ sent word to Muʿādh that they should stand against him and that he should hold the people to remaining upon Islam. A man called Fīrūz killed him. The Prophet ﷺ gave word that al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī had been killed — a blessed man killed him — while he was in the illness of his death. It was said to him: who is the blessed man? He said: ⟨Fīrūz.⟩

Then the Messenger ﷺ passed away that night. This was on the twelfth of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and at the end of the month the report came from Yemen that Fīrūz had killed al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, just as he ﷺ had given word. And Musaylima the Liar apostatised in al-Yamāma and wrote to the Messenger ﷺ: ⟨From Musaylima⟩

⟨the Messenger of Allah, to Muḥammad the Messenger of Allah: the earth between us is two halves, half for me and half for you.⟩ His two envoys came to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said to them: ⟨Do you two believe in this?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ The Prophet ﷺ said: ⟨Were it not that envoys are not to be killed, I would strike off your two necks.⟩ And the Prophet ﷺ wrote him a reply: ⟨From Muḥammad the Messenger of Allah to Musaylima the Liar:⟩ «The earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the outcome belongs to the godfearing» (Q. 7:128). When the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abū Bakr sent out an army whose commander was Khālid b. al-Walīd, and they came and raided them, and Waḥshī — the slave of Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī, the one who killed Ḥamza at the battle of Uḥud — killed him. For this reason he used to say: ⟨I killed the best of men in the Jāhiliyya and the worst of men in Islam⟩ — meaning in his Jāhiliyya and in his Islam: when he was an unbeliever he was the one who killed Ḥamza, and when he was a Muslim he was the one who killed Musaylima the Liar. And Ṭulayḥa too laid claim to prophethood and apostatised, and a group apostatised with him. Abū Bakr fought them and gained mastery over them, and Ṭulayḥa fled to Syria, and after that he returned to Islam; Allah guided him and he died a Muslim. These three sects apostatised in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. And in the time of Abū Bakr seven sects apostatised. The Arabs apostatised entirely, from Syria and Yemen and Iraq; none remained but the people of Mecca and the people of Medina — on account of the zakat. They said: ⟨We will perform the prayer as Allah said; as for the zakat, our properties shall not be seized from us after the Prophet ﷺ. Allah said:⟩ «Take from their properties an alms» (Q. 9:103) ⟨and the one who was addressed with ‘take’ has gone⟩

⟨We will not give anything of our properties after the Prophet ﷺ.⟩ So Abū Bakr stood up and said: ⟨By Allah, if they withheld from me a hobbling-cord that they used to hand over to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them over it.⟩ ʿUmar said to him: ⟨Gently, Abū Bakr! Will you fight one who performs the prayer and bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah?⟩ Abū

Bakr said: ⟨Away from me, ʿUmar! A tyrant in unbelief, a weakling in Islam! By Allah, I will never separate the prayer from the zakat. Allah says:⟩ «Perform the prayer and give the zakat» (Q. 2:43). And he girded on his sword alone. ʿUmar said: ⟨When I saw that in Abū Bakr I knew that this which he held to was the truth.⟩ They had disliked this matter at the beginning and loved it at the end. So they fought the Arabs: everyone who did not render the zakat they would fight, until they returned to accepting the zakat. Were it not for Abū Bakr this pillar would have fallen and they would have made light of Islam. For this reason ʿUmar said: ⟨By Allah, no child has been born after the prophets better than Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; and were it not for him the Arabs would all have apostatised by abandoning the zakat.⟩ And one sect apostatised in the time of ʿUmar: Jabala b. al-Ayham, the king of Ghassān. He came and embraced Islam, and he travelled with ʿUmar to the hajj. He was circumambulating the House, trailing his cloak behind him, and one of the Companions trod on his cloak — and he was a proud king — so he struck him in the face. The man complained of that to ʿUmar, and ʿUmar summoned him and said to him: ⟨Allah's judgement is retaliation.⟩ He said: ⟨Retaliation? I am a king and he is a commoner:⟩

⟨shall he retaliate against me?⟩ ʿUmar said to him: ⟨There is nothing of this in Islam. Islam has made us equal; the king and the commoner are alike, and Allah's judgement is retaliation.⟩ He said to him: ⟨I will give you a hundred camels, and you do not retaliate against me.⟩ The man said: ⟨I will only retaliate.⟩ He said: ⟨I will give you a thousand camels, and you do not retaliate against me.⟩ The man refused, and ʿUmar said: ⟨You must be retaliated against.⟩ So he said: ⟨Commander of the Faithful, grant me a little respite until tomorrow.⟩ So ʿUmar granted him respite, and he fled and apostatised. He said: ⟨A religion that makes equal⟩

⟨between the king and the commoner — this is a religion that is not to be accepted.⟩ This is the one who apostatised in the time of ʿUmar, and Allah gave word of this before it came to pass. «O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble» — tender — «toward the believers, mighty» — severe — «toward the unbelievers» (Q. 5:54). The Messenger ﷺ was asked about these, and he said: ⟨The people of Yemen; faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni.⟩ And he was asked a second time, and he pointed to Salmān and said: ⟨The people of this man.⟩ ⟨Were Islam in the Pleiades, men from among these would reach it⟩ — an indication of the black-skinned, when they believe in Allah. And he was asked again, and he said: ⟨The people of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī.⟩ And the point holds for everyone who answers to these descriptions: «humble toward the believers, mighty toward the unbelievers» (Q. 5:54). The Muslims have now reversed
this matter: they are harsh toward the Muslims and merciful toward the unbelievers. «they struggle»

«in the way of Allah, and they do not fear the blame of any blamer» — as the hypocrites fear the blame of the unbelievers — «That» — the aforementioned among the descriptions — «is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-encompassing» — abundant in bounty — «knowing» (Q. 5:54). «Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger» — this came down when Ibn Salām said: O Messenger of Allah, our people have shunned us; everyone who has entered Islam, his unbelieving people have cut him off and taken him as an enemy. So Allah said: «Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish the prayer and give the zakat, and they are bowing» — humbly submissive (Q. 5:55). And this ruling has remained until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever is content with Allah as Lord and with Islam as religion — Allah is his ally, and His Messenger, and the believers all together. «And whoever takes Allah as ally, and His Messenger and those who believe» — so He helps them and gives them victory — «then indeed the party of Allah — they are the victors» — by His giving them the victory (Q. 5:56). «O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in mockery» — this came down concerning the hypocrites and the Jews. The Messenger ﷺ was greatly concerned about something by which the people might be called to the prayer, so he consulted the Companions and said: We should like to find something by which the times of the prayer may be announced. Among them one said: We shall kindle a fire; when they see smoke in the daytime they know that the time has come, and when it is at night, when they see the light they know that the time has come. But the Prophet ﷺ disliked the fire. Among them one said: We shall strike a bell. But he disliked the bell. So they dispersed; and a group of the Companions, all of them, saw the call to prayer (adhān) in sleep: Abū Ṣudāʾ saw the call to prayer, and Bilāl, and a group. So the Prophet ﷺ ordered the call to prayer, and they began to call it. The Jews laughed a great laugh and said: We have never seen a religion more hideous than the religion of Muḥammad; this braying of a donkey that he has brought — no religion ever brought the like of it. So He said: «O you who believe, do not take those who take your religion in mockery» — a thing mocked at — «and sport, from among those who were given the Book before you, and the unbelievers» — the polytheists — «as allies; and fear Allah, if you are believers» (Q. 5:57). «And when you call» — you summon — «to the prayer» — with the call to prayer — «they take it» — that is, the prayer — «in mockery and sport» — in that
they mock it and laugh together on hearing the call to prayer. «That» — the taking of it so — «is because they» — by reason of their being a people

«do not reason» — they have no intellect (Q. 5:58). So the call to prayer: it is not that it was established by a dream alone, for a group of the Companions; rather it was established by this verse as well. This verse established the ruling of the call to prayer. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨The muezzins will be the longest of neck on the Day of Resurrection⟩. And he said: Four — the earth does not eat their bodies when they die:

the prophets — the earth does not eat their bodies; and the bearers of the Muḥammadan shariʿa, the scholars who act upon their knowledge; and the bearers of the Qurʾan; and the muezzins — whoever has given the call to prayer for seven years, the earth does not eat his body. He is in the lofty rank: the prophets, the bearers of the shariʿa, the bearers of the Qurʾan, and the muezzin. And the repeating of the call to prayer is recommended for everyone who hears it: when he says Allah is greater, you say Allah is greater; when he says I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, you say I bear witness that there is no god but Allah; and when he says I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, you say I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah; when he says Come to the prayer, you say There is no capacity and no power save by Allah; and when he says: Come to prosperity, you say: What Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not

[by] transforming them, and of them him who «worshipped the false deity» — Satan, by obeying him. A group of them prostrated themselves to al-Jibt and to the false deity when they came to Abū Sufyān at Mecca. «Those are worse in station» — a specifying accusative (tamyīz) — they have nothing but the Fire

«and further astray from the even path» (Q. 5:60) — the road of truth; and the root meaning of sawāʾ is the middle. «And when they come to you» — the hypocrites of the Jews — «they say, ‘We believe,’ while they have entered» — upon you, clothed — «with unbelief, and they have gone out» — from you, clothed with unbelief likewise — «with it» — with unbelief; and they did not believe — «and Allah knows best what they were concealing» (Q. 5:61) — of hypocrisy. «And you see many of them» — the Jews — «hastening» — falling swiftly — «into sin» — into lying

«and aggression» — wrongdoing — «and their consuming what is unlawfully got» — the forbidden, such as bribes — «evil indeed is what they were doing» (Q. 5:62) — this deed of theirs. «Why do the rabbis not forbid them» — why did the ulama who act upon their knowledge not forbid them — «and the scholars» — among them — «from their uttering of sin» — lying — «and their consuming what is unlawfully got? Evil indeed is what they were working» (Q. 5:63) — their leaving off forbidding them. The severest verse upon the ulama. «Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their uttering of sin and their consuming what is unlawfully got? Evil indeed is what they were working» (Q. 5:63). «And the Jews said» — when Allah straitened them on account of their calling the Prophet ﷺ a liar, after they had been the wealthiest of people in property they became poor, and they said — «The hand of Allah is fettered» — withheld — «Their hands are fettered»

May Allah withhold their hands from the doing of every good — this is an imprecation against them. «And they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched» (Q. 5:64) — an intensification in describing Him as liberal; and He put the hand in the dual to convey abundance, since the utmost that the generous man expends of his wealth is to give with both his hands. Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His two hands are outstretched. The hand of Allah is not a bodily limb, by the proof of ⟨both His hands are right hands⟩. These attributes that have come in the Qurʾan and the hadith — the early generations used to affirm them according to their outward sense and to commit the meaning to Allah, Blessed and Exalted: we believe in it as Allah intends, we believe in it as intended by

the Messenger of Allah. The later scholars interpret figuratively, and so they interpreted the hand as power. And if they interpret the hand as power, what will they do with the two hands here? Power is one, and this is a dual. And it has come in the plural: «And the heaven — We built it with hands» (Q. 51:47). This is a plural of more than two; we do not know whether it is six or eight. So the right course is that the hand be left according to its outward sense and that we commit the meaning to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. His two hands are not two hands as ours are. «He spends how He wills» — in enlarging and in straitening; there is no objection against Him — «and what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them» — of the Qurʾan — «in insolence and unbelief» — because of their unbelief in it — «and We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection» — and every sect of them opposes the other — «Whenever they kindle a fire for war» — for war against the Prophet ﷺ — «Allah extinguishes it, and they strive on the earth in corruption» — working corruption by acts of disobedience — «and Allah does not love the workers of corruption» (Q. 5:64). «And had the People of the Book believed» — in Muḥammad — «and guarded against» — unbelief — «We would have effaced from them their evil deeds and admitted them into gardens of bliss» (Q. 5:65). «And had they upheld the Torah» — that is, acted by the Torah — «and the Gospel» — they acted by what is in them both, and what is in them both is faith in the Prophet ﷺ. The mention of Muḥammad has come in the Torah and the Gospel; both of them gave tidings of him. ʿĪsā said: ⟨I shall go, and the Paraclete will come to you.⟩ «and what was sent down to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet» (Q. 5:66). Had they acted by what the Torah and the Gospel directed them to, which is faith in Muḥammad ﷺ, Allah would have opened to them and enlarged their provision and poured upon them from every side. «Among them is a moderate community» — yes, among them is a group that acts by it, and they are ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām — «and many of them — evil is what they do» (Q. 5:66). «O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord» — and do not conceal anything of it for fear that some harm reach you — «and if you do not do so» — convey all that has been sent down to you — «then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people» (Q. 5:67) — from their killing you. And he ﷺ used to be kept under guard until it came down, and he said: ⟨Disperse, for I have been protected by⟩

⟨Allah!⟩ «Indeed Allah does not guide the unbelieving people» (Q. 5:67). The Messenger ﷺ, when a verse came down that was severe upon the unbelievers, would hesitate to convey it to them, fearing that they would increase in unbelief; and so this verse came down upon him: «O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not do so, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people» (Q. 5:67). So he conveyed everything that had been sent down to him. For this reason ʿĀʾisha said: ⟨Whoever claims that Muḥammad concealed anything of what Allah taught him has fabricated a monstrous calumny against Allah⟩ — that is, the lie. And the Messenger ﷺ: Allah gave him the knowledge of the first and the last and gave him more besides. He gave him three knowledges: a knowledge over which Allah took the covenant from him that he convey it and conceal nothing of it — and he conveyed it and did not conceal a letter of it, and that is the Qurʾan and everything he was asked about of the rulings of the shariʿa. And a knowledge in which Allah gave him the choice: if he wished he conveyed it and if he wished he did not convey it — so he conveyed that knowledge to the elect and concealed it from the rest; and it is the knowledge that the majādhīb (those seized by divine attraction) utter when they reach sheer annihilation. And a knowledge over which the covenant was taken from him to conceal it, and he concealed it — and it is the knowledge of the secret of the decree; he conveyed it to no one. «Convey what has been sent down to you» — this pertains to the Qurʾan and to the whole of the shariʿa, or to something he was asked about — «And Allah will protect you from the people» — Allah promised him protection.
So when night came, a guard would stand at his door; and when this verse came down he raised the curtain from the door and said:
⟨Disperse, disperse, for Allah has sufficed me.⟩ «Say: O People of the Book, you stand upon nothing» — of religion that counts for anything

«until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord» — by acting upon what is in it, which is faith in the Messenger ﷺ — «and what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them» — of the Qurʾan — «in insolence and unbelief» — because of their unbelief in it — «so do not grieve» — do not be sad — «over the unbelieving people» (Q. 5:68) — if they do not believe in you, do not concern yourself with them. «Indeed those who believe and those who are Jews» — they are the Jews — «and the Sabians» — a sect of them — «and the Christians — whoever believes» — of them — «in Allah and the Last Day and does righteousness: no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve» (Q. 5:69) — in the hereafter. Islam has done away with division by race. «whoever believes in Allah» — so all the believers are brothers: «Indeed the believers are brothers» (Q. 49:10). Whether his origin is Jewish or Christian or Sabian or Magian, or black or red or Arab — Islam has made them all brothers to one another when they pronounced the two testimonies of faith (al-shahādatān), and they are equals. «Indeed We took the covenant of the Children of Isrāʾīl» — upon faith in Allah and His Messenger — «and We sent to them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them» — of them — «with what their souls did not desire» — of the truth, they declared him a liar — «a party» — of them — «they declared liars, and a party»

of them — «they slay» (Q. 5:70) — they killed him, like Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā; and the expression 'they slay' rather than 'they killed' tells a past state in the present, out of regard for the rhyming verse-end. «And they thought» — they supposed — «that there would not be» — befall — «a trial» — a punishment upon them for their declaring the messengers liars and for killing them — «so they were blinded» — to the truth, so they did not see it — «and deafened» — to hearing it — «then Allah relented toward them» — when they repented — «then they were blinded and deafened» — a second time — «many of them; and Allah is seeing of what they do» (Q. 5:71) — so He requites them. «Indeed those have disbelieved who said: Allah is the Messiah son of Maryam» — a sect of them said that Allah is the Messiah — «And the Messiah said: O Children of Isrāʾīl, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord» — for I am a servant and not a god. The first thing he uttered was «Indeed I am the servant of Allah» (Q. 19:30). «Indeed whoever associates anything with Allah» — in worship, other than Him — «Allah has forbidden him the Garden, and his refuge is the Fire; and the wrongdoers have no helpers» (Q. 5:72) — who would defend them. «Indeed those have disbelieved who said: Allah is the third of three» — a sect said that the gods are three: Allah is a god, and ʿĪsā, and his mother; and they too are a sect — «and there is no god but one God. And if they do not desist from what they say» — of the trinity, and do not profess the oneness — «there shall surely touch those who disbelieved» — who held firm in unbelief — «of them a punishment»

«painful» (Q. 5:73). ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace, when he was raised up, left those who believed in him upon his religion, which is faith in Allah and that ʿĪsā is the servant of Allah and His messenger. The unbelievers used to fight the Muslims, and Allah would give the Muslims victory over them, until a man called Būlus led them astray — he is the one they call Paul down to our own day. When he had fought them for a time and was unable to overcome them, he made an outward show of Islam, that he had entered their religion. He entered their religion and strove hard until he gained great fame and renown and acceptance with them all. And one day, when they had prayed the dawn prayer, he said to them: I have seen the Deity. I saw ʿĪsā; he came down to me and entrusted to me a secret which I am to leave with a trustworthy man from among you; and I must draw near to Allah with my own self. So he summoned three: a man named Yaʿqūb, a man named Malkān, and a man named Nasṭūr. He took Yaʿqūb aside and said to him: Do you know that I entered your religion late and outstripped you all? Yes. That is for a secret which I have come to know and you do not know it; and so long as you do not hold this belief, you will gain no benefit from this religion. He said to him: And what is that? He said to him: The Deity is ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace. He came down in His own person and returned to His malakūt (unseen dominion). Whoever does not hold that ʿĪsā is Allah will never gain any benefit from this religion — until he had put this into his heart. When he knew that he had accepted it from him, he said to him: Set out towards this quarter, and admonish the people and call them to this creed. Then he took Malkān aside and said to him: I entered your religion late and outstripped you all by reason of a creed, which is the one by which Allah profited me; and so long as you do not know this, you will never profit. He said: And what is that creed? He said: The deities are three — ʿĪsā is a deity, and his mother is a deity, and Allah is a deity, the third of three. And when he accepted it from him, he sent him to another quarter to call the people to that creed.

Then Nasṭūr came, and he summoned him too and said to him: Do you know that I entered your religion newly and outstripped you all? Because I know a creed such that whoever does not know it gains no benefit from this religion. That creed, what is it? It is that ʿĪsā is a son to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And when he accepted it from him, he sent him out as a caller to a third quarter; and he himself — the enemy of Allah — took his own life, he killed himself

So those factions have remained, calling to these creeds down to our own day. And the fourth faction, which remained upon the Israelite creed of ʿĪsā, are those who believed that Allah is one and that ʿĪsā is the servant of Allah and His messenger. Among them was the Negus; and for this reason, when the Qurʾan reached him, he believed in the Prophet ﷺ and held him truthful, because it agreed with what
ʿĪsā had left them upon.

«And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely touch those of them who disbelieve» (Q. 5:73). «Will they not turn in repentance to Allah and seek His forgiveness» — for what they said; an interrogative of rebuke — «and Allah is forgiving» — to whoever repents — «merciful» — to him (Q. 5:74). «What is the Messiah»
«the son of Maryam but a messenger; there have gone» — passed away — «before him the messengers» — so he passes away as they did, and he is not a deity as

they claimed; otherwise he would not have passed away. «and his mother was a veracious woman» — an intensive form of truthfulness — «the two of them used to eat food» — like others among the animals; and whoever is so cannot be a deity, because of his being composite and his weakness and what issues from him of urine and excrement — «Look how We make clear to them the signs» — how Allah made His oneness plain by His words «the two of them used to eat food»: whoever eats food must needs relieve himself, and this does not befit the side of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «Look how We make clear to them the signs». «Then look how they are turned away» — they are turned aside from the truth, though the proof stands (Q. 5:75). «Say: do you worship, apart from Allah» — other than Him — «that which has no power to harm you or to profit you? And Allah is the Hearing» — of your words — «the Knowing»
of your circumstances (Q. 5:76). «Say: O People of the Book» — the Jews and the Christians — «do not go to excess» — do not pass beyond the limit — «in your religion»

an excess — «other than the truth» — by your putting ʿĪsā down or raising him above his right. Both factions went astray concerning ʿĪsā: the Jews accused his mother and said that Maryam was a fornicatress and that ʿĪsā was a child of fornication; and the Christians raised him above his measure.
And so they made him a son to Allah, or [said] he is Allah. Both factions went astray. «And do not follow the desires of a people who have gone astray before»
— by their excess — and they are their forebears — «and they led many astray» — of the people — «and strayed from the right way» — the way of truth (Q. 5:77),

And al-sawāʾ in origin is the middle. «Those who disbelieved among the Children of Isrāʾīl were cursed by the tongue of Dāwūd» — Dāwūd supplicated against them and they were transformed into apes, and they are the people of Ayla — «and ʿĪsā son of Maryam» — he supplicated against them and they were transformed into swine, and they are the people of the Table — «That» — the cursing — «was because they disobeyed» — on account of their disobedience — «and they were transgressing» (Q. 5:78). «They did not restrain one another» — none of them forbade another — «from» — repeating — «a wrong they had done» — the cause of their destruction was this — «Evil indeed was what they used to do» (Q. 5:79). And for this reason commanding the good and forbidding the wrong is obligatory. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand if he is able; and if not, then with his tongue; and if not, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.⟩ «You see» — O Muḥammad — «many of them taking those who disbelieve as allies» — of the people of Mecca, out of hatred for you — «Evil indeed is what their souls have sent ahead for them» — of the deeds for their return, which brings upon them — «that Allah is angry with them, and in the punishment they shall abide forever» (Q. 5:80). «And had they believed in Allah» — truly — «and the Prophet» — Muḥammad ﷺ — «and what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them» — the unbelievers — «as allies, but many of them are transgressors» (Q. 5:81) — they have gone out from faith. O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad and grant him peace.

«You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah». Allah, Blessed and Exalted, told us in this verse (āya) that the Jews are the most intense of people in enmity toward the Muslims, then the polytheists. «And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say: we are Christians». And you find the Christians nearer to affection for the Muslims than the Jews and than the polytheists. «That» — the nearness, the nearness of their affection for the believers — «is because among them are priests» — scholars — «and monks»

— worshippers — «and that they are not arrogant» (Q. 5:82) — against following the truth. In this verse He described the condition of the Jews and the condition of the Christians. It has been said that this is specific to the delegation of the Negus and not to all the Christians, because among the Christians are those who show the Muslims the most intense enmity; and it has been said that it is unrestricted. So the Jews are more intense in enmity toward the Muslims than the Christians — this, although the unbelief (kufr) of the Christians is grosser than the unbelief of the Jews. The Christians: their unbelief is in the divinity and in prophethood; and the Jews: their unbelief is in prophethood only. But the Jews were formed by nature to love this world, and because of the intensity of their love for this world they became worse than the Christians, who are the more intense in unbelief; so they became more intense in hostility toward the Muslims than others, on account of their envy and their arrogance and their love of leadership, on the strength of the hadith: ⟨The love of this world is the head of every sin.⟩ The Jews, when they have power over
each patrician (biṭrīq) among his patricians with gifts, so that they might incline the heart of the Negus toward them. And when the two of them came to the Negus, they said to him:

⟨There have appeared among us a people given to corruption. They have corrupted our land and have joined themselves to your land. Give us power over them, that we may take them away to our land; for they are not upon your religion and they are not upon our religion. Had they been upon your religion we would have been content with them, or upon our religion [we would have been content]; but they are not upon your religion nor upon our religion, and their case is such and such.⟩ So the Negus sent to a company of the Companions that they should attend his assembly, and they attended, with Jaʿfar al-Ṭayyār at their head. And when they reached the door they said: ⟨Peace be upon you.⟩ The two said: ⟨Did you hear? They did not greet you with what your people greet you with. This is a proof of what we are telling you.⟩ The Negus said to them: ⟨And why did you not greet me as people greet me?⟩ They said: ⟨We greeted you with the greeting of the Garden, and the greeting of Islam, and the greeting of our Prophet.⟩ He said: ⟨How noble is this! I am content.⟩ He asked them what their religion was, and they said to him: ⟨We were people of the Jāhiliyya: we worshipped the idol, and we severed the ties of kinship, and we did and we did, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and called us to Islam — the worship of Allah alone, and the performance of the prayer, and the fasting, and voluntary alms, and chastity, and the joining of the ties of kinship.⟩

He said: ⟨What does your companion say of our companion ʿĪsā?⟩ They said: «The Messenger of Allah and His word, which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him» (Q. 4:171). So he took a small stick and said: ⟨Your companion has not added to what our companion said by the measure of this stick. Have you anything of his Book?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ He said: ⟨Recite.⟩ So Jaʿfar recited Sūrat Maryam. Around the Negus were priests and monks, and they wept until their tears overflowed, and they said: ⟨How like this is to what the Spirit used to bring!⟩ The Negus said to the two envoys of the polytheists: ⟨May Allah disfigure you both! Is it against these men that you would mislead me?⟩ And he said to the Companions: ⟨You are sayūm⟩ — its meaning is: you are in safety — ⟨Go; you are at liberty in your affair.⟩ The affair of the two envoys who had come from Mecca was ruined; and between the two of them there had been intense enmity. So when ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ saw that their affair was ruined, he set about contriving the destruction of his companion. He said to ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd: ⟨You are a handsome man, and these kings — their women rule them. You must go in to the king's wife and show her affection, until there is friendship between you two, so that she may incline the king's heart toward us.⟩ So ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd took to frequenting the woman's house. Then ʿAmr b.

al-ʿĀṣ was alone with the king and said to him: ⟨My companion is an evil man; beware of him with respect to your women, for he is a wicked man.⟩ So the Negus entered his house one night and met ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd coming out of his wife's chamber. He seized him and beat him and tortured him, and blew into his urethra until his belly swelled, and cast him into the sea; and he went mad and took to roaming with the wild beasts. And ʿAmr returned to Mecca disappointed, and Allah destroyed ʿUmāra b. al-Walīd.

Then the Negus wrote to the Messenger ﷺ informing him of his Islam, and he sent his son and seventy riders; and when they were in the middle of the sea they drowned. In that period the husband of Umm Ḥabība bt. Abī Sufyān died, and the Messenger wrote to the king, the Negus, that he should ask for her hand on his behalf ﷺ. So he sent Abraha to her as an envoy; and when the envoy came to Umm Ḥabība and brought her the good news of the proposal of the Messenger ﷺ, she gave him all that the Negus had given her. They contracted her [in marriage] to al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ for four hundred dīnārs, and they prepared her and sent her to the Prophet ﷺ. Jaʿfar brought her on the day of the Prophet's ﷺ return from Khaybar. On that day he ﷺ says: ⟨I do not know by which of them I should rejoice: by the Islam of the Negus, or by the arrival of Jaʿfar, or by my bride, or by the conquest of Khaybar.⟩ And he said to Jaʿfar: ⟨You resemble me in my form and in my character.⟩

that the king, until he came to look at him, and he prayed over him. This is the occasion of the verse's revelation. The description is general, for all the Christians, the priests and the monks: they are lighter in enmity toward the Muslims, because of their renunciation of this world and because their religion is the leaving off of injury — the opposite of the Jews, who are the more intense in enmity on account of their love for this world. Whoever is avid for this world — whenever he sees a servant whom Allah has raised up, he envies him and shows him enmity and makes war on him, inescapably. «And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger» — of the Qurʾan — «you see their eyes overflow with tears at what they have recognised of the truth. They say: our Lord, we have believed» — we have affirmed the truth of Your Prophet and Your Book — «so write us down with those who bear witness» (Q. 5:83). This is the description of the monks and the priests. «You see their eyes overflow with tears» — they wept until their eyes overflowed with tears, from the abundance of their tears. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Two eyes the Fire shall not touch: an eye that has wept out of fear of Allah, and an eye that has passed the night guarding the Muslims in the path of Allah.⟩ And they said, in answer to those of the Jews who reproached them for Islam: «And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth» — the Qurʾan — «and hope that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people» (Q. 5:84) — the believers — into the Garden. The Exalted said: «So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein; and that is the recompense of those who do good» (Q. 5:85) — by faith. «And those who have disbelieved and denied Our signs, those are the companions of the Blaze» (Q. 5:86) — they enter the Fire. Whoever believes in Allah enters the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in Allah enters the Fire. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨All of you will enter the Garden except whoever refuses. Whoever believes in me and affirms my truth and says 'there is no god but Allah, Muḥammad⟩

⟨is the Messenger of Allah — he enters the Garden; and whoever refuses has refused to enter the Garden.⟩ A king rode out and came to a town in which Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī had lived, and he asked: ⟨Is there here anyone who met him?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes. There is an aged shaykh who lived in the time of Abū Yazīd.⟩ So the king summoned him and asked him: ⟨Have you retained anything of his speech? Have you memorised anything of what he used to say?⟩ He said: ⟨Yes. I heard him say: whoever has seen me, the Fire will not touch him.⟩ He said: ⟨Glory be to Allah!
