How can this be, when Abū Jahl saw the Messenger ﷺ and he is of the people of the Fire?⟩ He said to him: ⟨O king, Abū Jahl did not see the Messenger ﷺ; he only saw the orphan of Abū Ṭālib. Had he seen the Messenger ﷺ he would have believed in him and would have entered the Garden.⟩ So the king understood, and affirmed his truth. They are two kinds of form: the forms of persons and the forms of beliefs. The forms of beliefs, when they are present, suffice in place of the forms of persons; and the forms of persons, when they appear, do not suffice in place of the forms of beliefs. Here we are today in the fourteenth century: we have not seen the Messenger ﷺ, nor have we seen the miracles. We heard of him and we heard of the miracles, and we saw the Qurʾan, and so we believed in him and affirmed his truth. These, the Quraysh, witnessed his noble face and saw his miracles, and they did not believe.
May Allah grant us the beliefs.
«O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful to you»
The occasion of this verse's revelation is that the Prophet

ﷺ gave the Companions a penetrating admonition, at which hearts softened and eyes shed tears. Ten of the Companions gathered in the house of ʿUthmān b. Maẓʿūn, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: ⟨We must have monasticism, and castration, and the abandoning of the eating of meat and of perfume; and we shall fast forever and not⟩
⟨break the fast, and we shall pray forever and not sleep until we die.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ heard of that and said:

⟨Are you the ones who say that you are going out for monasticism, and for castration, and for abandoning the good things?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ said to them: ⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! The monasticism of my community is jihad. There is no monasticism in Islam.⟩ He said: ⟨Then I shall castrate myself.⟩ He said: ⟨The castration of my community is fasting.⟩ He said: ⟨Then I shall divorce the woman, or I shall never go in to her.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! If you are able to have two, or three, or four, then do so. For every time you lie with one of them and Allah does not decree a child for you, you will find a young servant in the Garden; and if Allah decrees a child for you and he dies before you, he will be a forerunner and an intercessor on the Day of Resurrection; and if you die before him, he will be a light for you on the Day of Resurrection.⟩ He said: ⟨Then I shall not eat meat.⟩ He said: ⟨Gently, ʿUthmān! I eat meat whenever I find it, and were I to ask my Lord He would feed it to me every day.⟩ He said: ⟨I shall give up perfume.⟩ He said: ⟨I do perfume myself. Jibrīl commanded me to perfume myself on alternate days; but on Friday perfume is indispensable.⟩ He said: ⟨Then I shall pray and never sleep, and fast and not break the fast.⟩ He said: ⟨Gently! I pray and I sleep, and I fast and I break the fast; and whoever turns away from my sunna is not [of me].⟩ So this verse came down. The verse accords with what comes before it, for the verse before it praised the priests
and the monks for their quality; and they had abandoned the world entirely. For this reason it was imagined by some people that that is better than partaking of

the good things. So this verse came down. He makes clear to them that even though those monks were described with a praiseworthy quality, the Muslims are better than they; for the verse forbids the Muslims to make unlawful what is lawful, just as it forbade them at the beginning of the sura to make lawful what is unlawful: «Fulfil the contracts; the beasts of the flocks have been made lawful for you» (Q. 5:1). One who makes the unlawful lawful is like one who makes the lawful unlawful. «Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you» — the delectable among foods: if they are lawful, do not forbid them — «and do not transgress» — do not overstep the command of Allah. The pivot is with the command of Allah alone: if Allah has forbidden a thing, leave it; and if He has made a thing lawful, partake of it — «Indeed Allah does not love the transgressors. And eat of what Allah has provided you, lawful and wholesome» — it is the lawful — «and fear Allah, in whom you are believers» (Q. 5:87–88). The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Allah, Exalted, has imposed obligations, so do not neglect them; and He has set bounds, so do not transgress them; and He has forbidden things, so do not violate them; and He has kept silent about things, out of mercy to you and not out of forgetfulness, so do not inquire into them.⟩ And the gravest in crime among the Muslims is one who asks about a thing that was lawful until it was made unlawful. «And fear Allah, in whom you are believers» (Q. 5:88). Partaking of the good things of provision is no deficiency in the servant's case. Yes — whoever is extravagant and occupies himself with procuring the delectable among food and drink, perhaps

that leads him to eagerness for acquiring them, and that drags him into occupation with this world and the abandoning of the worship of Allah and forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah. And whoever rejects these good things and takes to monasticism as the monks did — that too diminishes his constitution, and so diminishes his intellect; for some foods strengthen a man's constitution and strengthen his intellect, and recognition together with the loss of the intellect is impossible. There must be thought, and there must be reflection, and the way to that is the intellect. As for the monks, monasticism stripped them of their intellects, and so they did not arrive at the recognition of Allah, because their intellects were diminished. And those who occupied themselves with this world and scrambled greedily after the appetites and forgot the remembrance of Allah — they too did not arrive at recognition. And the end, in reality, is recognition. «And eat of what Allah has provided you, lawful and wholesome, and fear Allah, in whom you are believers» (Q. 5:88). «Allah will not take you to task for what is thoughtless in your oaths» — that which occurs in your oaths. The commentator said: ⟨It is what the tongue runs on to without the intent of swearing, as when a man says: No, by Allah; and Yes indeed, by Allah.⟩ And this is the school of al-Shāfiʿī. «but He will take you to task for what you have made binding» — [in one reading,] ʿāqadtum — «the oaths» — upon it, by swearing deliberately — «then its expiation» — if you break it — «is the feeding of ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families» (Q. 5:89). Whoever swears by Allah and breaks his oath, the expiation is upon him; and the expiation is the feeding of ten poor persons, for each poor person a dry measure of grain (mudd). «from the average of what you feed your families» — neither its highest nor its lowest. The imams differed over this — the feeding of ten poor persons. Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī said: for each one a dry measure of grain, and transfer of ownership suffices. Abū Ḥanīfa says: a midday meal and an evening meal suffice, because the text speaks of feeding, so feeding dispenses with transfer of ownership. And the Qurʾan says «the feeding of ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families» (Q. 5:89), and a man's custom in feeding his family is that he makes over to them their sustenance, not that he feeds them; for this reason making over ownership to the poor persons suffices, for each one a dry measure of grain. As for the midday meal and the evening meal — a man's midday meal may be less than a dry measure of grain, or more. And the sunna made clear that for each poor person a dry measure of grain. So on this basis the feeding of ten

poor persons, for each one a dry measure of grain. A dry measure of grain — that is the way. And if he feeds one poor person a dry measure of grain each day for ten days, that suffices him. «or clothing them» — with what is called clothing, such as a shirt, a turban and a waist-wrapper; and it does not suffice to hand over what has been mentioned to a single poor person, and al-Shāfiʿī holds this — «or the freeing of a slave» — a believing one, as in the expiation for killing and for the ẓihār oath (a man's likening of his wife to a woman forbidden to him), carrying the unrestricted upon the restricted — «and whoever does not find» — any one of what has been mentioned — «then the fasting of three days» — is his expiation. And the apparent sense of it is that there is no requirement of
consecutiveness — and al-Shāfiʿī holds this. «That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn» — and have broken them — «and guard»

that you do not break them, so long as it is not upon doing a good deed or making peace among people, as in Sūrat al-Baqara. ⟨Whoever swears to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever swears to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him.⟩ «Thus» — like what He has made clear to you of what
has been mentioned — «Allah makes clear to you His signs, that you may be thankful» (Q. 5:89) — you thank Him for that. «O you who»

«Wine, gambling, sacrificial stones and divining arrows are only» — this is the fourth verse concerning wine. When «Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying» (Q. 4:43) was revealed, ʿUmar said: ⟨O Allah, make clear to us concerning wine a clarification that suffices.⟩ «O you who believe, wine is only» — the intoxicant that overcomes the intellect — «and gambling» — wagering — «and sacrificial stones»

— the idols — «and divining arrows» — the arrows of divination by lot. These two items are unbelief (kufr). He coupled wine and gambling with these two items to confirm the prohibition of them both. «An abomination» — foul and loathsome — «of Satan's doing» — which he makes attractive — «so avoid it» — avoid the abomination, by which these things are designated, that you should do it — «that you may prosper. Satan only wants to sow enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling» (Q. 5:90–91) — Satan wanted to sow enmity among you at the drinking of wine, because the custom of the drinkers of wine is that they gather over it, their aim being affection; but when they have drunk and become drunk and their intellects are gone, they revile one another and strike one another and fight one another. And gambling is likewise. Gambling is a game by which they come by money without earning it: whoever wins takes the money, and whoever loses has his money taken, then he adds another sum of money

«believe and do righteous deeds, any blame» — this was revealed when the Muslims said: our brothers died on the day of Uḥud, and they had drunk wine and did not know of its prohibition; we fear that they may incur sin in that. And so this verse was revealed: «There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds in what they have eaten» — they partook of wine and of gambling before the prohibition —

«they guard against» — the forbidden things — «and believe and do righteous deeds, then guard against [evil] and believe» — they held firm to godfearing (al-taqwā) and faith (īmān) — «then guard against [evil] and do good; and Allah loves those who do good» (Q. 5:93). Some of the ignorant have adduced this verse as proof that wine is permitted. They said: «There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds in what they have eaten» — it is wine. And they would not accept that it was revealed concerning those who had died, because the verse comes with idhā, which is for the future. But they went astray. «There is no [blame] upon those who»
«believe and do righteous deeds, any blame in what they have eaten» — that is, they ate; and the eating here is the drinking. And […]
«and believe and do righteous deeds, then guard against [evil] and believe, then guard against [evil] and do good» — it was revealed concerning two parties: some of them

and some of them were absent at the time the verse was revealed, before the verse of prohibition reached them. If they were guarding against everything forbidden and complying with the command of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what they drank until the verse reaches them. And religion rests upon three pillars: submission (islām), faith, and iḥsān (excellence in worship). He repeated the godfearing three times: «then guard against [evil]» — in the station of submission — «and believe», «then guard against [evil]» — in the station of faith — «and do good», «and Allah loves those who do good». A person [must] submit, and believe, and do good: submission, faith and iḥsān. And iḥsān is the goal. The Messenger explained it
ﷺ — in terms to which nothing can be added: ⟨that you worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then He sees you⟩

«and Allah loves the doers of good» (Q. 5:93) — they have covered the distance — «O you who believe, Allah will surely try you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach» (Q. 5:94). When He had made clear what He had made lawful and what He had forbidden, He brought a particular kind, namely game, with respect to one in consecration (al-muḥrim), or within the sanctuary. «O you who believe, Allah will surely try you» — He will surely test you — «Allah with something» — which He sends to you — «of the game that reaches» — that take hold of it — «your hands and your lances» — the large among it — and that was at al-Ḥudaybiya, while they were in ritual consecration (iḥrām), and the wild beasts and the birds would crowd upon them in their camping places — «that Allah may know» — with a knowing that becomes manifest — «who fears Him unseen»

that is, being absent, not seeing Him, and so he refrains from the game — «then whoever transgresses after that» — after the prohibition of it, and hunts it — «his is a painful punishment» (Q. 5:94). «O you who believe, do not kill game while you are consecrated» — in consecration for the hajj or for the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumra) — «and whoever of you kills it deliberately, then the recompense is the like of what he killed of the cattle» — he owes a recompense the like of what he killed of the cattle, its counterpart in bodily form — «judged concerning it» — as to the like, by two men — «by two of justice from among you» — who have the acumen by which they distinguish the things that resemble it. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar and ʿAlī judged for the ostrich a sacrificial camel; Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿUbayda for the wild cow and the wild ass a cow; Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAwf for the gazelle a sheep; and Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar and others judged a sheep for the pigeon, because it resembles it in gulping water — «as an offering» — a recompense — «reaching the Kaʿba» — it is brought to the sanctuary and slaughtered there and given as alms to its poor; it is not permitted that it be slaughtered wherever he may be — «or an expiation, the feeding of poor persons» — or he owes an expiation, the feeding of poor persons: the feeding of the poor from the staple food of the land, to the value of the recompense, for each poor person a dry measure of grain (mudd) — «or the equivalent of that in fasting» — or he reckons for each dry measure a day's fast; and if a fraction occurs, he fasts a full day for it — «that he may taste the evil consequence of his deed» (Q. 5:95) — the weight of his recompense, the recompense of the deed which he did
Abū Qatāda had not entered consecration; and while they were travelling, they saw wild asses, and Abū Qatāda charged the asses and hamstrung one of them.

So they dismounted and ate of its flesh, and they said: ⟨Shall we eat the flesh of game while we are consecrated?⟩ So we carried what remained of the flesh of the she-ass. And when they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ they said: ⟨O Messenger of Allah, we had entered consecration, and Abū Qatāda had not entered consecration, and we saw wild asses, and Abū Qatāda charged them and hamstrung one of them, a she-ass. So we dismounted and ate of its flesh. Then we said: shall we eat the flesh of game while we are consecrated? So we carried what remained of its flesh.⟩ He said: ⟨Did any one of you command him to charge them, or point them out to him?⟩ They said: No. He said: ⟨Then eat what remains of its flesh.⟩

«the Sacred House» — the inviolable — «a support for the people» — by which the affair of their religion stands, through the pilgrimage to it, and their worldly life, through the security of whoever is within it and its not being assailed, and the gathering of the fruits of everything to it. The Kaʿba is the House of Allah which is at Mecca. Allah made it a sanctuary, and made it secure, and made it a support for the people — that is, that by which the interests of their religion and of their worldly life stand. As for their religion, the Kaʿba is the qibla of the Muslims in all the regions of the world, and the place of their rites, their hajj. And the interests of this world [lie] in the security which the people of the House find: in the Jāhiliyya they were in wars continually and had no security, except when the months of the hajj came, [when] they strove to earn their livelihood, every one of them earning the food of a year and gathering it before the sacred months ran out. That was a support for them, that is, the cause of their livelihood — «and the sacred month» — the sacred months: Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram and Rajab — a support for them in their security, since they knew that there was no fighting, and so they earned their livelihoods — «and the offering and the garlands»

He mentioned four things and made them a security for the people and a support for them: the Kaʿba itself, and the sacred month, and the offering — when a man garlands an offering, it is likewise — and the garlands. «That» — the making — «is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is knowing of all things» (Q. 5:97). For His making that in order to draw benefits to you and to ward off harms from you before they occur is a proof of His knowledge of what is in existence and of what is to be — «Know that Allah is severe in punishment» — to His enemies — «and that Allah is forgiving» — to His awliyāʾ (friends of Allah) — «merciful» (Q. 5:98). «severe in punishment, and that Allah is forgiving, merciful» — it is the practice of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in His Book that whenever He mentions a threat He joins to it a promise, as He has done in this verse: «Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is forgiving, merciful» (Q. 5:98). And in another verse: «Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving»

«the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment» (Q. 15:49–50). And as He said in another verse: «And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is kind to the servants» (Q. 3:30). And He said: «whoever fears al-Raḥmān» (Q. 50:33). When He mentioned the word of fear He joined it to al-Raḥmān. Had He joined it to «severe in punishment», fear would overcome hope; but whenever He mentions a fear He joins to it a hope, so that the servant may be always hoping and fearing — «Nothing is upon the Messenger but the conveying» — the delivering of the message — «and Allah knows what you disclose» — what you make manifest of deed — «and what you conceal» (Q. 5:99) — what you hide of it, and so He will requite you — «Say: not equal are the foul» — the forbidden —
«and the wholesome» — the lawful — «even though there please you» — delight you — «the abundance of the foul. So fear Allah» — in forsaking it — «O you who possess»
«understanding, that you may prosper» (Q. 5:100) — that you may win.

«O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they are disclosed to you, will grieve you» (Q. 5:101). The occasion of this verse's revelation is that they asked the Messenger ﷺ a great many questions, until one day he ﷺ grew angry and said:

⟨Ask me! By Allah, no one shall ask me about anything, so long as I stand in this place of mine, without my answering him.⟩ Then a man stood up, called ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥudhāfa, who was suspected of being ascribed to other than his father, and he said to him: O Messenger of Allah, who is my father? He said: ⟨Your father is Ḥudhāfa.⟩ And a man stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, where is my father? He said to him: ⟨Your father is in the Fire.⟩ ʿUmar knelt before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had repeated his words, 'Ask me, ask me, ask me' — ʿUmar knelt and said: ⟨We are content with Allah as Lord, and with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad as prophet; we shall not ask about anything.⟩ And this verse was revealed. And a man asked him: Is the hajj obligatory upon us every year? He was silent, and the man said it three times. He said: ⟨Leave me be so long as I leave you. For had I said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able. When I command you something, do of it what you are able; and when⟩
⟨I have forbidden you from a thing, then avoid it.⟩ Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made some things lawful and has forbidden some things and has been silent about

things, not being heedless [of them]; so do not search into that. Everything in which no prohibition and no permission is mentioned is among what Allah has been silent about, and it is pardoned. And so there was sent down: «O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if made manifest» — shown — «to you, would grieve you» — because of the hardship in them — «and if you ask about them» — if you ask about things — «when the Qurʾan is being sent down» — that is, in the time of the Prophet ﷺ — «they will be made manifest to you» — if you ask about things in his time, the Qurʾan must needs come down making them manifest; and whenever it makes them manifest, they grieve you, so do not ask about them. Indeed, «Allah has pardoned them» — [pardoned] your asking, so do not go back to it — «and Allah is forgiving and forbearing. A people before you asked about them, then became disbelievers because of them» (Q. 5:101–102). He restrained the Muslims from forbidding the lawful; and one who forbids the lawful is like one who makes the forbidden lawful. «Allah has not made»

Allah has not ordained — «any baḥīra, nor sāʾiba, nor waṣīla, nor ḥām» (Q. 5:103). The unbelievers of Quraysh used to assign certain things of their camels to their idols. «baḥīra» — she is the one whose milk is withheld for the idols, so that no one of the people milks her. The first to slit the ears of the baḥāʾir (the camels with slit ears dedicated to the idols) and to set loose the sawāʾib (the camels set loose by pagan vow) was ʿAmr b. Luḥayy. Quraysh were upon the religion of Ibrāhīm until the time of ʿAmr; he was the first to set these animals apart for their idols, and Quraysh followed him in it one after another. The Messenger said: ⟨I saw ʿAmr b. ʿĀmir b. Luḥayy al-Khuzāʿī dragging his entrails in the Fire.⟩ «The sāʾiba» — they would set her loose for their gods, so that no

one would load her. And the «waṣīla» — the first-bearing she-camel: she bears first, among the first offspring of the camels, a female, and then bears a female a second time; they would set her loose for their idols as well. The waṣīla — she joined the one to the other, with no male between the two. And the «ḥām»:

the stud of the camels: he covers a counted number of times, and when he has completed his covering they consign him to the idols. How extreme their folly! Allah did not ordain for them these baḥāʾir, nor the sawāʾib. «But those who disbelieve invent falsehood against Allah» — in that, and in ascribing it to Him — «and most of them do not reason» (Q. 5:103) — that that is an invention, because they imitated their fathers in it. «And when it is said to them, Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger» — to his judgement, in making lawful what you have forbidden — «they say, Sufficient for us» — enough for us — «is what we found our fathers upon» — of religion and shariʿa. That is their habit: whenever a guide came, they said: «Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon». He, Exalted, said: «A-» — is that enough for them? — «even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided» (Q. 5:104) — to the truth; and the interrogative is one of denial. Imitation of the fathers: if the fathers were guided, then praise be to Allah; and if they went astray, going astray is inevitable. And the religion of the fathers — the sons for the most part do not leave it. «O you who have believed, upon you is [the care of] your own souls» — guard them and undertake their setting right — «those who go astray will not harm you when you have been guided» (Q. 5:105). It is said: what is meant is that those who go astray among the People of the Book will not harm you; and it is said: what is meant is others than they, on the evidence of the ḥadīth of Abū Thaʿlaba al-Khushanī: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: ⟨Enjoin the good upon one another and forbid one another the wrong, until, when you see avarice obeyed, caprice followed, this world preferred, and every man of an opinion pleased with his own opinion⟩

⟨then hold to your own particular self.⟩ This verse is not [a warrant] for silence concerning enjoining the good or [forbidding] the wrong; rather it is about enjoining the good and forbidding the wrong.

The unbelievers and the Jews and the Christians are one side, and the Muslims another side. «upon you is [the care of] your own souls» — that is, your own souls, you, all the Muslims. A man gives his concern only to himself and to his Muslim brethren, enjoining them and forbidding them. «those who go astray will not harm you when you have been guided» — if the Christians and the Jews are in error and you Muslims are upon guidance, that does not harm you. For this reason, when they supposed that the verse was about abandoning the enjoining of the good and the forbidding of the wrong, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Enjoin the good upon one another and forbid one another the wrong, until, when you see avarice obeyed, caprice followed, this world preferred, and every man of an opinion pleased with his own opinion.⟩ When the world has become corrupt to the point that enjoining the good and forbidding the wrong is of no benefit, then at that point hold to your own particular selves. «To Allah is your return, all together» — this return of yours is to Allah — «then He will inform you of what you used to do» (Q. 5:105). «O you who have believed, testimony among you when there comes to one of you»

«death» (Q. 5:106). [This is] the most difficult verse (āya) in its parsing, its commentary, its meaning and its ruling. The occasion of its revelation: Tamīm al-Dārī and ʿAdī his brother, and the two of them were Christians upon the religion of the Christians, travelled to Syria, and with them was Budayl, the client of ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī. Budayl was a Muslim and his two companions were Christians, Tamīm al-Dārī and ʿAdī his brother. When they were midway along the road Budayl fell ill, and he wrote a document in which were the names of all his goods and hid it inside the goods, and he charged the two of them:

⟨When I die, deliver these goods to ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī.⟩ Then he died, and the two of them searched the goods and saw a goblet — a vessel of silver inlaid with three hundred mithqāls of gold — and they sold it for a thousand dīnārs and divided it between themselves. When they returned to Medina they delivered the goods to ʿAmr, and he searched them and saw the document and read what was in it, and saw the mention of the goblet.

So he came to the two of them and said to them: ⟨Your companion — perhaps he sold something of his goods before his death?⟩ The two said: ⟨No; he did not reach the place of the market, he died on the road.⟩ He said: ⟨Perhaps his illness was prolonged and he disposed of some of his property?⟩ The two said: ⟨No.⟩ He said: ⟨Then this goblet of silver, whose value is such and such — he mentioned it in his document.⟩ The two said: ⟨We did not see it.⟩ So ʿAmr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and the two verses came down. After a time the goblet was found in Mecca; rather, Tamīm al-Dārī embraced Islam and acknowledged the truthfulness of the Qurʾan — that the two of them had stolen the goblet and sold it for a thousand dīnārs; and he himself returned five hundred dīnārs, and he went to the heirs of his companion and took from them five hundred dīnārs. Concerning that case these verses came down: «the testimony among you» — let [two] bear witness among you — «when death approaches one of you» — its causes — «at the time»

«the bequest: two men of probity from among you» — what suffices by way of testimony is two Muslim men — «or two others from other than you» — if they do not find two Muslims, two others from outside your community bear witness, as Tamīm and ʿAdī did — «and if you have journeyed»
«you yourselves have journeyed» — you have travelled — «in the land, and the affliction of death befalls you: you shall detain the two of them» — you make the two of them stand — «from»
«after the prayer» — after the afternoon prayer — «and the two shall swear» — the two of them take an oath — «by Allah, if you are in doubt» — if you have doubted

about it. And the two of them say: «We will not take in exchange for it» — that is, for Allah — «a price» — a recompense — «even though he be a near relative; and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed we then» — if we concealed it — «would be among the sinful» (Q. 5:106). So the Messenger ﷺ summoned the two of them after the prayer of

the afternoon, and he made the two of them stand, and they swore — two unbelievers who took no care for the oath; they swore by Allah falsely. «But if it is discovered that the two of them have incurred sin» — and after a time it came to light, after their oath, that the two of them had lied; Tamīm acknowledged it when he embraced Islam — «then two others shall stand in their place from among those against whom the claim was established, the two nearest of kin» — then the heirs come forward and the two of them swear in place of the two unbelievers, from among the relatives of the deceased — «and the two shall swear by Allah: our testimony is truer than the testimony of those two, and we have not transgressed; indeed we would then be among the wrongdoers»

(Q. 5:107). When the second verse came down, the Messenger ﷺ sent to ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ, and he stood up and swore, he and a companion of his; the two of them swore by Allah that the two Christians had lied in what they had sworn to, and that it was the two of them who had stolen the goblet. So the Messenger ﷺ gave judgement against the two of them. And when Tamīm embraced Islam he acknowledged the truthfulness of the Qurʾan and returned the property. «That» — the ruling mentioned, the returning of the oath to the heirs — «is nearer» — closer to — «that they will bring»
the witnesses — «the testimony in its true form» (Q. 5:108). Since the oath passed over to the heirs, that is closer to the establishing of the right than

were the oath of the two unbelievers to be repeated, because the two of them do not fear Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «or that they fear that oaths will be turned back after their oaths» — upon the heirs — «And fear Allah» — by abandoning treachery and lying — «and listen» — to what you are commanded, a hearing of
acceptance. «And Allah does not guide the transgressing people» (Q. 5:108) — those who have gone out from His obedience; He does not guide them to the path of good.

And recall «the day Allah gathers the messengers» — it is the Day of Resurrection. It is the custom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that when He has mentioned rulings in His Book, until the rulings are established, He admonishes us with the hereafter. Recall the Day of Resurrection, the day Allah gathers the messengers. «Then He will say» — to them, in rebuke of their peoples — «what response were you given?» — what was it that you were answered when you called to al-tawḥīd (the divine oneness)? What did your people say? — «They will say: we have no knowledge» — of that — «indeed You, You are the Knower of the unseen» (Q. 5:109) — what is hidden from the servants. The knowledge of it left them for the intensity of the dread of the Day of Resurrection and their fright; then they bear witness against their communities once they are calmed. He mentioned that the messengers, for the intensity of the fright, «said: we have no knowledge; indeed You, You are the Knower of the unseen». And after that, when their minds returned to them, they bore witness against their communities that they had conveyed [the message] to them and that they had declared them liars. And this conflicts with «the greatest terror will not grieve them» (Q. 21:103): if some of the Muslims are secure on that day, then all the more the prophets and the messengers. Rather they observed proper comportment with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and committed the knowledge to Him, for He is the Knower of the unseen. ʿallām is said of Allah, and ʿallāma is not said of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; perhaps that is because of the tāʾ of the feminine. One says ʿālim and ʿallām. And recall «when Allah said: O ʿĪsā son of Maryam» — he is the first to be addressed on the Day of Resurrection, because of the going astray of his people — «remember My favour upon you and upon your mother» — by giving thanks for it — «when I strengthened you» — I gave you strength — «with the Holy Spirit» — Jibrīl — «you spoke to the people» — I strengthened you — «in the cradle» — an infant — «and in maturity» — this gives his descent before the Hour, since he was taken up before maturity, as came before in Āl ʿImrān — «and when I taught you the Book» — writing; he had a fine hand — «and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel» — he knew the Torah before the Gospel, and Allah sent down the Gospel upon him after that — «and when you create from the clay the likeness of a bird»
you shape a form like the bat — «then you blow into it and it becomes a bird by My permission» — Allah informed ʿĪsā, the spirit of Allah,
that they would bring him something of clay, and he would shape it into a bat, and he would blow into it, and it would fly by the permission of Allah. The bat is the most complete of

the birds: it has no feathers, and it does not lay eggs but gives birth as the animals give birth, and it menstruates, and it laughs, and it sees in the darkness and does not see in the light. Allah informed ʿĪsā, the spirit of Allah, that when he shaped clay and blew into it, there would come out a bird resembling the bat, until it passed from the sight of the people and fell down dead — a distinction between the creating of Allah and the creating of what is originated. «And you heal the blind-born and the leper by My permission» — when a human being born blind, or a leper, was brought to him, he wiped him and he was healed — «and when»
«you bring forth the dead» — from their graves; he did indeed revive the dead — «and when I restrained the Children of Isrāʾīl from you»
when they intended to kill you — «when you came to them with the clear proofs» — the miracles — «then those of them who disbelieved said: this is nothing»

which you have brought — «but manifest sorcery» (Q. 5:110). «And when I inspired the disciples» — I commanded them by his tongue — «that believe in Me and in My messenger» — ʿĪsā — «they said: we believe» — in the two of them — «and bear witness that we are muslims» (Q. 5:111). Recall «when the disciples said: O ʿĪsā son of Maryam, is He able» — will He do — «your Lord» — there are two readings: hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka — are you able to ask your Lord — or hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka — is your Lord able, that is, will your Lord do — «to send down to us a table from heaven» — so ʿĪsā said to them: «fear Allah» — in proposing signs — «if you are believers» (Q. 5:112). «They said: we desire» — to ask for it, for the sake of — «that we eat of it and that our hearts be at rest» — be settled, by an increase of certainty — «and that we know» — that we increase in knowledge — «that» — that you — «you have told us the truth» — in the claim of prophethood — «and that we be among those who witness to it» (Q. 5:113). When they had made plain the reason for their asking, ʿĪsā rose and performed the ablution and put on wool and prayed two cycles of the prayer (rakʿas), and he said this supplication: «ʿĪsā son of Maryam said: O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven that shall be for us» — on the day of its coming down — «a festival» — which we magnify and hold in honour — «for the first of us and the last of us» — of those who come after us — «and a sign from You» — of Your power and of my prophethood — «and provide for us» — it — «and You are the best»

«of providers» (Q. 5:114). Allah said, responding to him: «Indeed I am sending it down upon you; so whoever disbelieves afterward» — after its coming down — «of you, him I shall punish with a punishment wherewith I punish no other of the worlds» (Q. 5:115). So the angels came down with it from heaven, upon it seven loaves and seven fish, and they ate of it until they were filled. Ibn ʿAbbās said this. And in a hadith: ⟨The table was sent down from heaven with bread and meat, and they were commanded not to act treacherously and not to store up for the morrow; but they acted treacherously and stored up, and so they were transformed into apes and swine.⟩ ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace — his people asked that a table be sent down to them from heaven, so he prayed two cycles of the prayer and supplicated Allah, Blessed and Exalted, with this supplication: «O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven» — and then there was a cloud with a cloud above it, and between the two of them the table, until it came down before ʿĪsā, upon him be blessings and peace. He said:

⟨Let the most godfearing of you toward Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and the most hallowed of you, uncover — let him uncover this.⟩ They said: that is you. Shamʿūn said to him: ⟨You uncover it.⟩ So ʿĪsā uncovered it, and there was a fish that had no bones, cooked, part of it with olives and part of it with honey, and in it were all the kinds of food. ʿĪsā said to them: ⟨Eat, and give thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and do not store up, for every day it will come to you; and do not betray. Carry out Allah's command and leave off His prohibitions.⟩ Whoever ate of this food: if he was poor he became rich, and if he was sick he became sound, and if he was lowly he became eminent. So they ate, and the matter was so.

Then after that they quarrelled over it, and they took and stored up, and ʿĪsā supplicated against them, and they were transformed into apes and swine, just as Allah had threatened them: «Then indeed I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one among the worlds» (Q. 5:115) — they were transformed into apes and swine.

This Table came down on a Sunday, and for this reason the Christians took Sunday as a feast day among them, down to this day of ours — just as the Jews took Saturday as a feast day among them. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨You are the last, the foremost. Today is ours, and tomorrow is the Jews', and the day after tomorrow is the Christians'. This is the day which⟩

⟨they were given, and they differed over it, and Allah guided you to it: it is Friday.⟩ The feasts of the Muslims are at their completion of their acts of worship. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created this world [as] seven days. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

⟨This world is seven days.⟩ Its first is Saturday and its last is Friday. And Allah has made obligatory upon us five prayers in the day and the night; when Friday comes, and it is the seventh day, we have completed what is due from us of the prayers in the week. At the completion of what is due from us of the prayer in the week, Allah gave us Friday as a feast. For this reason we pray on Friday two cycles of the prayer (rakʿas) with a sermon (khuṭba), because a feast must have a sermon in it; the two sermons stand in the place of the two remaining cycles. The noon prayer is four cycles: two cycles are the two sermons, and two cycles are the prayer. This is the feast of the Muslims' completion of their prayer. And the second feast is the feast of their completion of their fasting, which is the day of the Breaking of the Fast; and the third feast is the feast of their completion of their hajj, which is the Feast of the Sacrifice. The Muslims have three feasts. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, manifests Himself to the people of the Garden, in the Garden, on the days of the feasts. So whoever has in the year only two feasts — the Breaking of the Fast and the Sacrifice — sees Allah in the Garden twice every year; and whoever has the feast of Friday sees Allah every week; and the people of the litanies — their feast is every morning and evening, and they see Allah every day, morning and evening; and the recognizers —

their feasts are the number of their breaths, because all their breaths are with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; and so their feasts in the Garden became the number of their breaths, and at every feast they must see Allah, Blessed and Exalted. As for the feast of those other than us: every community's feast is by its victory. If you see a community keeping a feast, it is only the day of its victory; and we — our feast is at our completion of
the worship of our Lord.

And remember «when [He] said» — [that is,] says — «Allah» — to ʿĪsā at the Resurrection. He is the first to be called to account and addressed on the Day of Resurrection, as a rebuke to his people. Allah says — while He manifests Himself by His name the Avenger — «O ʿĪsā son of Maryam, did you say to the people: take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?» — Allah asked him, though He knows that ʿĪsā did not say this — «He said»

ʿĪsā, and he had been set trembling from the intensity of fear — «Glory be to You» — declaring You free of what does not befit You, of a partner and of anything else — «It is not» — it is not fitting — «for me to say what is not mine by right» — the predicate of laysa lī — «If I had said it, You would have known it» — this saying: if I had said it, You would have known it — «You know what» — I conceal — «is within myself, and I do not know what» — You conceal — «is within Yourself» — of the things You know — «Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen things» (Q. 5:116) «I said to them nothing except what You commanded me» — and it is — «to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them» — a watcher, restraining them from what they say — «so long as I was among them. But when You took me» — You took me by raising [me] to heaven — «You were the Watcher over them, and You are, over all things» — of my saying to them and their saying after me and other than that — «a Witness» (Q. 5:117) — aware, knowing it — «If You punish them» — those of them who persisted in unbelief — «then indeed they are Your servants» — and You are their owner; You dispose of them as You will, and there is no objection against You — «and if You forgive them» — those of them who believed — «then indeed You are the Mighty» — the Prevailing in His affair — «the Wise» (Q. 5:118) — in His making. ʿĪsā answered; his answer in brief would have been: I did not say this to them — but in this there would be a want of adab (proper comportment). ʿĪsā did not say: I did not say it. He drew out the speech out of adab toward the Presence, and he did not state outright that he had not said this; rather he said: «If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what»

«in Yourself» (Q. 5:116). By this adab (proper comportment) he excelled. The prophets know adab with the Presence: «If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within me, and I do not know what is within Yourself» (Q. 5:116), instead of saying: I did not say this. As Ibrāhīm says: «And when I fall ill, it is He who heals me» (Q. 26:80). Sickness, since it was a deficiency, he did not ascribe it to al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted; he referred it back to himself, though he did not make himself sick. Rather: «when I fall ill, it is He who heals me» (Q. 26:80). The healing, which is good, he ascribed to the Lord; and the sickness, which is evil, he ascribed to himself. Such are the ādāb of the prophets with the Presence.

«If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise» — this verse (āya) pleased the Prophet ﷺ, so that he passed a whole night praying with it, adding nothing to it: «If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 5:118). «Allah said: This» — the Day of Resurrection — «is the Day on which the truthful will profit» — in the world, like ʿĪsā — «by their truthfulness: for them are gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them» — through their obedience to Him — «and they are pleased with Him» — with His reward — «that is the great attainment» (Q. 5:119). And the liars in the world are not profited by their truthfulness on that Day, like the unbelievers when they believe at the sight of the punishment. «To Allah belongs the dominion of»

«the heavens and the earth» — the treasuries of rain and of vegetation and of provision and others — «and what is in them» — He used mā by way of giving precedence to the non-rational — «and He is powerful over everything» (Q. 5:120), and of that is the rewarding of the truthful and the punishing of the liar. Reason excludes
His own essence [from “everything”], so He is not “powerful over” it.
Sūrat al-Anʿām

Meccan, except «And they did not esteem Allah» (Q. 6:91) — the three verses — and except «Say: Come» (Q. 6:151) — the three verses; and it is one hundred and sixty-five or one hundred and sixty-six verses.

«By Allah's Name: The Entirely Merciful, The Especially Merciful» The Qurʾan is of two parts: Meccan suras and Medinan suras. The Meccan suras are marked out by being more concise and more eloquent, because those addressed are Quraysh, and they are the Arabs of pure and eloquent speech: they understand of Arabic what others do not understand. In the Medinan suras there is the long expansion and the amplification, because those addressed are the Jews, and they are not like Quraysh in understanding and in acuity; so the Medinan suras needed an expansion of the speech greater than the Meccan suras. For this reason you find eloquence and rhetorical excellence and composition and inimitability in the Qurʾan, the Meccan of it and the Medinan alike; but concision is greater in the Meccan suras than in the Medinan suras, for this cause. And the Qurʾan is inimitable: its eloquence, its rhetorical excellence, the beauty of its composition, its announcing of the unseen, its freedom from contradiction, and its being ever new with the passing of the days. There is nothing that points more plainly to the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ than the Qurʾan. The Prophet ﷺ was unlettered; he grew up among an unlettered people, in a barren waste of the earth. He never saw a scholar, nor ever sat with a scholar; and he himself neither read writing nor wrote, and he never sat with a scribe nor with a reader. Then he brought this Book, a single sura of which defeats us — we study it night and day and it slips away from us — and he neither writes nor reads, yet he brought us this Book; and what came down in Mecca and what came down in Medina is all upon one pattern of eloquence and rhetorical excellence and brilliance and composition. For this He, Blessed and Exalted, addressed us: «Do they then not reflect upon the Qurʾan? And had it been from any other than Allah»

«they would have found in it much discrepancy» (Q. 4:82). The author among us, when he writes on history or on anything else, and it stays with him a year and he then goes back over it, is bound himself to replace something and change it, for the turning of the age — all the more so if another man criticizes him. You find that the books of history written in a past age do not suit this age of ours. And this Qurʾan: fourteen centuries have now passed, and the Qurʾan is new with every century; no event comes about that contradicts the Qurʾan, ever. Every nation and every state makes a constitution, and when years have passed the age outstrips that constitution and it needs changing — even Senegal: they have now taken to changing their constitution these four years past. And the Qurʾan is the constitution of all, in every age and in every place; no event comes about that contradicts the Qurʾan, ever, or belies the Qurʾan. And he who brought it was unlettered, born in a land of mountains; he never saw a sea, nor ever a city. This comes from none but Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

[When] they accused the Prophet ﷺ of having learned this Book from someone else, they said: ⟨Perhaps it was from his journey to Syria.⟩ Yes: the Prophet, when he reached twelve years, Abū Ṭālib took him out to Syria; and when they drew near to Syria the monks said to him: ⟨Take this boy back. Let the Jews not see him, for they are envious and will kill him.⟩ So Abū Ṭālib took him back. In that span of time, is it possible that he learned this Qurʾan from the rabbis of the Jews in Syria? They accused him with another piece of silliness: there was a smith in Mecca called Jabr, a Christian smith who had read the former scriptures and who believed in the Prophet ﷺ. Whenever the harm done by Quraysh to the Prophet ﷺ grew severe, he would bid him be patient and would encourage him, and say to him: ⟨The prophets before you — thus was it done with them.⟩ — supporting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Whenever the harm done to him grew severe, he ﷺ would go and sit with him, for the comfort he found in his speech. So they said: Now we know whence Muḥammad learned this Qurʾan — from this smith. And the smith does not speak Arabic;

the two of them cannot do without an interpreter. «It is only a human being who teaches him. The tongue of him to whom they incline is foreign, and this is a clear Arabic tongue» (Q. 16:103). They did not ponder the Qurʾan: «Do they not then ponder the Qurʾan?» (Q. 4:82)
This sura is Meccan — Sūrat al-Anʿām. It came down at one time. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

Glory be to Allah the Great, glory be to Allah the Great! ⟨This sura — seventy thousand angels escorted it, and they had a resounding chant of glorification.⟩ So when the Prophet ﷺ recited it, he ordered that it be written down, the whole of it, in a single night. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Whoever recites this sura, Allah appoints over him forty thousand angels who write for him the like of their worship until the Day of Resurrection; and an angel comes down from the seventh heaven with an iron mace with him, and when Satan means to whisper to him he strikes him, so that there are seventy veils between him and the devils. And on the Day of Resurrection, when he is raised from his grave, the Lord says: O man, walk in My shade on a day when there is no shade but My shade, and enter My Garden, and drink of al-Kawthar, for you are truly My servant and I am your Lord.⟩ And three verses from the beginning of this sura — whoever recites them every

day, Allah preserves him from the devils, and writes for him the number of the angels that came down with the sura, seventy thousand, their acts of worship until the Day of Resurrection; and nothing keeps him from entering the Garden but death. «The Praise is for Allah» (Q. 6:1). He began this sura with this word (kalima), and every sura Allah has begun with this word — the bliss of this world and of the hereafter must be brought to completion in it. It is at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, at the beginning of al-Anʿām, at the beginning of al-Kahf, at the beginning of Sabaʾ, and at the beginning of Fāṭir. And praise is

the description [of a thing] with what is beautiful; it is firmly established, and the laudation belongs to Allah — to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Praise, the whole of it, is for Allah and not for another. Yes: if a man honours you, you thank him and praise him; and if a king honours you, you thank him and praise him. ⟨He has not thanked Allah who has not thanked people.⟩ How, then, is praise His alone? Praise, the whole of it, is His. Praise, when it is for Allah, is His; and when it is for other than Allah, it is Allah's — for it is either His description or His act. The servant's praise of his Lord, and the Lord's praise of His servant, and the servant's praise of a servant, and the Lord's praise of Himself: all of this is for Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «Excellent is the Protector and excellent is the Helper» (Q. 8:40) — the praiser is Allah and the praised is Allah. «Excellent a servant» (Q. 38:44) — Ayyūb: the praiser is Allah and the praised is His servant, so the whole of it is for Allah. The servant says al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh: the praiser is the servant and the praised is Allah — this is for Allah. And when a servant praises a servant, the whole of it is for Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

He mentioned the name of Allah, which is the greatest of the names. «Who created the heavens and the earth» — He singled the two of them out for mention because they are the greatest of created things for those who behold — «and made the darknesses and the light» — every darkness and light, or the darknesses

of unbelief (kufr) and the light of faith (īmān). Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth — you see them both — and created the darknesses and created the light. He put the darknesses in the plural and the light in the singular, because the causes of darkness are many. «Then those who disbelieve» — with this proof standing — «ascribe equals to their Lord» (Q. 6:1) — yaʿdilūn — they set up others as equal with their Lord in worship. «He it is who created you from clay» — by creating your father Ādam from it — «then decreed a term» — for you; you die when it comes to its end — «and a term appointed» — fixed — «with Him» — for your resurrection — «then you» — O unbelievers — «doubt» (Q. 6:2) — you doubt the resurrection, after your knowing that He originated your creation; and whoever has power over the origination has more power over the restoring. «And He is Allah» — the worshipped One, who deserves worship — «in the heavens and in the earth. He knows your secret and your open speech» — what you keep secret and what you make open — «and He knows what you earn» (Q. 6:3) — what you do of good and of evil. «And there comes not to them» — the people of Mecca — «any sign of the signs of their Lord» — of the Qurʾan — «but that they turn away from it» (Q. 6:4). «So they have denied the truth» — the Qurʾan — «when it came to them; but there will come to them the tidings» — the consequences — «of what they used to mock» (Q. 6:5). «Have they not seen» — on their journeys to Syria — «how many» — many — «a generation We destroyed before them» — a community of the communities that have passed — «We established them» — We gave them a place — «in the earth» — in strength and in amplitude — «as We have not established» — what We did not give — «for you; and We sent the sky» — the rain — «upon them pouring down» — one following another — «and We made the rivers run beneath them» — beneath their dwellings — «then We destroyed them for their sins» — for their denying the prophets — «and We brought into being after them another generation» (Q. 6:6). «And had We sent down to you a book» — written — «on paper» — parchment, as they proposed — «and they touched it with their hands» — more conclusive than their having beheld it, since it more thoroughly excludes doubt — «those who disbelieve would say: this is nothing but manifest sorcery» (Q. 6:7) — out of captiousness and obstinacy. «And they said: why has there not been sent down to him» — to Muḥammad — «an angel» — to confirm him. Why did no angel come from heaven? He said: «And had We sent down an angel»

as they proposed, and then they did not believe, «the matter would have been decided» — by their destruction — «then they would not be granted respite» (Q. 6:8). Had the angel come, they would have been destroyed. «And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man» — this is a great secret. This angel that they asked for, had it come it would have become a man whom they look upon. It must needs come in the form of a man, so that they should be able to see it, when they do not know whether the man

is an angel or not? Because, had an angel come, it would have been a man. «and We would have confounded for them what they confound» — confusion must needs arise (Q. 6:9). «And messengers before you were indeed mocked» — the children of Ādam: among them are angels. Man was created with a capacity in him to be a devil (shayṭān), and a capacity in him to be a beast, and a capacity in him to be a predator, and a capacity in him to be an angel. If he strives against his soul and purifies it and returns it to its origin, he becomes of the kind of the angels. So then, had an angel come, it would have come as a man. «And messengers before you were indeed mocked, so there encompassed those of them who scoffed that at which they used to mock» (Q. 6:10) — and so likewise it will encompass whoever mocks you. «Say: travel in the earth, then look how was the end of the deniers» — of the messengers — by their destruction (Q. 6:11). «Say: to whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth? Say: to Allah» — there is no answer

other than it. «He has prescribed» — decreed — «upon Himself mercy» — as a bounty from Him; and in it is a gentleness in calling them to faith (īmān) — «He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection» — to requite you — «there is no doubt in it. Those who have lost their own souls — they do not believe» (Q. 6:12). «And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day» — everything; so He is its Lord and its Creator and its Owner. He said at the beginning of the sura: «created the heavens and the earth» (Q. 6:1) — this is place; place is the heavens and the earth. «And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day» — this is time. He has encompassed time and what exists in time, and place and what exists in place; all of this belongs to Him, Blessed and Exalted. «And He is the Hearing, the Knowing» (Q. 6:13). «Say: shall I take as a protector other than Allah» — whom I worship — «the Originator of the heavens and the earth» — He who brought them into being — «and He feeds» — He provides — «and is not fed» — He is not provided for — «Say: I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit» — to Allah. The commentator said: of this community. «And» — it was said to me — «do not be of the polytheists» — with Him (Q. 6:14). «Say: I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day» — that is the Day of Resurrection (Q. 6:15). «Whoever is averted from it on that day, He has had mercy on him» — Allah has willed good for him — «and that is the manifest triumph» (Q. 6:16). «And if Allah touches you with harm» — an affliction, such as sickness and poverty — «there is none to remove it but He; and if He touches you with good» — such as health and wealth — «then He is powerful over everything» (Q. 6:17). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨O boy, I shall teach you words: fear Allah⟩

⟨and He will preserve you; fear Allah and you will find Him before you. And when you ask, ask of Allah; and when you seek help, seek help of Allah. And know that if the community were to gather to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has written for you; and if the community were to gather to harm you, they would not harm you except with something Allah has already written against you. And know that what has struck you was not to miss you, and what has missed you was not to strike you. And know that victory is with patience, and that relief is with distress, and that with hardship there is ease.⟩ [This is] the tafsīr (Qurʾanic commentary) of this verse: «And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it but He; and if He touches you with good, then He is powerful over everything» (Q. 6:17). «And He is the Subduer» — the Omnipotent, whom nothing can thwart — exalted
«above His servants, and He is the Wise» — in His creation — «the Aware» — of their inmost selves (Q. 6:18). «Say: what thing is greatest in testimony»

It came down when they said to the Prophet ﷺ: bring us one who will testify for you to prophethood, for the People of the Book have denied you. «Say» — to them — «what thing is greatest in testimony? Say: Allah» — if they do not say it, there is no answer other than it; He is — «a witness between me»
«and between you» — to my truthfulness — «and this Qurʾan has been revealed to me that I may warn you» — O people of Mecca — «thereby» — by the Qurʾan —

«and whoever it reaches» — and whoever the Qurʾan reaches. So for this reason, everyone whom the Qurʾan reaches — it is as though the Prophet ﷺ had warned him face to face, of the jinn and of men. And it admits another interpretation (taʾwīl): «that I may warn you thereby, and whoever has come of age» — that is, every adult. «Do you indeed testify that along with Allah there are other gods? Say: I do not testify» — I do not testify to that — «Say: He is only one God, and I am quit of what you associate» — with Him, of the idols (Q. 6:19). «Say: He is only one God, and I am quit of what you associate». «Those to whom We gave the Book know him» — Muḥammad ﷺ, by his description in their books — «just as»

«they know their own sons. Those who have lost their own souls — they do not believe» — in him (Q. 6:20). «And who» — no one — «is more wrongdoing than he who invents a lie against Allah» — by ascribing shirk (associating partners with Allah) to Him — «or denies His signs» — the Qurʾan — «Indeed» — the matter being

«the wrongdoers do not prosper» (Q. 6:21). «And» — recall — «the day We shall gather them all, then We shall say to those who associated partners» — in rebuke — «where are your associates whom you used to claim» — that they were associates to Allah (Q. 6:22). «Then their plea will not be» — their excuse — «but that they say» — nothing but their saying — «By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists» (Q. 6:23). He, Exalted, said: «Look» — O Muḥammad — «how they lied against themselves» — by denying shirk of themselves — «and that which they used to invent has gone astray from them» (Q. 6:24). «And among them is he who listens to you» — when you recite — «and We have placed over their hearts veils» — coverings — «lest they understand it» — that they should not understand it — «and in their ears a heaviness» — deafness — so they do not hear it with the hearing of acceptance. «And though they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say: this is nothing» — this Qurʾan is nothing — «but legends» — falsehoods — «of the ancients» — like laughable tales and marvels (Q. 6:25); it is the plural of usṭūra, with ḍamma. «And they forbid from it» — it came down concerning Abū Ṭālib: when they wished to believe in the Prophet he prevented them, and if they wished to kill him he prevented them too. «And they forbid»
the people «from it» — from following the Prophet ﷺ — «and they keep away» — they withdraw far off — «from it» — and so [they do] not

believe in it. «And they destroy none but themselves» — because its harm falls upon them — «and they do not perceive» — that (Q. 6:26). «And if you could see» — O Muḥammad — «when they are made to stand» — presented — «at the Fire, and they say: Would that we were returned» — to the world — «and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers» (Q. 6:27). Had you seen this, you would have seen a tremendous thing. «Nay» — for retraction — «there has become apparent» — appeared — «to them what they used to hide before» — they were concealing it, by their saying: «By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists» (Q. 6:23). «And if they were returned» — to the world, hypothetically — «they would return to what they had been forbidden» — of shirk (associating partners with Allah) — «and indeed they are liars» (Q. 6:28). This verse (āya) is the most telling proof that the sign does not induce faith. The greatest sign is the Day of Resurrection; and when they saw the Day of Resurrection and what is in it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said that they, had they been returned to the world, would have returned to unbelief (kufr) as well. «And they said» — the deniers of the resurrection — «There is nothing but our life in this world, and we shall not be raised» (Q. 6:29). «And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord» — you would have seen a tremendous thing — «He says» — to them, upon the tongue of the angels — «Is this not» — the resurrection — «the truth? They say: Yes, by our Lord!» — it is indeed truth — «He says: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve» — in the world (Q. 6:30). «Lost indeed are those who denied the meeting with Allah» — the resurrection — «until, when the Hour comes upon them» — the Resurrection — «suddenly» — all at once — «they say: Oh, our grief» — that is, our regret — «for what we neglected» — we fell short — «therein, while they bear their burdens upon their backs» — in that their burdens come to them at the resurrection as the most hideous of things in form and the foulest in smell, and so they ride upon them

«Lo, evil is» — wretched is — «what they bear» — they carry (Q. 6:31). «And the life of this world» — that is, the occupation with it — «is nothing but play and diversion, and the abode of the hereafter» — the Garden — «is better for those who guard against» — shirk — «will you not then understand?» (Q. 6:32). «We know indeed that it» — the matter is — «grieves you, what they say» — to you, of denial — «indeed they do not call you a liar» — in secret, since they know that you are truthful — «but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah» (Q. 6:33) — they deny with their tongues while they hold it true in their hearts.

«And messengers before you were indeed called liars» — in this there is a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ — «so they bore with patience what they were called liars for and the harm they suffered, until Our help came to them» — by the destruction of their people; so be patient until the help comes to you, by the destruction of your people — «and there is no changing the words of Allah» — His promises — «and there has already come to you some of the tidings of the messengers» — that by which your heart is set at rest (Q. 6:34).

«And if it has been hard» — grievous — «upon you, their turning away» — from Islam, out of your eagerness for them — «then if you are able to seek a tunnel» — a burrow — «in the earth, or a ladder» — a means of ascent — «into the heaven, and bring them a sign» — of what they proposed
then do so. The meaning is that you are not able to do that, so be patient until Allah judges. «And had Allah willed» — their guidance
«He would have gathered them upon guidance» — but He did not will it — «so do not be» — O Muḥammad — «of the ignorant» — of that (Q. 6:35).
O Allah, bless our master Muḥammad.
«Only they respond» — to your call to faith — «who hear» — a hearing of understanding and of heeding — «and the dead»
the unbelievers; He likened them to the dead in their not hearing — «Allah will raise them» — in the hereafter — «then to Him they are returned»

they are brought back, and He requites them for their deeds (Q. 6:36). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, informed His Prophet that he is not able to make the unbelievers hear, because they are dead, and that Allah is able to make them hear, because He has power to raise them. Yastajīb (to respond) and yujīb (to answer) do not have one and the same meaning. Yastajīb means a responding that is acceptance, unlike yujīb; yujīb is with acceptance or with refusal, whereas yastajīb is for nothing but acceptance. Those who hear with a hearing of understanding and of heeding respond to the call of the Prophet ﷺ and so believe in Allah; and the dead never respond. But Allah will raise them, if He wills, in this world or in the hereafter, and then they return to Him. He made the unbelievers dead. The unbeliever is as though he were a corpse in his grave, buried in his corporeality. A body without a spirit — that is a corpse; and the body, when it is emptied of the spirit, becomes putrid, and in it are the blood and the pus, and what is best for it is that it be buried beneath the earth. And the body in which there is a spirit without an intellect — its owner is a madman; when it is emptied of the intellect he behaves as madmen behave. And if there is in it a spirit and an intellect without recognition, the intellect is as though it were a thing gone to waste, of no profit. And if there is recognition in it, this is the living one who profits by his life. So recognition is the spirit of the spirit of the spirit. Recognition is the spirit of the intellect, and the intellect is the spirit of the spirit, and the spirit is the spirit of the body

When they were emptied of all these spirits they became dead, and so Allah named them «dead»; and if He wills He gives them life by the spirit and the intellect and recognition, and then they respond to the summons of the Messenger ﷺ, and then they return to Him and He requites them for their deeds. This raising — if He wills, it is in this world, by the sending of these spirits; and if not, then in the hereafter they must be raised and return to Allah, and He requites them for their deeds. «And they said» — the unbelievers of Mecca — «why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?» — why has a sign not been sent down upon the Messenger from his Lord, such as the she-camel that Ṣāliḥ brought forth from the mountain, or a staff like the staff of Mūsā, or a table like the table of ʿĪsā? They asked for signs from the Prophet ﷺ — not as some of the ignorant say. For some of the ignorant among the misguided sects say that the Prophet ﷺ showed no miracle: had they seen a miracle they would not have said «why has a sign not been sent down upon him from his Lord?», and he answers with His saying «Say: Allah is able to send down a sign». The meaning of this, with them, is that the Prophet ﷺ did not display so much as a single miracle. This is not what is meant. Rather, as for the Messenger ﷺ, were we to suppose that we had witnessed no miracle at all, the Qurʾan would suffice him as a miracle, because Allah issued the challenge with a sura, and that is three verses; so the Qurʾan comprises more than two thousand miracles. But they proposed signs when the signs were there, out of obstinacy and contrariness. They said: let him bring us a she-camel like the she-camel of Ṣāliḥ, and a staff like the staff of Mūsā, and a table like the table of ʿĪsā. «Say» — to them — «Allah is able to send down a sign» — of what they proposed; Allah has power over that — «but most of them do not know» — that its sending down is an affliction for them, since their destruction becomes necessary if they deny it (Q. 6:37). He withheld from them the sending down of the signs, because if they saw these signs after they had proposed them and then did not believe, they would perish on the spot. And it has already passed that the community of Muḥammad is not destroyed; for this reason Allah withheld from them the signs they proposed. To propose signs when the signs are there is obstinacy and contrariness.

And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. He said: «And had your Lord willed, whoever is in the earth would have believed, all of them together» (Q. 10:99); «and had Allah willed He would have gathered them upon guidance» (Q. 6:35). So He willed in pre-eternity that a portion of His servants He would guide to the Garden — may Allah make us and you among them — and a portion He would not guide, so that they are made wretched and go to

the Fire. So the signs guide no one. The greatest of the signs is the Day of Resurrection, and it was already mentioned yesterday: «And were they returned, they would go back to what they were forbidden» (Q. 6:28). Were they to witness the Day of Resurrection and the wonders that are in it, and then return to this world, they would return as unbelievers. So the signs avail nothing. Allah guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. It passed in pre-eternity that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, took a handful of mankind and said: ⟨These to the Garden, and I do not care.⟩ And He took a handful and said: ⟨These to the Fire, and I do not care.⟩ So whoever was in the luminous handful, Allah guides him; and whoever was in the other, no one is able to guide him. «And there is no creature» — that walks — «in the earth, nor a bird that flies» — in

the air — «with its two wings, but they are communities like you» — in the ordering of their creation and their provision and their states (Q. 6:38). The animals in this world are either a thing that crawls upon the earth — and everything that crawls upon the earth is of the kind of the crawling creatures — or a bird that flies in the air, and that is of the kind of the birds. He mentioned the earth because the creation in heaven does not enter into this; for they are all of them believers, obedient: «they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded» (Q. 66:6). As for the crawling creatures of the earth and everything that flies in the air, all of them are communities like you. He did not mention the animals of the sea, because they enter into the crawling creatures: for if their going in the sea is a crawling, they are among the crawling creatures, and if swimming in the sea is a flying, they are among the birds. So when He mentioned the crawling creatures and the birds, He mentioned everything that Allah created upon the face of the earth, on the land and in the sea: all of them are communities like you. Allah has ordered their creation and their provision and all their states.
in

we write it — «then to their Lord they are gathered» (Q. 6:38) — and judgement is given between them, and retaliation is taken for the hornless beast from the horned; then He says to them: Be dust! In this verse Allah informed [us] that He has mentioned everything that is needed in the Book, which is al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ on one interpretation, or it is the Qurʾan. «We have not neglected in the Book» — which is the Qurʾan — «anything» — if it is the Qurʾan. They found this problematic: that some of the medical sciences and the sciences of arithmetic and the like the Qurʾan did not bring in detail, even if it brought the whole of it in summary. They said: the meaning of «We have not neglected in the Book anything» is: of the matter of religion. Everything that is needed of the matter of religion the Qurʾan has made clear, and that is such as the recognition of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in His essence and His attributes and His names. Of this the Qurʾan has comprised what no book has comprised. And the rulings, such as the clarifying of the lawful and the forbidden, likewise. And the kinds of worship, such as the prayer and zakat and fasting and the hajj, likewise: of this kind it has made clear what no book the like of it has made clear. And since religion is what counts, when it made religion clear it made everything clear. Or: «We have not neglected in the Book anything» — of the matter of this world and the hereafter: there is no thing but that it is in the Qurʾan, and this is the truth. Al-Shāfiʿī sat one day and said: ⟨Ask me. You will not ask me about a question but that I answer it from the Qurʾan.⟩ A questioner said to him: ⟨May one in ritual consecration (iḥrām) kill a hornet?⟩ He said: ⟨Yes; there is nothing upon him.⟩ He said to him: ⟨Where is this in the Qurʾan?⟩ He said to him: Allah, Exalted, said: «And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it» (Q. 59:7); and the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Hold fast to my sunna and the sunna of the rightly-guided caliphs after me⟩; and ʿUmar said: ⟨There is nothing upon one in ritual consecration for killing a hornet.⟩ He derived this ruling from the Qurʾan: from the saying of ʿUmar, and the saying of ʿUmar from the sunna of the Messenger,

and the sunna of the Messenger — the Qurʾan said: «And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it» (Q. 59:7). Rather, in the Qurʾan there is everything. Ibn ʿAbbās says: ⟨Even the hobble of my camel, if it strays from me, I am able to find it in the Qurʾan.⟩

A story: I was at Rabat last year, and we were in a place in which the Christians and the Muslims and the boys had gathered. A Christian, who knew Arabic, said: the Qurʾan says «We have not neglected anything in the Book» (Q. 6:38) — and I have seen a thing that is not small, a very great thing, and the Qurʾan has not mentioned it. A boy said to him: and what is it? He said to him: the Qurʾan mentioned Mecca as a town, and mentioned Egypt as a town, and I know a town much greater than the two of them, and the Qurʾan has not named it. The boy said to him: and what is this town? He said to him: Paris. He said to him: the Qurʾan has mentioned it — «I shall show you the abode of the transgressors» (Q. 7:145).
I was waiting, so that if the lad proved unable I would answer him; but the lad answered him with an answer better than every answer. He said to him:

Allah said: «I shall show you the abode of the transgressors» (Q. 7:145) — this is Paris. «We have not neglected anything in the Book, then unto their Lord they shall be gathered» (Q. 6:38) — and judgement is passed between them, and retaliation is exacted for the hornless beast from the horned. Al-Shāfiʿī was asked about these ships of the sea and of the land: whence has the Qurʾan mentioned them? Al-Shāfiʿī said: «And horses and mules and donkeys, for you to ride them, and as adornment; and He creates what you do not know» (Q. 16:8). These ships, all of them, have entered into «and He creates what you do not know». I was asked about this question in Medina. I mentioned to them al-Shāfiʿī's answer, and I said to them: and I see a second answer
«And there is not a thing but that with Us are its storehouses, and We do not send it down save in a known measure» (Q. 15:21). «And those who denied Our signs» — the Qurʾan
«are deaf» — as to hearing them with a listening of acceptance — «and dumb» — as to uttering the truth — «in darknesses» — unbelief — «whom»
«Allah wills» — to lead him astray — «He leads astray; and whom He wills» — to guide him — «He sets upon a straight path» (Q. 6:39) — the religion of Islam.

Abū Jahl was sitting one day, and Iblīs came to him and said to him: take this idol of yours and set it down with the Messenger ﷺ; perhaps you will hear from him what will gladden you. Abū Jahl's idol was inlaid with jewels and rubies. So Abū Jahl carried his idol and set it before the Messenger ﷺ, and said to it: this is Muḥammad — he reviles us and curses our gods and taunts us continually, and you are our god, and you avail nothing at all in this.

So Satan entered into the idol and spoke, and he fell to cursing the Prophet ﷺ and reviling him. The Prophet ﷺ grew angry and entered his house, and one who had come knocked at the door upon him and said to him: command me with whatever you wish and I shall do it.
