The Messenger ﷺ said to him: who are you? He said: I am a jinnī. I was in the seventh earth, and when the idol spoke before you what it spoke, Jibrīl summoned me to come; and I have killed the Satan who spoke in the hollow of the idol, and I have come to you that you may command me with whatever you wish. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: what is your strength? He said to him: I am able to bring together the two mountains of Abū Qubays and Quʿayqiʿān and to lay waste what is between them. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: Allah suffices me. He said to him: go back to the idol. And the Prophet ﷺ went back, and the idol fell to saying: there is no god but Allah, Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah; I am an idol, I avail nothing, I neither profit nor harm; I am an idol; there is no god but Allah, Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah; believe in Muḥammad — the truth is with him. Abū Jahl grew angry and broke it, and said: Muḥammad has bewitched everything, until he has bewitched the idols. This one — had Allah willed his guidance He would have guided him, but He did not will it. «Say: have you considered» — tell me — «if Allah's punishment should come upon you» — in this world — «or the Hour should come upon you» — the Resurrection, which comprises it, suddenly — «would you call upon any other than Allah?» — no — «if you are truthful» (Q. 6:40) — in that
the idols profit you, so call upon them. «Rather Him» — not another — «you call upon» — in hardships — «and He removes that for which you call»
[that is, you call] that He should remove from you the harm and the like of it, if He wills to remove it — «and you forget» — you leave — «what»

«you associate» (Q. 6:41) — with Him, of the idols; so you do not call upon them. «And We did indeed send to nations before you» — messengers, and they denied them — «so We seized them with misery» — the severity of poverty — «and hardship» — sickness — «that perhaps they might humble themselves» (Q. 6:42) — abase themselves, and so believe. «Then why, when Our might came to them, did they not humble themselves» — would that they had humbled themselves when Our might came to them; that is, they did not do that, though what called for it was present — «but their hearts hardened» — so they did not soften to faith — «and Satan made alluring to them what they used to do» (Q. 6:43) — of acts of disobedience, and so they persisted in them. «Then when they forgot» — left — «what they had been reminded of» — they were admonished and made to fear

«with it» — of the hardship and the adversity — and they did not take heed — «We opened upon them the gates of everything» — of the blessings, as an istidrāj (being drawn on to ruin by degrees) for them — «until, when they rejoiced in what they were given» — the rejoicing of insolence — «We seized them» — We destroyed them with the punishment — «suddenly» — all at once — «and at once they were in despair» (Q. 6:44) — despairing of every good — «So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off»
their last, in that they were extirpated. «And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds» (Q. 6:45) — for the victory of the messengers and the destruction of the unbelievers.

Praise is obligatory in every condition. Praise for safety, and praise for the destruction of the enemies, and praise in the time of blessing. The praise of Nūḥ — and Nūḥ's praise was for safety: «It was said: O Nūḥ, descend in peace from Us, and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you» (Q. 11:48) — and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. As for the community of Muḥammad, they are the praisers (al-ḥammādūn); they were named in the former Books as being the praisers. Their messenger is Muḥammad and Aḥmad, and the head of their Book is: praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. When they eat they say: praise be to Allah; and when they drink they say: praise be to Allah; and when they clothe themselves they say: praise be to Allah; and when they wake they say: praise be to Allah; and when they die it is said: praise be to Allah; and when they are raised up they say: praise be to Allah; and when they enter the Garden they say: praise be to Allah; and their banner on the Day of Resurrection is the Banner of Praise. The praising community that was praised in the Torah and the Gospel is this community — and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. When Allah bestows a blessing upon His servant he says: praise be to Allah, praise be to Allah by whose blessing good works are completed; and when an affliction befalls he says: praise be to Allah in every condition. Praise at
affliction, because every affliction, however far it may reach in severity, it lay within the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that it be more severe
than what it is; so then praise is obligatory upon him in every condition. «Say: Have you considered» — tell me — «if Allah took»
«your hearing» — if Allah made you deaf — «and your sight» — made you blind — «and set a seal upon your hearts» — stamped them, so you do not

know anything — «who is a god other than Allah who could bring it to you?» — with what He took from you, by your claim. If Allah were to take these three — among the most exalted of Allah's blessings upon His servant is the hearing faculty. The Qurʾan always puts hearing before sight, because the attachment of faith to hearing is stronger than its attachment to sight. A man hears the verses (āyāt) of Allah even if he is blind, and he believes in Allah; and were it not for hearing, guidance would never have been possible for him. So hearing is more profitable than sight. This hearing faculty, and this seeing faculty, and this perceiving faculty — the heart — are three blessings; were Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to take them, the servant would never find anyone to bring them to him. «Look how We vary» — We make clear — «the signs» — those indicating Our oneness — «yet still they turn away» (Q. 6:46). They used to worship gods, but they could not claim that their gods would bring them this. «Say: Have you considered — if the punishment of Allah came upon you suddenly or openly» — by night or by day — «would any be destroyed but the wrongdoing people?» (Q. 6:47) — the unbelievers; that is, none are destroyed but they. «And We send not the messengers except as bearers of good tidings» — to whoever believes, of the Garden — «and as warners» — to whoever disbelieves, of the Fire — «so whoever believes» — in them — «and makes amends» — his deed — «no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve» (Q. 6:48) — in the hereafter. «And those who denied Our signs — the punishment shall touch them for that they used to transgress»

they go out from obedience. «Say» — to them — «I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah» — from which He provides — «nor do I know the unseen» — I do not say to you that I know the unseen, what is hidden from me and has not been revealed to me — «nor do I say to you that I am an angel» — of the angels — «I follow only what is revealed to me. Say: are the blind» — the unbeliever — «and the seeing equal? Will you not then reflect?» (Q. 6:50). He mentioned in this verse that the Prophet ﷺ does not claim that the treasuries of Allah are with him, nor does he claim knowledge of the unseen, nor does he claim that he is an angel; for a claim is ugly even when it is sound. «I do not say to you» — this does not indicate that he does not have them. «I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah» — and even if there were

with me the treasuries of Allah. «And nor do I know the unseen» — I do not say to you that I know the unseen, even though I do know the unseen. «And nor do I say to you that I am an angel» — even though I am more exalted in rank than the angels. «I follow only what is revealed to me».

The Messenger ﷺ follows only what is revealed to him, and this agrees with His word «Nor does he speak from caprice; it is only a revelation revealed» (Q. 53:3–4). By this some of the ulama held fast who said that the Messenger has no independent judgement (ijtihād): «I follow only what is revealed to me», «Nor does he speak from caprice; it is only a revelation revealed». The correct view is that he has

[leave] to exercise independent judgement; and when he exercises it, it falls within the revelation, on the evidence of the verse (āya) «We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you» (Q. 4:105). When he exercises independent judgement and arrives at an opinion, it is what Allah has commanded in the Qurʾan, and so his independent judgement is revelation. He who said that he exercises independent judgement spoke truly, and so did he who said that he does not: he follows only what is revealed to him. Among them are those who annulled analogy (qiyās), [holding] that the ruling of the law is the Qurʾan and the sunna only. But analogy — another verse brought it: «If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger» (Q. 4:59), «And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those of them who draw out the meaning would have known it» (Q. 4:83). «Will you not then reflect?» — upon that — «And warn with it» — with the Qurʾan — «those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord; they have, apart from Him» — other than Him — «no protector» — to help them — «nor intercessor» — to intercede for them — «that they may be godfearing» (Q. 6:51) — by their desisting from what they are in. «And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His face» (Q. 6:52). The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the chiefs of the polytheists came to the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ and found him ﷺ sitting, and with him were ʿAmmār and Bilāl and Ṣuhayb and Salmān al-Fārisī, the poor among the Muslims, the People of the Bench (ahl al-ṣuffa). They addressed the Prophet ﷺ: are you not ashamed to sit with these? Drive them away, if you would like us to believe in you and to sit with you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨I am not one to drive away the believers.⟩ They said: then appoint for us two assemblies — an assembly in which you sit with the poor, and when we come to you, you set us apart by ourselves in an assembly until we go, and then you may sit with them if you wish. ʿUmar said to the Messenger ﷺ that he should accept this from them, so that they might see whether they would be guided or not. So the Prophet

ﷺ wished to accept that from them, out of desire for their guidance. So they said: order someone to write you a document to that effect. He called ʿAlī and was about to write, and then this verse came down: «And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, desiring His face» (Q. 6:52) — not anything of the trappings of this world; and they are the poor. The polytheists had impugned them and had asked that he drive them away so that they might sit with him. ʿUmar said: ⟨I offer you my excuse, O Messenger of Allah⟩ — because he had counselled accepting this opinion. And here is Nūḥ, upon him be blessing and peace: when they ordered him to drive away the weak among the believers he said «I am not one to drive away the believers» (Q. 26:114); and the Messenger ﷺ at first answered ⟨I am not one to drive away the believers⟩; but from the breadth of his mercy, when they asked of him that he appoint two assemblies for them, out of desire for their acceptance of Islam he inclined to this opinion, until Allah forbade him

Blessed and Exalted. This does not show that the Prophet ﷺ went against [the command], or that he is not preserved from error, on account of His words at the end of the verse, «so that you drive them away and become one of the wrongdoers»; for he did not resolve upon driving them away, but only upon dealing gently with those men, and he says: ⟨I was sent as one who deals gently, so deal gently.⟩ When the verse came down, the Prophet ﷺ drove the polytheists away and held firm to sitting with the poor. «And no part of their reckoning is upon you» — they had said: these men are not truthful in their submission, they are only poor men who live by being near you — «in anything, nor any part of your reckoning upon them in anything, so that you drive them away and become one of the wrongdoers» (Q. 6:52) — if you were to do that. People fall into classes. The sons of this world want this world only: «Whoever desires the tillage of the hereafter, We increase for him in his tillage; and whoever desires the tillage of this world, We give him of it, and he has no share in the hereafter» (Q. 42:20). And the sons of the hereafter want the hereafter: «And whoever desires the hereafter»

«and strives for it with the striving due to it, being a believer — those, their striving shall be thanked» (Q. 17:19). And the people of Allah want the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening desiring His face» (Q. 6:52) — they want neither this world nor the next. The elect: al-Ḥaqq drew them away from the hand of this world and set them apart for the hereafter. As for the elect of the elect, He stripped them of this world and of the hereafter and set them apart for the beholding of His noble face. They are the people of Allah. «And thus We tried» — We tested — «some of them by others» (Q. 6:53). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made a difference between the portions: He made a noble man and a lowly man, a rich man and a poor man — a trial by which He tried some of them through others. The noble man and the rich man, if they give thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and humble themselves before the poor man and the lowly man, that is thankfulness on their part; and if they grow proud and withhold the due of the destitute, they have spurned the favour of Allah.

And the lowly man and the poor man, if they envy, they have not given thanks; and if they are steadfast, they have given thanks for the favour of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. People are either a rich man who gives thanks or a poor man who is patient. They differed over which of the two is better: it is said, the rich man who gives thanks; and it is said, the poor man who is patient

⟨Shall I not teach you something by which you may overtake those who have gone before you, and outstrip those who come after you, and none shall be more excellent than you save one who does the like of what you have done?⟩ They said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah. He said: ⟨You shall glorify Allah, and magnify Allah, and praise Allah after every prayer thirty-three times.⟩ Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ⟨The poor among the Muhājirūn came back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Our brethren, the people of wealth, have heard of what we did and have done the like of it.⟩ So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills».

Had what they are upon been guidance, they would not have got to it before us. He, Exalted, said: «Is not Allah best aware of the thankful» (Q. 6:53) — to Him, and so guides them? Yes indeed. «And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you. [Your Lord] has prescribed»

«your Lord upon Himself mercy» — Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave this community good tidings that He has prescribed mercy for Himself. He says: ⟨My mercy has outstripped My wrath.⟩ «that whoever among you does an evil in ignorance» — commits an act of disobedience in ignorance. Ignorance is of two kinds: the ignorance of straying, like the ignorance of the unbelievers; and an ignorance belonging to the deeply ignorant, an ignorance of […]. Ignorance is of two kinds: ignorance of Allah and of the rights of His divinity, which requires its possessor's everlasting abiding (khulūd) in the Fire; and the ignorance which is the very recognition of Allah, which is ignorance of the innermost reality of the Essence inasmuch as it is what it is, and which requires its possessor's everlasting abiding in the Garden. «And man bore it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, deeply ignorant» (Q. 33:72). So then, whoever among you does an evil in ignorance
«then repents» — turns back — «after it» — after his deed — «and makes amends» — his deed — «then He» — that is, Allah — «is forgiving» — to him —

«merciful» (Q. 6:54) — to him. «And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you». This peace (salām) is the greeting between Muslims among themselves in this world, and with it the angel greets them when they enter the Garden: «Peace be upon you; you have been good» (Q. 39:73) — until the Lord Himself greets them with peace: «Peace — a word from a merciful Lord» (Q. 36:58). «Your Lord has prescribed mercy for Himself»
The first thing Allah, Blessed and Exalted, brought into being was the Pen. He said to it: Write. The Pen spoke: What shall I write? He said: Write

what has been and what shall be until the Day of Resurrection. So it began to write. Write: Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace — I shall send him to his people, and whoever believes in him I shall admit to the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in him I shall admit to the Fire. Write: Ibrāhīm, likewise. Write: Mūsā, likewise. ʿĪsā, likewise. Write: Muḥammad. So it wrote Muḥammad, and said: He is sent to his community, and whoever believes in him I shall admit to the Garden, and whoever disbelieves in him — al-Jalīl spoke: Observe proper comportment, O Pen; this is the ḥabīb (the beloved). The Pen shuddered until it split, and so it does not write unless it is split. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write — the community of Muḥammad is a community that sins, and I am a forgiving Lord, and My mercy has outstripped My wrath in their regard. al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh. This is the meaning of «He has prescribed mercy for Himself». «And thus We detail» — We make clear — «the signs» — the Qurʾan — so that the truth may appear and be acted upon — «and so that there may become clear» — may appear — «the way of the sinners» (Q. 6:55) — the path of the sinners, so that it may be shunned. «Say: I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon» — whom you worship — «apart from Allah. Say: I do not follow your desires» — in worshipping them — «I should then have gone astray»

if I were to follow them. «And I would not be among the rightly guided» (Q. 6:56). «Say: I am upon a clear proof» — a clear statement — «from my Lord, and you have denied it» — and you have indeed denied «it», that is, my Lord, in that you have associated partners with Him — «I do not have that which you seek to hasten» — they asked him to send the punishment down at once, and he answered: «I do not have that which you seek to hasten» — of punishment — «The judgement is not» — in that and in other than it — «but Allah's; He recounts» — He says — «the truth, and He is the best of deciders» (Q. 6:57) — those who judge. «Say» — to them — «if I had that which you seek to hasten, the matter between me and you would have been decided» — by my hastening it for you, so that I might be at rest; but it is with Allah — «and Allah knows best the wrongdoers» (Q. 6:58) — when He will punish them. «And with Him» — Exalted — «are the keys of the unseen» — His treasuries, or the roads that lead to knowledge of it — «none knows them but He» (Q. 6:59). None knows the unseen but Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and they are the five that are in His words, Exalted: «Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour» (Q. 31:34), to the end of the verse. He has mentioned in this verse that the keys of the unseen — none knows them

but He. And the keys of the unseen — the hadith has explained them by the verse of Luqmān: «Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour; and He sends down the rain; and He knows what is in the wombs; and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; and no soul knows in what land it will die» (Q. 31:34)

We have seen many of the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) and of the righteous telling of these things before they occur, and the truth of what they have told of comes about. This does not conflict with «None knows them but He» (Q. 6:59), because this is of the knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. The unseen which none knows save Allah is a single unseen: the coming of the Hour, and that alone. As for «and He sends down the rain, and knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die» (Q. 31:34) — the knowledge of all this is with some of the servants of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, by Allah's knowledge. Shaykh Aḥmad al-Tijānī, may Allah be pleased with him, says that were he to die
and be buried, and then taken out and asked about these five, he would surely tell of them. «And He knows what is in the land» — the wastes — «and the sea»

— the villages which are upon the rivers — «And no leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear book» (Q. 6:59) — it is al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ — «And He it is who takes your souls by night» — He seizes

your spirits in sleep — «and He knows what you have committed» — earned — «by day, then He raises you up therein» — in the day, by returning your spirits — «that a stated term be fulfilled» — it is the term of life — «then to Him is your return, then He will inform you of what you used to do» (Q. 6:60) — and so He will requite you — «And He is the subduer» — exalted high — «over His servants» — overmastering them — «and He sends over you keepers» — angels who number your deeds — «until, when death comes to one of you» — its causes — «Our messengers take him»

«By those that tear out violently, and those that draw out gently» (Q. 79:1–2). The Angel of Death has deputies over the seizing of spirits, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is in reality the one who seizes the spirits. For this He said: «Say: the angel of death, who has been given charge of you, will take you» (Q. 32:11); and He said here: «Our messengers take him» (Q. 6:61); and another time: «Allah takes the souls at the time of their death» (Q. 39:42). The one who seizes in reality is Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and He deputes the angel. The angel, when he is commanded to seize the spirit of a servant, seizes it; and a servant whose spirit he has not been commanded to seize — he is powerless to approach him. And the servant: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has appointed over him angels who guard him, one on his right and one on his left, and one before him and one behind him, and the two keepers who write down everything he sends forward of deed, good or evil. And of the prevailing of His mercy: Raqīb is on the man's right and ʿAtīd on his left, and Raqīb is the commander over ʿAtīd. When he does a good deed, he commands that it be written ten times, or more, up to seven hundred. And when he does an evil deed, ʿAtīd does not write it unless Raqīb commands him; he says: give him respite for six hours — if he repents, or asks forgiveness, or does a good deed, do not write it. And when six hours have passed and the servant has not asked forgiveness and has not done a good deed, he says to him: write it a single time. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Woe to him whose ones have overcome his tens.⟩ The good deed is tenfold its like, and the evil deed is written only as a single evil deed, and if he asks forgiveness within the space of six hours it is not written. So whoever is heedless until these ones become more than these tens, he is heedless, and Allah is the granter of success. «Then they are returned to Allah their Master» — their owner — «the Real» — the established, the just — that He may requite them — «Lo, His is the judgement» — the decree carried into effect upon them — «and He is the swiftest of reckoners» (Q. 6:62) — He reckons all creatures in the measure of half a day of the days of this world, for a hadith to that effect. Our master ʿAlī was asked: how does

Allah reckon creation in half a day? He said: how does He feed them in half a day?! He feeds them all, and that does not render Him powerless. «Say» — to them, O Muḥammad — «who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea» — their terrors in your journeys — when
«you call upon Him in humility» — openly — «and in secret» — secretly — you say: «and if You deliver us» — if Allah delivers us — «from»
«these» — the darknesses and the hardships — «we shall surely be among the thankful» (Q. 6:63) — the believers — «Say» — to them — «Allah delivers you»

«from it and from every distress» — a grief other than it — «then you associate others» (Q. 6:64) — with Him — «Say: He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you» — Allah is able to rain down upon the community stones from the heaven, or a cry — «or from beneath your feet» — such as being swallowed up by the earth — «or to confound you» — to mix you — «in sects» — parties differing in their
whims — «and make some of you taste the violence of others» (Q. 6:65) — by fighting. When this verse was revealed, «a punishment from above you»

the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩ And He said: «or from beneath your feet» — he said: ⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩ And when He said: «or to confound you in sects and make some of you taste the violence of others» (Q. 6:65) — he said: ⟨O Allah, I seek refuge in Your face.⟩ He said: ⟨The pen has dried; the decree has passed upon that.⟩ So the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨This is lighter and easier.⟩ And for this the community does not cease to be divided, some of them making others taste violence.

It began with the killing of ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, and so on and so forth. The sovereignty of divinity, when it attaches to a thing, is turned back neither by a sent prophet nor by an angel brought near. The most exalted of the prophets in station with Allah are three: Muḥammad and Ibrāhīm

and Mūsā. Ibrāhīm — when Allah willed the destruction of the people of Lūṭ and he wanted to intercede for them: «O Ibrāhīm, turn away from this. The command of your Lord has already come» (Q. 11:76), and al-Khalīl was of no avail in it. And Mūsā — when the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya knew neither a god nor a messenger and were fighting the Children of Isrāʾīl, and the Children of Isrāʾīl in that age were Muslims while these were unbelievers in their Jāhiliyya, yet among them was one who is a forefather of al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ: Mūsā wanted to invoke [Allah] against these Arabs, and he was rebuked from the Presence, that he should not invoke against them. The sovereignty of divinity. And the Prophet ﷺ, when He said «or to confound you in sects and make some of you taste the violence of others» (Q. 6:65), said: ⟨O Allah, I take refuge in Your face.⟩ He said: the Pen has run dry. «Look how We diversify the signs» — those that point to Our power — «that perhaps they may understand» (Q. 6:65). «And it has been denied» — the Qurʾan — «by your people, while it is the truth» — the veracity — «Say: I am not a guardian over you» — not a compeller, that I should requite you; I am only a warner, and your affair rests with Allah (Q. 6:66) — and this was before the command to fight. «For every tiding» — report — «there is a fixed time» — a time at which it falls out — «and you shall come to know» — a threat to them (Q. 6:67). «And when you see those who plunge into Our signs» — the Qurʾan, in mockery — «then turn away from them» — do not sit with them — «until they plunge into some other talk. And if Satan should make you forget» — move you to forgetfulness, so that you sat with them — «then do not sit, after the reminder,» — when you remember, do not sit with them — «with the wrongdoing people» (Q. 6:68). And the Muslims said: if we rise every time they plunge [into such talk], we shall not be able to sit in the mosque or to make the circumambulation. So there came down: «And nothing is upon those who fear» — Allah
«of their account» — that is, of those who plunge [into such talk] — «anything» — if they sit with them — «but» — upon them is — «a reminder» — a reminding

for them, and an admonition. «that perhaps they may guard themselves» — against plunging [into such talk] (Q. 6:69). «And leave those who have taken their religion» — which they were charged with — «as play and diversion» — by their mocking it — «and whom the life of this world has deluded» — so do not concern yourself with them; this was before the command to fight.
«And remind» — admonish — «by it» — the Qurʾan — «lest a soul be given up to destruction» — lest a soul be delivered over to perdition — «by what»

«it has earned» — done — «there is not for it, besides Allah,» — other than Him — «any protector» — helper — «nor intercessor» — to ward off the punishment from it — «and though it offer every ransom» — ransom itself with every ransom — «it will not be taken from it» — what it ransoms itself with — «those are they who are given up to destruction for what they earned. For them is a drink of scalding water» — water reaching the utmost of heat — «and a painful punishment» — hurtful — «because they used to disbelieve» — on account of their unbelief (Q. 6:70). «Say: shall we call upon» — shall we worship — «besides Allah what neither profits us» — by worshipping it — «nor harms us» — by leaving it; and that is the idols — «and be turned back upon our heels» — return as idolaters — «after Allah has guided us» — to Islam — «like one whom the devils have lured away» — led astray — «in the earth, bewildered» — perplexed, not knowing where he goes — «he has companions» — comrades — «calling him to guidance» — to guide him to the road, and they say to him — «Come to us» — but he does not answer them, and so he perishes — «Say: the guidance of Allah» — which is Islam — «is the guidance» — and what is other than it is error — «and we have been commanded to submit» — that we should submit — «to the Lord of the worlds» (Q. 6:71), «and that» — and [we were commanded] that — «you establish the prayer and fear Him» — fear Him, Exalted — «and He it is to whom you will be gathered» — you will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning (Q. 6:72). «And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth» — truly — «and» — recall — «the day He says» — to a thing — «Be, and it is»

and that thing is the Day of Resurrection: He says to creation, Arise, and they arise. «His word is the truth» — the veracity that comes to pass inescapably — «and to Him belongs the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown» — the horn; the second blast, from Isrāfīl. No one other than He has dominion on it: «To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Overpowering» (Q. 40:16). «Knower of the unseen and the witnessed» — what is absent and what is beheld — «and He is the Wise» — in His creation — «the Aware» — of the inward of things as of their outward (Q. 6:73).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: what is the Trumpet? He said: ⟨A horn which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and in it is a hole for every spirit of all living creatures.⟩ And when Allah wills the passing away of this creation, He commands the angel to blow the Trumpet, and he blows the Trumpet: «and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth is terrified» (Q. 27:87). Then he blows a second time: «and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls dead, save whom Allah wills» (Q. 39:68). Then he blows

a third time, and Allah raises up everyone who had died. The blasts are in reality two blasts: the blast of the swoon, at which he dies along with [all] created beings, and the blast of the raising. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ⟨Between the two blasts is forty.⟩ It was said to Abū Hurayra: forty years? He said: I decline. It was said: forty days? He said: I decline. That is, he refused to interpret it, because the Prophet ﷺ did not interpret it. ⟨Between the two blasts is forty⟩ — whether it is forty years or forty months or forty days, Allah knows best. When the Trumpet has been blown so that the created beings have died, they remain forty, asleep; the sky rains upon them the water of semen and they grow — their bodies grow in that span — until, when it is blown a second time, they are raised. For this they say: «Woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting-place?» (Q. 36:52). «save whom»

«Allah wills» (Q. 39:68) — its interpretation will come: that they are the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise (ḥūr al-ʿīn) or the four angels, Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl. They are the last to die, as will come. So when it is blown a second time — and this is after the raising of the Prophet ﷺ — he said: ⟨I am the first over whom the earth will split open, and I shall sit up straight, and I shall speak to Abū Bakr and he will rise, and I shall speak to ʿUmar and he will rise.⟩ When Allah wills to raise all created beings, He sends Jibrīl and the servant of the Garden and al-Burāq and servants with them: bring me my beloved, this is the Day of Resurrection. Then they lose the way. They say: Jibrīl, you are the one who knows the road to Medina, because you went to and fro to it often. So Jibrīl leads them to the burial-place of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they awaken the Prophet ﷺ and clothe him, and he mounts his beast and goes to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. After that the Trumpet is blown, and all created beings are raised, and they are gathered to the place of gathering. The hadith of the raising and the intercession will come at its full length.

«And» — recall — «when Ibrāhīm said to his father Āzar» — Āzar is his byname; his name is Tārakh — «do you take idols as gods?» — worshipping them? An interrogative of rebuke — «I see you» — O Āzar — «and your people» — by your taking them — «in error» — away from the truth — «manifest» (Q. 6:74). Ibrāhīm speaks to his father Āzar, forbidding him the worship of idols; and this runs against the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saying that Allah moved him through the loins of believing men and believing women, from Ādam, from Shīth, to Ibrāhīm, to Ismāʿīl, to ʿAdnān, to ʿAbd Allāh and Āmina — that he was not born of fornication but of sound marriage. Ibn ʿAbbās said: ⟨I wrote out five hundred forefathers for the Prophet ﷺ; I did not see unbelief among them.⟩ How this is reconciled

This, along with his being of the progeny of Ibrāhīm — and Ibrāhīm says this to his father? Answers have been given to it. The ulama answered that this preservation from sin (ʿiṣma) belongs to the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ so long as the light of the Prophet ﷺ is in their loins; but once the light has passed on, that one is merely like any one of creation. And Āzar, at the time he was worshipping the idols — the light had already passed to Ibrāhīm. This answer is not satisfactory. The Qurʾan supports that the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ were all of them Muslims, by His saying «and your turning about among those who prostrate» (Q. 26:219) — that is, in the loins of those who pray.

The best that has been answered on this is what our shaykh, Shaykh al-Tijānī, may Allah be pleased with him, answered. He said: ⟨Āzar is a paternal uncle of Ibrāhīm, and the eloquence of the Qurʾan yields this. A man's father who begot him — he does not say of him 'my father so-and-so'; he says only 'my father'. And when it is said 'my father so-and-so', its meaning is only the paternal uncle. So had Āzar been Ibrāhīm's father, He would have been content with His saying:⟩ «And when Ibrāhīm said to his father» ⟨alone. But as for His saying⟩ «to his father Āzar» (Q. 6:74) ⟨— this is another father, other than the father.⟩ If this is sound the difficulty is removed; and if not, then what is ruled out of the forefathers of the Prophet ﷺ is fornication, and that the light of the Prophet ﷺ should come into being without a contract of marriage — and the marriages of the unbelievers are valid in the shariʿa of Islam. In sum: this Āzar, Ibrāhīm addressed him: «Do you take idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in manifest error» (Q. 6:74). He said this speech when he was sixteen months old. «And thus We show Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those who are certain» (Q. 6:75). Namrūd saw a fire that came out of some of the houses and burned

his kingdom. So he asked the astrologers about this vision. They said to him: A child will be born among these people who will be the cause of your kingship's passing away. He said: Then my kingship shall never pass away. So he separated the men from the women and forbade that a man should come to his wife, and a man came to see his wife only in the days of menstruation — they used to keep away from women in the time of menstruation, and everyone whose wife menstruated was given leave to go in to her. It happened that a need arose for Namrūd, and he sent the father of Ibrāhīm, who was his minister, to go to the town and attend to his need for him, and [warned] him against going near his wife. He said to him: I am more jealous for your kingship than you are; I shall never go near her. And when he entered the village and had attended to the king's need, he went in to the woman, and Allah made her fair in his eyes, and he had no command of himself until he lay with her. So she conceived Ibrāhīm. And when she had conceived Ibrāhīm, Allah concealed the pregnancy: whenever the pregnancy grew, the belly grew small, and the marks of pregnancy did not appear upon her, until the time of her delivery came. She fled to the open country and entered a cave — it had been a spring that had sunk away — and she bore him in it, and there he was, Ibrāhīm. She covered the mouth of the cave with a stone and returned to the village, and she became pure on the instant, as a protection from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. She took to going back and forth to him, and would find him sucking from his fingers: water from this finger, milk from this one, honey from this one, oil from this one, dates from this one. And he grew in a month as a child grows in a year, and after sixteen months he became a strong young man.

His mother came to him. When Ibrāhīm looked at her he said: O my mother, who is my Lord? She said: I am your Lord. He said: And who is your Lord? She said: My Lord is your father. He said: And who is my father's Lord? She said: Namrūd. He said: And who is Namrūd's Lord? She fled and came to her husband and told him the news. She said to him: The child he used to fear is this son of mine; come and hear from him. So he came to Ibrāhīm. He said to him: O my father, who is my Lord? He said: Your Lord is your mother. He said: And who is the Lord of

my mother? He said: I am. He said: And who is your Lord? He said: Namrūd. And who is Namrūd's Lord? He slapped him. So he went away from him and took to looking, wishing to know his Lord. «And when the night grew dark over him» — they brought him out of the cave; this was the first time he had seen the sky — «he saw a star» — it is al-Zuhara. He said to his people, and they were astrologers — «he said: this is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not those that set» (Q. 6:76) — that I should take them as lords, because change is not possible for the Lord — «But when he saw the moon rising» — coming up — «he said: this is my Lord. But when it set, he said: if my Lord does not guide me I shall surely be of the people who go astray» (Q. 6:77). «But when he saw the sun rising» — and on the morrow he saw the sun, the first time he had seen it — «he said: this is my Lord, this is greater» — greater than the star and the moon — «But when it set» — it went down — «he said: O my people, I am quit of what you associate» (Q. 6:78) — with Allah, of the idols and the originated bodies — «Indeed I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of those who associate» (Q. 6:79). «And thus» — as We showed him the straying of his father — «We show Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those who are certain» (Q. 6:75). Ibrāhīm is the pole of tawḥīd (the divine oneness); Allah, Blessed and Exalted, never mentioned him but that He declared him quit of shirk (associating partners with Allah),

because he said: this is my Lord. Had he meant that the star was his lord, this would have been shirk; but he did not mean the star. At that time he was immersed in tawḥīd, seeing nothing but Allah, Blessed and Exalted. When he saw the star he said: this is my Lord. I say: had he meant the star he would have said 'that', because it is far from him; and of the sun he would have said 'that one', because it is feminine. But on every occasion he said «this is my Lord» — his Lord is nearer to him than these things; he means the real Lord. For this reason, whenever Allah mentions him He says «and he was not of those who associate» (Q. 3:67). He was annihilated in tawḥīd, and the annihilation of the prophets does not last long. So too the Muḥammadiyyūn: when Allah wills for a servant that others should benefit by him, He annihilates him and restores him on the instant; he returns to his senses and others benefit from him. Ibrāhīm said «this is my Lord» when he saw the star, «this is my Lord» when he saw the moon, «this is my Lord» when he saw the sun. He came to himself: «O my people, I am quit of what you associate»
«Indeed I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining to the truth, and I am not of those who associate» (Q. 6:79). «And thus We show»

«Ibrāhīm the dominion of the heavens and the earth» (Q. 6:75). He mentioned that Allah showed Ibrāhīm the malakūt (the unseen dominion) of the heavens and the earth. The malakūt is what is hidden and the mulk (dominion) is what is manifest: the unseen and the witnessed, this world and the hereafter, the sensory (ḥissī) and the notional (maʿnawī), the outward and the inward, creation and command, the mulk and the malakūt — all these are synonymous names. The mulk is what is manifest and the malakūt is what is hidden. Allah showed Ibrāhīm the malakūt of the heavens and the earth, and He showed Muḥammad «of Our signs»: «Glory be to Him who carried His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs» (Q. 17:1). He brought in the partitive min in the case of Muḥammad ﷺ; and for Ibrāhīm, «the dominion of the heavens and the earth», and there is no partitive min in it. This does not require that Ibrāhīm is of loftier station than Muḥammad. Rather, Ibrāhīm was shown the malakūt of the heavens and the earth, and Muḥammad was shown some of the signs — but the signs of what? They are not the signs of the heavens nor the signs of the earth: «of Our signs» — the signs of Allah. That Presence has no end, and for this reason the servant can do nothing but look upon some of it while some remains. «And his people disputed with him» — they argued with him about his religion and threatened him with the idols, that they would strike him with evil — «he said: do you dispute with me» — do you argue with me — «concerning» — the oneness of — «Allah, when He has guided me» — the Exalted [has guided me] to it — «and I do not fear what you associate with Him» — of the idols, that they should strike me with evil, since they have no power over anything; your idols are nothing — «except» — but — «that my Lord should will a thing» — if my Lord wills something hateful, it strikes me — «My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge» — His knowledge encompasses all things — «Will you not then remember?» (Q. 6:80) — this, and so believe — «And how should I fear what you have associated» — with Allah, when they neither harm nor profit — «and you do not fear» — you, of Allah — «that you have associated with Allah» — you threaten me with fear of your gods, and you do not fear Allah — «that for which He has not sent down» — for the worship of it — «upon you any authority» — a proof and a demonstration; and He is the one powerful over everything — «so which of the two parties is more deserving of security» — is it we or you? — «if you know» (Q. 6:81) — who is the more deserving of it, we or you? We are. The Exalted said: «Those who believe and have not confounded» — mixed —
«their faith with wrongdoing» — with shirk — «those are they who have security» — from the punishment — «and they are rightly guided» (Q. 6:82). He mentioned security

in this verse, and He mentioned it in another verse: «Do they feel secure from the scheme of Allah? None feels secure from the scheme of Allah except the losing people» (Q. 7:99). And here He said: «Those who believed and did not confound their faith with wrongdoing — those have security, and they are rightly guided» (Q. 6:82). So security is of two kinds: the security of the people of the divine overpowering and of loss. They were addressed with His saying: «Do they feel secure from the scheme of Allah? None feels secure from the scheme of Allah except the losing people» (Q. 7:99). They opposed the command of Allah and did not draw near to Him, and with that they felt secure. This security is a scheme; its possessor ends in loss. And the security of the people of the divine gentleness, who arrived at the presence of Lordship and believed with a complete faith in which there is no shirk (associating partners with Allah). The wrongdoing is al-shirk; another verse has explained it: «O my son, do not associate [partners] with Allah; indeed associating partners is a great wrong» (Q. 31:13). Those felt secure — Allah informed [us] that they felt secure — and their security did not prevent them from guidance. «Those who believed and did not confound their faith with wrongdoing — those have security, and they are rightly guided» (Q. 6:82). You find among the prophets and the awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) one who is made certain of his felicity and his triumph and his entering the Garden, and this is not security from the scheme of Allah, because that security does not belong to that rank. «And that was Our argument» — with which Ibrāhīm argued for the oneness of Allah, from the setting of the stars and what comes after it — «which We gave to Ibrāhīm»

We directed him to it as an argument «against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will» — with the annexed reading — «Indeed your Lord is Wise» — in what He fashions — «Knowing» (Q. 6:83). «And We bestowed upon him Isḥāq» — his son — «and Yaʿqūb» — his son's son — «and each» — of the two — «We guided. And Nūḥ We guided before» — that is, before Ibrāhīm — «and of his descendants Dāwūd and Sulaymān» — his son — «and Ayyūb and Yūsuf»

the son of Yaʿqūb «and Mūsā and Hārūn. And thus» — as We recompensed them — «do We recompense the doers of good» (Q. 6:84). «And Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā» — the son of Maryam. This yields that 'descendants' takes in the children of the daughter — «and Ilyās» — the son of the brother of Hārūn, the brother of Mūsā — «all of them among the righteous» (Q. 6:85). «And Ismāʿīl» — the son of Ibrāhīm — «and al-Yasaʿ and Yūnus and Lūṭ»
the son of Hārān, the brother of Ibrāhīm. «And each» — of them — «We favoured above the worlds» (Q. 6:86) — through prophethood — «and of their fathers»

«and their descendants and their brethren; and We chose them» — We selected them — «and guided them to a straight path» (Q. 6:87). «That» — the religion to which they were guided — «is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He will of His servants. And had they associated [others with Him]» — hypothetically — «there would have been nullified»
«from them what they used to do» (Q. 6:88). «Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book» — in the sense of the books — «and the judgement» — wisdom —

«and prophethood. So if there disbelieve in them» — in these three — «these» — the people of Mecca — «then We have entrusted it» — We have set them in readiness for it — «to a people who are not disbelievers in it» (Q. 6:89) — they are the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār — «Those are the ones whom Allah has guided» — Allah guided them —

«so by their guidance» — their way, of tawḥīd (the divine oneness) and steadfast patience (ṣabr) — «follow [their] example» — follow them all, O Muḥammad, may Allah bless you and give you peace. This verse is the most telling proof of the superiority of the Messenger ﷺ over all the prophets and the messengers. Allah mentioned them, each one, and every one of them has a praiseworthy quality in which he surpassed the rest. All of them took on all the praiseworthy traits, but each of them was singled out by a quality for which he became known. Dāwūd and Sulaymān were of the people of thankfulness: they joined kingship and prophethood together and gave thanks to Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so the two of them are of the people of thankfulness. And Ayyūb was of the people of steadfast patience. And Mūsā of the people of the dazzling miracles. And Zakariyyāʾ and Yaḥyā and ʿĪsā of the people of renunciation of this world. And Yūsuf combined steadfast patience and thankfulness: in his beginning patient, and in his end thankful. Since they took on these traits, each one of them, Muḥammad ﷺ was commanded to follow the example of them all. This is a proof that he is more excellent than all of them, because there was gathered in him what was dispersed among them. «Say: I ask of you for it» — for the Qurʾan — «no reward. It is only a reminder» — an admonition — «to the worlds» (Q. 6:90) — mankind and the jinn. «And they did not measure Allah with His true measure» (Q. 6:91). It came down concerning Mālik b. al-Ṣayf. The Jews sent him to the Messenger ﷺ at Mecca, and when he came to dispute with

the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: ⟨I adjure you by Allah: have you read in the Torah that Allah hates the fat rabbi?⟩ And he himself was a fat rabbi. So he grew angry and said: «Allah has not sent down anything upon any human being» (Q. 6:91). When he returned, the Jews blamed him, and he said: Abū al-Qāsim angered me, so I said this. They said: so when you are angry you disbelieve in Allah and disbelieve in what Allah has sent down? And he was their rabbi, so they deposed him and put Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf in his place, [one worse than him]. «And they did not measure» — that is, the Jews — «Allah with His true measure» — they did not magnify Him as He deserves to be magnified, or they did not know Him as He deserves to be known — «when they said» — to the Prophet ﷺ — «Allah has not sent down anything upon any human being. Say: who sent down the Book which Mūsā brought, a light and a guidance for the people, which you make into sheets» — they write it in separated quires — «disclosing it» — that is, you disclose of it what you like to disclose — «and concealing much» — of what is in it, such as the description of Muḥammad ﷺ — «and you were taught» — O you Jews, in the Qurʾan — «what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers»

what was made obscure to you in the Torah — all of it the Qurʾan has explained for you. «Say: Allah» — He sent it down; if they do not say it, there is no answer other than it — «then leave them in their vain discourse» — their falsehood — «playing» (Q. 6:91). «And this» — the Qurʾan — «is a Book We have sent down, blessed»

(Q. 6:92) — abundant in blessing, abundant in good for whoever believes in it, and an evil for whoever disbelieves in it. And of its blessing is the endurance of this world, and the sprouting of the earth, and the raining of the sky, so long as the Qurʾan remains. When the Qurʾan is lifted away, a gentle wind comes, and by it every believer dies, and the unbelievers remain. So the endurance of good upon the earth lasts as long as the Qurʾan endures upon it. A blessed Book — it is this Qurʾan — blessed: it calls the common people to their Lord, and it guides the elect to their Lord, and it brings the elect of the elect to their Lord. And this

Qurʾan — its blessing is manifest. Whoever recites it attains a great reward, and whoever listens to its recitation likewise, and whoever holds the written codex (muṣḥaf) in his hand finds a recompense by that. A Muslim man died and was buried, and among the company who attended his burial there was a righteous man. When the people had departed, the righteous man heard a violent blow, and a black dog came out, and the righteous man addressed it. He said to it: Who are you? It said: I am his evil deed. And the blow that I heard — did it fall upon you, or upon him? It said: Rather upon me. I wanted to be joined to him, and a sura of the Qurʾan that he used to recite struck me and drove me out of the grave. He ﷺ says: ⟨Whoever recites the Qurʾan has for every letter ten good deeds. I do not say to you that alif lām mīm is a letter; rather I say that alif is a letter, and lām is a letter, and mīm is a letter.⟩ When the Qurʾan became famous for its blessing, and Musaylima the Liar laid claim to a Qurʾan with which to rival the Qurʾan, he sent envoys to the Prophet ﷺ: ⟨From Musaylima the Messenger of Allah to Muḥammad the Messenger of Allah: the earth between us is two halves⟩ — until he said: ⟨Indeed We have given you the jewels⟩ — he wishes to rival Sūrat al-Kawthar — ⟨so pray to your Lord and proclaim aloud.⟩ This, for all the feebleness of its wording, is a lie. The jewels do not equal al-Kawthar, and we know of no jewels that Allah gave to the Messenger ﷺ in this world; and what comparison is there between jewels and the prayer? When the two came to the Messenger ﷺ, he said to them: ⟨Were it not that envoys are not to be killed, I would have killed you two.⟩ So they went to Musaylima and said to him:

⟨Muḥammad the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — whenever a child of his companions falls ill they bring him to him, and he recites the Qurʾan over him, and Allah heals him.⟩ He said: ⟨Yes — bring me the sick.⟩ So when they brought him a sick man and he recited over him, he would die on the spot; and when they brought him one with inflamed eyes, he would go blind on the spot. Muḥammad ﷺ would recite and spit into salt water, and it would become sweet; and whenever Musaylima spat into a well, that well sank away. Musaylima is not blessed.

«confirming that which is before it» (Q. 6:92). It was sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ over a period of twenty-three years, and whenever a verse came down they would write it on stones, and on the leaves of trees, and on bones; and the Qurʾan was not collected. Nine of his companions memorised the Qurʾan in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. When the Messenger ﷺ died, and Abū Bakr fought at al-Yamāma, and a company of the bearers of the Qurʾan were martyred, ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb came to Abū Bakr and said to him: ⟨I hold that this Qurʾan should be collected and written down, because martyrdom has become frequent among the bearers of the Qurʾan; and if this happens a second time, those who bear the Qurʾan will die out, and I fear that the Qurʾan will be taken away from us.⟩

Abū Bakr said to him: ⟨If the mountains of Tihāma were loaded upon me, they would be light upon me; but a thing the Messenger ﷺ did not do — there is no way to accept it.⟩ ʿUmar kept swearing to him until Allah gave light to the heart of the caliph, and he saw what ʿUmar saw. So the two of them summoned Zayd b. Thābit, who had been the scribe of the Prophet ﷺ — and Jibrīl used to present the Qurʾan to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ every year, and in the year of his death he presented the Qurʾan to him twice, each time in the presence of Zayd b. Thābit. The two shaykhs summoned him and said to him: ⟨We order you to write the Qurʾan for us.⟩ He said to them: ⟨The mountains of Tihāma are lighter upon me than that I should do a thing the Messenger ﷺ did not do.⟩ And he refused. So the two shaykhs swore to him until Allah gave light to his heart, and he accepted from them. And they said: Zayd is the one who undertakes the writing, and he writes no verse unless two upright witnesses testify to it. And they set about writing: whenever a verse was written, he would attach it

in its place in its sura, by the affirmation of twelve thousand of the Companions — and ⟨my community will not agree upon an error⟩ — until Zayd said: ⟨There remains of the Qurʾan only two verses, at the end of al-Tawba.⟩ A man of the Companions called Khuzayma came with these two verses. They sought a second [witness] and did not find him. Then they remembered that the Prophet ﷺ had one day stood him before them and said to them: ⟨I have made the testimony of this man stand in the place of two testimonies.⟩ So they wrote the two verses: «There has come to you» (Q. 9:128) — to the end of the sura. So the codex was completed, unordered, and it was with Abū Bakr; and when he died it was with

ʿUmar; and when ʿUmar died it was with Ḥafṣa. When ʿUthmān took charge — and he was of the bearers of the Qurʾan — he took this that had been collected and ordered it according to the order of the Qurʾan, from the beginning of al-Baqara to the end of the Qurʾan, in this order that is in the written copies today. ʿUthmān is the one who collected it thus, by the consensus of the Companions, and he wrote seven codices:

a codex that was in his own hand — it is the Imam [the master copy]; a codex he sent to Mecca; a codex he sent to Kūfa; a codex he sent to Egypt; a codex he sent to Baghdad; a codex he sent to Syria; and a codex he sent to the Maghrib. The reading of the Maghrib codex is the one that has reached us. — Last year, or two years ago, on my going to Cairo, I saw a codex in the hand of ʿUthmān, present now in Cairo, and a codex in the hand of ʿAlī. I never knew that this was in the world at all. — «confirming that which is before it» — what was before it of the books — «and that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it; and those who believe in the hereafter believe in it, and they are mindful of their prayer» (Q. 6:92) — out of fear of its punishment. «And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah» — by claiming

prophethood, like Musaylima the Liar. «or says, It has been revealed to me, when nothing has been revealed to him» — it came down concerning Musaylima the Liar — «and who says, I shall send down the like of what Allah has sent down» (Q. 6:93) — and they are the mockers [who said]: «Had we willed, we could have said the like of this» (Q. 8:31). «And if you could see»
O Muḥammad — «when the wrongdoers are in the throes of death» — the agonies of death — «and the angels stretching out their hands»

toward them in striking and torment, saying to them in rebuke: «Give up your souls» — to Us, that We may seize them — «Today you are recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say against Allah other than the truth» — by the claim to prophethood and to inspiration, falsely — «and because you used to be arrogant toward His signs» (Q. 6:93) — you behaved haughtily. Had you seen this, you would have seen a dreadful thing. «And» — it is said to them when they are raised up — «you have indeed come to Us alone» — singly, apart from family and property and child — «as We created you the first time» — barefoot, naked, uncircumcised — «and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you» — We gave you — «behind your backs» — in this world, without your choosing — «And» — it is said to them in reproach — «We do not see with you your intercessors» — the idols — «whom you claimed»

«that they were, with respect to you,» — in deserving your worship — «partners» — with Allah — «The bond between you is severed» — your connection; your gathering is scattered — «and gone» — departed — «from you is what you used to claim» (Q. 6:94) — in this world. «You have indeed come to Us alone». The way of tawḥīd (the divine oneness) is the way of recognition: tajrīd (stripping bare) and tafrīd (singling out) and tawḥīd. tajrīd is a stripping away from all created things; tafrīd is that you single yourself out apart from every family and property and child; and tawḥīd is that Allah alone remains in the heart, with no partner to Him. The beginning is in the end and the end is in the beginning. Man was born stripped bare, having no rag to cover his nakedness (ʿawra), and he will return to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in just that way. And the end is in the beginning: if he strips himself now of everything and Allah remains, he has entered a Garden such that he does not long for the Garden that is awaited. «Indeed Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone» — He who splits the grain for the plant, and the date-stone for the palm — «He brings forth the living from the dead» — as man and bird from the sperm-drop and the egg — «and He brings forth the dead»

the sperm-drop and the egg — «from the living. That is» — the Splitter, the Bringer-forth — «Allah; so how are you turned away?» (Q. 6:95) — so how are you turned away from faith, when the proofs stand? — «the Cleaver of the daybreak» — who splits the column of dawn — «and He made the night for repose»
in which created beings find rest from weariness — «and the sun and the moon for reckoning» — they run by a reckoning, that is, they succeed one another —
«That» — what has been mentioned — «is the ordaining of the Mighty» — in His dominion — «the Knowing» (Q. 6:96) — of His creation — «And it is He who made for you the stars»
«that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea» — on journeys — «We have detailed the signs» — which point to

Our power — «for a people who know» (Q. 6:97). «And it is He who brought you into being» — created you — «from a single soul, and there is a lodging-place» — some of you, in the womb — «and a place of deposit» — some of you, in the loins — «We have detailed the signs for a people who understand» (Q. 6:98). «And it is He who sent down water from the sky, and We brought forth» — in it there is a shift of address (iltifāt) away from the third person — «by it» — by the water — «the growth of every thing, and We brought forth from it greenery» — something green — «from which We bring forth» — from the greenery — «grain heaped one upon another» — one part riding upon another, as the ears of wheat — «and from the palm, from its spathe» — the first thing that comes forth from it — «clusters» — date-stalks — «hanging low»

near one to another; and We brought forth — «and gardens» — orchards — «of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, resembling» — their leaves — «and not resembling» — their fruit — «Look» — O you who are addressed, with a looking of consideration — «at its fruit when it bears fruit» — the first of what appears, and how it is — «and its ripening» — its coming to maturity — «Indeed in that are signs» — pointing to

His power — «for a people who believe» (Q. 6:99). «And they made the jinn partners with Allah» — in that they obeyed them — «and He created them» — and He it was who created them — «and they invented» — they fabricated — «for Him sons and daughters without knowledge» — in that they said: ʿUzayr is the son of Allah, and the angels are the daughters of Allah — «Glory be to Him» — declaring Him free of that — «and exalted above what they describe» (Q. 6:100). «the Originator of the heavens and the earth» — their originator — «How should He have a son when He has had no consort» — a wife — «and He created every thing» — [every thing] whose nature it is to be created — «and He is knowing of all things» (Q. 6:101). «That is Allah your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things; so worship Him» — declare Him one — «and He is guardian over all things» (Q. 6:102) — a keeper. «The sights do not grasp Him» — they do not see Him. Grasping is other than seeing: a man sees

a thing and does not grasp it — «and He grasps the sights» — He sees them and grasps them. Just as we know Him and do not grasp Him, we see Him and do not grasp Him — «and He is the Subtle» — to His awliyāʾ (the friends of Allah) — «the Aware» (Q. 6:103) — of them. «There have come to you clear proofs» — arguments — «from your Lord; so whoever sees» — sees them and so believes — «it is for his own soul» — he sees, for the reward of his seeing is his — «and whoever is blind» — to them, and so goes astray — «it is against it» — the evil consequence of his being led astray — «and I am not a keeper over you» (Q. 6:104) — a watcher over your deeds. I am only a warner.
«And thus» — as We have made plain what has been mentioned — «do We vary» — We make plain — «the signs» — that they may take heed — «and so that they may say» — the unbelievers, in

the outcome of the matter — «You have studied» — that is, you have read the books of those who went before — «and so that We may make it clear to a people who know» (Q. 6:105). «Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord» — the Qurʾan — «there is no god but He; and turn away from the polytheists» (Q. 6:106). «And had Allah willed, they would not have associated partners; and We have not made you a keeper over them» — a watcher — «and you are not a guardian over them» — so that you should compel them to faith (Q. 6:107). «And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah» — it was revealed concerning a group who reviled the idols, whereupon the unbelievers reviled the Master, Mighty and Exalted. He, the Exalted, said: «And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah» — the idols — «and so they revile Allah out of enmity» — in transgression and wrongdoing — «without knowledge» — on this basis, every act of obedience that draws one on to disobedience is itself disobedience, because reviling the idols is an act of worship; but when it drew them on to reviling Allah they were forbidden it. «Thus have We made fair-seeming to every community their deed» — of good and of evil — «then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do» — and He will requite them (Q. 6:108). «And they swore» — the unbelievers of Mecca — «by Allah with their most earnest oaths that if a sign came to them» — of what they proposed — «they would surely believe in it. Say: signs are only with Allah. And what will make you perceive that, when it comes, they will not believe» — it had already gone forth in Allah's knowledge that they would not believe (Q. 6:109). «And We turn about»
«their hearts» — We turn their hearts away from the truth — «and their eyes» — away from beholding the truth, so they do not believe — «as they did not»
«believe in it the first time, and We leave them» — We abandon them — «in their insolence» — their straying — «wandering blindly» — they waver about in bewilderment (Q. 6:110).

«And even if We had sent down to them the angels» (Q. 6:111). We mentioned that the sura came down all at once at Mecca, and this conflicts with this verse (āya) having come down on account of the saying of the unbelievers, or with the unbelievers’ having proposed these signs and this sura having then come down, with these verses in it as an answer to them. As for a verse of this sura having an occasion of revelation of its own, after we have made clear that it came down all at once — that is among the things that are hard for the commentator. But in any case, the mockers of the Prophet ﷺ and of the Qurʾan — they were five, and they were of Quraysh: al-Aswad b. ʿAbd Yaghūth, and al-Aswad b. al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Ḥārith, and al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, and Abū Jahl b. Hishām
they gathered

to the Messenger ﷺ and said: Show us the angels. If you wish us to believe you, then show us the angels, that we may ask them. And once they said: Bring us Allah, that we may see Him and ask Him about your truthfulness. And once they said to him: Bring back to life for us Quṣayy b. Kilāb, our forefather, that we may ask him whether you are truthful or not. al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted, answered: «And even if We»
«had sent down to them the angels» — as they had proposed — «and the dead had spoken to them» — and the dead spoke to them, such as Quṣayy b.
Kilāb and others — «and We had gathered» — assembled — «against them everything» — and We added to that, until We gathered for them every

thing — «face to face» — in plain view, so that they beheld it — «they would not have believed» — had all this come to pass they would not have believed, because of what had gone before in Allah’s knowledge — «except» — but — «that Allah should will» — until Allah wills the faith of a servant, and so he becomes a believer; and whoever He does not will

his faith, he does not believe. «But most of them are ignorant» (Q. 6:111) — most people do not know that. Faith is by the will of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. For the sign, however great it be, does not bring [one] to faith except by the will of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

The greatest sign is the Day of Resurrection, and it has already been mentioned: «And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden; and indeed they are liars» (Q. 6:28). For it went before in pre-eternity that Allah sprinkled a sprinkling of light upon spirits, and those cannot but come to faith; and whoever missed that sprinkling, it cannot come about that he believe. And the signs profit none but the people of guidance and of divinely granted success. Every miracle of a prophet and every karāma (saintly miracle) of a walī (friend of Allah), whether it be of knowledge or other than that, is a training for the people of his time. So whoever is prepared is trained by the first indication and profits; and whoever has no preparedness in him says: had we seen a true guide we would have clung to his hem and attached ourselves to him, and we would have profited and we would have entered upon the path. And he whom Allah grants success, and whom the solicitude of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has met, finds the guide nearer to him than that he should seek him. For this He, Blessed and Exalted, told us that faith is by the will, not by the signs; for the signs are manifest to the eye, but none sees them except those granted success. «And thus We appointed for every prophet an enemy» — as We have made these men your enemies, We made for every prophet an enemy: Allah made Iblīs for Ādam, and made for Nūḥ his son Kanʿān, and for Ibrāhīm Namrūd, and for Mūsā Firʿawn (Pharaoh), and for ʿĪsā the Jews, and for Muḥammad Abū Jahl and his people; and likewise He appointed [one] for every veracious one (ṣiddīq), and so on — «devils of mankind» — the rebels among mankind — «and jinn» — and the rebels among the jinn — «inspiring» — whispering — «one another with embellished speech» — speciously decked out, drawn from falsehood — «in delusion. And if»

«your Lord had willed, they would not have done it» — the inspiring that was mentioned — «so leave them» — leave the unbelievers — «and what they fabricate» (Q. 6:112) — of unbelief and other than it, of what has been made alluring to them. And this was before the command to fight. Those enemies are a benefit to the servant of Allah whom He has chosen, because they disturb him and so he returns to his Creator and his Maker; for if he found in creation no one to harm him, he would incline to them by his nature and they would snatch away something of his heart. And al-Ḥaqq, Blessed and Exalted, loves to be alone in possession of the heart. So if your kind, and the sons of your kind, and the kinsfolk around you, agree with you in everything you love, and you see from them nothing but what you love, you must needs incline to them, and they take a great share of your heart if they do not take possession of it outright. And when harm disturbs you from every side, you return to your Creator and your Maker, and He chooses you for Himself; and this is better for you than this world and what is in it. «and that the hearts of those who do not believe in the hereafter may incline to it» — they incline to what the enemies of Allah deck out speciously — «and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit» — acquire — «what they are committing» (Q. 6:113) — of sins, so that they are punished for it. «Shall I then seek other than Allah» — I do not

seek other than Allah — «as judge» — a judge between me and you. They also wanted the Messenger to appoint a judge between them and him, while he seeks no judge other than Allah. «And He it is who sent down to you the Book» — the Qurʾan — «in detail»

making clear in it the truth from the falsehood — «And those to whom We gave the Book» — the Torah, such as ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām and his companions — «know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so be not among the doubters» (Q. 6:114) — those who doubt it — «And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled» — in rulings and in promises — «in truth and justice» — accusatives of specification (tamyīz) — «there is no changing His words» — by annulment or by breach — «and He is the Hearing» — of what is said — «the Knowing» (Q. 6:115) — of what is done — «And if you obey most of those on the earth»

the unbelievers — «they will lead you astray from the way of Allah» — from His religion — «they follow nothing but conjecture» — in their disputing with you about the matter of carrion, when they said: what Allah has killed is more deserving that you eat it than what you have killed — «and they do nothing but guess» (Q. 6:116) — they lie in that. «Indeed your Lord, He knows best» — knowing — «who strays from His way, and He knows best the rightly guided» (Q. 6:117) — and so He requites each of them. «So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned» — if you wish to eat, then eat of that over which the name of Allah was mentioned at its slaughtering — «if you are believers in His signs» (Q. 6:118). «And what is it with you, that you should not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned» — of

the slaughtered animals. «And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you» — He has made clear to you what He has forbidden you, in the verse (āya) «Forbidden to you is carrion» (Q. 5:3) — «except what you have been compelled to» — except a thing you are compelled to; necessities make the forbidden permissible. Whoever is compelled to eat carrion, carrion is lawful for him. «And indeed many lead astray by their desires» — by what their souls desire, of declaring carrion lawful and other things — «without knowledge» — upon which they might rely — «Indeed your Lord — He knows best the transgressors» (Q. 6:119) — those who pass beyond the lawful to the forbidden. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded in this verse that the animals be slaughtered in the name of Allah, and that is for a wisdom: because the throes of death are severe, so much so that the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Prompt your dying with 'there is no god but Allah'⟩ — it makes the throes of death easy for them, for the sweetness of the remembrance of Allah takes away the bitterness of the throes of death. So too the animals: when they are slaughtered in the name of Allah, the sweetness of the name of Allah takes away the bitterness of death. Whoever slaughters without the name of Allah has wronged the animal and committed an offence against it, and for this reason eating it is forbidden; and if it is slaughtered in the name of Allah it is lawful. «And forsake the outward of sin and its inward» — leave it.

He said: «And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you». The commentator said: in the verse «Forbidden» (Q. 5:3). They found this problematic, because the verse «Forbidden» was revealed in Sūrat al-Māʾida, and Sūrat al-Māʾida is among the last of what was revealed at Medina. How then can one argue from something in Sūrat al-Māʾida before it was revealed? The ulama gave several answers, among them that it was prior in the knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that in the ordering of the Qurʾan al-Māʾida comes before al-Anʿām, so that arguing from what is in Sūrat al-Māʾida is sound, because Allah's knowledge has in it neither past nor future. And it has been answered that the correct [sense of] «And He has set out in detail for you what He has forbidden you» is in the verse «Say: I do not find» (Q. 6:145), which is to come: the four forbidden things in that verse — and the sura is Meccan — are the four forbidden things

in Sūrat al-Baqara, and they are the four forbidden things in Sūrat al-Māʾida, exactly alike. The truth is that Allah, Blessed and Exalted — His presence has in it neither past nor future; so it is sound that He has made clear to you what He has forbidden you, even though the sura had not yet been revealed. «And forsake the outward of sin and its inward» (Q. 6:120). Sin is of two kinds, outward and inward. The outward is what a person commits with his limbs, and the inward is what he commits in his heart. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbade all of that. Killing a soul and fornication, for instance, are outward disobedience; and pride, envy, hatred and rancour — all these are inward acts of disobedience. Leave all of that.

«Indeed those who earn sin shall be requited» — in the hereafter — «for what they used to commit» (Q. 6:120) — acquire. «And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned» — in that it died of itself or was slaughtered in the name of other than Him; otherwise, what a Muslim has slaughtered without pronouncing the name over it, whether deliberately or forgetfully, is lawful. Ibn ʿAbbās said this, and al-Shāfiʿī holds it. «And indeed it» — that is, eating of it — «is transgression» — a going out from what is lawful — «And indeed the devils inspire» — whisper — «to their friends» — the unbelievers — «that they may dispute with you» — over declaring carrion lawful — «and if you obey them» — in that — «you are indeed polytheists» (Q. 6:121) — like them. It was revealed concerning Abū Jahl and Ḥamza. The Prophet ﷺ was praying in the Sacred Mosque about the House, and a company of the chiefs of Quraysh were looking at him. They talked among themselves, and there was there dung and a foul stench which they found repugnant. One of them said: can any of you take some of that filth and put it on Muḥammad while he is prostrate? ʿUqba b. Abī Muʿayṭ said: I can. So he took that foul thing — the afterbirth of a slaughtered camel, and dung — and placed it upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was prostrate. The unbelievers of Quraysh fell to laughing, laughing and mocking the Prophet ﷺ, rejoicing at that, until Fāṭima came to him

«the greatest of its criminals» — the wont of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: the transgressors of Mecca were the great ones, and they were the criminals who showed enmity to al-Muṣṭafā ﷺ. So too you find in every town that the great ones are
criminals,

enemies of the awliyāʾ (friends) of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «that they may plot therein» — because the great ones are the ones who have wealth and standing in abundance, and whoever has this is more able to treachery and betrayal and wrongdoing than anyone else. Whoever has much wealth and has standing must needs be eager to increase his wealth and his standing, and that increase is not had except by every foul deed, such as hatred, envy, talebearing, backbiting and swearing by false oaths. All this they must needs acquire, to guard their leadership and out of eagerness to increase their wealth.
